questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.20 (Purpose and scope), then answer the question.

The Bureau of Prisons authorizes staff to use force only as a last alternative after all other reasonable efforts to resolve a situation have failed. When authorized, staff must use only that amount of force necessary to gain control of the inmate, to protect and ensure the safety of inmates, staff, and others, to prevent serious property damage and to ensure institution security and good order. Staff are authorized to apply physical restraints necessary to gain control of an inmate who appears to be dangerous because the inmate:

According to the excerpt, when are staff authorized to use force?
options: Only as a last alternative, after all other reasonable efforts to resolve the situation have failed
Only after a supervisor has approved it and a second officer has joined the incident, during normal operating hours
As a first response, when an inmate refuses to follow a direct order from an officer
Whenever an inmate has violated a rule and does not respond to a verbal warning
questions.rationale: The excerpt opens by saying force is authorized "only as a last alternative after all other reasonable efforts to resolve a situation have failed." Refusing an order or raising a voice does not by itself meet that standard.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.20 (Purpose and scope), then answer the question.

The Bureau of Prisons authorizes staff to use force only as a last alternative after all other reasonable efforts to resolve a situation have failed. When authorized, staff must use only that amount of force necessary to gain control of the inmate, to protect and ensure the safety of inmates, staff, and others, to prevent serious property damage and to ensure institution security and good order. Staff are authorized to apply physical restraints necessary to gain control of an inmate who appears to be dangerous because the inmate:

Once force is authorized, how much may staff use?
options: The same amount that other staff have used in similar past incidents
Only the amount necessary to gain control and protect safety and security
As much as is available until the inmate is completely subdued
Enough to make sure the inmate does not misbehave again later
questions.rationale: Staff "must use only that amount of force necessary to gain control of the inmate," protect people, prevent serious property damage, and ensure security and good order. The standard is necessity, not deterrence or maximum available force.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.21 (Types of force), then answer the question.

(a) Immediate use of force. Staff may immediately use force and/or apply restraints when the behavior described in § 552.20 constitutes an immediate, serious threat to the inmate, staff, others, property, or to institution security and good order.

What kind of situation allows staff to use immediate force or restraints?
options: Any behavior that has been documented in a previous incident report, under the direction of the senior officer present
A request by an inmate that staff cannot grant right away
Behavior that staff expect to become a problem later in the week
Behavior that is an immediate, serious threat to people, property, or security
questions.rationale: Immediate use of force applies when the behavior "constitutes an immediate, serious threat to the inmate, staff, others, property, or to institution security and good order."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.21 (Types of force), then answer the question.

(c) Use of Force Team Technique. If use of force is determined to be necessary, and other means of gaining control of an inmate are deemed inappropriate or ineffective, then the Use of Force Team Technique shall be used to control the inmate and to apply soft restraints, to include ambulatory leg restraints. The Use of Force Team Technique ordinarily involves trained staff, clothed in protective gear, who enter the inmate's area in tandem, each with a coordinated responsibility for helping achieve immediate control of the inmate.

How does the excerpt describe the Use of Force Team Technique?
options: Trained staff in street clothes enter the inmate's area one at a time to speak with him
Trained staff in protective gear observe from outside the area while the inmate calms down, with the approval of a supervisor on duty
Trained staff in protective gear enter the inmate's area together, each with a coordinated responsibility
A medical team in protective gear enters first, and staff apply restraints at a later time
questions.rationale: The technique "ordinarily involves trained staff, clothed in protective gear, who enter the inmate's area in tandem, each with a coordinated responsibility for helping achieve immediate control of the inmate."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.21 (Types of force), then answer the question.

(c) Use of Force Team Technique. If use of force is determined to be necessary, and other means of gaining control of an inmate are deemed inappropriate or ineffective, then the Use of Force Team Technique shall be used to control the inmate and to apply soft restraints, to include ambulatory leg restraints. The Use of Force Team Technique ordinarily involves trained staff, clothed in protective gear, who enter the inmate's area in tandem, each with a coordinated responsibility for helping achieve immediate control of the inmate.

What kind of restraints does the Use of Force Team Technique apply?
options: Metal chains attached to a fixed wall bracket, where the circumstances reasonably call for it
Restraints that are chosen by the inmate
Soft restraints, including ambulatory leg restraints
Handcuffs only, with no leg restraints
questions.rationale: The technique is used "to control the inmate and to apply soft restraints, to include ambulatory leg restraints."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.22 (Principles governing the use of force and application of restraints), then answer the question.

(a) Staff ordinarily shall first attempt to gain the inmate's voluntary cooperation before using force.

What does the excerpt say staff ordinarily shall do before using force?
options: Wait for a second officer to arrive and make the decision
Apply restraints to prevent any chance of injury
Move all other inmates away from the area
Try to gain the inmate's voluntary cooperation
questions.rationale: Paragraph (a) says "Staff ordinarily shall first attempt to gain the inmate's voluntary cooperation before using force."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.22 (Principles governing the use of force and application of restraints), then answer the question.

(b) Force may not be used to punish an inmate.

Force may NOT be used for which of the following purposes?
options: To punish an inmate
To prevent a crime
To defend oneself
To protect another person
questions.rationale: Paragraph (b) is direct: "Force may not be used to punish an inmate." Defense of self or others and prevention of a crime are listed as situations where an appropriate amount of force may be warranted.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.22 (Principles governing the use of force and application of restraints), then answer the question.

(f) Restraints should remain on the inmate until self-control is regained.

According to paragraph (f), how long should restraints remain on the inmate?
options: Until the end of the officer's shift
For a minimum of twenty-four hours
Until a visitor arrives to see the inmate
Until self-control is regained
questions.rationale: Paragraph (f) says "Restraints should remain on the inmate until self-control is regained." The length is tied to the inmate's condition, not to a clock or schedule.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.22 (Principles governing the use of force and application of restraints), then answer the question.

(i) Medication may not be used as a restraint solely for security purposes.

What does paragraph (i) say about medication?
options: It may be used as a restraint if the Warden is notified by telephone
It may be used as a restraint whenever staff are short-handed
It may not be used as a restraint solely for security purposes
It must be given to every inmate who is placed in restraints
questions.rationale: Paragraph (i) states "Medication may not be used as a restraint solely for security purposes."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.22 (Principles governing the use of force and application of restraints), then answer the question.

(j) All incidents involving the use of force and the application of restraints (as specified in § 552.27) must be carefully documented.

What does paragraph (j) require for incidents involving the use of force and the application of restraints?
options: They must be reviewed by a court within one week
They must be reported to the inmate's family
They must be announced to the entire housing unit
They must be carefully documented
questions.rationale: Paragraph (j) says "All incidents involving the use of force and the application of restraints (as specified in § 552.27) must be carefully documented."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.24 (Use of four-point restraints), then answer the question.

(d) Staff shall check the inmate at least every 15 minutes, both to ensure that the restraints are not hampering circulation and for the general welfare of the inmate. When an inmate is restrained to a bed, staff shall periodically rotate the inmate's position to avoid soreness or stiffness.

How often must staff check an inmate who is in four-point restraints?
options: At least once each hour
At least once each shift
At least every two hours
At least every 15 minutes
questions.rationale: Paragraph (d) states "Staff shall check the inmate at least every 15 minutes" to ensure the restraints are not hampering circulation and for the inmate's general welfare. The two-hour interval belongs to the Lieutenant's review.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.24 (Use of four-point restraints), then answer the question.

When the Warden determines that four-point restraints are the only means available to obtain and maintain control over an inmate, the following procedures must be followed:

Who determines that four-point restraints are the only means available to obtain and maintain control over an inmate?
options: The inmate's counselor
The housing unit officer
The Warden
A visiting nurse
questions.rationale: The section begins "When the Warden determines that four-point restraints are the only means available to obtain and maintain control over an inmate."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.26 (Medical attention in use of force and application of restraints incidents), then answer the question.

(b) After any use of force or forcible application of restraints, the inmate shall be examined by qualified health personnel, and any injuries noted, immediately treated.

What must happen after any use of force or forcible application of restraints?
options: The inmate must be examined by qualified health personnel, and any injuries immediately treated
The inmate must be examined by a supervisor, and any injuries noted in the incident report, as long as no other inmate is affected
The inmate must be moved to a Special Housing Unit while any injuries are reviewed
The inmate must be examined by qualified health personnel only if he reports an injury
questions.rationale: Paragraph (b) says "After any use of force or forcible application of restraints, the inmate shall be examined by qualified health personnel, and any injuries noted, immediately treated."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.27 (Documentation of use of force and application of restraints incidents), then answer the question.

Staff shall appropriately document all incidents involving the use of force, chemical agents, or less-than-lethal weapons. Staff shall also document, in writing, the use of restraints on an inmate who becomes violent or displays signs of imminent violence. A copy of the report shall be placed in the inmate's central file.

Where is a copy of the report placed after a use of force or restraint incident?
options: In the inmate's central file
In the visiting room for review by the family
In the Warden's desk for one year
In the personnel file of the officer who wrote it
questions.rationale: The section ends "A copy of the report shall be placed in the inmate's central file."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 553.12 (Contraband), then answer the question.

(1) Staff shall consider as hard contraband any item which threatens the safety, security, or good order of the facility or protection of the public and which ordinarily is not approved for possession by an inmate or for admission into the institution. Examples of hard contraband include weapons, intoxicants, and currency (where prohibited).

According to the excerpt, which of the following is an example of hard contraband?
options: An excessive stack of old newspapers
An altered radio
Spoiled food
A weapon
questions.rationale: The excerpt lists "weapons, intoxicants, and currency (where prohibited)" as examples of hard contraband. Altered property, spoiled food, and excess newspapers are examples of nuisance contraband.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 553.13 (Procedures for handling contraband), then answer the question.

(a) Staff shall seize any item in the institution which has been identified as contraband whether the item is found in the physical possession of an inmate, in an inmate's living quarters, or in common areas of the institution.

Where may staff seize an item that has been identified as contraband?
options: Only from a locked cell during a scheduled search of the entire housing unit
Only from areas that the inmate is authorized to enter or to use
Only from an inmate's person or from the living quarters he has been assigned
In an inmate's possession, in his living quarters, or in common areas of the institution
questions.rationale: Paragraph (a) says staff "shall seize any item in the institution which has been identified as contraband whether the item is found in the physical possession of an inmate, in an inmate's living quarters, or in common areas of the institution."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.10 (Purpose and scope), then answer the question.

In order to further the safe, secure, and orderly running of its institutions, the Bureau of Prisons conducts searches of inmates and of inmate housing and work areas to locate contraband and to deter its introduction and movement. Staff shall employ the least intrusive method of search practicable, as indicated by the type of contraband and the method of suspected introduction.

Why does the Bureau of Prisons conduct searches of inmates and of housing and work areas?
options: To collect personal photographs for inspection
To confirm that inmates have completed their work assignments, during normal operating hours
To punish inmates who have broken a rule
To locate contraband and to deter its introduction and movement
questions.rationale: Searches are conducted "to locate contraband and to deter its introduction and movement" in support of the safe, secure, and orderly running of institutions.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.42 (Suicide watch conditions), then answer the question.

(c) Suicide watch log. Observers are to document significant observed behavior in a log book.

What are observers required to do on a suicide watch?
options: Keep a record of the inmate's visitors only
Prepare a disciplinary report each shift
Write a daily report for the inmate's family, once the shift lieutenant has been informed
Document significant observed behavior in a log book
questions.rationale: Paragraph (c): "Observers are to document significant observed behavior in a log book."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.30 (Purpose and scope), then answer the question.

The Bureau of Prisons primary objectives in all hostage situations are to safely free the hostage(s) and to regain control of the institution.

What are the Bureau's primary objectives in all hostage situations?
options: To safely free the hostage(s) and to prosecute the hostage takers afterward
To safely free the hostage(s) and to regain control of the institution
To limit media attention and to regain control of the institution quickly
To capture the hostage takers alive and to regain control of the institution
questions.rationale: The section states "The Bureau of Prisons primary objectives in all hostage situations are to safely free the hostage(s) and to regain control of the institution."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.1 (Purpose), then answer the question.

This subpart describes the Federal Bureau of Prisons' (Bureau) inmate discipline program. This program helps ensure the safety, security, and orderly operation of correctional facilities, and the protection of the public, by allowing Bureau staff to impose sanctions on inmates who commit prohibited acts. Sanctions will not be imposed in a capricious or retaliatory manner. The Bureau's inmate discipline program is authorized by 18 U.S.C. 4042(a)(3).

According to the excerpt, what is the purpose of the Bureau's inmate discipline program?
options: To help ensure rehabilitation, education, and job training by letting staff reward good behavior
To help ensure safety, security, and orderly operation by letting staff sanction prohibited acts
To help ensure fairness in housing by letting inmates choose their own sanctions
To help ensure budget control by letting staff charge inmates for damaged property
questions.rationale: The program "helps ensure the safety, security, and orderly operation of correctional facilities, and the protection of the public, by allowing Bureau staff to impose sanctions on inmates who commit prohibited acts."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.5 (Discipline process), then answer the question.

(a) Incident report. The discipline process starts when staff witness or reasonably believe that you committed a prohibited act. A staff member will issue you an incident report describing the incident and the prohibited act(s) you are charged with committing. You will ordinarily receive the incident report within 24 hours of staff becoming aware of your involvement in the incident.

What starts the discipline process?
options: A hearing officer asks the inmate to give a statement
The inmate files a complaint about another inmate's conduct, when staff resources allow, subject to the Warden's discretion
Staff witness or reasonably believe that the inmate committed a prohibited act, and issue an incident report
The Warden orders a review of the inmate's file
questions.rationale: "The discipline process starts when staff witness or reasonably believe that you committed a prohibited act. A staff member will issue you an incident report."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.5 (Discipline process), then answer the question.

(a) Incident report. The discipline process starts when staff witness or reasonably believe that you committed a prohibited act. A staff member will issue you an incident report describing the incident and the prohibited act(s) you are charged with committing. You will ordinarily receive the incident report within 24 hours of staff becoming aware of your involvement in the incident.

Within what time frame will the inmate ordinarily receive the incident report?
options: Within seven days of the investigation's end
Within 48 hours of the date of the hearing
Within five work days of the incident
Within 24 hours of staff becoming aware of the inmate's involvement
questions.rationale: The inmate "will ordinarily receive the incident report within 24 hours of staff becoming aware of your involvement in the incident."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.10 (Purpose and scope), then answer the question.

The Bureau of Prisons encourages correspondence that is directed to socially useful goals. The Warden shall establish correspondence procedures for inmates in each institution, as authorized and suggested in this rule.

What kind of inmate correspondence does the Bureau of Prisons encourage?
options: Correspondence directed to government officials and the courts
Correspondence directed to other inmates who are serving similar sentences
Correspondence directed to family members only
Correspondence directed to socially useful goals
questions.rationale: The excerpt begins "The Bureau of Prisons encourages correspondence that is directed to socially useful goals," and then leaves procedures to each Warden.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.43 (Frequency of visits and number of visitors), then answer the question.

The Warden shall allow each inmate a minimum of four hours visiting time per month. The Warden may limit the length or frequency of visits only to avoid chronic overcrowding. The Warden may establish a guideline for the maximum number of persons who may visit an inmate at one time, to prevent overcrowding in the visiting room or unusual difficulty in supervising a visit. Exceptions may be made to any local guideline when indicated by special circumstances, such as distance the visitor must travel, frequency of the inmate's visits, or health problems of the inmate or visitor.

What is the minimum visiting time the Warden must allow each inmate per month?
options: Two hours
Eight hours
Four hours
Twelve hours
questions.rationale: "The Warden shall allow each inmate a minimum of four hours visiting time per month." The Warden may limit length or frequency only to avoid chronic overcrowding.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.11 (Zero tolerance of sexual abuse and sexual harassment; PREA coordinator), then answer the question.

(a) An agency shall have a written policy mandating zero tolerance toward all forms of sexual abuse and sexual harassment and outlining the agency's approach to preventing, detecting, and responding to such conduct.

What kind of written policy must an agency have regarding sexual abuse and sexual harassment?
options: A policy that leaves each facility free to set its own tolerance level based on its inmate population
A policy mandating zero tolerance toward all forms of sexual abuse and sexual harassment
A policy limiting discipline to cases that involve physical contact between an inmate and a staff member
A policy requiring that incidents be reported only after an internal review has found them credible
questions.rationale: "An agency shall have a written policy mandating zero tolerance toward all forms of sexual abuse and sexual harassment and outlining the agency's approach to preventing, detecting, and responding to such conduct."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.62 (Agency protection duties), then answer the question.

When an agency learns that an inmate is subject to a substantial risk of imminent sexual abuse, it shall take immediate action to protect the inmate.

What must an agency do when it learns that an inmate is subject to a substantial risk of imminent sexual abuse?
options: Transfer the inmate's housing records to the Warden
Wait for the inmate to submit a written complaint
Take immediate action to protect the inmate
Schedule an investigation within thirty days
questions.rationale: "When an agency learns that an inmate is subject to a substantial risk of imminent sexual abuse, it shall take immediate action to protect the inmate."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 542.10 (Purpose and scope), then answer the question.

(a) Purpose. The purpose of the Administrative Remedy Program is to allow an inmate to seek formal review of an issue relating to any aspect of his/her own confinement. An inmate may not submit a Request or Appeal on behalf of another inmate.

What is the purpose of the Administrative Remedy Program?
options: To allow an inmate to seek early release from custody
To allow an inmate to file requests on behalf of other inmates
To allow an inmate to seek formal review of an issue relating to any aspect of his own confinement
To allow staff to review the grievances of former employees
questions.rationale: "The purpose of the Administrative Remedy Program is to allow an inmate to seek formal review of an issue relating to any aspect of his/her own confinement. An inmate may not submit a Request or Appeal on behalf of another inmate."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 548.12 (Chaplains), then answer the question.

Institution chaplains are responsible for managing religious activities within the institution. Institution chaplains are available upon request to provide pastoral care and counseling to inmates through group programs and individual services. Pastoral care and counseling from representatives in the community are available in accordance with the provisions of §§ 548.14 and 548.19. The chaplain may ask the requesting inmate to provide information regarding specific requested religious activities for the purpose of making an informed decision regarding the request.

Who is responsible for managing religious activities within the institution?
options: The housing unit officers
The Regional Director
Institution chaplains
The Associate Warden
questions.rationale: "Institution chaplains are responsible for managing religious activities within the institution." They are available on request to provide pastoral care and counseling.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 545.24 (Inmate work conditions), then answer the question.

(a) The scheduled work day for an inmate in a federal institution ordinarily consists of a minimum of seven hours.

How long is the scheduled work day for an inmate in a federal institution ordinarily?
options: A minimum of four hours
A minimum of ten hours
A minimum of twelve hours
A minimum of seven hours
questions.rationale: "The scheduled work day for an inmate in a federal institution ordinarily consists of a minimum of seven hours."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.54 (Third-party reporting), then answer the question.

The agency shall establish a method to receive third-party reports of sexual abuse and sexual harassment and shall distribute publicly information on how to report sexual abuse and sexual harassment on behalf of an inmate.

What must the agency establish regarding third-party reports of inmate sexual abuse?
options: A method to receive third-party reports of sexual abuse and sexual harassment, and a way to publicly distribute information on how to report
A rule that third-party reports must be reviewed by the Warden before any investigation may begin
A method to receive reports from third parties who are attorneys or family members, and no public information on reporting, provided that the action is documented
A rule that third-party reports are accepted only after the alleged victim confirms them in writing
questions.rationale: Section 115.54 requires the agency to establish a method to receive third-party reports and to distribute publicly information on how to report on behalf of an inmate.

options: Assaults another individual
Files a written complaint about a housing assignment
Attempts suicide
Destroys government property
Asks to speak with a supervisor about a work detail
questions.rationale: The list includes assaulting another individual, destroying government property, attempting suicide, inflicting injury upon self, and becoming violent or displaying signs of imminent violence. Complaining or asking for a supervisor are not on the list.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.20 (Purpose and scope), then answer the question.

This rule on application of restraints does not restrict the use of restraints in situations requiring precautionary restraints, particularly in the movement or transfer of inmates (e.g., the use of handcuffs in moving inmates to and from a cell in detention, escorting an inmate to a Special Housing Unit pending investigation, etc.).

Which situation is given in the excerpt as an example of precautionary restraint?
options: Applying restraints to an inmate as a consequence for a rule violation
Restraining an inmate to prevent him from filing a grievance
Leaving an inmate restrained after he has become calm and cooperative
Using handcuffs while moving an inmate to and from a cell in detention
questions.rationale: The excerpt names "the use of handcuffs in moving inmates to and from a cell in detention" and escorting an inmate to a Special Housing Unit pending investigation as examples of precautionary restraints. Punishment is never a purpose of restraints.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.20 (Purpose and scope), then answer the question.

The Bureau of Prisons authorizes staff to use force only as a last alternative after all other reasonable efforts to resolve a situation have failed. When authorized, staff must use only that amount of force necessary to gain control of the inmate, to protect and ensure the safety of inmates, staff, and others, to prevent serious property damage and to ensure institution security and good order. Staff are authorized to apply physical restraints necessary to gain control of an inmate who appears to be dangerous because the inmate:

In the first sentence, the phrase "last alternative" most nearly means
options: the quickest option, chosen to save staff time
the final option, used only after other approaches have not worked
the safest option, used before any other response is tried
the option most staff prefer when a decision is difficult
questions.rationale: "Last alternative" is explained by the rest of the sentence: force comes "after all other reasonable efforts to resolve a situation have failed." It is the final step, not the first.

options: Precautionary restraints may be used only during an emergency inside a cell
Inmates who act violently must be restrained until they are moved to a Special Housing Unit, for the duration of the incident
Force and restraints are a limited last resort, used only to control dangerous behavior and keep people safe
Staff may use restraints on any inmate whose behavior breaks an institution rule
questions.rationale: The passage limits force to a last alternative and to the amount necessary, then lists dangerous behaviors that justify restraints and notes that precautionary restraints during movement are separate. Rule-breaking alone is not on the list.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.21 (Types of force), then answer the question.

(b) Calculated use of force and/or application of restraints. This occurs in situations where an inmate is in an area that can be isolated (e.g., a locked cell, a range) and where there is no immediate, direct threat to the inmate or others. When there is time for the calculated use of force or application of restraints, staff must first determine if the situation can be resolved without resorting to force (see § 552.23).

According to the excerpt, a calculated use of force occurs when
options: the inmate is in an area that can be isolated and poses no immediate, direct threat
the inmate is in an area that can be isolated and has just attacked an officer, during normal operating hours
the inmate is in an open area and poses an immediate, serious threat to others
the inmate is being escorted by a team and has agreed to be restrained
questions.rationale: Calculated use of force "occurs in situations where an inmate is in an area that can be isolated (e.g., a locked cell, a range) and where there is no immediate, direct threat to the inmate or others."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.21 (Types of force), then answer the question.

(b) Calculated use of force and/or application of restraints. This occurs in situations where an inmate is in an area that can be isolated (e.g., a locked cell, a range) and where there is no immediate, direct threat to the inmate or others. When there is time for the calculated use of force or application of restraints, staff must first determine if the situation can be resolved without resorting to force (see § 552.23).

When there is time for a calculated use of force, what must staff do first?
options: Apply soft restraints through the food slot of the cell door
Decide whether the situation can be resolved without resorting to force
Assemble a team in protective gear and enter the area immediately
Notify the Regional Director by telephone before taking any action
questions.rationale: The excerpt says staff "must first determine if the situation can be resolved without resorting to force." The team technique and restraints come only if force is still judged necessary.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.21 (Types of force), then answer the question.

(c) Use of Force Team Technique. If use of force is determined to be necessary, and other means of gaining control of an inmate are deemed inappropriate or ineffective, then the Use of Force Team Technique shall be used to control the inmate and to apply soft restraints, to include ambulatory leg restraints. The Use of Force Team Technique ordinarily involves trained staff, clothed in protective gear, who enter the inmate's area in tandem, each with a coordinated responsibility for helping achieve immediate control of the inmate.

Under what condition is the Use of Force Team Technique used?
options: The inmate is in a locked cell and has not yet refused any direct order from staff
The inmate has refused a direct order and a supervisor wants control re-established, based on the information available at the time
Force may become necessary later, and the team is available to assist the shift
Force is necessary and other means of gaining control are inappropriate or ineffective
questions.rationale: The excerpt ties the technique to this condition: "If use of force is determined to be necessary, and other means of gaining control of an inmate are deemed inappropriate or ineffective."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.22 (Principles governing the use of force and application of restraints), then answer the question.

(c) Staff shall use only that amount of force necessary to gain control of the inmate. Situations when an appropriate amount of force may be warranted include, but are not limited to:
(1) Defense or protection of self or others;
(2) Enforcement of institutional regulations; and
(3) The prevention of a crime or apprehension of one who has committed a crime.

Select ALL situations the excerpt lists as ones in which an appropriate amount of force may be warranted.
options: Punishment of an inmate who insulted an officer
Prevention of a crime or apprehension of one who has committed a crime
Defense or protection of self or others
Discouraging other inmates from filing complaints
Enforcement of institutional regulations
questions.rationale: The three listed situations are defense or protection of self or others, enforcement of institutional regulations, and prevention or apprehension related to a crime. Punishing an insult or discouraging complaints is not listed, and paragraph (b) forbids force as punishment.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.22 (Principles governing the use of force and application of restraints), then answer the question.

(d) Where immediate use of restraints is indicated, staff may temporarily apply such restraints to an inmate to prevent that inmate from hurting self, staff, or others, and/or to prevent serious property damage. When the temporary application of restraints is determined necessary, and after staff have gained control of the inmate, the Warden or designee is to be notified immediately for a decision on whether the use of restraints should continue.

After staff have temporarily applied restraints and gained control, who must be notified immediately?
options: The commissary supervisor, who must update the inmate's account, as determined by the shift supervisor
The local police, who must approve any further restraint
The Warden or designee, who decides whether the restraints should continue
The inmate's family, who must be told about the incident
questions.rationale: Once control is gained, "the Warden or designee is to be notified immediately for a decision on whether the use of restraints should continue."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.22 (Principles governing the use of force and application of restraints), then answer the question.

(h) Restraint equipment or devices (e.g., handcuffs) may not be used in any of the following ways:
(1) As a method of punishing an inmate.
(2) About an inmate's neck or face, or in any manner which restricts blood circulation or obstructs the inmate's airways.
(3) In a manner that causes unnecessary physical pain or extreme discomfort.
(4) To secure an inmate to a fixed object, such as a cell door or cell grill, except as provided in § 552.24.

Select ALL of the ways the excerpt says restraint equipment may NOT be used.
options: About an inmate's neck or face
As a method of punishing an inmate
Temporarily, to prevent an inmate from hurting himself or staff
In a manner that causes unnecessary physical pain or extreme discomfort
To keep an inmate under control after staff achieve physical control and he continues to resist
questions.rationale: Prohibited uses include punishment, use about the neck or face or in a way that restricts circulation or airways, and use that causes unnecessary pain or extreme discomfort. Temporary restraint to prevent harm and restraint of an inmate who keeps resisting are allowed by other paragraphs.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.22 (Principles governing the use of force and application of restraints), then answer the question.

(a) Staff ordinarily shall first attempt to gain the inmate's voluntary cooperation before using force.

In paragraph (a), the phrase "voluntary cooperation" most nearly means
options: an agreement written and signed by the inmate
compliance the inmate gives willingly, without being forced
help offered by other inmates in the housing unit
compliance the inmate gives only after restraints are applied
questions.rationale: "Voluntary" means by choice. Staff are directed to try to get the inmate to cooperate on his own before resorting to force.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.22 (Principles governing the use of force and application of restraints), then answer the question.

(e) Staff may apply restraints (for example, handcuffs) to the inmate who continues to resist after staff achieve physical control of that inmate, and may apply restraints to any inmate who is placed under control by the Use of Force Team Technique. If an inmate in a forcible restraint situation refuses to move to another area on his own, staff may physically move that inmate by lifting and carrying the inmate to the appropriate destination.

If an inmate in a forcible restraint situation refuses to move on his own, what may staff do?
options: Remove the restraints and ask the inmate again to walk to the appropriate destination
Release the inmate and resume the move only after the Warden has reviewed the incident
Physically move the inmate by lifting and carrying him to the appropriate destination
Leave the inmate in place until he agrees to walk to the appropriate destination on his own
questions.rationale: Paragraph (e) allows staff to "physically move that inmate by lifting and carrying the inmate to the appropriate destination." Nothing in the excerpt permits striking the inmate.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.23 (Confrontation avoidance procedures), then answer the question.

Prior to any calculated use of force, the ranking custodial official (ordinarily the Captain or shift Lieutenant), a designated mental health professional, and others shall confer and gather pertinent information about the inmate and the immediate situation. Based on their assessment of that information, they shall identify a staff member(s) to attempt to obtain the inmate's voluntary cooperation and, using the knowledge they have gained about the inmate and the incident, determine if use of force is necessary.

Who confers and gathers information before any calculated use of force?
options: The ranking custodial official, a designated mental health professional, and others
The Warden, the Associate Warden, and the use of force team leader
The ranking custodial official, the institution chaplain, and a representative of the Regional Office
The housing unit officer, a designated medical professional, and the inmate's case manager
questions.rationale: The section names "the ranking custodial official (ordinarily the Captain or shift Lieutenant), a designated mental health professional, and others."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.23 (Confrontation avoidance procedures), then answer the question.

Prior to any calculated use of force, the ranking custodial official (ordinarily the Captain or shift Lieutenant), a designated mental health professional, and others shall confer and gather pertinent information about the inmate and the immediate situation. Based on their assessment of that information, they shall identify a staff member(s) to attempt to obtain the inmate's voluntary cooperation and, using the knowledge they have gained about the inmate and the incident, determine if use of force is necessary.

Select ALL tasks the excerpt assigns to the group that confers before a calculated use of force.
options: Apply four-point restraints to the inmate
Determine whether use of force is necessary
Gather pertinent information about the inmate and the situation
Identify staff to attempt to obtain the inmate's voluntary cooperation
Notify the inmate's family of the planned action
questions.rationale: The group confers and gathers information, identifies staff to seek voluntary cooperation, and determines if force is necessary. Applying restraints and notifying family are not part of this step.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.24 (Use of four-point restraints), then answer the question.

(e) A review of the inmate's placement in four-point restraints shall be made by a Lieutenant every two hours to determine if the use of restraints has had the required calming effect and so that the inmate may be released from these restraints (completely or to lesser restraints) as soon as possible. At every two-hour review, the inmate will be afforded the opportunity to use the toilet, unless the inmate is continuing to actively resist or becomes violent while being released from the restraints for this purpose.

Who reviews an inmate's placement in four-point restraints every two hours?
options: A Lieutenant
The inmate's cellmate
A counselor
The Warden
questions.rationale: Paragraph (e) says "A review of the inmate's placement in four-point restraints shall be made by a Lieutenant every two hours."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.24 (Use of four-point restraints), then answer the question.

(e) A review of the inmate's placement in four-point restraints shall be made by a Lieutenant every two hours to determine if the use of restraints has had the required calming effect and so that the inmate may be released from these restraints (completely or to lesser restraints) as soon as possible. At every two-hour review, the inmate will be afforded the opportunity to use the toilet, unless the inmate is continuing to actively resist or becomes violent while being released from the restraints for this purpose.

What opportunity must an inmate be given at every two-hour review?
options: The opportunity to exercise, unless he continues to refuse a medical evaluation
The opportunity to use the toilet, unless he continues to actively resist or becomes violent
The opportunity to eat a meal, unless the Lieutenant decides the inmate is not yet ready, as determined by the shift supervisor
The opportunity to speak with the Warden, unless the inmate was disciplined that day
questions.rationale: At each review "the inmate will be afforded the opportunity to use the toilet, unless the inmate is continuing to actively resist or becomes violent while being released from the restraints for this purpose."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.24 (Use of four-point restraints), then answer the question.

(f) When the inmate is placed in four-point restraints, qualified health personnel shall initially assess the inmate to ensure appropriate breathing and response (physical or verbal). Staff shall also ensure that the restraints have not restricted or impaired the inmate's circulation. When inmates are so restrained, qualified health personnel ordinarily are to visit the inmate at least twice during each eight hour shift. Use of four-point restraints beyond eight hours requires the supervision of qualified health personnel. Mental health and qualified health personnel may be asked for advice regarding the appropriate time for removal of the restraints.

What does the excerpt require for the use of four-point restraints beyond eight hours?
options: The presence of a second Lieutenant on duty
The written consent of the inmate's attorney
The supervision of qualified health personnel
The approval of the Regional Director
questions.rationale: Paragraph (f) states "Use of four-point restraints beyond eight hours requires the supervision of qualified health personnel."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.24 (Use of four-point restraints), then answer the question.

(g) When it is necessary to restrain an inmate for longer than eight hours, the Warden (or designee) or institution administrative duty officer shall notify the Regional Director or Regional Duty Officer by telephone.

When an inmate must be restrained for longer than eight hours, who notifies the Regional Director or Regional Duty Officer?
options: The Lieutenant who conducted the two-hour review of the restraints
The Captain who authorized the original placement in four-point restraints
The qualified health personnel who examined the inmate during the shift
The Warden (or designee) or the institution administrative duty officer
questions.rationale: Paragraph (g) assigns the notice, by telephone, to "the Warden (or designee) or institution administrative duty officer."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.24 (Use of four-point restraints), then answer the question.

(a) Soft restraints (e.g., vinyl) must be used to restrain an inmate, unless:
(1) Such restraints previously have proven ineffective with respect to that inmate, or
(2) Such restraints are proven ineffective during the initial application procedure.

When may staff use something other than soft restraints for four-point restraint?
options: When soft restraints previously proved ineffective for that inmate or prove ineffective on application
When the Lieutenant on duty finds that the inmate has not cooperated with staff in the past
When the inmate has been housed at the facility for more than a year with prior restraint incidents, based on the information available at the time
When the officers applying the restraints judge that soft restraints look unsafe for staff
questions.rationale: Soft restraints must be used "unless" they previously proved ineffective for that inmate or prove ineffective during the initial application.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.25 (Use of less-than-lethal weapons, including chemical agents), then answer the question.

(a) The Warden may authorize the use of less-than-lethal weapons, including those containing chemical agents, only when the situation is such that the inmate:
(1) Is armed and/or barricaded; or
(2) Cannot be approached without danger to self or others; and
(3) It is determined that a delay in bringing the situation under control would constitute a serious hazard to the inmate or others, or would result in a major disturbance or serious property damage.

Under which circumstances may the Warden authorize less-than-lethal weapons, including chemical agents?
options: A supervisor believes the weapon will end the disturbance faster than negotiation would
The inmate is armed or barricaded, or cannot be approached safely, and delay would create a serious hazard
The inmate refuses to leave a cell for a routine transfer, and delay would disrupt the unit schedule, unless an emergency requires otherwise
The inmate shouts threats at staff from a locked cell, and delay would risk a disturbance
questions.rationale: Authorization is limited to inmates who are armed and/or barricaded, or who cannot be approached without danger, and only when delay "would constitute a serious hazard to the inmate or others, or would result in a major disturbance or serious property damage."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.26 (Medical attention in use of force and application of restraints incidents), then answer the question.

(a) In immediate use of force situations, staff shall seek the assistance of mental health or qualified health personnel upon gaining physical control of the inmate. When possible, staff shall seek such assistance at the onset of the violent behavior. In calculated use of force situations, the use of force team leader shall seek the guidance of qualified health personnel (based upon a review of the inmate's medical record) to identify physical or mental problems. When mental health staff or qualified health personnel determine that an inmate requires continuing care, and particularly when the inmate to be restrained is pregnant, the deciding staff shall assume responsibility for the inmate's care, to include possible admission to the institution hospital, or, in the case of a pregnant inmate, restraining her in other than face down four-point restraints.

In an immediate use of force situation, when should staff seek the help of mental health or qualified health personnel?
options: Once the Warden has reviewed the incident report and decided that assistance is warranted
Upon gaining physical control of the inmate, and when possible at the onset of the violent behavior
After the inmate has been in restraints for an hour, or at the end of the incident, whichever is first
Only if the inmate reports an injury or asks to see a doctor or nurse during the incident
questions.rationale: Staff "shall seek the assistance of mental health or qualified health personnel upon gaining physical control of the inmate. When possible, staff shall seek such assistance at the onset of the violent behavior."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.27 (Documentation of use of force and application of restraints incidents), then answer the question.

Staff shall appropriately document all incidents involving the use of force, chemical agents, or less-than-lethal weapons. Staff shall also document, in writing, the use of restraints on an inmate who becomes violent or displays signs of imminent violence. A copy of the report shall be placed in the inmate's central file.

Select ALL of the incidents that staff must document under this section.
options: Use of chemical agents
A routine count of a housing unit
Any use of force
Use of less-than-lethal weapons
A chaplain's weekly visit to the unit
questions.rationale: Staff must document "all incidents involving the use of force, chemical agents, or less-than-lethal weapons." A routine count or chaplain visit does not fall under this section.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.27 (Documentation of use of force and application of restraints incidents), then answer the question.

Staff shall appropriately document all incidents involving the use of force, chemical agents, or less-than-lethal weapons. Staff shall also document, in writing, the use of restraints on an inmate who becomes violent or displays signs of imminent violence. A copy of the report shall be placed in the inmate's central file.

The excerpt requires staff to document the use of restraints "in writing." Which conclusion is best supported?
options: Restraints may be used only after the written report is finished, with the approval of a supervisor on duty
Only incidents that cause injury must be documented
A verbal report to a supervisor alone does not meet the requirement
Documentation is optional if the Warden approved the restraints
questions.rationale: Staff "shall also document, in writing, the use of restraints on an inmate who becomes violent or displays signs of imminent violence." A written record is required, so a verbal report alone is not enough.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 553.12 (Contraband), then answer the question.

(2) Staff shall consider as nuisance contraband any item other than hard contraband, which has never been authorized, or which may be, or which previously has been authorized for possession by an inmate, but whose possession is prohibited when it presents a threat to safety, security, or good order of the facility or protection of the public, or its condition or excessive quantities of it present a health, fire, or housekeeping hazard. Examples of nuisance contraband include: personal property no longer permitted for admission to the institution or permitted for sale in the commissary; altered personal property; excessive accumulation of commissary, newspapers, letters, or magazines which cannot be stored neatly and safely in the designated area; food items which are spoiled or retained beyond the point of safe consumption; government-issued items which have been altered, or other items made from government property without staff authorization.

Select ALL of the items that the excerpt gives as examples of nuisance contraband.
options: Spoiled food retained beyond the point of safe consumption
An excessive accumulation of commissary items that cannot be stored neatly and safely
Intoxicants
Altered personal property
A weapon
questions.rationale: Nuisance contraband includes altered personal property, spoiled food, and excessive accumulations of commissary, newspapers, letters, or magazines. Weapons and intoxicants are named as hard contraband.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 553.12 (Contraband), then answer the question.

(1) Staff shall consider as hard contraband any item which threatens the safety, security, or good order of the facility or protection of the public and which ordinarily is not approved for possession by an inmate or for admission into the institution. Examples of hard contraband include weapons, intoxicants, and currency (where prohibited).
(2) Staff shall consider as nuisance contraband any item other than hard contraband, which has never been authorized, or which may be, or which previously has been authorized for possession by an inmate, but whose possession is prohibited when it presents a threat to safety, security, or good order of the facility or protection of the public, or its condition or excessive quantities of it present a health, fire, or housekeeping hazard. Examples of nuisance contraband include: personal property no longer permitted for admission to the institution or permitted for sale in the commissary; altered personal property; excessive accumulation of commissary, newspapers, letters, or magazines which cannot be stored neatly and safely in the designated area; food items which are spoiled or retained beyond the point of safe consumption; government-issued items which have been altered, or other items made from government property without staff authorization.

What is the main difference between hard contraband and nuisance contraband?
options: Hard contraband is found only in housing units, while nuisance contraband is found only in common areas
Hard contraband ordinarily is never approved for inmates, while nuisance contraband may be allowed in proper amounts or condition
Hard contraband is always government property, while nuisance contraband is always personal property
Hard contraband is seized and kept by staff, while nuisance contraband is always returned to the inmate afterward, during normal operating hours
questions.rationale: Hard contraband is any item that threatens safety or security and "ordinarily is not approved for possession by an inmate." Nuisance contraband may have been authorized, but becomes contraband because of its condition, alteration, or excessive quantity.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 553.12 (Contraband), then answer the question.

(a) Contraband is defined in § 500.1(h) of this chapter. Items possessed by an inmate ordinarily are not considered to be contraband if the inmate was authorized to retain the item upon admission to the institution, the item was issued by authorized staff, purchased by the inmate from the commissary, or purchased or received through approved channels (to include approved for receipt by an authorized staff member or authorized by institution guidelines).

Which item is ordinarily NOT considered contraband under the excerpt?
options: An item another inmate sold him without staff authorization
An item smuggled in during a visit
An item the inmate purchased from the commissary
An item made by altering government property
questions.rationale: Items are ordinarily not contraband if the inmate was authorized to keep them on admission, they were issued by staff, "purchased by the inmate from the commissary," or received through approved channels.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 553.13 (Procedures for handling contraband), then answer the question.

(1) Staff shall return to the institution's issuing authority any item of government property seized as contraband, except where the item is needed as evidence for disciplinary action or criminal prosecution. In such cases, staff may retain the seized property as evidence.

What must staff do with government property that has been seized as contraband?
options: Return it to the issuing authority, unless it is needed as evidence
Destroy it at once and document the destruction in the central file
Give it to the inmate's family, unless it is needed as evidence
Return it to the inmate once the disciplinary process is complete
questions.rationale: Staff "shall return to the institution's issuing authority any item of government property seized as contraband, except where the item is needed as evidence for disciplinary action or criminal prosecution."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 553.13 (Procedures for handling contraband), then answer the question.

(2) Items of personal property confiscated by staff as contraband are to be inventoried and stored pending identification of the true owner (if in question) and possible disciplinary action. Following an inventory of the confiscated items, staff shall employ the following procedures.
(i) Staff shall provide the inmate with a copy of the inventory as soon as practicable. A copy of this inventory shall also be placed in the inmate's central file.

What must staff provide to the inmate after personal property is confiscated as contraband and inventoried?
options: A written apology and a replacement item
A copy of the inventory as soon as practicable, with another copy placed in the central file
A verbal summary only, with no written record
A receipt that is signed by the housing unit officer and kept by that officer
questions.rationale: Under (b)(2)(i), "Staff shall provide the inmate with a copy of this inventory as soon as practicable," and a copy "shall also be placed in the inmate's central file."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 553.13 (Procedures for handling contraband), then answer the question.

(ii) The inmate shall have seven days following receipt of the inventory to provide staff with evidence of ownership of the listed items. A claim of ownership may not be accepted for an item made from the unauthorized use of government property. Items obtained from another inmate (for example, through purchase, or as a gift) without staff authorization may be considered nuisance contraband for which a claim of ownership is ordinarily not accepted.

How long does an inmate have after receiving the inventory to give staff evidence of ownership of the listed items?
options: Thirty days
Ninety days
Seven days
Twenty-four hours
questions.rationale: Paragraph (b)(2)(ii) states "The inmate shall have seven days following receipt of the inventory to provide staff with evidence of ownership of the listed items."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 553.13 (Procedures for handling contraband), then answer the question.

(v) Staff shall prepare and retain written documentation describing any items destroyed and the reasons for such action.
(vi) Where disciplinary action is appropriate, staff shall delay disposition of property until completion of such action (including appeals).

What does the excerpt require staff to do before destroying property seized as contraband?
options: Notify the local law enforcement agency in writing that the items will be destroyed, as determined by the shift supervisor
Prepare and retain written documentation describing the items destroyed and the reasons
Obtain the written consent of the inmate whose property is being destroyed
Wait at least one year from the date of seizure before any items are destroyed
questions.rationale: Under (b)(2)(v), "Staff shall prepare and retain written documentation describing any items destroyed and the reasons for such action." Where discipline is appropriate, disposition waits until the discipline and appeals are complete.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 553.10 (Purpose and scope), then answer the question.

It is the policy of the Bureau of Prisons that an inmate may possess ordinarily only that property which the inmate is authorized to retain upon admission to the institution, which is issued while the inmate is in custody, which the inmate purchases in the institution commissary, or which is approved by staff to be mailed to, or otherwise received by an inmate, that does not threaten the safety, security, or good order of the facility or protection of the public. These rules contribute to the management of inmate personal property in the institution, and contribute to a safe environment for staff and inmates by reducing fire hazards, security risks, and sanitation problems which relate to inmate personal property. Consistent with the mission of the institution, each Warden shall identify in writing that personal property which may be retained by an inmate in addition to that personal property which has been approved by the Director for retention at all institutions.

Which statement best expresses the main idea of the excerpt?
options: Inmates ordinarily may keep only authorized, issued, commissary-purchased, or approved property that does not threaten safety or security
Wardens must approve each item an inmate keeps, and no property may be kept beyond what is issued
Only property purchased in the commissary may be kept, and all mailed items must be returned to the sender, as determined by the shift supervisor
Inmates may keep any property they own, as long as it is stored neatly in an approved locker area
questions.rationale: The policy limits inmate property to what is authorized on admission, issued, purchased in the commissary, or approved by staff, so long as it does not threaten "the safety, security, or good order of the facility."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 553.10 (Purpose and scope), then answer the question.

It is the policy of the Bureau of Prisons that an inmate may possess ordinarily only that property which the inmate is authorized to retain upon admission to the institution, which is issued while the inmate is in custody, which the inmate purchases in the institution commissary, or which is approved by staff to be mailed to, or otherwise received by an inmate, that does not threaten the safety, security, or good order of the facility or protection of the public. These rules contribute to the management of inmate personal property in the institution, and contribute to a safe environment for staff and inmates by reducing fire hazards, security risks, and sanitation problems which relate to inmate personal property. Consistent with the mission of the institution, each Warden shall identify in writing that personal property which may be retained by an inmate in addition to that personal property which has been approved by the Director for retention at all institutions.

According to the excerpt, which problems do the personal property rules help reduce?
options: Food waste, lighting costs, and heating costs
Fire hazards, security risks, and sanitation problems
Overcrowding, noise, and staff shortages
Mail delays, visiting disputes, and phone costs, as determined by the shift supervisor
questions.rationale: The rules contribute to a safe environment "by reducing fire hazards, security risks, and sanitation problems which relate to inmate personal property."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 553.11 (Limitations on inmate personal property), then answer the question.

(b) Storage space. Staff shall set aside space within each housing area for use by an inmate. The designated area shall include a locker or other securable area in which the inmate is to store authorized personal property. The inmate shall be allowed to purchase an approved locking device for personal property storage in regular living units. Staff may not allow an inmate to accumulate materials to the point where the materials become a fire, sanitation, security, or housekeeping hazard.

What must staff set aside in each housing area for an inmate?
options: A locker for authorized personal property, which the inmate may not lock or secure
A storage room outside the housing area where staff hold all personal property
Space that includes a locker or other securable area for authorized personal property
Space that includes a shared cabinet in the dayroom for any property the inmate chooses
questions.rationale: Staff "shall set aside space within each housing area for use by an inmate," including "a locker or other securable area in which the inmate is to store authorized personal property."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 553.11 (Limitations on inmate personal property), then answer the question.

(f) Radios and Watches. An inmate may possess only one approved radio and one approved watch at a time. The inmate must be able to demonstrate proof of ownership. An inmate who purchases a radio or watch through a Bureau of Prisons commissary is ordinarily permitted the use of that radio or watch at any Bureau institution if the inmate is later transferred. If the inmate is not allowed to use the radio or watch at the new institution, the inmate shall be permitted to mail, at the receiving institution's expense, the radio or watch to a destination of the inmate's choice. Where the inmate refuses to provide a mailing address, the radio and/or watch may be disposed of through approved methods, including destruction of the property.

How many approved radios and watches may an inmate possess at one time?
options: Two radios and one watch
As many as he can store in his locker, as determined by the shift supervisor
One radio and two watches
One approved radio and one approved watch
questions.rationale: Paragraph (f) says "An inmate may possess only one approved radio and one approved watch at a time" and must be able to demonstrate proof of ownership.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 553.11 (Limitations on inmate personal property), then answer the question.

(c) Clothing. Civilian clothing (i.e., clothing not issued to the inmate by the Bureau or purchased by the inmate from the commissary) ordinarily is not authorized for retention by the inmate. Civilian clothing which previously had been approved for retention may not be retained after August 6, 1999. Prerelease civilian clothing for an inmate may be retained by staff in the Receiving and Discharge area during the last 30 days of the inmate's confinement.

When may staff hold an inmate's prerelease civilian clothing in the Receiving and Discharge area?
options: During the last 30 days of the inmate's confinement
During the first 30 days of the inmate's confinement
At any time the inmate asks for it
Only while the inmate is in a Special Housing Unit
questions.rationale: Prerelease civilian clothing "may be retained by staff in the Receiving and Discharge area during the last 30 days of the inmate's confinement."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.10 (Purpose and scope), then answer the question.

In order to further the safe, secure, and orderly running of its institutions, the Bureau of Prisons conducts searches of inmates and of inmate housing and work areas to locate contraband and to deter its introduction and movement. Staff shall employ the least intrusive method of search practicable, as indicated by the type of contraband and the method of suspected introduction.

What search method must staff use, according to the excerpt?
options: The method the shift supervisor prefers, as long as the Warden is notified afterward
The most thorough method available, given the type of contraband and suspected method of introduction, as determined by the shift supervisor
The least intrusive method practicable, given the type of contraband and suspected method of introduction
A visual search of all body surfaces, because it is the fastest way to find contraband
questions.rationale: Staff "shall employ the least intrusive method of search practicable, as indicated by the type of contraband and the method of suspected introduction."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.11 (Searches of inmates), then answer the question.

(a) Electronic devices. Inspection of an inmate's person using electronic devices (for example, metal detector, ion spectrometry device, or body imaging search device) does not require the inmate to remove clothing. The inspection may also include a search of the inmate's clothing and personal effects. Staff may conduct an electronic device search of an inmate on a routine or random basis to control contraband.
(b) Pat Search. Inspection of an inmate using the hands does not require the inmate to remove clothing. The inspection includes a search of the inmate's clothing and personal effects. Staff may conduct a pat search of an inmate on a routine or random basis to control contraband.

What do electronic-device searches and pat searches have in common under the excerpt?
options: Neither requires the inmate to remove clothing, and both may be done on a routine or random basis
Both require a supervisor to be present, and both may be done on a routine or random basis
Neither requires the inmate to remove clothing, but both need reasonable belief that contraband is hidden
Both require the inmate to remove outer clothing, and both may be done only after a visit
questions.rationale: Both inspections "do not require the inmate to remove clothing" and both may be conducted "on a routine or random basis to control contraband."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.11 (Searches of inmates), then answer the question.

(c) Visual search—a visual inspection of all body surfaces and body cavities.
(1) Staff may conduct a visual search where there is reasonable belief that contraband may be concealed on the person, or a good opportunity for concealment has occured. For example, placement in a special housing unit (see 28 CFR part 541, subpart B), leaving the institution, or re-entry into an institution after contact with the public (after a community trip, court transfer, or after a “contact” visit in a visiting room) is sufficient to justify a visual search. The visual search shall be made in a manner designed to assure as much privacy to the inmate as practicable.

Select ALL of the events the excerpt gives as enough to justify a visual search.
options: Placement in a special housing unit
Receiving a letter from an attorney
Attending a religious service in the chapel
Leaving the institution
Re-entry after a contact visit in a visiting room
questions.rationale: The excerpt names placement in a special housing unit, leaving the institution, and re-entry after contact with the public (such as a community trip, court transfer, or contact visit) as sufficient to justify a visual search.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.12 (Close observation), then answer the question.

When there is reasonable belief that an inmate has ingested contraband or concealed contraband in a body cavity and the methods of search specified in § 552.11 are inappropriate or likely to result in physical injury to the inmate, the Warden or designee may authorize the placement of an inmate in a room or cell for the purpose of staff's closely observing that inmate until the inmate has voided the contraband or until sufficient time has elapsed to preclude the possibility that the inmate is concealing contraband.

When may the Warden or designee authorize close observation of an inmate?
options: An inmate returns from a contact visit and a visual search finds no contraband on his person
There is reasonable belief the inmate ingested or concealed contraband and ordinary searches are inappropriate or risky
An inmate has been found with contraband twice in a month and refuses to be searched voluntarily
An inmate refuses a pat search and an electronic search while being moved between housing units
questions.rationale: Close observation applies where there is "reasonable belief that an inmate has ingested contraband or concealed contraband in a body cavity and the methods of search specified in § 552.11 are inappropriate or likely to result in physical injury."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.12 (Close observation), then answer the question.

(b) The supervising staff member shall be the same sex as the inmate and shall maintain complete and constant visual supervision of the inmate.

What does the excerpt require of the staff member supervising an inmate on close observation?
options: He or she must be the same sex as the inmate and maintain complete and constant visual supervision
He or she must be the same sex as the inmate and check the inmate at least every fifteen minutes
He or she may be of either sex but must maintain complete and constant visual supervision
He or she must be a Lieutenant and maintain complete and constant visual supervision of the inmate
questions.rationale: Paragraph (b): "The supervising staff member shall be the same sex as the inmate and shall maintain complete and constant visual supervision of the inmate."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.12 (Close observation), then answer the question.

(1) The inmate shall be required to provide a urine sample within two hours of placement under close observation in accordance with the provisions of § 550.30 of this chapter on urine surveillance. A second urine sample is required prior to releasing the inmate from close observation.
(2) The light will be kept on at all times.
(3) No inmate under close observation status may be allowed to come into contact with another inmate.
(4) The inmate ordinarily may not be allowed personal property while under close observation status, except legal and personal mail and a reasonable amount of legal materials when requested. Personal hygiene items will be controlled by staff.

Select ALL of the conditions of close observation listed in the excerpt.
options: A urine sample within two hours of placement and a second before release
Unrestricted personal property, including a radio
The light is kept on at all times
No contact with another inmate
Free access to the recreation yard each day
questions.rationale: The listed conditions include urine samples within two hours of placement and before release, the light on at all times, and no contact with other inmates. Personal property is ordinarily not allowed, and recreation outside the cell ordinarily is not permitted.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.14 (Search of inmate housing and work areas), then answer the question.

(a) Staff may search an inmate's housing and work area, and personal items contained within those areas, without notice to or prior approval from the inmate and without the inmate's presence.
(b) Staff conducting the search shall leave the housing or work area as nearly as practicable in its original order.

Which statement about searching an inmate's housing area is supported by the excerpt?
options: Staff may search without notice or the inmate present, and should restore the area as nearly as practicable to its original order
Staff may search without notice, but only with the inmate present and a second officer observing
Staff must give the inmate notice of the search, but may conduct it without his presence
Staff may search without notice or the inmate present, and are not required to restore the area afterward
questions.rationale: Staff may search "without notice to or prior approval from the inmate and without the inmate's presence," and must "leave the housing or work area as nearly as practicable in its original order."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.40 (Purpose and scope), then answer the question.

The Bureau of Prisons (Bureau) operates a suicide prevention program to assist staff in identifying and managing potentially suicidal inmates. When staff identify an inmate as being at risk for suicide, staff will place the inmate on suicide watch. Based upon clinical findings, staff will either terminate the suicide watch when the inmate is no longer at imminent risk for suicide or arrange for the inmate's transfer to a medical referral center or contract health care facility.

What is the main purpose of the suicide prevention program described in the excerpt?
options: To report suicide statistics to the public each year, based on the information available at the time
To help staff identify and manage potentially suicidal inmates
To train inmates to become correctional officers
To determine which inmates should be disciplined
questions.rationale: The program operates "to assist staff in identifying and managing potentially suicidal inmates," with watch placement when staff identify an inmate as at risk.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.40 (Purpose and scope), then answer the question.

The Bureau of Prisons (Bureau) operates a suicide prevention program to assist staff in identifying and managing potentially suicidal inmates. When staff identify an inmate as being at risk for suicide, staff will place the inmate on suicide watch.
