Based upon clinical findings, staff will either terminate the suicide watch when the inmate is no longer at imminent risk for suicide or arrange for the inmate's transfer to a medical referral center or contract health care facility.

What are the two outcomes of a suicide watch, based on clinical findings?
options: The watch ends when the inmate completes a set number of days, or he is moved to the general population
The watch ends when the Warden orders a review, or the inmate is transferred to a disciplinary segregation unit
The watch ends when the inmate is no longer at imminent risk, or he is transferred to a medical referral center or health care facility
The watch ends when the inmate requests release in writing, or he is transferred to another institution
questions.rationale: "Based upon clinical findings, staff will either terminate the suicide watch when the inmate is no longer at imminent risk for suicide or arrange for the inmate's transfer to a medical referral center or contract health care facility."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.41 (Program procedures), then answer the question.

(c) Identification of at risk inmates. (1) Medical staff are to screen a newly admitted inmate for signs that the inmate is at risk for suicide. Ordinarily, this screening is to take place within twenty-four hours of the inmate's admission to the institution.
(2) Staff (whether medical or non-medical) may make an identification at any time based upon the inmate's observed behavior.

Who screens a newly admitted inmate for suicide risk, and when does this ordinarily take place?
options: Medical staff, ordinarily within seventy-two hours of admission
A psychologist, ordinarily within seven days of admission
Any housing unit officer, ordinarily within twenty-four hours of admission
Medical staff, ordinarily within twenty-four hours of admission
questions.rationale: "Medical staff are to screen a newly admitted inmate for signs that the inmate is at risk for suicide. Ordinarily, this screening is to take place within twenty-four hours of the inmate's admission."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.41 (Program procedures), then answer the question.

(2) Staff (whether medical or non-medical) may make an identification at any time based upon the inmate's observed behavior.

Who may identify an inmate as at risk for suicide?
options: Any staff member, medical or non-medical, at any time, based on the inmate's observed behavior
Any staff member, but only during the screening that takes place at admission
Only a psychologist, after a clinical assessment confirms that the inmate is at risk
Only medical staff, at any time, based on the inmate's observed behavior and medical history, based on the information available at the time
questions.rationale: Under (c)(2), "Staff (whether medical or non-medical) may make an identification at any time based upon the inmate's observed behavior."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.31 (Negotiations), then answer the question.

The Warden is not ordinarily involved directly in the negotiation process. Instead, this responsibility is ordinarily assigned to a team of individuals specifically trained in hostage negotiation techniques.
(a) Negotiators have no decision-making authority in hostage situations, but rather serve as intermediaries between hostage takers and command center staff.

What is the role of negotiators in a hostage situation?
options: They act as intermediaries between hostage takers and the Warden, with authority to release captors, once the shift lieutenant has been informed
They act as decision makers for the command center, with authority to grant minor demands
They act as intermediaries between hostage takers and command center staff, with no decision-making authority
They act as intermediaries between hostage takers and the media, with no decision-making authority
questions.rationale: Paragraph (a): "Negotiators have no decision-making authority in hostage situations, but rather serve as intermediaries between hostage takers and command center staff."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.31 (Negotiations), then answer the question.

(b) During the negotiation process, the following items are non-negotiable: release of captors from custody, providing of weapons, exchange of hostages, and immunity from prosecution.

Select ALL of the items the excerpt lists as non-negotiable during hostage negotiations.
options: Permission to speak with a family member
Release of captors from custody
Immunity from prosecution
Providing of weapons
Providing of a meal
questions.rationale: Non-negotiable items are "release of captors from custody, providing of weapons, exchange of hostages, and immunity from prosecution." The excerpt does not place meals or family contact on the list.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.1 (Purpose), then answer the question.

This subpart describes the Federal Bureau of Prisons' (Bureau) inmate discipline program. This program helps ensure the safety, security, and orderly operation of correctional facilities, and the protection of the public, by allowing Bureau staff to impose sanctions on inmates who commit prohibited acts. Sanctions will not be imposed in a capricious or retaliatory manner. The Bureau's inmate discipline program is authorized by 18 U.S.C. 4042(a)(3).

What does the excerpt say about the manner in which sanctions may be imposed?
options: They will not be imposed unless the inmate has admitted the act
They will be imposed in the same manner for every severity level
They will not be imposed in a capricious or retaliatory manner
They will be imposed in a manner chosen by the reporting officer
questions.rationale: The excerpt states directly: "Sanctions will not be imposed in a capricious or retaliatory manner."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.1 (Purpose), then answer the question.

This subpart describes the Federal Bureau of Prisons' (Bureau) inmate discipline program. This program helps ensure the safety, security, and orderly operation of correctional facilities, and the protection of the public, by allowing Bureau staff to impose sanctions on inmates who commit prohibited acts. Sanctions will not be imposed in a capricious or retaliatory manner. The Bureau's inmate discipline program is authorized by 18 U.S.C. 4042(a)(3).

In the excerpt, the word "capricious" most nearly means
options: based on the advice of mental health staff
based on the severity of the act
based on written policy and prior notice
based on sudden whim rather than reason
questions.rationale: A capricious sanction is one imposed on impulse or whim, without a reasoned basis. The excerpt pairs it with "retaliatory" as manners of imposing sanctions that are not allowed.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.2 (Application), then answer the question.

This program applies to sentenced and unsentenced inmates in Bureau custody. It also applies to sentenced and unsentenced inmates designated to any prison, institution, or facility in which persons are held in custody by direction of, or under an agreement with, the Bureau of Prisons.

To whom does the inmate discipline program apply?
options: Sentenced and unsentenced inmates in Bureau custody, including those held in facilities under an agreement with the Bureau
Sentenced inmates only, including those held in facilities under an agreement with the Bureau
Unsentenced inmates only, including those held in Bureau pretrial facilities
Sentenced and unsentenced inmates in Bureau-operated institutions, but not those held under an agreement, when staff resources allow
questions.rationale: The program "applies to sentenced and unsentenced inmates in Bureau custody" and also to those designated to any facility "in which persons are held in custody by direction of, or under an agreement with, the Bureau of Prisons."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.3 (Prohibited acts and available sanctions), then answer the question.

(a) Prohibited acts. The list of prohibited acts are divided into four separate categories based on severity: Greatest; High; Moderate; and Low. We describe the prohibited acts in Table 1—Prohibited Acts and Available Sanctions. Aiding, attempting, abetting, or making plans to commit any of the prohibited acts is treated the same as committing the act itself.

Into how many categories are the prohibited acts divided, and what are they based on?
options: Three categories, based on severity
Four categories, based on severity
Two categories, based on whether the act was violent
Four categories, based on the location of the act
questions.rationale: The list "are divided into four separate categories based on severity: Greatest; High; Moderate; and Low."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.3 (Prohibited acts and available sanctions), then answer the question.

(b) Available sanctions. The list of available sanctions for committing prohibited acts is listed in Table 1—Prohibited Acts and Available Sanctions. If you commit repetitive prohibited acts, we can impose increased sanctions, as listed in Table 2—Additional Available Sanctions for Repeated Prohibited Acts Within the Same Severity Level.

What does the excerpt say may happen if an inmate commits repetitive prohibited acts?
options: The inmate must complete a program before further sanctions
The inmate is automatically referred to the Warden for transfer, where the circumstances reasonably call for it
The incident reports are removed from the inmate's record
Increased sanctions may be imposed within the same severity level
questions.rationale: "If you commit repetitive prohibited acts, we can impose increased sanctions, as listed in Table 2—Additional Available Sanctions for Repeated Prohibited Acts Within the Same Severity Level."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.5 (Discipline process), then answer the question.

(2) Statement: When the investigator asks for your statement, you may give an explanation of the incident, request any witnesses be interviewed, or request that other evidence be obtained and reviewed. However, the staff investigation of the incident report may be suspended before requesting your statement if it is being investigated for possible criminal prosecution.

Select ALL of the things the excerpt says an inmate may do when the investigator asks for his statement.
options: Decide whether an incident report will be issued
Choose which staff member will investigate
Give an explanation of the incident
Request that witnesses be interviewed
Request that other evidence be obtained and reviewed
questions.rationale: The inmate "may give an explanation of the incident, request any witnesses be interviewed, or request that other evidence be obtained and reviewed." Choosing the investigator or deciding on the report is not mentioned.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.6 (Mentally ill inmates), then answer the question.

If it appears you are mentally ill at any stage of the discipline process, you will be examined by mental health staff.
(a) Competency to Participate in Disciplinary Proceedings. If evidence indicates that you cannot understand the nature of the disciplinary proceedings, or cannot help in your own defense, disciplinary proceedings may be postponed until you are competent to participate. The Unit Disciplinary Committee or Discipline Hearing Officer will make this decision based on evidence, including evidence presented by mental health staff.

What may happen if evidence indicates an inmate cannot understand the disciplinary proceedings or help in his own defense?
options: The inmate is transferred to a different institution immediately
The proceedings must continue without any change
The charges are dismissed permanently
The proceedings may be postponed until he is competent to participate
questions.rationale: If evidence indicates the inmate cannot understand the proceedings or help in his defense, "disciplinary proceedings may be postponed until you are competent to participate."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.7 (Unit Discipline Committee (UDC) review of the incident report), then answer the question.

A Unit Discipline Committee (UDC) will review the incident report once the staff investigation is complete. The UDC's review involves the following:
(a) Available dispositions. The UDC will make one of the following decisions after reviewing the incident report:
(1) You committed the prohibited act(s) charged, and/or a similar prohibited act(s) as described in the incident report;
(2) You did not commit the prohibited act(s) charged; or
(3) The incident report will be referred to the Discipline Hearing Officer (DHO) for further review, based on the seriousness of the prohibited act(s) charged.

Select ALL of the decisions the UDC may make after reviewing an incident report, according to the excerpt.
options: The report will be referred to the Discipline Hearing Officer
The report will be sent to the Regional Director for sentencing
The inmate will be placed in disciplinary segregation immediately
The inmate did not commit the prohibited act(s) charged
The inmate committed the prohibited act(s) charged or a similar act
questions.rationale: The UDC's available dispositions are a finding that the inmate committed the act (or a similar one), a finding that he did not, or referral to the DHO. Sentencing by the Regional Director and immediate segregation are not UDC dispositions.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.7 (Unit Discipline Committee (UDC) review of the incident report), then answer the question.

(4) If you are charged with a Greatest or High severity prohibited act, or are an inmate covered by § 541.4, the UDC will automatically refer the incident report to the DHO for further review.

An inmate is charged with a Greatest severity prohibited act. What will the UDC do with the incident report?
options: Resolve the case informally and remove it from records
Wait for the inmate to request a hearing
Automatically refer it to the DHO for further review
Decide the case itself and impose sanctions
questions.rationale: "If you are charged with a Greatest or High severity prohibited act, or are an inmate covered by § 541.4, the UDC will automatically refer the incident report to the DHO for further review."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.7 (Unit Discipline Committee (UDC) review of the incident report), then answer the question.

(b) UDC members. The UDC ordinarily consists of two or more staff. UDC members will not be victims, witnesses, investigators, or otherwise significantly involved in the incident.

Who is NOT allowed to serve as a UDC member for a particular incident?
options: A staff member who works in the same housing unit as the inmate
A staff member who is of a higher rank than the reporting officer, subject to the Warden's discretion
A staff member who has attended UDC training
A staff member who was a victim, witness, or investigator of the incident
questions.rationale: "UDC members will not be victims, witnesses, investigators, or otherwise significantly involved in the incident."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.7 (Unit Discipline Committee (UDC) review of the incident report), then answer the question.

(c) Timing. The UDC will ordinarily review the incident report within five work days after it is issued, not counting the day it was issued, weekends, and holidays. UDC review of the incident report may also be suspended if it is being investigated for possible criminal prosecution.

When will the UDC ordinarily review the incident report?
options: Within five work days after it is issued, not counting the day it was issued, weekends, and holidays
Within five work days after the DHO hearing, not counting weekends, unless an emergency requires otherwise
Within 24 hours after it is issued, counting weekends and holidays
Within ten calendar days after the investigation ends
questions.rationale: "The UDC will ordinarily review the incident report within five work days after it is issued, not counting the day it was issued, weekends, and holidays."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.7 (Unit Discipline Committee (UDC) review of the incident report), then answer the question.

(h) Written report. You will receive a written copy of the UDC's decision following its review of the incident report.
(i) Appeals. You may appeal the UDC's action(s) through the Administrative Remedy Program, 28 CFR part 542, subpart B.

What does the inmate receive following the UDC's review, and how may he challenge the UDC's action?
options: A written copy of the decision, and an appeal through the Administrative Remedy Program
A copy of the incident report only, and an appeal to the DHO
A written copy of the decision, and a new hearing before the same UDC
A verbal summary of the decision, and a request to the Warden
questions.rationale: "You will receive a written copy of the UDC's decision," and "You may appeal the UDC's action(s) through the Administrative Remedy Program, 28 CFR part 542, subpart B."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.8 (Discipline Hearing Officer (DHO) hearing), then answer the question.

The Discipline Hearing Officer (DHO) will only conduct a hearing on the incident report if referred by the UDC. The DHO's hearing involves the following:

When will the DHO conduct a hearing on an incident report?
options: In every case, after the UDC finishes its review, after a supervisor has reviewed the matter
Only if the UDC refers the incident report to the DHO
Whenever the inmate requests a hearing
Whenever the Warden schedules one
questions.rationale: "The Discipline Hearing Officer (DHO) will only conduct a hearing on the incident report if referred by the UDC."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.8 (Discipline Hearing Officer (DHO) hearing), then answer the question.

(b) Discipline Hearing Officer. The DHO will be an impartial decision maker who was not a victim, witness, investigator, or otherwise significantly involved in the incident.

What does the excerpt require of the DHO?
options: The DHO will be a member of the UDC who has reviewed the incident report
The DHO will be the Warden or a person the Warden appoints for each hearing, during normal operating hours, pending review by the appropriate official
The DHO will be an impartial decision maker who was not a victim, witness, investigator, or otherwise significantly involved in the incident
The DHO will be selected by the inmate from a list of eligible staff
questions.rationale: "The DHO will be an impartial decision maker who was not a victim, witness, investigator, or otherwise significantly involved in the incident."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.8 (Discipline Hearing Officer (DHO) hearing), then answer the question.

(c) Timing. You will receive written notice of the charge(s) against you at least 24 hours before the DHO's hearing. You may waive this requirement, in which case the DHO's hearing can be conducted sooner.

How much advance written notice of the charges must the inmate receive before the DHO's hearing?
options: At least 24 hours, which the inmate may not waive
At least 5 work days, which the inmate may waive
At least 48 hours, which the inmate may waive
At least 24 hours, which the inmate may waive
questions.rationale: "You will receive written notice of the charge(s) against you at least 24 hours before the DHO's hearing. You may waive this requirement, in which case the DHO's hearing can be conducted sooner."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.8 (Discipline Hearing Officer (DHO) hearing), then answer the question.

(2) How the staff representative will help you. Prior to the DHO's hearing, the staff representative will be available to help you understand the incident report charges and potential consequences. The staff representative may also assist you by speaking with and scheduling witnesses, obtaining written statements, and otherwise helping you prepare evidence for presentation at the DHO's hearing. During the DHO's hearing, you are entitled to have the staff representative appear and assist you in understanding the proceedings. The staff representative can also assist you in presenting evidence during the DHO's hearing.

Select ALL of the ways the excerpt says a staff representative may help the inmate before the hearing.
options: Questioning witnesses directly in place of the DHO
Speaking with and scheduling witnesses
Helping him understand the charges and potential consequences
Obtaining written statements and helping prepare evidence
Deciding the outcome of the hearing
questions.rationale: Before the hearing, the representative "will be available to help you understand the incident report charges and potential consequences" and may speak with and schedule witnesses, obtain written statements, and prepare evidence. Only the DHO decides the outcome and questions witnesses directly.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.8 (Discipline Hearing Officer (DHO) hearing), then answer the question.

(f) Evidence and witnesses. You are entitled to make a statement and present documentary evidence to the DHO on your own behalf. The DHO will consider all evidence presented during the hearing. The DHO's decision will be based on at least some facts and, if there is conflicting evidence, on the greater weight of the evidence. Witnesses may appear at the DHO's hearing as follows:

What does the inmate have the right to do at the DHO hearing, according to paragraph (f)?
options: Select the sanction to be imposed if he is found to have committed the act
Question witnesses directly during the hearing
Receive a verbatim transcript of the hearing
Make a statement and present documentary evidence on his own behalf
questions.rationale: The inmate "is entitled to make a statement and present documentary evidence to the DHO on your own behalf." Only the DHO may directly question witnesses, and the DHO is not required to prepare a verbatim record.

options: The reason(s) for the sanction(s) imposed
The evidence relied on by the DHO
Whether the inmate was advised of his rights
A word-for-word record of the hearing
The names of all staff who were on duty that day
questions.rationale: The report documents whether the inmate was advised of his rights, the evidence relied on, the decision, the sanction, and the reasons for it. The DHO "is not required to prepare a verbatim record of the hearing."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.8 (Discipline Hearing Officer (DHO) hearing), then answer the question.

(i) Appeals. You may appeal the DHO's action(s) through the Administrative Remedy Program, 28 CFR part 542, subpart B.

How may an inmate appeal the DHO's action?
options: By requesting a second hearing before the same DHO, as determined by the shift supervisor
Through the Administrative Remedy Program, 28 CFR part 542, subpart B
By submitting a written request to the Warden only
By asking the UDC to reconsider the decision
questions.rationale: Paragraph (i): "You may appeal the DHO's action(s) through the Administrative Remedy Program, 28 CFR part 542, subpart B."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.8 (Discipline Hearing Officer (DHO) hearing), then answer the question.

(a) Available dispositions. The DHO will make one of the following decisions after a hearing on the incident report:
(1) You committed the prohibited act(s) charged, and/or a similar prohibited act(s) as described in the incident report;
(2) You did not commit the prohibited act(s) charged; or
(3) The incident report will be referred back for further investigation, review, and disposition.

Which of the following is something the DHO may do that the UDC may not?
options: Find that the inmate committed the prohibited act charged
Find that the inmate did not commit the prohibited act charged
Refer the incident report back for further investigation, review, and disposition
Review the incident report once the staff investigation is complete, as long as no other inmate is affected
questions.rationale: The DHO's dispositions include referring the report "back for further investigation, review, and disposition." The UDC's third disposition is referral to the DHO instead.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.11 (Mail depositories), then answer the question.

The Warden shall establish at least one mail depository within the institution for an inmate to place outgoing correspondence. The Warden may establish a separate mail depository for outgoing special mail. Each item placed in a mail depository must contain a return address (see § 540.12(d)).

What must each item placed in a mail depository contain?
options: A return address
The inmate's register number and a staff signature
The name of the housing unit officer and the date mailed
A notice that the item is general or special mail
questions.rationale: "Each item placed in a mail depository must contain a return address (see § 540.12(d))." The Warden must set up at least one depository and may set up a separate one for outgoing special mail.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.12 (Controls and procedures), then answer the question.

(a) The Warden shall establish and exercise controls to protect individuals, and the security, discipline, and good order of the institution. The size, complexity, and security level of the institution, the degree of sophistication of the inmates confined, and other variables require flexibility in correspondence procedures. All Wardens shall establish open general correspondence procedures.

According to paragraph (a), what must all Wardens establish?
options: Separate correspondence procedures for each housing unit in the institution
Open general correspondence procedures
A single national mail procedure that every institution must follow
Restricted general correspondence procedures for every inmate
questions.rationale: Paragraph (a) ends with "All Wardens shall establish open general correspondence procedures," while allowing flexibility based on the institution's size, complexity, and security level.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.12 (Controls and procedures), then answer the question.

(b) Staff shall inform each inmate in writing promptly after arrival at an institution of that institution's rules for handling of inmate mail. This notice includes the following statement:
The staff of each institution of the Bureau of Prisons has the authority to open all mail addressed to you before it is delivered to you. “Special Mail” (mail from the President and Vice President of the U.S., attorneys, Members of the U.S. Congress, Embassies and Consulates, the U.S. Department of Justice (excluding the Bureau of Prisons but including U.S. Attorneys), other Federal law enforcement officers, State Attorneys General, Prosecuting Attorneys, Governors, U.S. Courts (including U.S. Probation Officers), and State Courts) may be opened only in your presence to be checked for contraband. This procedure occurs only if the sender is adequately identified on the envelope and the front of the envelope is marked “Special Mail—Open only in the presence of the inmate.” Other mail may be opened and read by the staff. If you do not want your general correspondence opened and read, the Bureau will return it to the Postal Service. This means that you will not receive such mail. You may choose whether you want your general correspondence delivered to you subject to the above conditions, or returned to the Postal Service. Whatever your choice, special mail will be delivered to you, after it is opened in your presence and checked for contraband. You can make your choice by signing part I or part II. Part I—General Correspondence to be Returned to the Postal Service I have read or had read to me the foregoing notice regarding mail. I do not want my general correspondence opened and read. I REQUEST THAT THE BUREAU OF PRISONS RETURN MY GENERAL CORRESPONDENCE TO THE POSTAL SERVICE. I understand that special mail will be delivered to me, after it is opened in my presence and checked for contraband. (Name) (Reg. No.) (Date) Part II—General Correspondence to be Opened, Read, and Delivered I have read or had read to me the foregoing notice regarding mail, I WISH TO RECEIVE MY GENERAL CORRESPONDENCE. I understand that the Bureau of Prisons may open and read my general correspondence if I choose to receive same. I also understand that special mail will be delivered to me, after it is opened in my presence and checked for contraband. (Name) (Reg. No.) (Date) Inmate (Name), (Reg. No.), refused to sign this form. He (she) was advised by me that the Bureau of Prisons retains the authority to open and read all general correspondence. The inmate was also advised that his (her) refusal to sign this form will be interpreted as an indication that he (she) wishes to receive general correspondence subject to the conditions in part II above. Staff Member's Signature Date

What does the notice given to each inmate on arrival say about opening his mail?
options: Staff may open mail only after he has signed a written consent form
Staff may open only general mail, and special mail may never be opened by anyone, based on the information available at the time, unless an emergency requires otherwise
Staff have the authority to open all mail addressed to him before it is delivered, but special mail may be opened only in his presence
Staff must open all mail in his presence to avoid any claim of tampering
questions.rationale: The notice states that staff "has the authority to open all mail addressed to you before it is delivered to you," but "Special Mail" "may be opened only in your presence to be checked for contraband."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.12 (Controls and procedures), then answer the question.

(c) Staff shall inform an inmate that letters placed in the U.S. Mail are placed there at the request of the inmate and the inmate must assume responsibility for the contents of each letter. Correspondence containing threats, extortion, etc., may result in prosecution for violation of federal laws. When such material is discovered, the inmate may be subject to disciplinary action, the written material may be copied, and all material may be referred to the appropriate law enforcement agency for prosecution.

What may happen if an inmate's correspondence contains threats or extortion?
options: He may be subject to disciplinary action, the writing may be copied, and the material may be referred for prosecution
The letter will be returned to him and no record of it will be kept
He will be placed on restricted special mail status for 180 days
The letter will be delivered with a warning stamped on the envelope
questions.rationale: Correspondence containing threats or extortion "may result in prosecution for violation of federal laws," and the inmate "may be subject to disciplinary action, the written material may be copied, and all material may be referred to the appropriate law enforcement agency."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.12 (Controls and procedures), then answer the question.

(d) The inmate is responsible for filling out the return address completely on envelopes provided for the inmate's use by the institution. If the inmate uses an envelope not provided by the institution, the inmate is responsible for ensuring that the envelope used contains all return address information listed on the envelope provided by the institution.

If an inmate uses an envelope not provided by the institution, what is he responsible for?
options: Paying the cost of postage for the envelope and its contents
Ensuring that it contains all the return address information listed on the institution's envelope
Marking the envelope as special mail so that it can be inspected, after a supervisor has reviewed the matter
Having a staff member approve the envelope before it is mailed
questions.rationale: If the inmate uses his own envelope, he "is responsible for ensuring that the envelope used contains all return address information listed on the envelope provided by the institution."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.14 (General correspondence), then answer the question.

(a) Institution staff shall open and inspect all incoming general correspondence. Incoming general correspondence may be read as frequently as deemed necessary to maintain security or monitor a particular problem confronting an inmate.

What must institution staff do with incoming general correspondence?
options: Open it only in the inmate's presence and read it only with the Warden's approval, when staff resources allow, once the shift lieutenant has been informed
Open and inspect all of it, and read it as frequently as deemed necessary to maintain security or monitor a problem
Deliver it unopened unless the inmate has asked staff to open it
Open and inspect only the items that look suspicious, and read none of it
questions.rationale: "Institution staff shall open and inspect all incoming general correspondence. Incoming general correspondence may be read as frequently as deemed necessary to maintain security or monitor a particular problem confronting an inmate."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.14 (General correspondence), then answer the question.

(b) Except for “special mail,” outgoing mail from a pretrial inmate may not be sealed by the inmate and may be read and inspected by staff.

How is outgoing mail from a pretrial inmate handled, other than special mail?
options: It is not sent out until the inmate's attorney has reviewed it
It may be sealed by the inmate and is sent out unopened
It may not be sealed by the inmate and may be read and inspected by staff
It may be sealed by the inmate but is read at the Warden's request
questions.rationale: "Except for 'special mail,' outgoing mail from a pretrial inmate may not be sealed by the inmate and may be read and inspected by staff."

options: Information of escape plots or plans to commit illegal activities
A letter that expresses disagreement with a staff decision
A letter that is written in blue ink instead of black
Matter which is nonmailable under law or postal regulations
Matter which encourages activities that may lead to physical violence or group disruption
questions.rationale: A Warden may reject matter nonmailable under law, matter encouraging violence or group disruption, and information about escape plots or illegal plans. Disagreement with staff or ink color is not among the grounds listed.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.18 (Special mail), then answer the question.

(a) The Warden shall open incoming special mail only in the presence of the inmate for inspection for physical contraband and the qualification of any enclosures as special mail. The correspondence may not be read or copied if the sender is adequately identified on the envelope, and the front of the envelope is marked “Special Mail—Open only in the presence of the inmate”.

How does the Warden handle incoming special mail?
options: Open it only in the inmate's presence for inspection for physical contraband and qualification of enclosures, without reading or copying it
Open it before delivery, inspect it for contraband, and read it for security reasons
Deliver it sealed and inspect it only if staff suspect it contains contraband
Open it outside the inmate's presence and give the inmate a copy of the contents
questions.rationale: The Warden "shall open incoming special mail only in the presence of the inmate for inspection for physical contraband and the qualification of any enclosures as special mail. The correspondence may not be read or copied."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.18 (Special mail), then answer the question.

(c)(1) Except as provided for in paragraph (c)(2) of this section, outgoing special mail may be sealed by the inmate and is not subject to inspection.

What does the excerpt say about outgoing special mail from an inmate who is not on restricted special mail status?
options: It may be sealed, but staff may read it before it is sent
It must be sent by certified mail, and the inmate pays the cost
It may be sealed by the inmate and is not subject to inspection
It must be left unsealed so that staff can check it for contraband
questions.rationale: Under (c)(1), "outgoing special mail may be sealed by the inmate and is not subject to inspection," except for inmates on restricted special mail status.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.19 (Legal correspondence), then answer the question.

(a) Staff shall mark each envelope of incoming legal mail (mail from courts or attorneys) to show the date and time of receipt, the date and time the letter is delivered to an inmate and opened in the inmate's presence, and the name of the staff member who delivered the letter. The inmate may be asked to sign as receiving the incoming legal mail. This paragraph applies only if the sender has marked the envelope as specified in § 540.18.

What must staff mark on each envelope of incoming legal mail from courts or attorneys?
options: The name of the sender, the date and time of the postmark, and the name of the staff member who inspected the letter for contraband
The date and time of receipt, the date and time of delivery and opening in the inmate's presence, and the name of the staff member who delivered the letter
The date and time of receipt, the name of the sender, and the case number of the matter, if any, listed in the letter
The date and time of receipt, the date and time of delivery to the housing unit, and the name of the mailroom officer who opened the letter, based on the information available at the time
questions.rationale: Staff "shall mark each envelope of incoming legal mail... to show the date and time of receipt, the date and time the letter is delivered to an inmate and opened in the inmate's presence, and the name of the staff member who delivered the letter."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.40 (Purpose and scope), then answer the question.

The Bureau of Prisons encourages visiting by family, friends, and community groups to maintain the morale of the inmate and to develop closer relationships between the inmate and family members or others in the community. The Warden shall develop procedures consistent with this rule to permit inmate visiting. The Warden may restrict inmate visiting when necessary to ensure the security and good order of the institution.

Why does the Bureau of Prisons encourage visiting?
options: To maintain the inmate's morale and to develop closer relationships with family members or others in the community
To reduce the number of inmates who are placed in a Special Housing Unit, as long as no other inmate is affected, with the approval of a supervisor on duty
To make sure inmates have a source of commissary funds while in custody
To give staff more time to complete required reports and counts
questions.rationale: The Bureau encourages visiting "to maintain the morale of the inmate and to develop closer relationships between the inmate and family members or others in the community."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.40 (Purpose and scope), then answer the question.

The Bureau of Prisons encourages visiting by family, friends, and community groups to maintain the morale of the inmate and to develop closer relationships between the inmate and family members or others in the community. The Warden shall develop procedures consistent with this rule to permit inmate visiting. The Warden may restrict inmate visiting when necessary to ensure the security and good order of the institution.

When may the Warden restrict inmate visiting?
options: Whenever the number of visitors exceeds ten for a month
When necessary to ensure the security and good order of the institution
Whenever the inmate has not paid for his phone calls
Whenever a visitor lives more than fifty miles from the institution
questions.rationale: "The Warden may restrict inmate visiting when necessary to ensure the security and good order of the institution."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.41 (Visiting facilities), then answer the question.

The Warden shall have the visiting room arranged so as to provide adequate supervision, adapted to the degree of security required by the type of institution. The Warden shall ensure that the visiting area is as comfortable and pleasant as practicable, and appropriately furnished and arranged. If space is available, the Warden shall have a portion of the visiting room equipped and set up to provide facilities for the children of visitors.

What does the excerpt require of the visiting room?
options: It must be located outside the security perimeter, adapted to the needs of families
It must have a fixed seating plan, adapted to the number of visitors expected each day
It must provide adequate supervision, adapted to the degree of security required, and be as comfortable and pleasant as practicable
It must be staffed by a Lieutenant, adapted to the number of inmates visiting
questions.rationale: The visiting room must be "arranged so as to provide adequate supervision, adapted to the degree of security required," and be "as comfortable and pleasant as practicable, and appropriately furnished and arranged."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.42 (Visiting times), then answer the question.

(a) Each Warden shall establish a visiting schedule for the institution. At a minimum, the Warden shall establish visiting hours at the institution on Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays. The restriction of visiting to these days may be a hardship for some families and arrangements for other suitable hours shall be made to the extent practicable. Where staff resources permit, the Warden may establish evening visiting hours.

At a minimum, on which days must the Warden establish visiting hours?
options: Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays
Weekday evenings only
Fridays through Mondays
Each day of the week
questions.rationale: "At a minimum, the Warden shall establish visiting hours at the institution on Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays." Evening hours are optional, where staff resources permit.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.44 (Regular visitors), then answer the question.

(a) Members of the immediate family. These persons include mother, father, step-parents, foster parents, brothers and sisters, spouse, and children. These individuals are placed on the visiting list, absent strong circumstances which preclude visiting.

Select ALL of the family members the excerpt lists as members of the immediate family.
options: Step-parents and foster parents
Mother and father
Spouse and children
Cousins
Grandparents
questions.rationale: Immediate family includes "mother, father, step-parents, foster parents, brothers and sisters, spouse, and children." Grandparents and cousins are "other relatives."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.44 (Regular visitors), then answer the question.

(b) Other relatives. These persons include grandparents, uncles, aunts, in-laws, and cousins. They may be placed on the approved list if the inmate wishes to have visits from them regularly and if there exists no reason to exclude them.

Under what condition may other relatives, such as grandparents or cousins, be placed on the approved list?
options: If the Warden receives a letter from each relative requesting a visit, pending review by the appropriate official
If the inmate wishes to have visits from them regularly and there is no reason to exclude them
If the inmate has had no disciplinary reports in the past year
If at least one immediate family member is also on the visiting list
questions.rationale: Other relatives "may be placed on the approved list if the inmate wishes to have visits from them regularly and if there exists no reason to exclude them."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.44 (Regular visitors), then answer the question.

(e) Children under sixteen. Children under the age of 16 may not visit unless accompanied by a responsible adult. Children shall be kept under supervision of a responsible adult or a children's program. Exceptions in unusual circumstances may be made by special approval of the Warden.

What does the excerpt require for children under age 16 who visit?
options: They may not visit unless accompanied by a responsible adult, though the Warden may make exceptions in unusual circumstances
They may visit alone if an immediate family member approves
They may visit only on weekends and holidays, in the presence of a staff member, as long as the unit team is notified, for the duration of the incident
They may not visit under any circumstances
questions.rationale: "Children under the age of 16 may not visit unless accompanied by a responsible adult... Exceptions in unusual circumstances may be made by special approval of the Warden."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.45 (Qualification as special visitor), then answer the question.

Persons in the categories listed in this section may qualify as special visitors rather than as regular visitors. Visits by special visitors ordinarily are for a specific purpose and ordinarily are not of a recurring nature. Except as specified, the conditions of visiting for special visitors are the same as for regular visitors.

How do special visits ordinarily differ from regular visits?
options: They are ordinarily held on weekdays and require the Warden's presence, under the direction of the senior officer present
They are ordinarily for a specific purpose and not of a recurring nature
They are ordinarily longer and are held in a private room
They are ordinarily limited to immediate family members
questions.rationale: "Visits by special visitors ordinarily are for a specific purpose and ordinarily are not of a recurring nature. Except as specified, the conditions of visiting for special visitors are the same as for regular visitors."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.52 (Penalty for violation of visiting regulations), then answer the question.

Any act or effort to violate the visiting guidelines of an institution may result in disciplinary action against the inmate, which may include the denial of future visits, possibly over an extended period of time. Moreover, criminal prosecution may be initiated against the visitor, the inmate, or both, in the case of criminal violations.

What may result from any act or effort to violate an institution's visiting guidelines?
options: Disciplinary action against the inmate, which may include denial of future visits, and possible criminal prosecution of the visitor, the inmate, or both
Disciplinary action against the visitor, which may include denial of future visits, and no action against the inmate
A written warning to the inmate and the visitor, with denial of future visits permitted only after a second violation
Criminal prosecution of the inmate only, with no effect on the inmate's future visits and no action against the visitor
questions.rationale: Violations "may result in disciplinary action against the inmate, which may include the denial of future visits, possibly over an extended period of time. Moreover, criminal prosecution may be initiated against the visitor, the inmate, or both."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.11 (Zero tolerance of sexual abuse and sexual harassment; PREA coordinator), then answer the question.

(b) An agency shall employ or designate an upper-level, agency-wide PREA coordinator with sufficient time and authority to develop, implement, and oversee agency efforts to comply with the PREA standards in all of its facilities.
(c) Where an agency operates more than one facility, each facility shall designate a PREA compliance manager with sufficient time and authority to coordinate the facility's efforts to comply with the PREA standards.

Which pair of positions does the excerpt require for an agency that operates more than one facility?
options: An outside auditor for the agency and a compliance manager chosen by the inmates of each facility
A PREA coordinator at each facility and a PREA compliance manager for the whole agency
An upper-level, agency-wide PREA coordinator and a PREA compliance manager at each facility
A single PREA compliance manager who must visit each facility once a month to monitor progress
questions.rationale: The agency employs or designates "an upper-level, agency-wide PREA coordinator," and "each facility shall designate a PREA compliance manager."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.13 (Supervision and monitoring), then answer the question.

(a) The agency shall ensure that each facility it operates shall develop, document, and make its best efforts to comply on a regular basis with a staffing plan that provides for adequate levels of staffing, and, where applicable, video monitoring, to protect inmates against sexual abuse. In calculating adequate staffing levels and determining the need for video monitoring, facilities shall take into consideration:

What is the purpose of the staffing plan described in paragraph (a)?
options: To describe how supervisors will evaluate the job performance of officers who work nights
To reduce the overall cost of staffing at each facility without lowering the number of inmates housed, subject to the Warden's discretion
To assign the same number of officers to every shift regardless of the programs held on that shift
To provide adequate staffing levels and, where applicable, video monitoring to protect inmates against sexual abuse
questions.rationale: Each facility must have "a staffing plan that provides for adequate levels of staffing, and, where applicable, video monitoring, to protect inmates against sexual abuse."

options: areas where staff or inmates may be isolated
areas where cameras record continuously
areas that have been closed for repair
areas that are open to the public
questions.rationale: The excerpt defines the term in context: "'blind-spots' or areas where staff or inmates may be isolated."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.13 (Supervision and monitoring), then answer the question.

(b) In circumstances where the staffing plan is not complied with, the facility shall document and justify all deviations from the plan.

What must a facility do when it does not comply with its staffing plan?
options: Ask the Regional Director to approve each deviation before it takes effect
Close the affected housing unit until full staffing returns
Document and justify all deviations from the plan
Report the deviations to the inmates in writing within a week
questions.rationale: Paragraph (b): "In circumstances where the staffing plan is not complied with, the facility shall document and justify all deviations from the plan."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.13 (Supervision and monitoring), then answer the question.

(c) Whenever necessary, but no less frequently than once each year, for each facility the agency operates, in consultation with the PREA coordinator required by § 115.11, the agency shall assess, determine, and document whether adjustments are needed to:

How often must the agency assess whether adjustments are needed to the staffing plan and video monitoring?
options: Once each quarter, with the results reported to the inmates
Only after a sexual abuse incident has been substantiated
Whenever necessary, but no less frequently than once every five years
Whenever necessary, but no less frequently than once each year
questions.rationale: Paragraph (c): "Whenever necessary, but no less frequently than once each year, for each facility the agency operates, in consultation with the PREA coordinator... the agency shall assess, determine, and document whether adjustments are needed."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.15 (Limits to cross-gender viewing and searches), then answer the question.

(a) The facility shall not conduct cross-gender strip searches or cross-gender visual body cavity searches (meaning a search of the anal or genital opening) except in exigent circumstances or when performed by medical practitioners.

When may a facility conduct a cross-gender strip search or visual body cavity search?
options: Whenever the inmate has been placed in a Special Housing Unit
Only in exigent circumstances or when performed by medical practitioners
Whenever same-gender staff are on another shift
Whenever a supervisor of the same gender as the inmate is present, in most circumstances
questions.rationale: "The facility shall not conduct cross-gender strip searches or cross-gender visual body cavity searches... except in exigent circumstances or when performed by medical practitioners."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.15 (Limits to cross-gender viewing and searches), then answer the question.

(c) The facility shall document all cross-gender strip searches and cross-gender visual body cavity searches, and shall document all cross-gender pat-down searches of female inmates.

Select ALL of the searches that the facility must document, according to the excerpt.
options: Same-gender pat-down searches of male inmates
Cross-gender strip searches
Cross-gender pat-down searches of female inmates
Electronic device searches of any inmate
Cross-gender visual body cavity searches
questions.rationale: The facility "shall document all cross-gender strip searches and cross-gender visual body cavity searches, and shall document all cross-gender pat-down searches of female inmates."

options: Training on defensive tactics, firearm use, and escorting inmates between buildings
Training on the zero-tolerance policy, prevention, detection, reporting and response duties, inmates' rights, and avoiding inappropriate relationships
Training on report writing, inventory control, and the preparation of visiting lists
Training on legal research, parole hearings, and the calculation of good conduct time, in accordance with the posted schedule, where the circumstances reasonably call for it
questions.rationale: The list covers the zero-tolerance policy, employee responsibilities, inmates' right to be free from abuse and retaliation, dynamics and reactions, detecting and responding to signs of abuse, avoiding inappropriate relationships, professional communication, and mandatory reporting.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.31 (Employee training), then answer the question.

(b) Such training shall be tailored to the gender of the inmates at the employee's facility. The employee shall receive additional training if the employee is reassigned from a facility that houses only male inmates to a facility that houses only female inmates, or vice versa.

What additional training must an employee receive when reassigned from a facility that houses only male inmates to one that houses only female inmates?
options: Additional training in the use of force on female inmates
A written test, which the employee must pass before the first shift
Additional training tailored to the gender of the inmates at the new facility
No additional training, because the original training covers all inmates, as long as the unit team is notified
questions.rationale: Training "shall be tailored to the gender of the inmates at the employee's facility. The employee shall receive additional training if the employee is reassigned from a facility that houses only male inmates to a facility that houses only female inmates, or vice versa."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.31 (Employee training), then answer the question.

(c) All current employees who have not received such training shall be trained within one year of the effective date of the PREA standards, and the agency shall provide each employee with refresher training every two years to ensure that all employees know the agency's current sexual abuse and sexual harassment policies and procedures. In years in which an employee does not receive refresher training, the agency shall provide refresher information on current sexual abuse and sexual harassment policies.

How often must the agency provide each employee with refresher training?
options: Every five years, with a written test provided at each session
Every six months, with refresher information provided on the employee's anniversary date
Every year, with refresher information provided only after an incident
Every two years, with refresher information provided in the years between
questions.rationale: The agency shall provide "refresher training every two years," and "In years in which an employee does not receive refresher training, the agency shall provide refresher information on current sexual abuse and sexual harassment policies."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.33 (Inmate education), then answer the question.

(a) During the intake process, inmates shall receive information explaining the agency's zero-tolerance policy regarding sexual abuse and sexual harassment and how to report incidents or suspicions of sexual abuse or sexual harassment.

What information must inmates receive during the intake process?
options: The schedule of visiting hours and the number of visitors permitted each month
The agency's zero-tolerance policy and how to report incidents or suspicions of sexual abuse or harassment
The procedures for ordering items from the commissary and for sending mail
The full list of prohibited acts and the sanctions available for each severity level, according to the institution's local guidelines
questions.rationale: "During the intake process, inmates shall receive information explaining the agency's zero-tolerance policy regarding sexual abuse and sexual harassment and how to report incidents or suspicions of sexual abuse or sexual harassment."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.33 (Inmate education), then answer the question.

(b) Within 30 days of intake, the agency shall provide comprehensive education to inmates either in person or through video regarding their rights to be free from sexual abuse and sexual harassment and to be free from retaliation for reporting such incidents, and regarding agency policies and procedures for responding to such incidents.

Within what period of intake must the agency provide comprehensive education to inmates?
options: Within 90 days
Within one year
Within 30 days
Within 72 hours
questions.rationale: "Within 30 days of intake, the agency shall provide comprehensive education to inmates either in person or through video." The 72-hour period belongs to intake screening.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.41 (Screening for risk of victimization and abusiveness), then answer the question.

(a) All inmates shall be assessed during an intake screening and upon transfer to another facility for their risk of being sexually abused by other inmates or sexually abusive toward other inmates.
(b) Intake screening shall ordinarily take place within 72 hours of arrival at the facility.
(c) Such assessments shall be conducted using an objective screening instrument.

When does intake screening for risk of victimization and abusiveness ordinarily take place?
options: Within 72 hours of arrival at the facility, using an objective screening instrument
Within 24 hours of arrival at the facility, using a staff interview
Within 30 days of arrival at the facility, using a medical examination
Within seven days of arrival at the facility, using the inmate's central file, as long as no other inmate is affected
questions.rationale: "Intake screening shall ordinarily take place within 72 hours of arrival at the facility," and the assessments are "conducted using an objective screening instrument."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.43 (Protective custody), then answer the question.

(b) Inmates placed in segregated housing for this purpose shall have access to programs, privileges, education, and work opportunities to the extent possible. If the facility restricts access to programs, privileges, education, or work opportunities, the facility shall document:
(1) The opportunities that have been limited;
(2) The duration of the limitation; and
(3) The reasons for such limitations.

If a facility restricts the programs, privileges, education, or work opportunities of an inmate in protective segregated housing, select ALL of the items it must document.
options: The opportunities that have been limited
The reasons for such limitations
The names of the inmates who requested the limitation
The cost savings from the limitation
The duration of the limitation
questions.rationale: The facility "shall document: (1) the opportunities that have been limited; (2) the duration of the limitation; and (3) the reasons for such limitations."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.51 (Inmate reporting), then answer the question.

(a) The agency shall provide multiple internal ways for inmates to privately report sexual abuse and sexual harassment, retaliation by other inmates or staff for reporting sexual abuse and sexual harassment, and staff neglect or violation of responsibilities that may have contributed to such incidents.
(b) The agency shall also provide at least one way for inmates to report abuse or harassment to a public or private entity or office that is not part of the agency, and that is able to receive and immediately forward inmate reports of sexual abuse and sexual harassment to agency officials, allowing the inmate to remain anonymous upon request. Inmates detained solely for civil immigration purposes shall be provided information on how to contact relevant consular officials and relevant officials at the Department of Homeland Security.

Which statement about inmate reporting methods is supported by the excerpt?
options: The agency must provide multiple internal ways to report privately, and at least one way to report to an outside entity that can forward reports and allow the inmate to remain anonymous
The agency must provide a single internal way to report, and the inmate must give his name
The agency must provide internal reporting methods only for inmates who have been placed in protective custody
The agency must provide only outside reporting methods, and staff may not take internal reports
questions.rationale: The agency must provide "multiple internal ways for inmates to privately report" and "at least one way for inmates to report abuse or harassment to a public or private entity or office that is not part of the agency," allowing the inmate to remain anonymous upon request.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.51 (Inmate reporting), then answer the question.

(c) Staff shall accept reports made verbally, in writing, anonymously, and from third parties and shall promptly document any verbal reports.

Select ALL of the kinds of reports that staff must accept under paragraph (c).
options: Reports made verbally
Reports made only during scheduled counts
Reports made only by the alleged victim
Reports made in writing
Reports made anonymously
questions.rationale: "Staff shall accept reports made verbally, in writing, anonymously, and from third parties and shall promptly document any verbal reports."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.61 (Staff and agency reporting duties), then answer the question.

(a) The agency shall require all staff to report immediately and according to agency policy any knowledge, suspicion, or information regarding an incident of sexual abuse or sexual harassment that occurred in a facility, whether or not it is part of the agency; retaliation against inmates or staff who reported such an incident; and any staff neglect or violation of responsibilities that may have contributed to an incident or retaliation.

What must the agency require all staff to do when they have knowledge, suspicion, or information about an incident of sexual abuse or sexual harassment?
options: Report it only if the alleged victim asks for an investigation
Report it only if the incident occurred in the agency's own facility
Report it immediately and according to agency policy
Report it at the end of the shift, after speaking with the inmates involved
questions.rationale: The agency "shall require all staff to report immediately and according to agency policy any knowledge, suspicion, or information regarding an incident of sexual abuse or sexual harassment that occurred in a facility, whether or not it is part of the agency."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.64 (Staff first responder duties), then answer the question.

(3) If the abuse occurred within a time period that still allows for the collection of physical evidence, request that the alleged victim not take any actions that could destroy physical evidence, including, as appropriate, washing, brushing teeth, changing clothes, urinating, defecating, smoking, drinking, or eating; and

Which of the following is listed as an action that could destroy physical evidence?
options: Washing, brushing teeth, changing clothes, urinating, defecating, smoking, drinking, or eating
Walking in the dayroom, exercising in the yard, or attending a program, unless an emergency requires otherwise
Reading, writing a letter, making a phone call, or watching television
Signing a statement, requesting a lawyer, or filing a grievance
questions.rationale: The list in the excerpt is "washing, brushing teeth, changing clothes, urinating, defecating, smoking, drinking, or eating."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.65 (Coordinated response), then answer the question.

The facility shall develop a written institutional plan to coordinate actions taken in response to an incident of sexual abuse, among staff first responders, medical and mental health practitioners, investigators, and facility leadership.

What must the facility develop to coordinate its response to an incident of sexual abuse?
options: A telephone list of outside rape crisis centers kept by the control center
A written plan that is shared only with investigators and facility leadership, for the duration of the incident, as determined by the shift supervisor
A written institutional plan coordinating staff first responders, medical and mental health practitioners, investigators, and facility leadership
A verbal agreement between the Warden and the PREA coordinator
questions.rationale: "The facility shall develop a written institutional plan to coordinate actions taken in response to an incident of sexual abuse, among staff first responders, medical and mental health practitioners, investigators, and facility leadership."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.67 (Agency protection against retaliation), then answer the question.

(a) The agency shall establish a policy to protect all inmates and staff who report sexual abuse or sexual harassment or cooperate with sexual abuse or sexual harassment investigations from retaliation by other inmates or staff, and shall designate which staff members or departments are charged with monitoring retaliation.
(b) The agency shall employ multiple protection measures, such as housing changes or transfers for inmate victims or abusers, removal of alleged staff or inmate abusers from contact with victims, and emotional support services for inmates or staff who fear retaliation for reporting sexual abuse or sexual harassment or for cooperating with investigations.

Whom must the agency's anti-retaliation policy protect?
options: Only the alleged victim of the sexual abuse until the investigation is complete
Only staff who report sexual abuse, since inmates are protected by housing policy, once the shift lieutenant has been informed
Only inmates who report sexual abuse, since staff are protected by other laws
All inmates and staff who report sexual abuse or sexual harassment or cooperate with investigations
questions.rationale: The agency "shall establish a policy to protect all inmates and staff who report sexual abuse or sexual harassment or cooperate with sexual abuse or sexual harassment investigations from retaliation by other inmates or staff."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.72 (Evidentiary standard for administrative investigations), then answer the question.

The agency shall impose no standard higher than a preponderance of the evidence in determining whether allegations of sexual abuse or sexual harassment are substantiated.

What is the highest evidentiary standard the agency may impose in deciding whether allegations of sexual abuse or sexual harassment are substantiated in an administrative investigation?
options: Proof beyond a reasonable doubt
Clear and convincing evidence
A signed confession from the accused
A preponderance of the evidence
questions.rationale: "The agency shall impose no standard higher than a preponderance of the evidence in determining whether allegations of sexual abuse or sexual harassment are substantiated."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.82 (Access to emergency medical and mental health services), then answer the question.

(a) Inmate victims of sexual abuse shall receive timely, unimpeded access to emergency medical treatment and crisis intervention services, the nature and scope of which are determined by medical and mental health practitioners according to their professional judgment.
(d) Treatment services shall be provided to the victim without financial cost and regardless of whether the victim names the abuser or cooperates with any investigation arising out of the incident.

What does the excerpt say about treatment services for victims of sexual abuse?
options: They are provided without financial cost and regardless of whether the victim names the abuser or cooperates with an investigation
They are provided only after the victim has agreed to name the abuser
They are provided at the victim's expense unless the abuser is a staff member, in most circumstances, as long as no other inmate is affected
They are provided only after the investigation is complete
questions.rationale: "Treatment services shall be provided to the victim without financial cost and regardless of whether the victim names the abuser or cooperates with any investigation arising out of the incident."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.86 (Sexual abuse incident reviews), then answer the question.

(a) The facility shall conduct a sexual abuse incident review at the conclusion of every sexual abuse investigation, including where the allegation has not been substantiated, unless the allegation has been determined to be unfounded.
(b) Such review shall ordinarily occur within 30 days of the conclusion of the investigation.

When must a facility conduct a sexual abuse incident review?
options: Only at the conclusion of substantiated investigations, ordinarily within 30 days
At the conclusion of every investigation, including unfounded ones, ordinarily within 90 days
At the conclusion of every sexual abuse investigation, including unsubstantiated ones but not unfounded ones, ordinarily within 30 days
Only when the Warden requests one, ordinarily within seven days
questions.rationale: "The facility shall conduct a sexual abuse incident review at the conclusion of every sexual abuse investigation, including where the allegation has not been substantiated, unless the allegation has been determined to be unfounded," and the review "shall ordinarily occur within 30 days."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.100 (Purpose and scope), then answer the question.

(a) The Bureau of Prisons extends telephone privileges to inmates as part of its overall correctional management. Telephone privileges are a supplemental means of maintaining community and family ties that will contribute to an inmate's personal development. An inmate may request to call a person of his or her choice outside the institution on a telephone provided for that purpose. However, limitations and conditions may be imposed upon an inmate's telephone privileges to ensure that these are consistent with other aspects of the Bureau's correctional management responsibilities. In addition to the procedures set forth in this subpart, inmate telephone use is subject to those limitations which the Warden determines are necessary to ensure the security or good order, including discipline, of the institution or to protect the public. Restrictions on inmate telephone use may also be imposed as a disciplinary sanction (see 28 CFR part 541).

According to paragraph (a), telephone privileges are best described as
options: a right that the Warden may not limit under any circumstances
a method for inmates to conduct business with persons outside the institution
a supplemental means of maintaining community and family ties
a reward granted only to inmates who have completed a program
questions.rationale: Paragraph (a) says "Telephone privileges are a supplemental means of maintaining community and family ties that will contribute to an inmate's personal development," and limitations and conditions may be imposed.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.100 (Purpose and scope), then answer the question.

(b) Except as provided in this rule, the Warden shall permit an inmate who has not been restricted from telephone use as the result of a specific institutional disciplinary sanction to make at least one telephone call each month.

What is the minimum telephone access the Warden shall permit an inmate who has not been restricted by a disciplinary sanction?
options: At least one telephone call each week, for the duration of the incident
At least one telephone call each year
At least one telephone call each day
At least one telephone call each month
questions.rationale: "The Warden shall permit an inmate who has not been restricted from telephone use as the result of a specific institutional disciplinary sanction to make at least one telephone call each month."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.101 (Procedures), then answer the question.

(a) Telephone list preparation. An inmate telephone call shall ordinarily be made to a number identified on the inmate's official telephone list. This list ordinarily may contain up to 30 numbers. The Associate Warden may authorize the placement of additional numbers on an inmate's telephone list based on the inmate's individual situation, e.g., size of family.

How many numbers may an inmate's telephone list ordinarily contain, and who may authorize more?
options: Up to 30 numbers; the Associate Warden may authorize additional numbers
Up to 100 numbers; the Captain may authorize additional numbers
Up to 30 numbers; the unit officer may authorize additional numbers, as long as the unit team is notified
Up to 10 numbers; the Warden alone may authorize additional numbers
questions.rationale: The list "ordinarily may contain up to 30 numbers. The Associate Warden may authorize the placement of additional numbers on an inmate's telephone list based on the inmate's individual situation, e.g., size of family."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.101 (Procedures), then answer the question.

(b) Telephone list update. Each Warden shall establish procedures to allow an inmate the opportunity to submit telephone list changes on at least a quarterly basis.

How often must each Warden allow inmates the opportunity to submit telephone list changes?
options: On at least a quarterly basis
On at least a yearly basis
On at least a weekly basis
Only when an inmate is transferred
questions.rationale: "Each Warden shall establish procedures to allow an inmate the opportunity to submit telephone list changes on at least a quarterly basis."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.101 (Procedures), then answer the question.

(c) Telephone access codes. An inmate may not possess another inmate's telephone access code number. An inmate may not give his or her telephone access code number to another inmate, and is to report a compromised telephone access code number immediately to unit staff.

An inmate learns that another inmate has been using his telephone access code. What does the excerpt direct him to do?
options: Ask the other inmate to stop using it and wait a week, unless an emergency requires otherwise
Report the compromised access code immediately to unit staff
Change the code himself at the next phone call
Mail a note to the Warden at the end of the month
questions.rationale: An inmate "is to report a compromised telephone access code number immediately to unit staff." He also may not give his code to another inmate or possess another inmate's code.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.101 (Procedures), then answer the question.

(d) Placement and duration of telephone call. The placement and duration of any telephone call is subject to availability of inmate funds. Ordinarily, an inmate who has sufficient funds is allowed at least three minutes for a telephone call. The Warden may limit the maximum length of telephone calling based on the situation at that institution (e.g., institution population or usage demand).

What is the minimum length of a telephone call that an inmate with sufficient funds is ordinarily allowed?
options: At least ten minutes
At least thirty minutes
At least three minutes
At least fifteen minutes
questions.rationale: "Ordinarily, an inmate who has sufficient funds is allowed at least three minutes for a telephone call." The Warden may limit maximum length based on population or usage demand.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.102 (Monitoring of inmate telephone calls), then answer the question.

The Warden shall establish procedures that enable monitoring of telephone conversations on any telephone located within the institution, said monitoring to be done to preserve the security and orderly management of the institution and to protect the public. The Warden must provide notice to the inmate of the potential for monitoring. Staff may not monitor an inmate's properly placed call to an attorney. The Warden shall notify an inmate of the proper procedures to have an unmonitored telephone conversation with an attorney.

Which call may staff NOT monitor?
options: An inmate's properly placed call to an attorney
An inmate's call to a friend outside the state
An inmate's call placed from a housing unit telephone
An inmate's call to a family member
questions.rationale: The Warden may monitor telephone conversations on any institutional phone, but "Staff may not monitor an inmate's properly placed call to an attorney."

questions.stem:
