Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.104 (Responsibility for inmate misuse of telephones), then answer the question.

The inmate is responsible for any misuse of the telephone. The Warden shall refer incidents of unlawful inmate telephone use to law enforcement authorities. The Warden shall advise an inmate that violation of the institution's telephone regulations may result in institutional disciplinary action (See part 541, subpart B).

Who is responsible for any misuse of an inmate telephone, and what happens to incidents of unlawful use?
options: The housing unit officer; the Warden refers incidents to the Regional Director
The person receiving the call; the Warden refers incidents to the postal inspector
The institution; the Warden refers incidents to the telephone company
The inmate; the Warden refers incidents of unlawful use to law enforcement authorities
questions.rationale: "The inmate is responsible for any misuse of the telephone. The Warden shall refer incidents of unlawful inmate telephone use to law enforcement authorities."

options: Establish procedures for receiving, recording, reviewing, investigating, and responding
Decide which inmates may file a Request in a given month
Limit each inmate to one Request per year
Conduct an investigation into each Request or Appeal
Acknowledge receipt of a Request or Appeal by returning a receipt to the inmate
questions.rationale: Responsible officials establish procedures, acknowledge receipt with a receipt to the inmate, conduct an investigation into each Request or Appeal, and respond and sign. They do not ration Requests.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 542.11 (Responsibility), then answer the question.

(b) Inmates have the responsibility to use this Program in good faith and in an honest and straightforward manner.

What responsibility do inmates have in using the program?
options: To use the program no more than once for each housing unit assignment, as long as the unit team is notified
To use the program on behalf of other inmates who cannot read
To use the program in good faith and in an honest and straightforward manner
To use the program only after an incident report has been issued
questions.rationale: "Inmates have the responsibility to use this Program in good faith and in an honest and straightforward manner."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 542.13 (Informal resolution), then answer the question.

(a) Informal resolution. Except as provided in § 542.13(b), an inmate shall first present an issue of concern informally to staff, and staff shall attempt to informally resolve the issue before an inmate submits a Request for Administrative Remedy. Each Warden shall establish procedures to allow for the informal resolution of inmate complaints.
(b) Exceptions. Inmates in CCCs are not required to attempt informal resolution. An informal resolution attempt is not required prior to submission to the Regional or Central Office as provided for in § 542.14(d) of this part. An informal resolution attempt may be waived in individual cases at the Warden or institution Administrative Remedy Coordinator's discretion when the inmate demonstrates an acceptable reason for bypassing informal resolution.

What must an inmate ordinarily do before submitting a formal Request for Administrative Remedy?
options: Obtain the signature of the housing unit officer on the form, based on the information available at the time
Submit a Request directly to the Regional Director
Wait for 20 days with no contact with staff
Present the issue informally to staff, and staff shall attempt to resolve it
questions.rationale: "An inmate shall first present an issue of concern informally to staff, and staff shall attempt to informally resolve the issue before an inmate submits a Request for Administrative Remedy." There are limited exceptions.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 542.14 (Initial filing), then answer the question.

(a) Submission. The deadline for completion of informal resolution and submission of a formal written Administrative Remedy Request, on the appropriate form (BP-9), is 20 calendar days following the date on which the basis for the Request occurred.

What is the deadline for completing informal resolution and submitting a formal written Request on the BP-9 form?
options: 20 calendar days following the date on which the basis for the Request occurred
30 calendar days following the date of the Warden's response
5 calendar days following the date on which the basis for the Request occurred
20 work days following the date on which the inmate arrived at the institution
questions.rationale: "The deadline for completion of informal resolution and submission of a formal written Administrative Remedy Request, on the appropriate form (BP-9), is 20 calendar days following the date on which the basis for the Request occurred."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 542.15 (Appeals), then answer the question.

(a) Submission. An inmate who is not satisfied with the Warden's response may submit an Appeal on the appropriate form (BP-10) to the appropriate Regional Director within 20 calendar days of the date the Warden signed the response. An inmate who is not satisfied with the Regional Director's response may submit an Appeal on the appropriate form (BP-11) to the General Counsel within 30 calendar days of the date the Regional Director signed the response. When the inmate demonstrates a valid reason for delay, these time limits may be extended. Valid reasons for delay include those situations described in § 542.14(b) of this part. Appeal to the General Counsel is the final administrative appeal.

Which appeal is the final administrative appeal?
options: The appeal to the Regional Director
The appeal to the Unit Discipline Committee
The appeal to the General Counsel
The appeal to the Warden
questions.rationale: The paragraph concludes "Appeal to the General Counsel is the final administrative appeal."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 542.17 (Resubmission), then answer the question.

(a) Rejections. The Coordinator at any level (CCM, institution, region, Central Office) may reject and return to the inmate without response a Request or an Appeal that is written by an inmate in a manner that is obscene or abusive, or does not meet any other requirement of this part.
(b) Notice. When a submission is rejected, the inmate shall be provided a written notice, signed by the Administrative Remedy Coordinator, explaining the reason for rejection. If the defect on which the rejection is based is correctable, the notice shall inform the inmate of a reasonable time extension within which to correct the defect and resubmit the Request or Appeal.

What happens when a submission is rejected for a defect that can be corrected?
options: The inmate receives a written notice explaining the reason, with a reasonable time extension to correct the defect and resubmit
The inmate receives a written notice, but he may not resubmit
The inmate receives no notice, and the submission is destroyed
The inmate receives a verbal notice, and the time extension is fifteen days, once the shift lieutenant has been informed, during normal operating hours
questions.rationale: A rejection requires "a written notice, signed by the Administrative Remedy Coordinator, explaining the reason for rejection. If the defect on which the rejection is based is correctable, the notice shall inform the inmate of a reasonable time extension within which to correct the defect and resubmit."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 548.10 (Purpose and scope), then answer the question.

(a) The Bureau of Prisons provides inmates of all faith groups with reasonable and equitable opportunities to pursue religious beliefs and practices, within the constraints of budgetary limitations and consistent with the security and orderly running of the institution and the Bureau of Prisons.

What does the Bureau of Prisons provide to inmates of all faith groups?
options: Opportunities to pursue beliefs in the chapel but not in the housing unit
Unlimited opportunities to hold religious activities regardless of security
Opportunities that are open only to groups with at least ten members
Reasonable and equitable opportunities to pursue religious beliefs and practices within budget limits and security needs
questions.rationale: The Bureau "provides inmates of all faith groups with reasonable and equitable opportunities to pursue religious beliefs and practices, within the constraints of budgetary limitations and consistent with the security and orderly running of the institution."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 548.10 (Purpose and scope), then answer the question.

(c) The Bureau of Prisons does not require an inmate to profess a religious belief. An inmate may designate any or no religious preference at his/her initial team screening. By notifying the chaplain in writing, an inmate may request to change this designation at any time, and the change will be effected in a timely fashion.

What does the excerpt say about an inmate's religious preference?
options: The Bureau requires the Warden to approve any change in religious preference
The Bureau does not require an inmate to profess a religious belief, and he may change his designation by notifying the chaplain in writing
The Bureau permits a change in designation only once each year
The Bureau requires an inmate to choose a religious preference at his first team screening and prohibits later changes, with the approval of a supervisor on duty
questions.rationale: "The Bureau of Prisons does not require an inmate to profess a religious belief. An inmate may designate any or no religious preference at his/her initial team screening. By notifying the chaplain in writing, an inmate may request to change this designation at any time."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 548.16 (Inmate religious property), then answer the question.

(a) Inmate religious property includes but is not limited to rosaries and prayer beads, oils, prayer rugs, phylacteries, medicine pouches, and religious medallions. Such items, which become part of an inmate's personal property, are subject to normal considerations of safety and security. If necessary, their religious significance shall be verified by the chaplain prior to the Warden's approval.

Which of the following does the excerpt list as inmate religious property?
options: Robes, flags, banners, and musical instruments
Religious books, cassette players, jewelry, and large statues, subject to the Warden's discretion, once the shift lieutenant has been informed
Candles, incense, matches, and ceremonial knives
Rosaries and prayer beads, oils, prayer rugs, phylacteries, medicine pouches, and religious medallions
questions.rationale: Inmate religious property "includes but is not limited to rosaries and prayer beads, oils, prayer rugs, phylacteries, medicine pouches, and religious medallions."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 543.11 (Legal research and preparation of legal documents), then answer the question.

(a) The Warden shall make materials in the inmate law library available whenever practical, including evening and weekend hours. The Warden shall allow an inmate a reasonable amount of time, ordinarily during the inmate's leisure time (that is, when the inmate is not participating in a scheduled program or work assignment), to do legal research and to prepare legal documents. Where practical, the Warden shall allow preparation of documents in living quarters during an inmate's leisure time.

When does the Warden ordinarily allow an inmate time to do legal research and prepare legal documents?
options: During the inmate's leisure time, when he is not in a scheduled program or work assignment
During visiting hours, as long as the inmate has a visitor present
During the evening count, as long as the housing unit officer is available to supervise
During the inmate's scheduled work assignment, as long as the work supervisor agrees
questions.rationale: The Warden allows "a reasonable amount of time, ordinarily during the inmate's leisure time (that is, when the inmate is not participating in a scheduled program or work assignment), to do legal research and to prepare legal documents."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 543.11 (Legal research and preparation of legal documents), then answer the question.

(c) Staff shall advise an inmate of rules and local procedures governing use of the inmate law library. Unauthorized possession of library materials by an inmate constitutes a prohibited act, generally warranting disciplinary action (see part 541 of this chapter).

What does the excerpt say about unauthorized possession of library materials by an inmate?
options: It is allowed if the inmate returns the materials by the end of the week
It is a prohibited act, generally warranting disciplinary action
It is a minor matter that staff should handle without a written report
It is allowed if the inmate is assisting another inmate with legal work
questions.rationale: "Unauthorized possession of library materials by an inmate constitutes a prohibited act, generally warranting disciplinary action (see part 541 of this chapter)."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 543.11 (Legal research and preparation of legal documents), then answer the question.

(e) An inmate is responsible for submitting his documents to court. Institution staff who are authorized to administer oaths shall be available to provide necessary witnessing of these documents, as requested by inmates and at times scheduled by staff.

Who is responsible for submitting an inmate's legal documents to court?
options: The unit team
The institution chaplain
The inmate
The Warden
questions.rationale: Paragraph (e): "An inmate is responsible for submitting his documents to court. Institution staff who are authorized to administer oaths shall be available to provide necessary witnessing."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 543.11 (Legal research and preparation of legal documents), then answer the question.

(g) The institution staff shall, upon an inmate's request and at times scheduled by staff, duplicate legal documents if the inmate demonstrates that more than one copy must be submitted to court and that the duplication cannot be accomplished by use of carbon paper. The inmate shall bear the cost, and the duplication shall be done so as not to interfere with regular institution operations. Staff may waive the cost if the inmate is without funds or if the material to be duplicated is minimal, and the inmate's requests for duplication are not large or excessive.

Who bears the cost of duplicating legal documents, and when may staff waive it?
options: The institution; staff may charge the inmate only if he is without funds
The inmate; staff may waive the cost if he is without funds or the material is minimal and his requests are not large or excessive
The inmate's attorney; staff may waive the cost if the attorney is a public defender
The inmate; staff may never waive the cost under any circumstances
questions.rationale: "The inmate shall bear the cost... Staff may waive the cost if the inmate is without funds or if the material to be duplicated is minimal, and the inmate's requests for duplication are not large or excessive."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 543.13 (Visits by attorneys), then answer the question.

(a) The Warden shall, under the conditions of this section, permit visits by the retained, appointed, or prospective attorney of an inmate or by an attorney who wishes to interview an inmate as a witness.
(b) The Warden generally may not limit the frequency of attorney visits since the number of visits necessary is dependent upon the nature and urgency of the legal problems involved. The Warden shall set the time and place for visits, which ordinarily take place during regular visiting hours. Attorney visits shall take place in a private conference room, if available, or in a regular visiting room in an area and at a time designed to allow a degree of privacy. The Warden may make exceptions according to local conditions or for an emergency situation demonstrated by the inmate or visiting attorney.

What does the excerpt say about the frequency of attorney visits?
options: The Warden generally may not limit it, since the number of visits needed depends on the nature and urgency of the legal problems
The Warden may limit it to one visit per month for every inmate
The Warden must limit it to the regular visiting hours on weekends
The Warden may limit it whenever the attorney is not licensed in the same state
questions.rationale: "The Warden generally may not limit the frequency of attorney visits since the number of visits necessary is dependent upon the nature and urgency of the legal problems involved."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 543.13 (Visits by attorneys), then answer the question.

(b) The Warden generally may not limit the frequency of attorney visits since the number of visits necessary is dependent upon the nature and urgency of the legal problems involved. The Warden shall set the time and place for visits, which ordinarily take place during regular visiting hours. Attorney visits shall take place in a private conference room, if available, or in a regular visiting room in an area and at a time designed to allow a degree of privacy. The Warden may make exceptions according to local conditions or for an emergency situation demonstrated by the inmate or visiting attorney.

Where should attorney visits take place?
options: In the law library, during regular library hours
In a private conference room, if available, or in a regular visiting room in an area and at a time designed to allow a degree of privacy
In the inmate's housing unit, with the door open for supervision
In the main visiting room, at a table close to the officer's station, pending review by the appropriate official, subject to the Warden's discretion
questions.rationale: "Attorney visits shall take place in a private conference room, if available, or in a regular visiting room in an area and at a time designed to allow a degree of privacy."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 543.13 (Visits by attorneys), then answer the question.

(f) The Warden may, at any time, subject an attorney to a search of his person and belongings for the purpose of ascertaining if contraband is present, as a condition of visiting an inmate.

What may the Warden do, as a condition of an attorney visiting an inmate?
options: Subject the attorney to a search of his person and belongings to see if contraband is present
Require the attorney to submit all notes for review before leaving the institution
Require the attorney to leave his briefcase with the front desk for the entire visit, based on the information available at the time
Require the attorney to wear a visitor badge issued by the inmate's unit manager
questions.rationale: "The Warden may, at any time, subject an attorney to a search of his person and belongings for the purpose of ascertaining if contraband is present, as a condition of visiting an inmate."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 543.14 (Limitation or denial of attorney visits and correspondence), then answer the question.

(d) The attorney may appeal any limitation or denial by the Warden of attorney visits or correspondence rights to the Regional Director. The inmate affected may appeal through the Administrative Remedy Procedures.

How may an attorney appeal a limitation or denial of attorney visits or correspondence?
options: To the Regional Director
To the Warden who imposed it
To the court where the case is pending
To the General Counsel
questions.rationale: "The attorney may appeal any limitation or denial by the Warden of attorney visits or correspondence rights to the Regional Director. The inmate affected may appeal through the Administrative Remedy Procedures."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 545.21 (Definitions), then answer the question.

(b) Institution work assignment. A work assignment which contributes to the day-to-day operation of the institution (e.g., carpentry, plumbing, food service).
(c) Industry assignment. A Federal Prison Industries (FPI) work assignment.
(d) Commissary assignment. A Trust Fund work assignment.

Which description matches an "industry assignment"?
options: A work assignment that contributes to the day-to-day operation of the institution
A Federal Prison Industries (FPI) work assignment
A Trust Fund work assignment
A work assignment in which the inmate performs only limited functions because of physical limitations
questions.rationale: The definitions are: institution work assignment (day-to-day operation), industry assignment ("A Federal Prison Industries (FPI) work assignment"), commissary assignment (a Trust Fund work assignment), and light duty (limited functions).

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 545.21 (Definitions), then answer the question.

(e) Full-time work assignment. A work assignment to which an inmate is assigned for the entire scheduled work day.
(f) Part-time work assignment. A work assignment to which an inmate is assigned for only a portion of the scheduled work day. Part-time work assignments are ordinarily made in conjunction with drug treatment programming, education, and/or vocational training programs.

How is a part-time work assignment ordinarily made?
options: In conjunction with a request for a transfer to another institution
In conjunction with a release date within the next ninety days
In conjunction with drug treatment programming, education, and/or vocational training programs
In conjunction with disciplinary segregation or administrative detention, based on the information available at the time
questions.rationale: Part-time assignments are for "only a portion of the scheduled work day" and "are ordinarily made in conjunction with drug treatment programming, education, and/or vocational training programs."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 545.23 (Inmate work/program assignment), then answer the question.

(a) Each sentenced inmate who is physically and mentally able is to be assigned to an institutional, industrial, or commissary work program. Exception shall be made to allow for inmate participation in an education, vocational, or drug abuse treatment program, on either a full or part-time basis, where this involvement is mandated by Bureau policy or statute (for example, the Literacy Program). Where such participation is not required by either policy or statute, exception may be made to allow an inmate to participate in an education, vocational, or drug abuse treatment program rather than work full-time upon the request of the inmate and approval of the Warden or designee.

Who is to be assigned to an institutional, industrial, or commissary work program?
options: Each sentenced inmate who is physically and mentally able
Only inmates who request a work assignment in writing
Each inmate of the institution, including pretrial inmates
Only inmates who are within five years of release
questions.rationale: "Each sentenced inmate who is physically and mentally able is to be assigned to an institutional, industrial, or commissary work program," with exceptions for mandated education or treatment programs.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 545.23 (Inmate work/program assignment), then answer the question.

(d) In making the work and/or program assignment(s), staff shall consider the inmate's capacity to learn, interests, requests, needs, and eligibility, and the availability of the assignment(s). An inmate's assignment shall be made with consideration of the institution's security and operational needs, and should be consistent with the safekeeping of the inmate and protection of the public.

Select ALL of the things staff shall consider in making work and program assignments.
options: The inmate's capacity to learn
The inmate's religious affiliation
The inmate's interests and requests
The institution's security and operational needs
The inmate's visiting list
questions.rationale: Staff consider "the inmate's capacity to learn, interests, requests, needs, and eligibility, and the availability of the assignment(s)" along with the institution's security and operational needs. Religious affiliation and visiting list are not factors.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 545.24 (Inmate work conditions), then answer the question.

(c) An inmate, regardless of assignment, is expected to perform all assigned tasks diligently and conscientiously. Disciplinary action may be taken against an inmate who refuses to work, who otherwise evades attendance and performance standards in assigned activities, or who encourages others to do so.

Against whom may disciplinary action be taken, according to paragraph (c)?
options: An inmate who refuses to work, evades attendance and performance standards, or encourages others to do so
An inmate who completes his assigned task earlier than expected
An inmate who requests a change of work assignment in writing
An inmate who reports an unsafe condition to the work supervisor, once the shift lieutenant has been informed
questions.rationale: "Disciplinary action may be taken against an inmate who refuses to work, who otherwise evades attendance and performance standards in assigned activities, or who encourages others to do so."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 545.24 (Inmate work conditions), then answer the question.

(e) An inmate is expected to perform the work assignment in a safe manner, using safety equipment as instructed by the work supervisor. In the event of any work related injury, the inmate shall notify the work supervisor so that appropriate action (for example, medical attention, and submission of necessary reports) may be taken.

An inmate is hurt on his work assignment. What does the excerpt direct him to do?
options: Wait until the end of the shift and report to the housing unit officer
Notify the work supervisor so that appropriate action, such as medical attention and necessary reports, may be taken
Complete a report himself and give it to the chaplain
Report the injury to the Warden by mail within seven days
questions.rationale: "In the event of any work related injury, the inmate shall notify the work supervisor so that appropriate action (for example, medical attention, and submission of necessary reports) may be taken."

options: Literacy program (GED) participation
Apprenticeship training
Institution work assignment
Participation in the visiting room
Participation in religious services
questions.rationale: Performance pay areas are an institution work assignment, literacy (GED) participation, apprenticeship training, and approved vocational training courses.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 545.26 (Performance pay provisions), then answer the question.

(h) An inmate's performance pay, once earned, becomes vested.
(i) Each inmate in performance pay status shall be notified of monthly earnings.

What does the excerpt say about performance pay once it has been earned?
options: It may be withdrawn at any time by the work supervisor, and the inmate is notified in writing
It becomes vested only after twelve months, and the inmate is notified at release
It remains pending until the end of the quarter, and the inmate is notified yearly
It becomes vested, and each inmate in performance pay status is notified of monthly earnings
questions.rationale: "An inmate's performance pay, once earned, becomes vested. Each inmate in performance pay status shall be notified of monthly earnings."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 549.12 (Testing), then answer the question.

(4) Inmate request. An inmate may request to be tested. The Bureau limits such testing to no more than one per 12-month period unless the Bureau determines that additional testing is warranted.
(5) Counseling. Inmates being tested for HIV will receive pre- and post-test counseling, regardless of the test results.

How often may an inmate request HIV testing, and what counseling does he receive?
options: No more than once per month, with counseling only if the result is positive, where the circumstances reasonably call for it
No more than once per 12-month period unless more is warranted, with pre- and post-test counseling regardless of results
Whenever he wishes, with counseling only before the test
No more than once per five years, with counseling only if requested
questions.rationale: "The Bureau limits such testing to no more than one per 12-month period unless the Bureau determines that additional testing is warranted," and inmates tested "will receive pre- and post-test counseling, regardless of the test results."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 549.12 (Testing), then answer the question.

(b) Tuberculosis (TB). (1) The Bureau screens each inmate for TB within two calendar days of initial incarceration.

When does the Bureau screen each inmate for tuberculosis after initial incarceration?
options: Within two weeks
Within two months
Within two calendar days
Within two years
questions.rationale: "The Bureau screens each inmate for TB within two calendar days of initial incarceration," then annually as medically indicated.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 549.31 (Inmates without funds), then answer the question.

(a) The Warden must establish procedures to provide up to two OTC medications per week for an inmate without funds. An inmate without funds is an inmate who has not had a trust fund account balance of $6.00 for the past 30 days.

How many over-the-counter (OTC) medications per week must the Warden provide procedures for, for an inmate without funds?
options: Only one each month
Up to ten
Up to two
Up to four
questions.rationale: "The Warden must establish procedures to provide up to two OTC medications per week for an inmate without funds."

options: Cosmetic procedures requested by the inmate
Mental health care
Prenatal care
Emergency services
Health care visits requested by the inmate without a referral
questions.rationale: No fee is charged for staff-referred services, staff-approved follow-up for a chronic condition, preventive care, emergency services, prenatal care, chronic infectious disease diagnosis or treatment, mental health care, and substance abuse treatment. Self-requested non-referred visits are not on the free list.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 551.1 (Policy), then answer the question.

The Bureau of Prisons permits an inmate to select the hair style of personal choice, and expects personal cleanliness and dress in keeping with standards of good grooming and the security, good order, and discipline of the institution.

What standards does the Bureau expect regarding an inmate's appearance?
options: A uniform hair style assigned by the institution, with dress chosen by the unit officer
A hair style of personal choice, with personal cleanliness and dress in keeping with good grooming and institutional security, good order, and discipline
A hair style approved by the chaplain, with personal cleanliness left to the inmate
A hair style that is short and neat, with dress chosen by the inmate's family
questions.rationale: The Bureau "permits an inmate to select the hair style of personal choice, and expects personal cleanliness and dress in keeping with standards of good grooming and the security, good order, and discipline of the institution."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 551.2 (Mustaches and beards), then answer the question.

An inmate may wear a mustache or beard or both. The Warden shall require an inmate with a beard to wear a beard covering when working in food service or where a beard could result in increased likelihood of work injury.

An inmate with a beard is assigned to work in food service. What does the excerpt require?
options: The inmate must obtain a chaplain's approval
The Warden shall require him to shave the beard
The Warden shall require him to wear a beard covering
The inmate may choose whether or not to wear a covering
questions.rationale: An inmate may wear a mustache or beard, but "The Warden shall require an inmate with a beard to wear a beard covering when working in food service or where a beard could result in increased likelihood of work injury."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 551.4 (Hair length), then answer the question.

(a) The Warden may not restrict hair length if the inmate keeps it neat and clean.
(b) The Warden shall require an inmate with long hair to wear a cap or hair net when working in food service or where long hair could result in increased likelihood of work injury.

What does the excerpt say about hair length?
options: The Warden may restrict hair length for inmates in food service only, and may require them to shave or cut their hair
The Warden may restrict hair length for any inmate housed in a segregation unit, and may require a cap or hair net in the unit
The Warden may restrict hair length to a uniform maximum for all inmates, but may exempt inmates who work in food service
The Warden may not restrict hair length if the inmate keeps it neat and clean, but may require a cap or hair net in food service or where long hair increases the likelihood of injury
questions.rationale: "The Warden may not restrict hair length if the inmate keeps it neat and clean," but "shall require an inmate with long hair to wear a cap or hair net when working in food service or where long hair could result in increased likelihood of work injury."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 551.13 (Application to marry), then answer the question.

(c) All expenses of the marriage (for example, a marriage license) shall be paid by the inmate, the inmate's intended spouse, the inmate's family, or other appropriate source approved by the Warden. The Warden may not permit appropriated funds to be used for an inmate marriage.

Who pays the expenses of an inmate marriage, such as a marriage license?
options: The Regional Office, using the budget for inmate programs, in accordance with the posted schedule
The inmate, the intended spouse, the inmate's family, or another source approved by the Warden
The institution, using appropriated funds
The chaplain, using the religious services fund
questions.rationale: "All expenses of the marriage (for example, a marriage license) shall be paid by the inmate, the inmate's intended spouse, the inmate's family, or other appropriate source approved by the Warden. The Warden may not permit appropriated funds to be used for an inmate marriage."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 551.34 (Organization activities), then answer the question.

(b) The Warden may approve the request if the activity:
(1) Does not conflict with scheduled inmate work or program activities;
(2) Has confirmation of staff supervision;
(3) Can be appropriately funded when applicable (see § 551.36); and
(4) Does not conflict with the security, good order, or discipline of the institution.

Select ALL of the conditions the Warden considers in approving an organization activity.
options: It is open to the public
It does not conflict with scheduled inmate work or program activities
It does not conflict with the security, good order, or discipline of the institution
It will be led by an outside volunteer
It has confirmation of staff supervision
questions.rationale: The Warden may approve the activity if it does not conflict with work or program activities, has confirmation of staff supervision, can be appropriately funded when applicable, and does not conflict with security, good order, or discipline.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 551.162 (Smoking generally prohibited), then answer the question.

Smoking is generally prohibited in and on the grounds of Bureau institutions and offices, with the following two exceptions:
(a) Smoking is permitted as part of an authorized inmate religious activity; and
(b) For Bureau staff and official visitors, smoking is permitted only in smoking areas designated by the Warden.

Smoking is generally prohibited at Bureau institutions. Which exceptions does the excerpt allow?
options: Smoking by inmates who have earned privileges, and by staff in the control center
Smoking as part of an authorized inmate religious activity, and by staff and official visitors in smoking areas designated by the Warden
Smoking by inmates in the dayroom, and by staff anywhere outside the housing units, in accordance with the posted schedule, once the shift lieutenant has been informed
Smoking by inmates in the yard, and by visitors in the visiting room
questions.rationale: The two exceptions are "smoking as part of an authorized inmate religious activity" and, "for Bureau staff and official visitors, smoking is permitted only in smoking areas designated by the Warden."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.5 (General definitions), then answer the question.

Unfounded allegation means an allegation that was investigated and determined not to have occurred.

According to the definitions, an "unfounded allegation" is one that was
options: reported anonymously and never investigated
investigated and found to have insufficient evidence either way
investigated and determined not to have occurred
investigated and determined to have occurred
questions.rationale: "Unfounded allegation means an allegation that was investigated and determined not to have occurred." A substantiated allegation was determined to have occurred; an unsubstantiated allegation lacked enough evidence for a final determination.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.5 (General definitions), then answer the question.

Substantiated allegation means an allegation that was investigated and determined to have occurred.

Which description matches a "substantiated allegation"?
options: An allegation that was made by a staff member rather than an inmate
An allegation that was investigated but produced insufficient evidence
An allegation that was investigated and determined not to have occurred
An allegation that was investigated and determined to have occurred
questions.rationale: "Substantiated allegation means an allegation that was investigated and determined to have occurred."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.5 (General definitions), then answer the question.

Direct staff supervision means that security staff are in the same room with, and within reasonable hearing distance of, the resident or inmate.

What does "direct staff supervision" require?
options: Security staff are in the same building as the resident or inmate and check hourly, when staff resources allow
Security staff are in the same room with, and within reasonable hearing distance of, the resident or inmate
Security staff watch the resident or inmate through a camera from a control room
Security staff are within sight of the resident or inmate and carrying a radio
questions.rationale: "Direct staff supervision means that security staff are in the same room with, and within reasonable hearing distance of, the resident or inmate."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.5 (General definitions), then answer the question.

Exigent circumstances means any set of temporary and unforeseen circumstances that require immediate action in order to combat a threat to the security or institutional order of a facility.

Which phrase best defines "exigent circumstances"?
options: Permanent conditions that require a change in facility policy and a vote by the staff, provided that the action is documented
Emergency conditions that require evacuation of the facility and notice to the public
Temporary and unforeseen circumstances that require immediate action to combat a threat to security or institutional order
Planned events that require extra staffing and prior approval from the Warden
questions.rationale: "Exigent circumstances means any set of temporary and unforeseen circumstances that require immediate action in order to combat a threat to the security or institutional order of a facility."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.5 (General definitions), then answer the question.

Pat-down search means a running of the hands over the clothed body of an inmate, detainee, or resident by an employee to determine whether the individual possesses contraband.

What is a "pat-down search" as defined in the excerpt?
options: A search that requires a person to remove clothing so that body surfaces can be visually inspected
A search by an electronic device that does not require the person to be touched
A search of a person's cell and belongings carried out by two or more employees
A running of the hands over the clothed body of an individual by an employee to determine whether the individual possesses contraband
questions.rationale: "Pat-down search means a running of the hands over the clothed body of an inmate, detainee, or resident by an employee to determine whether the individual possesses contraband."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.5 (General definitions), then answer the question.

Strip search means a search that requires a person to remove or arrange some or all clothing so as to permit a visual inspection of the person's breasts, buttocks, or genitalia.

How does the excerpt define a "strip search"?
options: A search that requires a person to remove or arrange some or all clothing so as to permit a visual inspection of the breasts, buttocks, or genitalia
A search conducted by an officer's hands over a person's clothing
A search conducted by medical staff using simple instruments inside a body cavity
A search that requires a person to remove only outer garments such as a coat or shoes, as long as the unit team is notified, unless an emergency requires otherwise
questions.rationale: "Strip search means a search that requires a person to remove or arrange some or all clothing so as to permit a visual inspection of the person's breasts, buttocks, or genitalia."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.5 (General definitions), then answer the question.

Security staff means employees primarily responsible for the supervision and control of inmates, detainees, or residents in housing units, recreational areas, dining areas, and other program areas of the facility.

Which employees does the excerpt define as "security staff"?
options: Employees primarily responsible for the care of inmates in medical units and mental health programs
Employees primarily responsible for the supervision and control of inmates in housing units, recreational areas, dining areas, and other program areas
Employees primarily responsible for the administration and budget of the facility
Employees primarily responsible for training other employees in security procedures
questions.rationale: "Security staff means employees primarily responsible for the supervision and control of inmates, detainees, or residents in housing units, recreational areas, dining areas, and other program areas of the facility."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.5 (General definitions), then answer the question.

Youthful inmate means any person under the age of 18 who is under adult court supervision and incarcerated or detained in a prison or jail.

Who is a "youthful inmate"?
options: A person under 25 who is serving a sentence of less than one year
A person under 18 who is held in a juvenile facility under juvenile court supervision, after a supervisor has reviewed the matter
A person under 18 who is under adult court supervision and incarcerated or detained in a prison or jail
A person under 21 who is housed in any facility in the agency
questions.rationale: "Youthful inmate means any person under the age of 18 who is under adult court supervision and incarcerated or detained in a prison or jail."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.2 (Definitions), then answer the question.

(1) Open general correspondence means general correspondence which is not limited to a list of authorized correspondents, except as provided in § 540.17.
(2) Restricted general correspondence means general correspondence which is limited to a list of authorized correspondents.

What is the difference between open general correspondence and restricted general correspondence?
options: Open general correspondence is read by staff, while restricted correspondence is read by the Warden
Open general correspondence includes packages, while restricted includes only letters
Open general correspondence is not limited to a list of authorized correspondents, while restricted is limited to such a list
Open general correspondence is incoming only, while restricted is outgoing only
questions.rationale: "Open general correspondence means general correspondence which is not limited to a list of authorized correspondents... Restricted general correspondence means general correspondence which is limited to a list of authorized correspondents."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.2 (Definitions), then answer the question.

(a) General correspondence means incoming or outgoing correspondence other than special mail. General correspondence includes packages sent through the mail.

Under the definition of general correspondence, which is true?
options: It means all mail that is sent to or from an attorney
It means only incoming letters from family, and excludes packages, according to the institution's local guidelines, with the approval of a supervisor on duty
It means only mail sent to elected officials
It means incoming or outgoing correspondence other than special mail, and includes packages sent through the mail
questions.rationale: "General correspondence means incoming or outgoing correspondence other than special mail. General correspondence includes packages sent through the mail."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.62 (Institutional visits), then answer the question.

(c) The Warden may suspend all media visits during an institutional emergency and for a reasonable time after the emergency.
(d) An inmate currently confined in an institution may not be employed or act as a reporter.

Which statement about media visits is supported by the excerpt?
options: The Warden may suspend media visits only at the request of the media
An inmate confined in an institution may act as a reporter if he gets approval, according to the institution's local guidelines, based on the information available at the time
The Warden may suspend all media visits during an institutional emergency and for a reasonable time afterward, and an inmate may not act as a reporter
Media visits may be made without an appointment
questions.rationale: "The Warden may suspend all media visits during an institutional emergency and for a reasonable time after the emergency" and "An inmate currently confined in an institution may not be employed or act as a reporter." Media must make advance appointments.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 551.101 (Definitions), then answer the question.

(a) Pretrial inmate. For purpose of this rule, “pretrial inmate” means a person who is legally detained but for whom the Bureau of Prisons has not received notification of conviction. Thus, “pretrial inmate” ordinarily includes a person awaiting trial, being tried, or awaiting a verdict.
(1) Civil contempt, deportable aliens, or material witnesses. For purpose of this rule, an inmate committed for civil contempt, or as a deportable alien, or as a material witness is considered a pretrial inmate.

Who is a "pretrial inmate" under the definition?
options: A person who has been released on bail and reports to the institution at set times, for whom the Bureau has not received notice
A person legally detained for whom the Bureau has not received notification of conviction, ordinarily including one awaiting trial, being tried, or awaiting a verdict
A person who has been convicted by a court and is awaiting sentencing, for whom the Bureau has received notification of conviction
A person who has completed a sentence and is being held for release processing, for whom the Bureau has received notice
questions.rationale: "'Pretrial inmate' means a person who is legally detained but for whom the Bureau of Prisons has not received notification of conviction. Thus, 'pretrial inmate' ordinarily includes a person awaiting trial, being tried, or awaiting a verdict."

options: Contact with the inmate's employer
A tour of the institution for the inmate's family
Verification of commitment papers
Opportunity for waiver of right not to work
Photographing and fingerprinting
questions.rationale: Admission procedures include verification of commitment papers, a search, photographing and fingerprinting, disposition of clothing and possessions, intake screening, telephone guidelines, hygiene provisions, orientation, an opportunity for waiver of the right not to work, and housing assignment.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 551.107 (Pretrial inmate reviews), then answer the question.

(a) Each pretrial inmate shall be scheduled for an initial review by the unit team within 21 calendar days of the inmate's first arrival at the institution, and subsequent reviews shall be conducted at least every 90 days.

When is a pretrial inmate's initial review by the unit team scheduled, and how often are subsequent reviews held?
options: Within 21 calendar days of first arrival, then at least every 90 days
Within 7 calendar days of first arrival, then at least every 30 days, when staff resources allow
Within 48 hours of first arrival, then at least every week
Within 90 calendar days of first arrival, then at least every year
questions.rationale: "Each pretrial inmate shall be scheduled for an initial review by the unit team within 21 calendar days of the inmate's first arrival at the institution, and subsequent reviews shall be conducted at least every 90 days."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 551.107 (Pretrial inmate reviews), then answer the question.

(b) The inmate shall be notified at least 48 hours prior to the inmate's scheduled review.
(c) A pretrial inmate is expected to attend these reviews. If the inmate refuses to appear, staff shall document in the record of the meeting the inmate's refusal and, if known, the reason for refusal.
(d) Inmate reviews are to be documented on the Pretrial Inmate Review Report.

What must staff do if a pretrial inmate refuses to appear at his scheduled review?
options: Report the refusal to the court the same day
Document the refusal in the record of the meeting and, if known, the reason for the refusal
Reschedule the review every week until he appears
Cancel all of his privileges for thirty days
questions.rationale: "A pretrial inmate is expected to attend these reviews. If the inmate refuses to appear, staff shall document in the record of the meeting the inmate's refusal and, if known, the reason for refusal." He must be notified at least 48 hours in advance.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 551.115 (Recreation), then answer the question.

(b) At a minimum, and except as noted in paragraph (d) of this section, staff shall provide the pretrial inmate with the following recreational opportunities:
(1) One hour daily of outside recreation, weather permitting; or
(2) Two hours daily of indoor recreation.

What is the minimum recreation staff must provide to a pretrial inmate?
options: Thirty minutes daily of outside recreation, or one hour daily of indoor recreation, when staff resources allow
Two hours daily of outside recreation, or four hours daily of indoor recreation
One hour daily of outside recreation, weather permitting, or two hours daily of indoor recreation
One hour weekly of outside recreation, or two hours weekly of indoor recreation
questions.rationale: At a minimum, staff provide "one hour daily of outside recreation, weather permitting; or two hours daily of indoor recreation."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 551.116 (Discipline), then answer the question.

(b) Staff shall advise the court, through the U.S. Marshal, of repeated or serious disruptive behavior by a pretrial inmate.

Whom must staff advise, through the U.S. Marshal, of repeated or serious disruptive behavior by a pretrial inmate?
options: The court
The Regional Director
The sentencing commission
The inmate's family
questions.rationale: "Staff shall advise the court, through the U.S. Marshal, of repeated or serious disruptive behavior by a pretrial inmate."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 551.117 (Access to legal resources), then answer the question.

(a) The Warden shall provide the opportunity for pretrial inmate-attorney visits on a seven-days-a-week basis.
(b) Staff shall provide pretrial inmates with access to legal materials in the institution.
(c) Staff shall allow the pretrial inmate, upon the inmate's request, to telephone the inmate's attorney as often as resources of the institution allow.

Select ALL of the provisions the excerpt requires regarding pretrial inmates' access to legal resources.
options: Free attorneys provided by the institution
A guarantee of unlimited private visits at any hour
Opportunity for attorney visits seven days a week
Access to legal materials in the institution
Telephone calls to the inmate's attorney as often as institution resources allow
questions.rationale: The Warden provides attorney visits on a seven-days-a-week basis, staff provide access to legal materials, and staff allow calls to the inmate's attorney "as often as resources of the institution allow."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 551.120 (Visiting), then answer the question.

Staff shall allow pretrial inmates to receive visits in accordance with the Bureau's rule and local institution guidelines on visiting. Staff may allow a pretrial inmate special visits to protect the inmate's business interests or to help prepare for trial.

For what purposes may staff allow a pretrial inmate special visits?
options: To attend the funeral of a distant relative
To discuss potential employment after release, when staff resources allow, provided that the action is documented
To celebrate a holiday with extended family
To protect the inmate's business interests or to help prepare for trial
questions.rationale: "Staff may allow a pretrial inmate special visits to protect the inmate's business interests or to help prepare for trial."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.18 (Upgrades to facilities and technologies), then answer the question.

(a) When designing or acquiring any new facility and in planning any substantial expansion or modification of existing facilities, the agency shall consider the effect of the design, acquisition, expansion, or modification upon the agency's ability to protect inmates from sexual abuse.

When designing or acquiring a new facility or planning a substantial expansion, what must an agency consider?
options: The effect of the design, acquisition, expansion, or modification upon its ability to protect inmates from sexual abuse
The effect of the design, acquisition, expansion, or modification upon the number of staff needed on each shift
The effect of the design, acquisition, expansion, or modification upon the cost of construction and maintenance
The effect of the design, acquisition, expansion, or modification upon the ability of inmates to access programs, provided that the action is documented
questions.rationale: Section 115.18 requires agencies to consider "the effect of the design, acquisition, expansion, or modification upon the agency's ability to protect inmates from sexual abuse."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.22 (Policies to ensure referrals of allegations for investigations), then answer the question.

(a) The agency shall ensure that an administrative or criminal investigation is completed for all allegations of sexual abuse and sexual harassment.

What must the agency ensure regarding allegations of sexual abuse or sexual harassment?
options: That allegations by staff are investigated, but those by inmates are not
That an administrative or criminal investigation is completed for all allegations
That an investigation is begun only if the alleged victim files a grievance
That a criminal investigation is completed for substantiated allegations only
questions.rationale: Section 115.22(a) requires that "an administrative or criminal investigation is completed for all allegations of sexual abuse and sexual harassment."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.71 (Procedures), then answer the question.

(a)(1) At all Bureau institutions, an inmate may receive hardcover publications and newspaper only from the publisher, from a book club, or from a bookstore.

From whom may an inmate at any Bureau institution receive hardcover publications?
options: Only from the publisher, a book club, or a bookstore
Only from the institution library or the chaplain's office
Only from family members who are on the approved visiting list
From any source, as long as the book is inspected first
questions.rationale: "At all Bureau institutions, an inmate may receive hardcover publications and newspaper only from the publisher, from a book club, or from a bookstore."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.71 (Procedures), then answer the question.

(b) The Warden may reject a publication only if it is determined detrimental to the security, good order, or discipline of the institution or if it might facilitate criminal activity. The Warden may not reject a publication solely because its content is religious, philosophical, political, social or sexual, or because its content is unpopular or repugnant. Publications which may be rejected by a Warden include but are not limited to publications which meet one of the following criteria:

On what basis may the Warden reject a publication?
options: If the Warden finds that the content is repugnant, even if it poses no security concern
If its content is religious, political, or unpopular with other staff members
If it is published by an organization that the Warden has not approved in writing
Only if it is determined detrimental to the security, good order, or discipline of the institution or might facilitate criminal activity
questions.rationale: "The Warden may reject a publication only if it is determined detrimental to the security, good order, or discipline of the institution or if it might facilitate criminal activity. The Warden may not reject a publication solely because its content is religious, philosophical, political, social or sexual, or because its content is unpopular or repugnant."

options: A publication that criticizes a political leader
A publication that contains an unpopular religious viewpoint
A publication that is written in code
A publication that describes procedures for the construction or use of weapons or bombs
A publication that encourages or instructs in the commission of criminal activity
questions.rationale: Rejectable publications include those that describe weapon or bomb construction, methods of escape, brewing alcohol or making drugs, are written in code, encourage violence or group disruption, instruct in crime, or are harmful sexually explicit material. Political or religious viewpoints alone are not grounds.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.71 (Procedures), then answer the question.

(f) The Warden may set limits locally (for fire, sanitation or housekeeping reasons) on the number or volume of publications an inmate may receive or retain in his quarters. The Warden may authorize an inmate additional storage space for storage of legal materials in accordance with the Bureau of Prisons procedures on personal property of inmates.

For what reasons may the Warden set local limits on the number or volume of publications an inmate may keep in his quarters?
options: For fire, sanitation, or housekeeping reasons
For security, discipline, or gang-related reasons
For religious, political, or social reasons
For budget, staffing, or record-keeping reasons
questions.rationale: "The Warden may set limits locally (for fire, sanitation or housekeeping reasons) on the number or volume of publications an inmate may receive or retain in his quarters."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.64 (Press pools), then answer the question.

(a) The Warden may establish a press pool whenever he or she determines that the frequency of requests for interviews and visits reaches a volume that warrants limitations.
(b) Whenever the Warden establishes a press pool, the Warden shall notify all news media representatives who have requested interviews or visits that have not been conducted. Selected representatives are admitted to the institution to conduct the interviews under the specific guidelines established by the Warden.

When may the Warden establish a press pool?
options: Whenever the Regional Director requests that media contact be limited
Whenever the frequency of requests for interviews and visits reaches a volume that warrants limitations
Whenever an institutional emergency occurs, and for a reasonable time afterward
Whenever a news organization requests a visit that the Warden does not want to approve, provided that the action is documented
questions.rationale: "The Warden may establish a press pool whenever he or she determines that the frequency of requests for interviews and visits reaches a volume that warrants limitations."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.65 (Release of information), then answer the question.

(a) The Warden shall promptly make announcements stating the facts of unusual, newsworthy incidents to local news media. Examples are deaths, inside escapes, and institution emergencies.

What must the Warden promptly announce to local news media?
options: The facts of unusual, newsworthy incidents, such as deaths, inside escapes, and institution emergencies
The names of all inmates involved in a disturbance, with their register numbers, according to the institution's local guidelines
The results of staff disciplinary actions taken after an incident
The sentences of inmates who have recently been transferred to the institution
questions.rationale: "The Warden shall promptly make announcements stating the facts of unusual, newsworthy incidents to local news media. Examples are deaths, inside escapes, and institution emergencies."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.40 (Purpose and scope), then answer the question.

(a) In an effort to maintain a safe and orderly environment within its institutions, the Bureau of Prisons operates control unit programs intended to place into a separate unit those inmates who are unable to function in a less restrictive environment without being a threat to others or to the orderly operation of the institution. The Bureau of Prisons provides written criteria for the:

What is the purpose of the Bureau's control unit programs?
options: To place into a separate unit those inmates who have completed disciplinary segregation and need medical treatment
To place into a separate unit those inmates who are awaiting transfer to another institution or a court appearance
To place into a separate unit those inmates who have requested protection from other inmates in the general population
To place into a separate unit those inmates who cannot function in a less restrictive environment without threatening others or the orderly operation of the institution
questions.rationale: Control unit programs are "intended to place into a separate unit those inmates who are unable to function in a less restrictive environment without being a threat to others or to the orderly operation of the institution."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.46 (Programs and services), then answer the question.

(1) Each inmate shall have the opportunity to receive a minimum of seven hours weekly recreation and exercise out of the cell.

What is the minimum weekly recreation and exercise out of the cell for a control unit inmate?
options: Seven hours
Three hours
Ten hours
Five hours
questions.rationale: "Each inmate shall have the opportunity to receive a minimum of seven hours weekly recreation and exercise out of the cell."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.46 (Programs and services), then answer the question.

(h) Medical services. A member of the medical staff shall visit control unit inmates daily. A physician will visit the unit as the need arises.

How often does a member of the medical staff visit control unit inmates?
options: Weekly
Daily
Only on request
Monthly
questions.rationale: "A member of the medical staff shall visit control unit inmates daily. A physician will visit the unit as the need arises."

options: The criteria for release from the unit
A list of the staff members who recommended placement
A copy of the inmate's central file
Notice of the projected duration of the inmate's confinement
A summary of the guidelines and disciplinary procedures applicable in the unit
questions.rationale: Staff provide notice of projected duration, allowable property, a summary of guidelines and disciplinary procedures, an explanation of activities, expectations, and release criteria. The central file and recommenders' names are not on the list.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 551.151 (Definitions), then answer the question.

(a) For purpose of this rule, victim is generally defined as someone who suffers direct or threatened physical, emotional, or financial harm as the result of the commission of a crime. The term “victim” also includes the immediate family of a minor or a homicide victim.

How does the excerpt define a "victim" for the purpose of the notification rule?
options: Someone who has provided information to a law enforcement agency about a crime
Someone who is physically injured by an inmate while the inmate is in the custody of the Bureau, unless local procedures say otherwise
Someone who suffers direct or threatened physical, emotional, or financial harm as the result of the commission of a crime
Someone who has been named in a court order as having been harmed by a specific inmate
questions.rationale: "Victim is generally defined as someone who suffers direct or threatened physical, emotional, or financial harm as the result of the commission of a crime. The term 'victim' also includes the immediate family of a minor or a homicide victim."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 551.152 (Procedures), then answer the question.

(b) Institution staff shall promptly notify the victim and/or witness when his or her request for notification has been received. Staff shall advise each approved victim and/or witness of that person's responsibility for notifying the Bureau of Prisons of any address and/or telephone number changes.

What must staff advise each approved victim or witness?
options: That he or she will be notified only of the inmate's death or escape
That he or she is responsible for notifying the Bureau of Prisons of any address or telephone number changes
That he or she must contact the Warden each month to confirm the request, subject to the Warden's discretion, unless an emergency requires otherwise
That he or she must pay the cost of each notice sent by the institution
questions.rationale: Staff "shall advise each approved victim and/or witness of that person's responsibility for notifying the Bureau of Prisons of any address and/or telephone number changes."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.21 (Payment of postage), then answer the question.

(b) Writing paper and envelopes are provided at no cost to the inmate. Inmates who use their own envelopes must place a return address on the envelope (see § 540.12(d)).

What does the excerpt say about writing paper and envelopes?
options: They are provided at no cost to the inmate, and an inmate who uses his own envelopes must place a return address on them
They are provided at a reduced cost, and an inmate who uses his own envelopes must pay a fee
They are sold in the commissary only, and an inmate who uses his own envelopes needs a staff signature
They are provided at no cost only for legal mail, and an inmate who uses his own envelopes needs approval, during normal operating hours
questions.rationale: "Writing paper and envelopes are provided at no cost to the inmate. Inmates who use their own envelopes must place a return address on the envelope."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.25 (Change of address and forwarding of mail for inmates), then answer the question.

(b) Inmates are responsible for informing their correspondents of a change of address.
(c) Postage for mailing change of address cards is paid by the inmate.

Who is responsible for informing correspondents of a change of address, and who pays the postage for change of address cards?
options: The inmate is responsible for informing correspondents, and the inmate pays the postage
The inmate is responsible for informing correspondents, and the institution pays the postage
The institution is responsible for informing correspondents, and the institution pays the postage
The Warden is responsible for informing correspondents, and the inmate pays the postage
questions.rationale: "Inmates are responsible for informing their correspondents of a change of address. Postage for mailing change of address cards is paid by the inmate."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.20 (Purpose and scope), then answer the question.

This rule on application of restraints does not restrict the use of restraints in situations requiring precautionary restraints, particularly in the movement or transfer of inmates (e.g., the use of handcuffs in moving inmates to and from a cell in detention, escorting an inmate to a Special Housing Unit pending investigation, etc.).

Which conclusion is best supported by the final paragraph of the excerpt?
options: Restraints may be used as a precaution during movement even when the inmate has not been violent
The rule on restraints applies only to inmates who are housed in a detention unit
Handcuffs may be used on inmates in transit only with the Warden's written approval
Restraints may be used during movement only on inmates who have already been violent, during normal operating hours
questions.rationale: The paragraph says the rule "does not restrict the use of restraints in situations requiring precautionary restraints, particularly in the movement or transfer of inmates." Precaution does not require prior violence.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.21 (Types of force), then answer the question.

(a) Immediate use of force. Staff may immediately use force and/or apply restraints when the behavior described in § 552.20 constitutes an immediate, serious threat to the inmate, staff, others, property, or to institution security and good order.
(b) Calculated use of force and/or application of restraints. This occurs in situations where an inmate is in an area that can be isolated (e.g., a locked cell, a range) and where there is no immediate, direct threat to the inmate or others. When there is time for the calculated use of force or application of restraints, staff must first determine if the situation can be resolved without resorting to force (see § 552.23).

An inmate locked in a cell refuses to come out for a transfer. He is not threatening anyone, and no one is in danger. If force later becomes necessary, which type does the excerpt point to?
options: Calculated use of force, because the inmate is in an area that can be isolated and poses no immediate threat
Neither type applies, because force may never be used on an inmate who is locked in a cell
Immediate use of force, because refusing a transfer is an immediate, serious threat to security
Immediate use of force, because the inmate is in a cell that can be isolated from the unit
questions.rationale: A locked cell is the excerpt's own example of an area that can be isolated, and no immediate, direct threat exists. That fits calculated use of force, which allows time to look for a non-force resolution first.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.21 (Types of force), then answer the question.

(d) Exceptions. Any exception to this rule is prohibited, except where the facts and circumstances known to the staff member would warrant a person using sound correctional judgment to reasonably believe other action is necessary (as a last resort) to prevent serious physical injury, or serious property damage which would immediately endanger the safety of staff, inmates, or others.

According to the last paragraph, an exception to the rule is allowed only when
options: a supervisor verbally approves the exception and the action is needed to keep order in the housing unit, pending review by the appropriate official
a reasonable corrections professional would see other action as a last resort to prevent serious injury or immediately dangerous property damage
the inmate has a history of violence and staff believe other action will protect them from future harm
other inmates are watching the incident and staff believe a show of force will prevent a disturbance
questions.rationale: Exceptions are prohibited "except where the facts and circumstances known to the staff member would warrant a person using sound correctional judgment to reasonably believe other action is necessary (as a last resort)" to prevent serious physical injury or serious, immediately endangering property damage.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.22 (Principles governing the use of force and application of restraints), then answer the question.

(g) Except when the immediate use of restraints is required for control of the inmate, staff may apply restraints to, or continue the use of progressive restraints on, an inmate while in a cell in administrative detention or disciplinary segregation only with approval of the Warden or designee.

When may staff apply restraints to an inmate in an administrative detention or disciplinary segregation cell without the approval of the Warden or designee?
options: When the immediate use of restraints is required for control of the inmate
When the inmate has been in the cell more than 72 hours and has become agitated
When the inmate has refused a meal and a nurse has recommended added restraint
When another inmate has complained that he feels unsafe near this particular inmate
questions.rationale: Approval is required "except when the immediate use of restraints is required for control of the inmate." In that case staff may act first.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.22 (Principles governing the use of force and application of restraints), then answer the question.

(h) Restraint equipment or devices (e.g., handcuffs) may not be used in any of the following ways:
(1) As a method of punishing an inmate.
(2) About an inmate's neck or face, or in any manner which restricts blood circulation or obstructs the inmate's airways.
(3) In a manner that causes unnecessary physical pain or extreme discomfort.
(4) To secure an inmate to a fixed object, such as a cell door or cell grill, except as provided in § 552.24.

An officer handcuffs a calm inmate to a cell door grill for an hour so he will "think about what he did." Which part of the excerpt does this violate?
options: Restraints may not be used to punish an inmate or to secure an inmate to a fixed object such as a cell door
Restraints must be removed within fifteen minutes of the time they are applied to the inmate
Restraints may be used only on inmates who are being held in a Special Housing Unit cell
Restraints may not be used on any inmate unless the Warden is physically present in the housing unit, unless local procedures say otherwise
questions.rationale: Restraint equipment may not be used "as a method of punishing an inmate" or "to secure an inmate to a fixed object, such as a cell door or cell grill" except as provided in § 552.24. The inmate was calm, so no safety purpose applied.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.22 (Principles governing the use of force and application of restraints), then answer the question.

(a) Staff ordinarily shall first attempt to gain the inmate's voluntary cooperation before using force.
(b) Force may not be used to punish an inmate.
(c) Staff shall use only that amount of force necessary to gain control of the inmate. Situations when an appropriate amount of force may be warranted include, but are not limited to:

Which conclusion is best supported by paragraphs (a) through (c)?
options: Force should be used at the highest level available to prevent further problems
Force is the preferred first step whenever an inmate disobeys an order
Staff are free to decide how much force to use based on their own experience
The purpose of force is to gain control and protect people, not to discipline
questions.rationale: Staff must first seek voluntary cooperation, may never use force as punishment, and may use "only that amount of force necessary to gain control of the inmate." Together these show force serves control and protection.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.23 (Confrontation avoidance procedures), then answer the question.

Prior to any calculated use of force, the ranking custodial official (ordinarily the Captain or shift Lieutenant), a designated mental health professional, and others shall confer and gather pertinent information about the inmate and the immediate situation. Based on their assessment of that information, they shall identify a staff member(s) to attempt to obtain the inmate's voluntary cooperation and, using the knowledge they have gained about the inmate and the incident, determine if use of force is necessary.

What is the most likely purpose of including a mental health professional in the conference?
options: To approve the use of force on behalf of the Warden before the team assembles
To testify at a later disciplinary hearing about the inmate's state of mind
To help staff understand the inmate and decide whether force can be avoided
To select which type of restraints will be applied once the team enters the area
questions.rationale: The conference gathers "pertinent information about the inmate" so staff can try to obtain cooperation and decide whether force is necessary. A mental health professional's knowledge supports that goal.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.24 (Use of four-point restraints), then answer the question.

(b) Inmates will be dressed in clothing appropriate to the temperature.
