(c) Beds will be covered with a mattress, and a blanket/sheet will be provided to the inmate.
(d) Staff shall check the inmate at least every 15 minutes, both to ensure that the restraints are not hampering circulation and for the general welfare of the inmate. When an inmate is restrained to a bed, staff shall periodically rotate the inmate's position to avoid soreness or stiffness.

Select ALL of the requirements the excerpt lists for an inmate in four-point restraints.
options: A mattress covering the bed, with a blanket or sheet provided
Removal of all clothing to prevent self-harm
Clothing appropriate to the temperature
Isolation from all medical personnel until restraints are removed
A staff check at least every 15 minutes
questions.rationale: The listed requirements include clothing appropriate to the temperature, a mattress with a blanket or sheet, and checks at least every 15 minutes. Removing all clothing or keeping medical staff away is the opposite of the excerpt's welfare provisions.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.24 (Use of four-point restraints), then answer the question.

(f) When the inmate is placed in four-point restraints, qualified health personnel shall initially assess the inmate to ensure appropriate breathing and response (physical or verbal). Staff shall also ensure that the restraints have not restricted or impaired the inmate's circulation. When inmates are so restrained, qualified health personnel ordinarily are to visit the inmate at least twice during each eight hour shift. Use of four-point restraints beyond eight hours requires the supervision of qualified health personnel. Mental health and qualified health personnel may be asked for advice regarding the appropriate time for removal of the restraints.

Why does the excerpt require qualified health personnel to assess an inmate when he is first placed in four-point restraints?
options: To confirm the inmate understands why the restraints were applied and how long they will last
To decide whether the inmate should be referred for discipline once he has calmed down
To determine whether the inmate needs to be moved to a different housing unit afterward
To confirm the inmate is breathing and responding and that circulation is not restricted
questions.rationale: Health personnel "shall initially assess the inmate to ensure appropriate breathing and response (physical or verbal)" and that the restraints have not restricted or impaired circulation. The purpose is safety.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.24 (Use of four-point restraints), then answer the question.

(e) A review of the inmate's placement in four-point restraints shall be made by a Lieutenant every two hours to determine if the use of restraints has had the required calming effect and so that the inmate may be released from these restraints (completely or to lesser restraints) as soon as possible. At every two-hour review, the inmate will be afforded the opportunity to use the toilet, unless the inmate is continuing to actively resist or becomes violent while being released from the restraints for this purpose.
(f) When the inmate is placed in four-point restraints, qualified health personnel shall initially assess the inmate to ensure appropriate breathing and response (physical or verbal). Staff shall also ensure that the restraints have not restricted or impaired the inmate's circulation. When inmates are so restrained, qualified health personnel ordinarily are to visit the inmate at least twice during each eight hour shift. Use of four-point restraints beyond eight hours requires the supervision of qualified health personnel. Mental health and qualified health personnel may be asked for advice regarding the appropriate time for removal of the restraints.
(g) When it is necessary to restrain an inmate for longer than eight hours, the Warden (or designee) or institution administrative duty officer shall notify the Regional Director or Regional Duty Officer by telephone.

An inmate has been in four-point restraints for nine hours. Based on the excerpt, which statement must be true?
options: Qualified health personnel are supervising the restraint, and the Regional Director or Duty Officer has been notified by telephone
The Regional Director has traveled to the institution and personally examined the inmate
A Lieutenant reviewed the placement at the start, and no further reviews are needed after eight hours, according to the institution's local guidelines
The inmate has been moved to hard restraints, and the Regional Director has been notified by mail
questions.rationale: Use beyond eight hours "requires the supervision of qualified health personnel," and restraint "longer than eight hours" requires telephone notice to the Regional Director or Regional Duty Officer. Lieutenant reviews continue every two hours.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.25 (Use of less-than-lethal weapons, including chemical agents), then answer the question.

(b) The Warden may delegate the authority under this regulation to one or more supervisors on duty and physically present, but not below the position of Lieutenant.

To whom may the Warden delegate the authority to authorize less-than-lethal weapons?
options: One or more supervisors on duty and physically present, not below the position of Captain
Any supervisor on duty who can be reached by telephone, not below the position of Lieutenant
One or more supervisors on duty and physically present, not below the position of Lieutenant
Any correctional officer on duty who has completed use-of-force training
questions.rationale: Paragraph (b) allows delegation "to one or more supervisors on duty and physically present, but not below the position of Lieutenant."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.25 (Use of less-than-lethal weapons, including chemical agents), then answer the question.

(b) The Warden may delegate the authority under this regulation to one or more supervisors on duty and physically present, but not below the position of Lieutenant.

The Warden is away from the institution during a barricade incident. Which of these staff members could be delegated the authority to authorize less-than-lethal weapons?
options: A counselor who has been trained in chemical agents
A Lieutenant who is off duty and reachable by phone
A Senior Officer who is stationed in the control center
A Captain who is on duty and physically present
questions.rationale: Delegation is limited to supervisors "on duty and physically present, but not below the position of Lieutenant." A Captain who is on duty and present qualifies; an off-duty Lieutenant, a Senior Officer, or a counselor does not.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.26 (Medical attention in use of force and application of restraints incidents), then answer the question.

(a) In immediate use of force situations, staff shall seek the assistance of mental health or qualified health personnel upon gaining physical control of the inmate. When possible, staff shall seek such assistance at the onset of the violent behavior. In calculated use of force situations, the use of force team leader shall seek the guidance of qualified health personnel (based upon a review of the inmate's medical record) to identify physical or mental problems. When mental health staff or qualified health personnel determine that an inmate requires continuing care, and particularly when the inmate to be restrained is pregnant, the deciding staff shall assume responsibility for the inmate's care, to include possible admission to the institution hospital, or, in the case of a pregnant inmate, restraining her in other than face down four-point restraints.

In a calculated use of force, what does the use of force team leader review in order to identify physical or mental problems?
options: The inmate's visiting list
The inmate's commissary purchases
The inmate's medical record
The inmate's work performance reports
questions.rationale: The team leader "shall seek the guidance of qualified health personnel (based upon a review of the inmate's medical record) to identify physical or mental problems."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.26 (Medical attention in use of force and application of restraints incidents), then answer the question.

(a) In immediate use of force situations, staff shall seek the assistance of mental health or qualified health personnel upon gaining physical control of the inmate. When possible, staff shall seek such assistance at the onset of the violent behavior. In calculated use of force situations, the use of force team leader shall seek the guidance of qualified health personnel (based upon a review of the inmate's medical record) to identify physical or mental problems. When mental health staff or qualified health personnel determine that an inmate requires continuing care, and particularly when the inmate to be restrained is pregnant, the deciding staff shall assume responsibility for the inmate's care, to include possible admission to the institution hospital, or, in the case of a pregnant inmate, restraining her in other than face down four-point restraints.

What does the excerpt say about restraining a pregnant inmate?
options: She may not be restrained under any circumstances
She may be restrained only after a court gives permission
She must be restrained in face down four-point restraints for her own safety
She may be restrained in other than face down four-point restraints
questions.rationale: When the inmate to be restrained is pregnant, the deciding staff assume responsibility for her care, including "restraining her in other than face down four-point restraints."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 553.13 (Procedures for handling contraband), then answer the question.

(ii) The inmate shall have seven days following receipt of the inventory to provide staff with evidence of ownership of the listed items. A claim of ownership may not be accepted for an item made from the unauthorized use of government property. Items obtained from another inmate (for example, through purchase, or as a gift) without staff authorization may be considered nuisance contraband for which a claim of ownership is ordinarily not accepted.

Why would a claim of ownership ordinarily not be accepted for an item an inmate got from another inmate without staff authorization?
options: Such an item is always hard contraband and must be destroyed
Such an item has always been government property
Such an item is not covered by the inventory process
Such an item may be treated as nuisance contraband
questions.rationale: The excerpt says items obtained from another inmate "without staff authorization may be considered nuisance contraband for which a claim of ownership is ordinarily not accepted."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 553.13 (Procedures for handling contraband), then answer the question.

(iii) If the inmate establishes ownership, but the item is identified as contraband, staff shall mail such items (other than hard contraband), at the inmate's expense, to a destination of the inmate's choice. The Warden or designee may authorize the institution to pay the cost of such mailings when the item had not been altered and originally had been permitted for admission to the institution or had been purchased from the commissary, or where the inmate has insufficient funds and no likelihood of new funds being received. Where the inmate has established ownership of a contraband item, but is unwilling, although financially able to pay postage as required, or refuses to provide a mailing address for return of the property, the property is to be disposed of through approved methods, including destruction of the property.

An inmate proves he owns an altered radio that is now contraband but not hard contraband. What does the excerpt say staff shall do?
options: Mail the item, at the inmate's expense, to a destination of his choice
Hold the item in storage, at the inmate's expense, until his release
Destroy the item immediately, at the inmate's expense, and document it
Return the item to the inmate's cell, at the Warden's expense
questions.rationale: If ownership is established but the item is contraband, "staff shall mail such items (other than hard contraband), at the inmate's expense, to a destination of the inmate's choice," unless the Warden approves paying the cost.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 553.13 (Procedures for handling contraband), then answer the question.

(c) Staff shall retain items of hard contraband for disciplinary action or prosecution or both. The contraband items may be delivered to law enforcement personnel for official use. When it is determined that the item is not needed for criminal prosecution, the hard contraband shall be destroyed as provided in paragraph (b)(2)(v) of this section. Written documentation of the destruction shall be maintained for at least two years.

For how long must written documentation of the destruction of hard contraband be maintained?
options: At least thirty days
At least six months
At least two years
Only until the next audit
questions.rationale: Paragraph (c) ends "Written documentation of the destruction shall be maintained for at least two years."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 553.13 (Procedures for handling contraband), then answer the question.

(d) Staff may not allow an inmate to possess funds in excess of established institutional limits. Staff shall deliver to the cashier any cash or negotiable instruments found in an inmate's possession which exceed the institution's allowable limits. Funds determined to be contraband shall be confiscated for crediting to the U.S. Treasury.
(1) Where disciplinary action against the inmate is appropriate, staff shall delay final disposition of the funds until such action (including appeals) is completed.
(2) Prior to a decision on the disposition of funds, staff shall allow the inmate a reasonable amount of time to prove ownership.

An officer finds cash in an inmate's locker that exceeds the institution's limit, and a disciplinary action is pending. What does the excerpt direct?
options: Hold the cash in the officer's desk until the end of the shift, then transfer it to the Captain for review
Credit the cash to the U.S. Treasury right away, since the inmate was over the limit, and then begin discipline
Return the cash to the inmate once he has signed a receipt and has been warned about the institution's limit
Deliver the cash to the cashier, delay final disposition until discipline and appeals end, and allow time to prove ownership
questions.rationale: Staff "shall deliver to the cashier any cash or negotiable instruments found in an inmate's possession which exceed the institution's allowable limits," delay final disposition until discipline and appeals are completed, and allow the inmate a reasonable time to prove ownership.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 553.11 (Limitations on inmate personal property), then answer the question.

(e) Hobbycraft materials. Staff shall limit an inmate's hobby shop projects within the cell or living area to those projects which the inmate may store in designated personal property containers. Staff may make an exception for an item (for example, a painting) where size would prohibit placing the item in a locker. This exception is made with the understanding that the placement of the item is at the inmate's own risk. Staff shall require that hobby shop items be removed from the living area when completed, and be disposed of in accordance with the provisions of part 544, subpart D, of this chapter.

Why does the excerpt allow an exception for a large item such as a painting that cannot fit in a locker?
options: Large items are always hard contraband unless the Warden has approved them in advance
Size alone should not prohibit a hobby project, but the inmate keeps it at his own risk
Large items are allowed only if they are stored in the hobby shop until the project is finished
Size should not prohibit a hobby project, and staff become responsible for the item once it is placed
questions.rationale: Staff may make an exception "where size would prohibit placing the item in a locker," but "with the understanding that the placement of the item is at the inmate's own risk."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.11 (Searches of inmates), then answer the question.

(2) Staff of the same sex as the inmate shall make the search, except where circumstances are such that delay would mean the likely loss of contraband. Where staff of the opposite sex makes a visual search, staff shall document the reasons for the opposite sex search in the inmate's central file.

When may a visual search be made by staff of the opposite sex?
options: When same-sex staff are not on duty in the unit, and the reasons are noted on the shift log, during normal operating hours
When the inmate agrees in writing, and the reasons are documented in the central file
When delay would mean the likely loss of contraband, and the reasons are documented in the central file
When a supervisor is present to observe, and the search is completed within ten minutes
questions.rationale: Same-sex staff make the search "except where circumstances are such that delay would mean the likely loss of contraband," and staff "shall document the reasons for the opposite sex search in the inmate's central file."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.11 (Searches of inmates), then answer the question.

(d) Digital or simple instrument search—inspection for contraband or any other foreign item in a body cavity of an inmate by use of fingers or simple instruments, such as an otoscope, tongue blade, short nasal speculum, and simple forceps. A digital or simple instrument search may be conducted only by designated qualified health personnel (for example, physicians, physician assistants, and nurses) upon approval of the Warden or Acting Warden and only if the Warden or Acting Warden has reasonable belief that an inmate is concealing contraband in or on his person. If located, the contraband or foreign item may be removed immediately by medical staff if such removal can easily be effected by use of fingers or the simple instruments referred to above. Staff shall document all digital and simple instrument searches and the reasons for the searches in the inmate's central file.
(1) Staff shall solicit the inmate's written consent prior to conducting a digital or simple instrument search. However, the inmate's consent is not required.
(2) Staff may not conduct a digital or simple instrument search if it is likely to result in physical injury to the inmate.

Who may conduct a digital or simple instrument search, and with whose approval?
options: Any trained correctional officer, with the approval of the Warden or Acting Warden
Designated qualified health personnel, with the approval of the Captain or shift Lieutenant
The inmate's case manager, with the approval of the Segregation Review Official
Designated qualified health personnel, with the approval of the Warden or Acting Warden
questions.rationale: A digital or simple instrument search "may be conducted only by designated qualified health personnel (for example, physicians, physician assistants, and nurses) upon approval of the Warden or Acting Warden."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.11 (Searches of inmates), then answer the question.

(1) Staff shall solicit the inmate's written consent prior to conducting a digital or simple instrument search. However, the inmate's consent is not required.
(2) Staff may not conduct a digital or simple instrument search if it is likely to result in physical injury to the inmate.

Which statement about consent for a digital or simple instrument search is supported by the excerpt?
options: Staff must ask for written consent, but the search may proceed without it
The search may proceed only if the inmate signs a consent form, during normal operating hours
Consent is required only for pat searches
Staff must never ask the inmate about the search
questions.rationale: Staff "shall solicit the inmate's written consent prior to conducting" the search, but "the inmate's consent is not required." The search is not allowed if it is likely to result in physical injury.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.12 (Close observation), then answer the question.

(a) The length of close observation status will be determined on an individual basis. Ordinarily, the Captain, in consultation with qualified health personnel, shall determine when termination is appropriate. The status of an inmate under close observation for as long as three days must be reviewed by the Segregation Review Official according to the provisions in § 541.22(c) of this chapter, and the initial SRO review conducted within three work days shall be a formal hearing. Maintaining an inmate under close observation beyond seven days requires approval of the Warden, who makes this decision in consultation with the Captain and qualified health personnel.

Who must approve maintaining an inmate under close observation beyond seven days?
options: The Captain, in consultation with the Warden and qualified health personnel
The Warden, in consultation with the unit manager and the psychology staff
The Warden, in consultation with the Captain and qualified health personnel
The Segregation Review Official, in consultation with the Warden and the Captain
questions.rationale: "Maintaining an inmate under close observation beyond seven days requires approval of the Warden, who makes this decision in consultation with the Captain and qualified health personnel."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.12 (Close observation), then answer the question.

(a) The length of close observation status will be determined on an individual basis. Ordinarily, the Captain, in consultation with qualified health personnel, shall determine when termination is appropriate. The status of an inmate under close observation for as long as three days must be reviewed by the Segregation Review Official according to the provisions in § 541.22(c) of this chapter, and the initial SRO review conducted within three work days shall be a formal hearing. Maintaining an inmate under close observation beyond seven days requires approval of the Warden, who makes this decision in consultation with the Captain and qualified health personnel.

What happens when an inmate has been under close observation for as long as three days?
options: The Warden must review the status, and the first review within three work days is an informal visit
The Captain must review the status, and the first review within seven work days is a formal hearing
The Segregation Review Official must review the status, and the first review within three work days is a written report
The Segregation Review Official must review the status, and the first review within three work days is a formal hearing
questions.rationale: "The status of an inmate under close observation for as long as three days must be reviewed by the Segregation Review Official," and the initial review within three work days "shall be a formal hearing."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.12 (Close observation), then answer the question.

(5) When the inmate is lying on a bed, the inmate shall be required to lie on top of the mattress in full view, weather and room temperature permitting. When necessary for the inmate to use cover, hands must remain visible at all times so that staff can observe any attempt to move contraband.

Why must the inmate's hands remain visible when he uses a cover on the bed?
options: So staff can make sure the inmate is awake for the next count
So staff can confirm the inmate is warm enough to sleep
So staff can observe any attempt to move contraband
So staff can verify that the inmate has not harmed himself
questions.rationale: Hands must remain visible "so that staff can observe any attempt to move contraband." The condition supports the purpose of the watch.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.12 (Close observation), then answer the question.

(7) The inmate is to be served the same meals as those served to the general population, unless medically contraindicated.
(8) No medications may be given to the inmate except for those prescribed and given by hospital personnel. No laxatives may be given except natural laxatives, i.e., coffee, prune juice, etc.
(9) When the inmate needs to urinate and/or defecate, the inmate will be furnished an empty hospital bed pan.

What does the excerpt say about medications and laxatives for an inmate on close observation?
options: Only medications prescribed by hospital personnel, but any laxative may be given by custody staff
No medication of any kind and no laxative of any kind until the watch has ended
Only natural laxatives such as coffee or prune juice, but medications may be given by the unit officer, based on the information available at the time
Only medications prescribed and given by hospital personnel, and only natural laxatives such as coffee or prune juice
questions.rationale: "No medications may be given to the inmate except for those prescribed and given by hospital personnel. No laxatives may be given except natural laxatives, i.e., coffee, prune juice, etc."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.41 (Program procedures), then answer the question.

(d) Referral. Staff who identify an inmate to be at risk for suicide will have the inmate placed on suicide watch.
(e) Assessment. A psychologist will clinically assess each inmate placed on suicide watch.
(f) Intervention. Upon completion of the clinical assessment, the Program Coordinator or designee will determine the appropriate intervention that best meets the needs of the inmate.

Which sequence matches the program procedures in the excerpt?
options: Staff identify the inmate, the Program Coordinator chooses the intervention, and a psychologist then assesses him once the watch begins
Staff identify the inmate and place him on watch, a psychologist assesses him, then the Program Coordinator or designee chooses the intervention
The Warden places the inmate on watch, staff then identify the risk, and a psychologist chooses the intervention last
A psychologist assesses the inmate first, staff then place him on watch, and the Program Coordinator chooses the intervention
questions.rationale: Referral comes first (staff "will have the inmate placed on suicide watch"), then a psychologist "will clinically assess each inmate," and "upon completion of the clinical assessment" the Program Coordinator or designee determines the intervention.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.42 (Suicide watch conditions), then answer the question.

(b) Observation. (1) Staff or trained inmate observers operating in scheduled shifts are responsible for keeping the inmate under constant observation.
(2) Only the Warden may authorize the use of inmate observers.
(3) Inmate observers are considered to be on an institution work assignment when they are on their scheduled shift.

Who may authorize the use of inmate observers on a suicide watch?
options: The psychologist alone
Any Lieutenant
Only the Warden
The Program Coordinator
questions.rationale: Paragraph (b)(2) states "Only the Warden may authorize the use of inmate observers." Inmate observers are considered to be on a work assignment during their scheduled shift.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.42 (Suicide watch conditions), then answer the question.

(a) Housing. Each institution must have one or more rooms designated specifically for housing an inmate on suicide watch. The designated room must allow staff to maintain adequate control of the inmate without compromising the ability to observe and protect the inmate.

What two goals must the designated suicide watch room balance, according to paragraph (a)?
options: Controlling the inmate adequately and still being able to observe and protect him
Controlling the inmate adequately and still being able to limit the cost to the institution
Observing the inmate closely and still allowing him regular contact with other inmates
Keeping the inmate comfortable and still being able to limit his contact with staff
questions.rationale: The room "must allow staff to maintain adequate control of the inmate without compromising the ability to observe and protect the inmate."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 552.31 (Negotiations), then answer the question.

The Warden is not ordinarily involved directly in the negotiation process. Instead, this responsibility is ordinarily assigned to a team of individuals specifically trained in hostage negotiation techniques.

What does the first sentence suggest about who ordinarily handles negotiation?
options: A specially trained team rather than the Warden
The Warden, supported by a specially trained team
The command center staff rather than a trained team
A specially trained team chosen by the hostage takers
questions.rationale: The Warden "is not ordinarily involved directly in the negotiation process," which is "ordinarily assigned to a team of individuals specifically trained in hostage negotiation techniques."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.3 (Prohibited acts and available sanctions), then answer the question.

(a) Prohibited acts. The list of prohibited acts are divided into four separate categories based on severity: Greatest; High; Moderate; and Low. We describe the prohibited acts in Table 1—Prohibited Acts and Available Sanctions. Aiding, attempting, abetting, or making plans to commit any of the prohibited acts is treated the same as committing the act itself.

Two inmates plan together to commit a prohibited act, but the act is never carried out. Based on the excerpt, how is this treated?
options: It is not a prohibited act, because only completed acts are charged, when staff resources allow, where the circumstances reasonably call for it
As a separate low severity violation, because no harm resulted
The same as committing the act itself, because making plans to commit a prohibited act is treated the same way
As a lesser violation, because the act was never actually committed
questions.rationale: "Aiding, attempting, abetting, or making plans to commit any of the prohibited acts is treated the same as committing the act itself."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.4 (Loss of good conduct sentence credit as a mandatory sanction), then answer the question.

(b) If you are an inmate in one of the above groups and commit a prohibited act, you will lose good conduct sentence credit as a mandatory disciplinary sanction. The amount of good conduct sentence credit you will lose depends on the severity level of the prohibited act(s) committed, as follows:
(1) Greatest Severity Level Offenses. You will lose at least 41 days, or 75% of available credit if less than 54 days are available for the prorated period, for each act committed.
(2) High Severity Level Offenses. You will lose at least 27 days, or 50% of available credit if less than 54 days are available for the prorated period, for each act committed.

For an inmate covered by the mandatory sanction rule, what is the minimum good conduct sentence credit lost for each Greatest severity act?
options: At least 41 days, or 75% of available credit if less than 54 days are available
At least 14 days, or 25% of available credit if less than 54 days are available
At least 7 days, or 12.5% of available credit if less than 54 days are available
At least 27 days, or 50% of available credit if less than 54 days are available
questions.rationale: Greatest severity offenses cost "at least 41 days, or 75% of available credit if less than 54 days are available for the prorated period, for each act committed." The other figures belong to High, Moderate, and Low acts.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.4 (Loss of good conduct sentence credit as a mandatory sanction), then answer the question.

(3) Moderate Severity Level Offenses. You will lose at least 14 days, or 25% of available credit if less than 54 days are available for the prorated period, after committing two or more Moderate severity acts during the current year of your good conduct sentence credit availability.
(4) Low Severity Level Offenses. You will lose at least 7 days, or 12.5% of available credit if less than 54 days are available for the prorated period, after committing three or more Low severity acts during the current year of your good conduct sentence credit availability.

What condition must be met before an inmate loses credit for Low severity acts under the mandatory sanction rule?
options: He must commit one Low severity act while serving a disciplinary sanction
He must commit three or more Low severity acts during the current year of credit availability
He must commit two or more Low severity acts during the current year of credit availability
He must commit three or more Low severity acts since entering the institution
questions.rationale: For Low severity offenses, the loss follows "after committing three or more Low severity acts during the current year of your good conduct sentence credit availability." For Moderate acts the number is two.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.5 (Discipline process), then answer the question.

(1) Information: The investigator will specifically inform you:
(A) of the charge(s) against you; and
(B) that you may remain silent at all stages of the discipline process, but that your silence may be used to draw an adverse inference against you at any stage of the process. Your silence alone, however, cannot be the basis for finding you committed the prohibited act(s).

What may the investigator tell the inmate about remaining silent?
options: He may remain silent at all stages, but silence may be used to draw an adverse inference, though silence alone cannot be the basis for finding he committed the act
He may remain silent at all stages, and silence can never be considered in any way
He must answer all questions, and refusal to answer is itself a prohibited act
He may remain silent, and silence alone is enough to find that he committed the act, provided that the action is documented, for the duration of the incident, unless local procedures say otherwise
questions.rationale: The inmate is informed that "you may remain silent at all stages of the discipline process, but that your silence may be used to draw an adverse inference against you at any stage of the process. Your silence alone, however, cannot be the basis for finding you committed the prohibited act(s)."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.5 (Discipline process), then answer the question.

(3) Informally resolving the incident report. The incident report may be informally resolved at any stage of the disciplinary process, except for prohibited acts in the Greatest and High severity levels, or as otherwise required by law or these regulations. If the incident report is informally resolved, it will be removed from your records.

An inmate is charged with a Moderate severity act. Based on the excerpt, what may happen to the incident report?
options: It must be referred to a hearing officer without any informal resolution
It may be informally resolved, but it stays in his records
It may be informally resolved at any stage, and if so it is removed from his records
It may be informally resolved only after the hearing officer's decision
questions.rationale: The report "may be informally resolved at any stage of the disciplinary process, except for prohibited acts in the Greatest and High severity levels," and if resolved informally, "it will be removed from your records."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.6 (Mentally ill inmates), then answer the question.

(b) Responsibility for Conduct. You will not be disciplined for conduct committed when, as the result of a severe mental disease or defect, you were unable to appreciate the nature and quality, or wrongfulness of the act. The UDC or DHO will make this decision based on evidence, including evidence presented by mental health staff.

Under what circumstance will an inmate NOT be disciplined for his conduct?
options: When, as the result of a severe mental disease or defect, he was unable to appreciate the nature, quality, or wrongfulness of the act
When he had been under stress because of a recent change in housing
When he had not been warned about the act by a staff member
When he did not understand the written institution rules at the time of the act, for the duration of the incident, during normal operating hours
questions.rationale: "You will not be disciplined for conduct committed when, as the result of a severe mental disease or defect, you were unable to appreciate the nature and quality, or wrongfulness of the act."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.7 (Unit Discipline Committee (UDC) review of the incident report), then answer the question.

(d) Inmate appearance. You are permitted to appear before the UDC during its review of the incident report, except during UDC deliberations or when your presence would jeopardize institution security, at the UDC's discretion. Also:
(1) You may appear either in person or electronically (for example, by video or telephone conferencing) at the UDC's discretion.
(2) You may waive your appearance before the UDC. If you waive your appearance, the UDC will review the incident report in your absence.
(3) If you escape or are otherwise absent from custody, the UDC will conduct a review in your absence at the institution where you were last confined.

An inmate waives his appearance before the UDC. What happens, according to the excerpt?
options: The review is conducted by the DHO instead
The UDC reviews the incident report in his absence
The review is postponed until he agrees to appear, in most circumstances
The incident report is dismissed
questions.rationale: Paragraph (d)(2): "You may waive your appearance before the UDC. If you waive your appearance, the UDC will review the incident report in your absence."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.7 (Unit Discipline Committee (UDC) review of the incident report), then answer the question.

(f) Sanctions. If you committed a prohibited act or prohibited acts, the UDC can impose any of the available sanctions in Tables 1 and 2 of § 541.3, except loss of good conduct time credit, FSA Time Credits, disciplinary segregation, or monetary fines.

Which sanctions can the UDC NOT impose? Select ALL that apply.
options: Loss of visiting privileges
Loss of good conduct time credit
Monetary fines
Loss of commissary privileges
Disciplinary segregation
questions.rationale: The UDC can impose any available sanction "except loss of good conduct time credit, FSA Time Credits, disciplinary segregation, or monetary fines." Loss of commissary or visiting privileges can be imposed by the UDC.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.7 (Unit Discipline Committee (UDC) review of the incident report), then answer the question.

(e) Evidence. You are entitled to make a statement and present documentary evidence to the UDC on your own behalf. The UDC will consider all evidence presented during its review. The UDC's decision will be based on at least some facts and, if there is conflicting evidence, on the greater weight of the evidence.

What standard does the UDC use if the evidence in the case is conflicting?
options: Proof beyond a reasonable doubt
The statement of the reporting officer
A unanimous vote of the committee
The greater weight of the evidence
questions.rationale: "The UDC's decision will be based on at least some facts and, if there is conflicting evidence, on the greater weight of the evidence."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.8 (Discipline Hearing Officer (DHO) hearing), then answer the question.

(1) How to get a staff representative. You may request the staff representative of your choice, so long as that person was not a victim, witness, investigator, or otherwise significantly involved in the incident. If your request(s) cannot be fulfilled, and you still want a staff representative, the Warden will appoint one. The Warden will also appoint a staff representative if it appears you are unable to adequately represent yourself before the DHO, for example, if you are illiterate or have difficulty understanding the charges against you.

An inmate asks for a staff representative, but the staff member he chose cannot be provided, and he still wants a representative. What will happen?
options: The Warden will appoint a staff representative
The DHO will select a representative from the UDC
The hearing will proceed without a representative
The hearing will be postponed until the chosen staff member is available
questions.rationale: "If your request(s) cannot be fulfilled, and you still want a staff representative, the Warden will appoint one." The Warden will also appoint one if the inmate cannot adequately represent himself, such as when he is illiterate.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.8 (Discipline Hearing Officer (DHO) hearing), then answer the question.

(3) How the staff representative may appear. Your staff representative may appear either in person or electronically (for example, by video or telephone conferencing) at the DHO's discretion. If your staff representative is not available for the scheduled hearing, you may either select another staff representative, request the hearing be postponed for a reasonable amount of time until your staff representative can appear, or proceed without a staff representative.

If an inmate's staff representative is not available on the hearing date, which choice is NOT one the inmate is given?
options: Proceed without a staff representative
Request that the hearing be postponed for a reasonable time
Require the DHO to dismiss the charges
Select another staff representative
questions.rationale: If the representative is unavailable the inmate "may either select another staff representative, request the hearing be postponed for a reasonable amount of time until your staff representative can appear, or proceed without a staff representative." Dismissal of the charges is not an option.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.8 (Discipline Hearing Officer (DHO) hearing), then answer the question.

(2) The DHO will call witnesses who have information directly relevant to the charge(s) and who are reasonably available. However, the DHO need not call witnesses adverse to you if their testimony is adequately summarized in the incident report or other investigation materials.

Which witnesses will the DHO call?
options: Those who have information directly relevant to the charge(s) and who are reasonably available
Every staff member who was on duty at the time of the incident
Only witnesses who agree with the inmate's account
Only witnesses who were not involved in the investigation
questions.rationale: "The DHO will call witnesses who have information directly relevant to the charge(s) and who are reasonably available." The DHO need not call adverse witnesses whose testimony is adequately summarized in the incident report.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.8 (Discipline Hearing Officer (DHO) hearing), then answer the question.

(3) You or your staff representative may request witnesses appear at the hearing to testify on your behalf. Your requested witnesses may not appear if, in the DHO's discretion, they are not reasonably available, their presence at the hearing would jeopardize institution security, or they would present repetitive evidence.

Select ALL of the reasons the excerpt gives for why a requested witness may not appear at the hearing.
options: The witness is not reasonably available
The witness is a friend of the inmate
The witness's presence would jeopardize institution security
The witness would present repetitive evidence
The witness has a prior disciplinary record
questions.rationale: Requested witnesses may not appear if "they are not reasonably available, their presence at the hearing would jeopardize institution security, or they would present repetitive evidence." Friendship or a prior record is not listed.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.8 (Discipline Hearing Officer (DHO) hearing), then answer the question.

(5) Only the DHO may directly question witnesses at the DHO's hearing. Any questions by you or your staff representative must be submitted to the DHO, who will present the question to the witness in his/her discretion.

Who may directly question witnesses at the DHO hearing?
options: The inmate and his staff representative, after the DHO finishes, according to the institution's local guidelines
The Warden and the DHO together
Only the DHO; questions from the inmate or his staff representative are submitted to the DHO
The reporting officer and the inmate, in turn
questions.rationale: "Only the DHO may directly question witnesses at the DHO's hearing. Any questions by you or your staff representative must be submitted to the DHO, who will present the question to the witness in his/her discretion."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.8 (Discipline Hearing Officer (DHO) hearing), then answer the question.

(6) The DHO may consider evidence provided by a confidential informant (CI) that the DHO finds reliable. You will not be informed of the CI's identity. You will be informed of the CI's testimony to the extent it will not jeopardize institution security, at the DHO's discretion.

Which statement about confidential informants (CIs) is supported by the excerpt?
options: The DHO may consider CI evidence only if the CI appears in person, based on the information available at the time
The inmate is always told the CI's identity before the hearing
The DHO may not consider any evidence provided by a CI
The DHO may consider reliable CI evidence, and the inmate is not told the CI's identity
questions.rationale: "The DHO may consider evidence provided by a confidential informant (CI) that the DHO finds reliable. You will not be informed of the CI's identity," though the inmate is told of the CI's testimony to the extent security permits.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.12 (Controls and procedures), then answer the question.

The staff of each institution of the Bureau of Prisons has the authority to open all mail addressed to you before it is delivered to you. “Special Mail” (mail from the President and Vice President of the U.S., attorneys, Members of the U.S. Congress, Embassies and Consulates, the U.S. Department of Justice (excluding the Bureau of Prisons but including U.S. Attorneys), other Federal law enforcement officers, State Attorneys General, Prosecuting Attorneys, Governors, U.S. Courts (including U.S. Probation Officers), and State Courts) may be opened only in your presence to be checked for contraband. This procedure occurs only if the sender is adequately identified on the envelope and the front of the envelope is marked “Special Mail—Open only in the presence of the inmate.” Other mail may be opened and read by the staff. If you do not want your general correspondence opened and read, the Bureau will return it to the Postal Service. This means that you will not receive such mail. You may choose whether you want your general correspondence delivered to you subject to the above conditions, or returned to the Postal Service. Whatever your choice, special mail will be delivered to you, after it is opened in your presence and checked for contraband. You can make your choice by signing part I or part II. Part I—General Correspondence to be Returned to the Postal Service I have read or had read to me the foregoing notice regarding mail. I do not want my general correspondence opened and read. I REQUEST THAT THE BUREAU OF PRISONS RETURN MY GENERAL CORRESPONDENCE TO THE POSTAL SERVICE. I understand that special mail will be delivered to me, after it is opened in my presence and checked for contraband. (Name) (Reg. No.) (Date) Part II—General Correspondence to be Opened, Read, and Delivered I have read or had read to me the foregoing notice regarding mail, I WISH TO RECEIVE MY GENERAL CORRESPONDENCE. I understand that the Bureau of Prisons may open and read my general correspondence if I choose to receive same. I also understand that special mail will be delivered to me, after it is opened in my presence and checked for contraband. (Name) (Reg. No.) (Date) Inmate (Name), (Reg. No.), refused to sign this form. He (she) was advised by me that the Bureau of Prisons retains the authority to open and read all general correspondence. The inmate was also advised that his (her) refusal to sign this form will be interpreted as an indication that he (she) wishes to receive general correspondence subject to the conditions in part II above. Staff Member's Signature Date

Under what conditions will special mail be opened only in the inmate's presence?
options: The sender is a family member and the envelope is marked "Personal and Confidential"
The inmate has requested in writing that all mail be opened in his presence
The Warden has approved the sender in advance and the envelope bears the Warden's initials, after a supervisor has reviewed the matter
The sender is adequately identified on the envelope and the front is marked "Special Mail—Open only in the presence of the inmate"
questions.rationale: Special mail is opened in the inmate's presence "only if the sender is adequately identified on the envelope and the front of the envelope is marked 'Special Mail—Open only in the presence of the inmate.'"

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.13 (Notification of rejections), then answer the question.

When correspondence is rejected, the Warden shall notify the sender in writing of the rejection and the reasons for the rejection. The Warden shall also give notice that the sender may appeal the rejection. The Warden shall also notify an inmate of the rejection of any letter addressed to that inmate, along with the reasons for the rejection and shall notify the inmate of the right to appeal the rejection. The Warden shall refer an appeal to an official other than the one who originally disapproved the correspondence. The Warden shall return rejected correspondence to the sender unless the correspondence includes plans for or discussion of commission of a crime or evidence of a crime, in which case there is no need to return the correspondence or give notice of the rejection, and the correspondence should be referred to appropriate law enforcement authorities. Also, contraband need not be returned to the sender.

When correspondence is rejected, whom must the Warden notify in writing, and of what?
options: The inmate only, of the rejection and the reasons for it
The sender only, and only if the correspondence is returned
The sender, of the rejection and the reasons and the right to appeal
The inmate and the local postmaster, of the rejection and the date, based on the information available at the time
questions.rationale: "The Warden shall notify the sender in writing of the rejection and the reasons for the rejection" and give notice of the right to appeal. The Warden also notifies the inmate of a rejected letter addressed to him.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.13 (Notification of rejections), then answer the question.

When correspondence is rejected, the Warden shall notify the sender in writing of the rejection and the reasons for the rejection. The Warden shall also give notice that the sender may appeal the rejection. The Warden shall also notify an inmate of the rejection of any letter addressed to that inmate, along with the reasons for the rejection and shall notify the inmate of the right to appeal the rejection. The Warden shall refer an appeal to an official other than the one who originally disapproved the correspondence. The Warden shall return rejected correspondence to the sender unless the correspondence includes plans for or discussion of commission of a crime or evidence of a crime, in which case there is no need to return the correspondence or give notice of the rejection, and the correspondence should be referred to appropriate law enforcement authorities. Also, contraband need not be returned to the sender.

When is rejected correspondence NOT required to be returned to the sender?
options: When it was written in a language that the mailroom staff cannot read
When the inmate has asked that it not be returned to the sender
When it was mailed from outside the state in which the institution is located
When it includes plans for or discussion of commission of a crime or evidence of a crime, in which case it is referred to law enforcement
questions.rationale: The Warden returns rejected correspondence "unless the correspondence includes plans for or discussion of commission of a crime or evidence of a crime," in which case it is referred to law enforcement. Contraband also need not be returned.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.13 (Notification of rejections), then answer the question.

When correspondence is rejected, the Warden shall notify the sender in writing of the rejection and the reasons for the rejection. The Warden shall also give notice that the sender may appeal the rejection. The Warden shall also notify an inmate of the rejection of any letter addressed to that inmate, along with the reasons for the rejection and shall notify the inmate of the right to appeal the rejection. The Warden shall refer an appeal to an official other than the one who originally disapproved the correspondence. The Warden shall return rejected correspondence to the sender unless the correspondence includes plans for or discussion of commission of a crime or evidence of a crime, in which case there is no need to return the correspondence or give notice of the rejection, and the correspondence should be referred to appropriate law enforcement authorities. Also, contraband need not be returned to the sender.

Who reviews an appeal of a rejection of correspondence?
options: An official other than the one who originally disapproved the correspondence
The Warden, who may not delegate the review
The postal inspector assigned to the institution's zip code
The same official who originally disapproved the correspondence
questions.rationale: "The Warden shall refer an appeal to an official other than the one who originally disapproved the correspondence."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.14 (General correspondence), then answer the question.

(c)(1) Outgoing mail from a sentenced inmate in a minimum or low security level institution may be sealed by the inmate and, except as provided for in paragraphs (c)(1)(i) through (iv) of this section, is sent out unopened and uninspected. Staff may open a sentenced inmate's outgoing general correspondence:
(i) If there is reason to believe it would interfere with the orderly running of the institution, that it would be threatening to the recipient, or that it would facilitate criminal activity;
(ii) If the inmate is on a restricted correspondence list;
(iii) If the correspondence is between inmates (see § 540.17); or
(iv) If the envelope has an incomplete return address.

A sentenced inmate in a minimum security institution may seal his outgoing general mail. Select ALL of the situations in which staff may open it.
options: The correspondence is between inmates
The letter is longer than two pages
The envelope has an incomplete return address
The inmate is on a restricted correspondence list
The letter is addressed to a relative in another state
questions.rationale: Staff may open outgoing mail if there is reason to believe it would interfere with the institution, threaten the recipient, or facilitate crime; if the inmate is on a restricted list; if it is between inmates; or if the return address is incomplete. Destination and length are not listed.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.14 (General correspondence), then answer the question.

(2) Except for “special mail,” outgoing mail from a sentenced inmate in a medium or high security level institution, or an administrative institution may not be sealed by the inmate and may be read and inspected by staff.

What is the rule for outgoing general mail from a sentenced inmate in a medium or high security institution?
options: It may not be sealed by the inmate and may be read and inspected by staff
It may be sealed by the inmate and is sent out unopened unless there is a reason to open it
It may be sealed by the inmate but may be read by any officer on request
It may not be sent out unless the Warden has approved each letter in writing
questions.rationale: "Except for 'special mail,' outgoing mail from a sentenced inmate in a medium or high security level institution, or an administrative institution may not be sealed by the inmate and may be read and inspected by staff."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.14 (General correspondence), then answer the question.

(4) Direction of an inmate's business (See § 541.13, Prohibited Act No. 408). An inmate, unless a pre-trial detainee, may not direct a business while confined.
This does not, however, prohibit correspondence necessary to enable an inmate to protect property and funds that were legitimately the inmate's at the time of commitment. Thus, for example, an inmate may correspond about refinancing an existing mortgage or sign insurance papers, but may not operate a mortgage or insurance business while in the institution.

A sentenced inmate wants to write to his bank about refinancing a mortgage on a house he owned before coming to prison. Based on the excerpt, how is this treated?
options: It is prohibited, because an inmate may not write about any business matter, unless local procedures say otherwise, as determined by the shift supervisor
It is allowed only if he agrees to operate a mortgage business
It is allowed, because correspondence to protect property legitimately his at the time of commitment is not prohibited
It is prohibited unless the Warden receives a copy of the bank's reply
questions.rationale: Directing a business is prohibited, "This does not, however, prohibit correspondence necessary to enable an inmate to protect property and funds that were legitimately the inmate's at the time of commitment," such as refinancing an existing mortgage.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.14 (General correspondence), then answer the question.

(8) Contraband. (See § 500.1 of this chapter. A package received without prior authorization by the Warden is considered to be contraband.)

Under paragraph (d)(8), how is a package received without prior authorization by the Warden treated?
options: It is returned only if the sender pays the postage
It is delivered after a staff inspection
It is held for thirty days until the inmate claims it
It is considered to be contraband
questions.rationale: The excerpt says "A package received without prior authorization by the Warden is considered to be contraband."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.18 (Special mail), then answer the question.

(b) In the absence of either adequate identification or the “special mail” marking indicated in paragraph (a) of this section appearing on the envelope, staff may treat the mail as general correspondence and may open, inspect, and read the mail.

An envelope from a law firm arrives with the firm's name but without the "Special Mail—Open only in the presence of the inmate" marking. How may staff treat it?
options: As special mail, which they must open in the inmate's presence
As general correspondence, which they may open, inspect, and read
As rejected mail, which they must return to the sender
As contraband, which they must destroy
questions.rationale: "In the absence of either adequate identification or the 'special mail' marking... staff may treat the mail as general correspondence and may open, inspect, and read the mail."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.18 (Special mail), then answer the question.

(i) An inmate may be placed on restricted special mail status if the Warden, with the concurrence of the Regional Counsel, documents in writing that the special mail either has posed a threat or may pose a threat of physical harm to the recipient (e.g., the inmate has previously used special mail to threaten physical harm to a recipient).
(ii) The Warden shall notify the inmate in writing of the reason the inmate is being placed on restricted special mail status.

What is required to place an inmate on restricted special mail status?
options: The Warden alone documents in writing that the inmate has two disciplinary reports for threats, and tells the inmate the reason in writing
The housing unit officer writes a report that the inmate used special mail improperly, and the Captain tells the inmate the reason in writing
The Warden, with the concurrence of the Regional Counsel, documents in writing that the inmate's mail has been delayed, and tells the inmate the reason verbally

The Warden, with the concurrence of the Regional Counsel, documents in writing that the inmate's special mail has posed or may pose a threat of physical harm to the recipient, and tells the inmate the reason in writing
questions.rationale: An inmate may be placed on restricted special mail status "if the Warden, with the concurrence of the Regional Counsel, documents in writing that the special mail either has posed a threat or may pose a threat of physical harm to the recipient," and the Warden notifies the inmate in writing of the reason.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.18 (Special mail), then answer the question.

(iv) The Warden shall review an inmate's restricted special mail status at least once every 180 days. The inmate is to be notified of the results of this review. An inmate may be removed from restricted special mail status if the Warden determines, with the concurrence of the Regional Counsel, that the special mail does not threaten or pose a threat of physical harm to the intended recipient.

How often must the Warden review an inmate's restricted special mail status?
options: At least once every 180 days
Only when the inmate requests a review
At least once every year
At least once every 30 days
questions.rationale: "The Warden shall review an inmate's restricted special mail status at least once every 180 days. The inmate is to be notified of the results of this review."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.19 (Legal correspondence), then answer the question.

(b) The inmate is responsible for advising any attorney that correspondence will be handled as special mail only if the envelope is marked with the attorney's name and an indication that the person is an attorney, and the front of the envelope is marked “Special Mail—Open only in the presence of the inmate”. Legal mail shall be opened in accordance with special mail procedures (see § 540.18).

Who is responsible for advising an attorney how the envelope must be marked for correspondence to be handled as special mail?
options: The court that appointed the attorney
The Warden
The inmate
The mailroom officer
questions.rationale: "The inmate is responsible for advising any attorney that correspondence will be handled as special mail only if the envelope is marked with the attorney's name and an indication that the person is an attorney."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.19 (Legal correspondence), then answer the question.

(d) In order to send mail to an attorney's assistant or to a legal aid student or assistant, an inmate shall address the mail to the attorney or legal aid supervisor, or the legal organization or firm, to the attention of the student or assistant.

An inmate wants to write to a paralegal who works for his attorney. How must he address the mail?
options: To the Warden, with a note asking that it be forwarded to the paralegal, as determined by the shift supervisor
To the attorney's home address, marked "Special Mail" on the front
To the paralegal alone, with the word "Paralegal" written on the front
To the attorney or the legal organization or firm, to the attention of the assistant
questions.rationale: Paragraph (d): "an inmate shall address the mail to the attorney or legal aid supervisor, or the legal organization or firm, to the attention of the student or assistant."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.41 (Visiting facilities), then answer the question.

(a) Institutions of minimum and low security levels may permit visits beyond the security perimeter, but always under supervision of staff.
(b) Institutions of medium and high security levels, and administrative institutions may establish outdoor visiting, but it will always be inside the security perimeter and always under supervision of staff.

Which statement about outdoor visiting is supported by the excerpt?
options: Only medium and high security institutions may permit outdoor visits, and always inside the perimeter and under staff supervision
All institutions may permit outdoor visits beyond the security perimeter under staff supervision, if a family member requests it in writing

Minimum and low security institutions may permit visits beyond the security perimeter without supervision, while medium and high security institutions may not permit outdoor visits, in most circumstances, pending review by the appropriate official

Minimum and low security institutions may permit visits beyond the security perimeter under staff supervision, while medium and high security institutions may have outdoor visits only inside the perimeter
questions.rationale: Minimum and low security institutions "may permit visits beyond the security perimeter, but always under supervision of staff"; medium and high security institutions "may establish outdoor visiting, but it will always be inside the security perimeter."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.42 (Visiting times), then answer the question.

(b) Consistent with available resources, such as space limitations and staff availability, and with concerns of institution security, the Warden may limit the visiting period. With respect to weekend visits, for example, some or all inmates and visitors may be limited to visiting on Saturday or on Sunday, but not on both days, in order to accommodate the volume of visitors. There is no requirement that every visitor has the opportunity to visit on both days of the weekend, nor that every inmate has the opportunity to have visits on both days of the weekend.

Which conclusion is best supported by paragraph (b)?
options: A Warden may never limit the visiting period, because every visitor must be able to visit on both weekend days
A Warden may limit weekend visits to one day to handle the volume of visitors, and not every visitor must be able to visit both days
A Warden may limit weekend visits to one day only if the Regional Director approves, and every inmate must be able to have visits on both days
A Warden may limit weekend visits to one day only for inmates in segregation, and every other visitor must be able to visit both days
questions.rationale: The Warden "may limit the visiting period," and "There is no requirement that every visitor has the opportunity to visit on both days of the weekend, nor that every inmate has the opportunity to have visits on both days."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.43 (Frequency of visits and number of visitors), then answer the question.

The Warden shall allow each inmate a minimum of four hours visiting time per month. The Warden may limit the length or frequency of visits only to avoid chronic overcrowding. The Warden may establish a guideline for the maximum number of persons who may visit an inmate at one time, to prevent overcrowding in the visiting room or unusual difficulty in supervising a visit. Exceptions may be made to any local guideline when indicated by special circumstances, such as distance the visitor must travel, frequency of the inmate's visits, or health problems of the inmate or visitor.

Select ALL of the special circumstances the excerpt says may justify an exception to a local guideline on the number of visitors.
options: The visitor's occupation
The frequency of the inmate's visits
The health problems of the inmate or visitor
The distance the visitor must travel
The inmate's housing unit assignment
questions.rationale: Exceptions may be made "when indicated by special circumstances, such as distance the visitor must travel, frequency of the inmate's visits, or health problems of the inmate or visitor."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.44 (Regular visitors), then answer the question.

(c) Friends and associates. The visiting privilege ordinarily will be extended to friends and associates having an established relationship with the inmate prior to confinement, unless such visits could reasonably create a threat to the security and good order of the institution. Exceptions to the prior relationship rule may be made, particularly for inmates without other visitors, when it is shown that the proposed visitor is reliable and poses no threat to the security or good order of the institution.

What does the excerpt say about friends and associates as visitors?
options: The privilege ordinarily goes to anyone the inmate names who is over the age of 21, unless a visit could reasonably threaten security
The privilege ordinarily goes to those the inmate met after confinement, unless the chaplain objects to the visit
The privilege ordinarily goes to those with an established relationship before confinement, unless a visit could reasonably threaten security and good order
The privilege ordinarily goes to those with an established relationship before confinement, unless the inmate's family objects in writing, unless local procedures say otherwise
questions.rationale: "The visiting privilege ordinarily will be extended to friends and associates having an established relationship with the inmate prior to confinement, unless such visits could reasonably create a threat to the security and good order of the institution."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.44 (Regular visitors), then answer the question.

(d) Persons with prior criminal convictions. The existence of a criminal conviction alone does not preclude visits. Staff shall give consideration to the nature, extent and recentness of convictions, as weighed against the security considerations of the institution. Specific approval of the Warden may be required before such visits take place.

A proposed visitor has a prior criminal conviction. Based on the excerpt, how should staff treat the request?
options: The conviction is not considered at all, and the visit is approved if the inmate and visitor are related
The conviction precludes a visit unless the offense was a misdemeanor, in which case staff must approve it in writing
The conviction automatically precludes a visit until the visitor has been free of supervision for at least five years
The conviction alone does not preclude a visit; staff weigh the nature, extent, and recentness of the conviction against security considerations
questions.rationale: "The existence of a criminal conviction alone does not preclude visits. Staff shall give consideration to the nature, extent and recentness of convictions, as weighed against the security considerations of the institution."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.45 (Qualification as special visitor), then answer the question.

(b) Consular visitors. When it has been determined that an inmate is a citizen of a foreign country, the Warden must permit the consular representative of that country to visit on matters of legitimate business. The Warden may not withhold this privilege even though the inmate is in disciplinary status. The requirement for the existence of an established relationship prior to confinement does not apply to consular visitors.

An inmate who is a citizen of another country is in disciplinary status. His country's consular representative asks to visit on legitimate business. What does the excerpt require?
options: The Warden may deny the visit until the disciplinary sanction has ended
The Warden must refer the request to the Regional Director for a decision
The Warden must permit the visit and may not withhold the privilege because the inmate is in disciplinary status
The Warden may permit the visit only if the inmate has a prior relationship with the representative
questions.rationale: "The Warden must permit the consular representative of that country to visit on matters of legitimate business. The Warden may not withhold this privilege even though the inmate is in disciplinary status."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.45 (Qualification as special visitor), then answer the question.

(c) Representatives of community groups. The Warden may approve visits on a recurring basis to representatives from community groups (for example, civic, volunteer, or religious organizations) who are acting in their official capacity. These visits may be for the purpose of meeting with an individual inmate or with a group of inmates. The requirement for the existence of an established relationship prior to confinement for visitors does not apply to representatives of community groups.
(d) Clergy, former or prospective employers, sponsors, and parole advisors. Visitors in this category ordinarily provide assistance in release planning, counseling, and discussion of family problems. The requirement for the existence of an established relationship prior to confinement for visitors does not apply to visitors in this category.

Which of the following visitors is NOT described as exempt from the established-relationship requirement?
options: A prospective employer or parole advisor
A member of the clergy
A representative of a community group acting in an official capacity, where the circumstances reasonably call for it
A friend whom the inmate met only after being admitted and wants as a regular visitor
questions.rationale: The requirement for an established relationship prior to confinement does not apply to consular visitors, community group representatives, or clergy, employers, sponsors, and parole advisors. Regular friends and associates ordinarily need that relationship.

options: The composition of the inmate population
The number and placement of supervisory staff
Any findings of inadequacy from internal or external oversight bodies
The commissary prices charged to inmates
The number of visitors who arrive on weekends
questions.rationale: Factors include findings of inadequacy from oversight bodies, the composition of the inmate population, the number and placement of supervisory staff, physical plant blind-spots, and programs on a particular shift. Commissary prices and visitor counts are not listed.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.13 (Supervision and monitoring), then answer the question.

(d) Each agency operating a facility shall implement a policy and practice of having intermediate-level or higher-level supervisors conduct and document unannounced rounds to identify and deter staff sexual abuse and sexual harassment. Such policy and practice shall be implemented for night shifts as well as day shifts. Each agency shall have a policy to prohibit staff from alerting other staff members that these supervisory rounds are occurring, unless such announcement is related to the legitimate operational functions of the facility.

A supervisor conducts an unannounced round on the night shift. Another officer radios a warning to staff on the unit so they will be "ready." Based on the excerpt, how is this treated?
options: It is prohibited, because staff may not alert other staff that supervisory rounds are occurring unless it relates to legitimate operational functions
It is prohibited only if the supervisor has not filed a written round plan
It is permitted, because staff are required to announce all supervisory rounds
It is permitted, because the warning applies only to day shift rounds
questions.rationale: Agencies must "have a policy to prohibit staff from alerting other staff members that these supervisory rounds are occurring, unless such announcement is related to the legitimate operational functions of the facility." The policy applies to night shifts as well as day shifts.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.15 (Limits to cross-gender viewing and searches), then answer the question.

(d) The facility shall implement policies and procedures that enable inmates to shower, perform bodily functions, and change clothing without nonmedical staff of the opposite gender viewing their breasts, buttocks, or genitalia, except in exigent circumstances or when such viewing is incidental to routine cell checks. Such policies and procedures shall require staff of the opposite gender to announce their presence when entering an inmate housing unit.

What must staff of the opposite gender do when entering an inmate housing unit?
options: Request permission from the inmate on duty
Wait for a same-gender officer to enter first
Sign a log kept by the unit manager
Announce their presence
questions.rationale: The required policies "shall require staff of the opposite gender to announce their presence when entering an inmate housing unit."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.15 (Limits to cross-gender viewing and searches), then answer the question.

(e) The facility shall not search or physically examine a transgender or intersex inmate for the sole purpose of determining the inmate's genital status. If the inmate's genital status is unknown, it may be determined during conversations with the inmate, by reviewing medical records, or, if necessary, by learning that information as part of a broader medical examination conducted in private by a medical practitioner.

Under paragraph (e), may a facility search a transgender inmate for the sole purpose of determining his or her genital status?
options: No; the status may be learned from conversations, medical records, or as part of a broader private medical examination
Yes, if a supervisor of the same gender is present for the search
No; the facility may never learn the inmate's genital status in any way
Yes, if the search is documented in the central file within 24 hours
questions.rationale: "The facility shall not search or physically examine a transgender or intersex inmate for the sole purpose of determining the inmate's genital status."
