It may be determined through conversations, medical records, or a broader medical examination conducted in private by a medical practitioner.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.31 (Employee training), then answer the question.

(d) The agency shall document, through employee signature or electronic verification, that employees understand the training they have received.

Why does paragraph (d) require employee signature or electronic verification?
options: To document that employees understand the training they received
To record that employees have been issued the facility's policy manual
To show that employees have been cleared to conduct searches
To confirm that employees have been assigned to a new post
questions.rationale: The agency "shall document, through employee signature or electronic verification, that employees understand the training they have received."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.33 (Inmate education), then answer the question.

(d) The agency shall provide inmate education in formats accessible to all inmates, including those who are limited English proficient, deaf, visually impaired, or otherwise disabled, as well as to inmates who have limited reading skills.

The excerpt requires inmate education to be provided in formats accessible to which inmates?
options: Only inmates who are housed in a unit with a staff member trained in sign language
All inmates except those who have been placed in a Special Housing Unit
Only inmates who request an accessible format in writing before the education session
All inmates, including those who are limited English proficient, deaf, visually impaired, or otherwise disabled, and those with limited reading skills
questions.rationale: "The agency shall provide inmate education in formats accessible to all inmates, including those who are limited English proficient, deaf, visually impaired, or otherwise disabled, as well as to inmates who have limited reading skills."

options: The inmate's own perception of vulnerability
Whether the inmate has a mental, physical, or developmental disability
The inmate's religious affiliation
The age and physical build of the inmate
The length of the inmate's sentence
questions.rationale: The minimum criteria include disability, age, physical build, prior incarceration, criminal history, prior sex offense convictions, perceived identity, prior victimization, the inmate's own perception of vulnerability, and civil immigration detention. Religion and sentence length are not listed.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.41 (Screening for risk of victimization and abusiveness), then answer the question.

(f) Within a set time period, not to exceed 30 days from the inmate's arrival at the facility, the facility will reassess the inmate's risk of victimization or abusiveness based upon any additional, relevant information received by the facility since the intake screening.
(g) An inmate's risk level shall be reassessed when warranted due to a referral, request, incident of sexual abuse, or receipt of additional information that bears on the inmate's risk of sexual victimization or abusiveness.

When must the facility reassess an inmate's risk of victimization or abusiveness after the intake screening?
options: Once each year on the anniversary of arrival, and again whenever the inmate transfers
Only when the inmate asks for a reassessment in writing
Within a set period not to exceed 30 days from arrival, and again when warranted by a referral, request, incident, or new information
Within a set period not to exceed 72 hours from arrival, and only after a substantiated incident, under the direction of the senior officer present
questions.rationale: The facility reassesses "within a set time period, not to exceed 30 days from the inmate's arrival," and reassesses "when warranted due to a referral, request, incident of sexual abuse, or receipt of additional information."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.41 (Screening for risk of victimization and abusiveness), then answer the question.

(h) Inmates may not be disciplined for refusing to answer, or for not disclosing complete information in response to, questions asked pursuant to paragraphs (d)(1), (d)(7), (d)(8), or (d)(9) of this section.

Which statement about inmates who refuse to answer certain screening questions is supported by paragraph (h)?
options: They may be disciplined only if staff already know the true answer
They must be disciplined if they refuse to answer any screening question, subject to the Warden's discretion, provided that the action is documented
They may be disciplined only after being warned a second time
They may not be disciplined for refusing to answer or for not disclosing complete information on those questions
questions.rationale: "Inmates may not be disciplined for refusing to answer, or for not disclosing complete information in response to, questions asked pursuant to paragraphs (d)(1), (d)(7), (d)(8), or (d)(9)."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.41 (Screening for risk of victimization and abusiveness), then answer the question.

(i) The agency shall implement appropriate controls on the dissemination within the facility of responses to questions asked pursuant to this standard in order to ensure that sensitive information is not exploited to the inmate's detriment by staff or other inmates.

What is the most likely reason for the controls on dissemination of screening responses in paragraph (i)?
options: To ensure sensitive information is not exploited to the inmate's detriment by staff or other inmates
To prevent inmates from reading their own screening results
To make sure the responses are available to every officer in the housing unit
To limit the number of screening instruments the facility must keep on file
questions.rationale: The controls exist "in order to ensure that sensitive information is not exploited to the inmate's detriment by staff or other inmates."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.43 (Protective custody), then answer the question.

(a) Inmates at high risk for sexual victimization shall not be placed in involuntary segregated housing unless an assessment of all available alternatives has been made, and a determination has been made that there is no available alternative means of separation from likely abusers. If a facility cannot conduct such an assessment immediately, the facility may hold the inmate in involuntary segregated housing for less than 24 hours while completing the assessment.

A facility wants to place an inmate at high risk for sexual victimization in involuntary segregated housing right away, but cannot complete the alternatives assessment immediately. What does the excerpt allow?
options: Holding the inmate in involuntary segregated housing for 72 hours while the assessment is completed
Holding the inmate in involuntary segregated housing for less than 24 hours while completing the assessment
Holding the inmate in involuntary segregated housing for up to 30 days before the assessment
Holding the inmate in involuntary segregated housing with no time limit if the Warden approves
questions.rationale: If a facility cannot conduct the assessment immediately, it "may hold the inmate in involuntary segregated housing for less than 24 hours while completing the assessment."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.43 (Protective custody), then answer the question.

(c) The facility shall assign such inmates to involuntary segregated housing only until an alternative means of separation from likely abusers can be arranged, and such an assignment shall not ordinarily exceed a period of 30 days.
(e) Every 30 days, the facility shall afford each such inmate a review to determine whether there is a continuing need for separation from the general population.

For how long may involuntary segregated housing ordinarily last for an inmate at high risk of victimization, and how often is it reviewed?
options: Ordinarily not more than 90 days, with a review every 90 days
Ordinarily not more than 72 hours, with a review every 24 hours
Ordinarily not more than 30 days, with a review every 30 days
Ordinarily not more than one year, with a review every six months
questions.rationale: The assignment is "only until an alternative means of separation from likely abusers can be arranged, and such an assignment shall not ordinarily exceed a period of 30 days," and "Every 30 days, the facility shall afford each such inmate a review."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.61 (Staff and agency reporting duties), then answer the question.

(b) Apart from reporting to designated supervisors or officials, staff shall not reveal any information related to a sexual abuse report to anyone other than to the extent necessary, as specified in agency policy, to make treatment, investigation, and other security and management decisions.

Apart from reporting to designated supervisors or officials, to whom may staff reveal information related to a sexual abuse report?
options: To the inmate's family members, with the approval of a shift supervisor, so that they can support the inmate, unless an emergency requires otherwise
To any staff member on the same shift who asks, since all staff may be needed to assist in the response
To other inmates who may have witnessed the incident, so that they can give their own accounts
Only to the extent necessary, as specified in agency policy, to make treatment, investigation, and other security and management decisions
questions.rationale: Staff "shall not reveal any information related to a sexual abuse report to anyone other than to the extent necessary, as specified in agency policy, to make treatment, investigation, and other security and management decisions."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.61 (Staff and agency reporting duties), then answer the question.

(c) Unless otherwise precluded by Federal, State, or local law, medical and mental health practitioners shall be required to report sexual abuse pursuant to paragraph (a) of this section and to inform inmates of the practitioner's duty to report, and the limitations of confidentiality, at the initiation of services.

What must medical and mental health practitioners tell inmates at the start of services?
options: Of the practitioner's duty to report sexual abuse, and the limitations of confidentiality
That the practitioner must receive the Warden's permission before making any report, unless local procedures say otherwise
That all information shared with the practitioner is strictly confidential
That the practitioner will report only if the inmate names the abuser
questions.rationale: Practitioners are required to report and "to inform inmates of the practitioner's duty to report, and the limitations of confidentiality, at the initiation of services."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.61 (Staff and agency reporting duties), then answer the question.

(d) If the alleged victim is under the age of 18 or considered a vulnerable adult under a State or local vulnerable persons statute, the agency shall report the allegation to the designated State or local services agency under applicable mandatory reporting laws.

The alleged victim of a reported sexual abuse is 17 years old. What additional step does the excerpt require?
options: The agency must wait until the victim turns 18 before reporting it
The agency must report the allegation to the designated State or local services agency under applicable mandatory reporting laws
The agency must obtain the victim's parents' written permission before reporting it
The agency must handle the report internally and notify the victim's family by mail
questions.rationale: "If the alleged victim is under the age of 18 or considered a vulnerable adult under a State or local vulnerable persons statute, the agency shall report the allegation to the designated State or local services agency under applicable mandatory reporting laws."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.64 (Staff first responder duties), then answer the question.

(a) Upon learning of an allegation that an inmate was sexually abused, the first security staff member to respond to the report shall be required to:
(1) Separate the alleged victim and abuser;
(2) Preserve and protect any crime scene until appropriate steps can be taken to collect any evidence;
(3) If the abuse occurred within a time period that still allows for the collection of physical evidence, request that the alleged victim not take any actions that could destroy physical evidence, including, as appropriate, washing, brushing teeth, changing clothes, urinating, defecating, smoking, drinking, or eating; and
(4) If the abuse occurred within a time period that still allows for the collection of physical evidence, ensure that the alleged abuser does not take any actions that could destroy physical evidence, including, as appropriate, washing, brushing teeth, changing clothes, urinating, defecating, smoking, drinking, or eating.

Upon learning of an allegation that an inmate was sexually abused, select ALL of the actions the first security staff member to respond must take.
options: Interview the alleged abuser to obtain a written confession
Separate the alleged victim and abuser
Preserve and protect any crime scene until evidence can be collected
Move the alleged victim to the Special Housing Unit for the rest of the shift
Request that the alleged victim not take actions that could destroy physical evidence
questions.rationale: The first security responder must separate the alleged victim and abuser, preserve and protect the crime scene, and request (and ensure for the abuser) that no one takes actions such as washing, changing clothes, or eating that could destroy physical evidence. Interviewing for a confession is an investigator's job.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.64 (Staff first responder duties), then answer the question.

(b) If the first staff responder is not a security staff member, the responder shall be required to request that the alleged victim not take any actions that could destroy physical evidence, and then notify security staff.

The first staff member to respond to a report of sexual abuse is a teacher, not a security staff member. What is the teacher required to do?
options: Interview the alleged victim in the classroom, and then notify security staff
Request that the alleged victim not take any actions that could destroy physical evidence, and then notify security staff
Separate the alleged victim and abuser, and then notify the Warden
Take no action, and wait for the end of the class period before notifying security staff
questions.rationale: "If the first staff responder is not a security staff member, the responder shall be required to request that the alleged victim not take any actions that could destroy physical evidence, and then notify security staff."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.67 (Agency protection against retaliation), then answer the question.

(c) For at least 90 days following a report of sexual abuse, the agency shall monitor the conduct and treatment of inmates or staff who reported the sexual abuse and of inmates who were reported to have suffered sexual abuse to see if there are changes that may suggest possible retaliation by inmates or staff, and shall act promptly to remedy any such retaliation. Items the agency should monitor include any inmate disciplinary reports, housing, or program changes, or negative performance reviews or reassignments of staff. The agency shall continue such monitoring beyond 90 days if the initial monitoring indicates a continuing need.

For how long must the agency monitor those who reported sexual abuse, and those reported to have suffered it, for signs of retaliation?
options: At least 90 days, and longer if the initial monitoring shows a continuing need
At least 30 days, and shorter if no retaliation is reported
At least 180 days, regardless of what the initial monitoring shows
At least one year, unless the inmate is transferred to another facility
questions.rationale: "For at least 90 days following a report of sexual abuse, the agency shall monitor... The agency shall continue such monitoring beyond 90 days if the initial monitoring indicates a continuing need."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.67 (Agency protection against retaliation), then answer the question.

(c) For at least 90 days following a report of sexual abuse, the agency shall monitor the conduct and treatment of inmates or staff who reported the sexual abuse and of inmates who were reported to have suffered sexual abuse to see if there are changes that may suggest possible retaliation by inmates or staff, and shall act promptly to remedy any such retaliation. Items the agency should monitor include any inmate disciplinary reports, housing, or program changes, or negative performance reviews or reassignments of staff. The agency shall continue such monitoring beyond 90 days if the initial monitoring indicates a continuing need.

Select ALL of the items the agency should monitor for signs of retaliation, according to the excerpt.
options: The inmate's commissary spending
Negative performance reviews or reassignments of staff
Housing or program changes
Inmate disciplinary reports
The inmate's weight and sleep patterns
questions.rationale: Items to monitor "include any inmate disciplinary reports, housing, or program changes, or negative performance reviews or reassignments of staff."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.67 (Agency protection against retaliation), then answer the question.

(f) An agency's obligation to monitor shall terminate if the agency determines that the allegation is unfounded.

When does the agency's obligation to monitor for retaliation terminate?
options: Once the alleged abuser is transferred out of the facility
Once the 90-day monitoring period has ended
If the agency determines that the allegation is unfounded
If the person who made the report asks that monitoring stop
questions.rationale: Paragraph (f): "An agency's obligation to monitor shall terminate if the agency determines that the allegation is unfounded."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.82 (Access to emergency medical and mental health services), then answer the question.

(b) If no qualified medical or mental health practitioners are on duty at the time a report of recent abuse is made, security staff first responders shall take preliminary steps to protect the victim pursuant to § 115.62 and shall immediately notify the appropriate medical and mental health practitioners.

A report of recent abuse is made at night, when no qualified medical or mental health practitioners are on duty. What must security staff first responders do?
options: Examine the victim themselves and write a medical report
Take preliminary steps to protect the victim and immediately notify the appropriate medical and mental health practitioners
Wait until the morning shift arrives and then notify medical staff, with the approval of a supervisor on duty, as determined by the shift supervisor
Refer the victim to the PREA coordinator by mail
questions.rationale: "If no qualified medical or mental health practitioners are on duty at the time a report of recent abuse is made, security staff first responders shall take preliminary steps to protect the victim pursuant to § 115.62 and shall immediately notify the appropriate medical and mental health practitioners."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.86 (Sexual abuse incident reviews), then answer the question.

(c) The review team shall include upper-level management officials, with input from line supervisors, investigators, and medical or mental health practitioners.

Who is included on the incident review team?
options: Investigators only, with input from the alleged victim's family
The Warden only, with input from the agency's legal counsel
Line supervisors only, with input from the inmates who were involved, after a supervisor has reviewed the matter, during normal operating hours
Upper-level management officials, with input from line supervisors, investigators, and medical or mental health practitioners
questions.rationale: "The review team shall include upper-level management officials, with input from line supervisors, investigators, and medical or mental health practitioners."

options: Examine the area where the incident allegedly occurred for physical barriers that may enable abuse
Interview the alleged victim a second time
Assess the adequacy of staffing levels in that area during different shifts
Decide what sanction the alleged abuser will receive
Consider whether the allegation indicates a need to change policy or practice
questions.rationale: The team considers policy changes, examines the area for physical barriers, assesses staffing on different shifts, and assesses monitoring technology. Sanctions are decided through discipline processes, not the incident review.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.86 (Sexual abuse incident reviews), then answer the question.

(e) The facility shall implement the recommendations for improvement, or shall document its reasons for not doing so.

What must the facility do with the review team's recommendations for improvement?
options: Send them to the inmates for comment before implementing any of them
Implement them, or document its reasons for not doing so
Implement them only if the Regional Director approves each one
Hold them for one year before deciding which to implement
questions.rationale: "The facility shall implement the recommendations for improvement, or shall document its reasons for not doing so."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.101 (Procedures), then answer the question.

(1) During the admission and orientation process, an inmate who chooses to have telephone privileges shall prepare a proposed telephone list. At the time of submission, the inmate shall acknowledge that, to the best of the inmate's knowledge, the person or persons on the list are agreeable to receiving the inmate's telephone call and that the proposed calls are to be made for a purpose allowable under Bureau policy or institution guidelines.

What must an inmate acknowledge when he submits his proposed telephone list?
options: The persons listed have already been approved to appear on his visiting list
To the best of his knowledge, the persons listed are agreeable to receiving his calls, and the calls are for a purpose allowable under policy
The persons listed will pay for the calls he makes to them through a third-party billing arrangement
The persons listed have each signed a written consent form on file with the unit team
questions.rationale: At submission, "the inmate shall acknowledge that, to the best of the inmate's knowledge, the person or persons on the list are agreeable to receiving the inmate's telephone call and that the proposed calls are to be made for a purpose allowable under Bureau policy or institution guidelines."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.101 (Procedures), then answer the question.

(3) The Associate Warden may deny placement of a telephone number on an inmate's telephone list if the Associate Warden determines that there is a threat to institution security or good order, or a threat to the public. Any disapproval must be documented in writing to both the inmate and the proposed recipient. As with concerns about any correctional issue, including any portion of these telephone regulations, an inmate may appeal the denial through the administrative remedy procedure (see 28 CFR part 542). The Associate Warden will notify the denied recipient that he or she may appeal the denial by writing to the Warden within 15 days of the receipt of the denial.

Who may deny placement of a telephone number on an inmate's list, and on what grounds?
options: The unit officer, if the number belongs to a person with a criminal record
The Warden, if the inmate has had more than one incident report in the past year, as long as no other inmate is affected
The Associate Warden, if the number poses a threat to institution security or good order, or to the public
The chaplain, if the number belongs to a person not related to the inmate
questions.rationale: "The Associate Warden may deny placement of a telephone number on an inmate's telephone list if the Associate Warden determines that there is a threat to institution security or good order, or a threat to the public."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.101 (Procedures), then answer the question.

(3) The Associate Warden may deny placement of a telephone number on an inmate's telephone list if the Associate Warden determines that there is a threat to institution security or good order, or a threat to the public. Any disapproval must be documented in writing to both the inmate and the proposed recipient. As with concerns about any correctional issue, including any portion of these telephone regulations, an inmate may appeal the denial through the administrative remedy procedure (see 28 CFR part 542). The Associate Warden will notify the denied recipient that he or she may appeal the denial by writing to the Warden within 15 days of the receipt of the denial.

How may a denied recipient appeal the denial of a telephone number?
options: By telephoning the Associate Warden within 5 days of receipt of the denial
By asking the inmate to file a grievance within 20 days of receipt of the denial
By writing to the Regional Director within 30 days of receipt of the denial
By writing to the Warden within 15 days of receipt of the denial
questions.rationale: "The Associate Warden will notify the denied recipient that he or she may appeal the denial by writing to the Warden within 15 days of the receipt of the denial."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.101 (Procedures), then answer the question.

(e) Exception. The Warden may allow the placement of collect calls for good cause. Examples of good cause include, but are not limited to, inmates who are new arrivals to the institution, including new commitments and transfers; inmates confined at Metropolitan Correctional Centers, Metropolitan Detention Centers, or Federal Detention Centers; pretrial inmates; inmates in holdover status; inmates who are without funds (see § 540.105(b)); and in cases of family emergencies.

Select ALL of the examples of "good cause" for allowing collect calls that are given in the excerpt.
options: Inmates who work in the commissary
Inmates who are without funds
Inmates who have been disciplined for phone misuse
Inmates who are new arrivals to the institution
Pretrial inmates
questions.rationale: Good cause includes "new arrivals to the institution," pretrial inmates, holdover status, inmates without funds, and family emergencies. A disciplinary history or a commissary job is not listed.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.102 (Monitoring of inmate telephone calls), then answer the question.

The Warden shall establish procedures that enable monitoring of telephone conversations on any telephone located within the institution, said monitoring to be done to preserve the security and orderly management of the institution and to protect the public. The Warden must provide notice to the inmate of the potential for monitoring. Staff may not monitor an inmate's properly placed call to an attorney. The Warden shall notify an inmate of the proper procedures to have an unmonitored telephone conversation with an attorney.

What must the Warden do regarding monitoring of telephone calls?
options: Provide notice of monitoring to the person receiving the call, but not to the inmate
Establish procedures that enable monitoring and provide notice to the inmate of the potential for monitoring
Establish procedures that prevent monitoring and provide notice only after a call has been monitored, in most circumstances
Allow monitoring only when an inmate has been convicted of a disciplinary violation
questions.rationale: The Warden "shall establish procedures that enable monitoring of telephone conversations... to preserve the security and orderly management of the institution and to protect the public. The Warden must provide notice to the inmate of the potential for monitoring."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.103 (Inmate telephone calls to attorneys), then answer the question.

The Warden may not apply frequency limitations on inmate telephone calls to attorneys when the inmate demonstrates that communication with attorneys by correspondence, visiting, or normal telephone use is not adequate.

Which conclusion is best supported by the excerpt on telephone calls to attorneys?
options: Frequency limits never apply to any call an inmate places
Frequency limits apply to attorney calls only on weekends and holidays
Frequency limits may not be applied to attorney calls once the inmate shows other forms of communication are not adequate
Frequency limits apply to attorney calls unless the attorney is on the telephone list, during normal operating hours, unless local procedures say otherwise
questions.rationale: "The Warden may not apply frequency limitations on inmate telephone calls to attorneys when the inmate demonstrates that communication with attorneys by correspondence, visiting, or normal telephone use is not adequate."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.105 (Expenses of inmate telephone use), then answer the question.

(a) An inmate is responsible for the expenses of inmate telephone use. Such expenses may include a fee for replacement of an inmate's telephone access code that is used in an institution which has implemented debit billing for inmate telephone calls. Each inmate is responsible for staying aware of his or her account balance through the automated process provided by the system. Third party billing and electronic transfer of a call to a third party are prohibited.

Which practice is prohibited in paragraph (a)?
options: Third party billing and electronic transfer of a call to a third party
Calls placed with a debit billing account
Calls to numbers on the inmate's telephone list
Collect calls placed to the inmate's immediate family, for the duration of the incident
questions.rationale: Paragraph (a) ends "Third party billing and electronic transfer of a call to a third party are prohibited."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.105 (Expenses of inmate telephone use), then answer the question.

(b) The Warden shall provide at least one collect call each month for an inmate who is without funds. An inmate without funds is defined as an inmate who has not had a trust fund account balance of $6.00 for the past 30 days. The Warden may increase the number of collect calls based upon local institution conditions (e.g., institution population, staff resources, and usage demand). To prevent abuses of this provision (e.g., inmate shows a pattern of depleting his or her commissary funds prior to placing collect calls), the Warden may impose restrictions on the provisions of this paragraph (b).

How does the excerpt define an "inmate without funds"?
options: An inmate who has not had a trust fund account balance of $60.00 for the past 6 months
An inmate who has not had a trust fund account balance of $6.00 for the past 30 days
An inmate whose trust fund account balance is zero on the day of the call
An inmate who has not made a commissary purchase for the past 30 days
questions.rationale: "An inmate without funds is defined as an inmate who has not had a trust fund account balance of $6.00 for the past 30 days." The Warden provides at least one collect call each month for such an inmate.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 542.10 (Purpose and scope), then answer the question.

(b) Scope. This Program applies to all inmates in institutions operated by the Bureau of Prisons, to inmates designated to contract Community Corrections Centers (CCCs) under Bureau of Prisons responsibility, and to former inmates for issues that arose during their confinement. This Program does not apply to inmates confined in other non-federal facilities.

To whom does the Administrative Remedy Program NOT apply?
options: Inmates designated to contract Community Corrections Centers
Inmates in institutions operated by the Bureau of Prisons
Former inmates with issues that arose during their confinement
Inmates confined in other non-federal facilities
questions.rationale: The Program "applies to all inmates in institutions operated by the Bureau of Prisons, to inmates designated to contract Community Corrections Centers (CCCs)... and to former inmates for issues that arose during their confinement. This Program does not apply to inmates confined in other non-federal facilities."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 542.10 (Purpose and scope), then answer the question.

(c) Statutorily-mandated procedures. There are statutorily-mandated procedures in place for tort claims (28 CFR part 543, subpart C), Inmate Accident Compensation claims (28 CFR part 301), and Freedom of Information Act or Privacy Act requests (28 CFR part 513, subpart D). If an inmate raises an issue in a request or appeal that cannot be resolved through the Administrative Remedy Program, the Bureau will refer the inmate to the appropriate statutorily-mandated procedures.

Why does the excerpt mention tort claims, Inmate Accident Compensation claims, and Freedom of Information Act requests?
options: These are handled by statutorily-mandated procedures, and the Bureau refers inmates there when an issue cannot be resolved through the program
These are claims that inmates must file before using the program
These are claims that may be decided by the Warden alone
These are the only issues that the program will accept from an inmate
questions.rationale: "If an inmate raises an issue in a request or appeal that cannot be resolved through the Administrative Remedy Program, the Bureau will refer the inmate to the appropriate statutorily-mandated procedures."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 542.14 (Initial filing), then answer the question.

(b) Extension. Where the inmate demonstrates a valid reason for delay, an extension in filing time may be allowed. In general, valid reason for delay means a situation which prevented the inmate from submitting the request within the established time frame. Valid reasons for delay include the following: an extended period in-transit during which the inmate was separated from documents needed to prepare the Request or Appeal; an extended period of time during which the inmate was physically incapable of preparing a Request or Appeal; an unusually long period taken for informal resolution attempts; indication by an inmate, verified by staff, that a response to the inmate's request for copies of dispositions requested under § 542.19 of this part was delayed.

Select ALL of the valid reasons for delay that the excerpt lists for an extension in filing time.
options: An extended period during which the inmate was physically incapable of preparing a Request or Appeal
The inmate forgot the filing deadline
The inmate was busy with a work assignment
An extended period in-transit during which the inmate was separated from documents needed to prepare the Request
An unusually long period taken for informal resolution attempts
questions.rationale: Valid reasons include extended transit separated from documents, being physically incapable of preparing the Request, an unusually long informal resolution attempt, and a verified delay in receiving requested copies. Forgetting or being busy is not listed.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 542.14 (Initial filing), then answer the question.

(2) The inmate shall place a single complaint or a reasonable number of closely related issues on the form. If the inmate includes on a single form multiple unrelated issues, the submission shall be rejected and returned without response, and the inmate shall be advised to use a separate form for each unrelated issue. For DHO and UDC appeals, each separate incident report number must be appealed on a separate form.

An inmate puts three unrelated complaints about food, mail, and a work assignment on a single BP-9 form. What will happen?
options: The submission will be accepted, but only the first issue will be answered
The submission will be accepted, and the Warden will answer the issues in order
The submission will be rejected and returned without response, and he will be told to use a separate form for each unrelated issue
The submission will be forwarded to the Regional Director for review
questions.rationale: "If the inmate includes on a single form multiple unrelated issues, the submission shall be rejected and returned without response, and the inmate shall be advised to use a separate form for each unrelated issue."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 542.14 (Initial filing), then answer the question.

(d) Exceptions to initial filing at institution—(1) Sensitive issues. If the inmate reasonably believes the issue is sensitive and the inmate's safety or well-being would be placed in danger if the Request became known at the institution, the inmate may submit the Request directly to the appropriate Regional Director. The inmate shall clearly mark “Sensitive” upon the Request and explain, in writing, the reason for not submitting the Request at the institution. If the Regional Administrative Remedy Coordinator agrees that the Request is sensitive, the Request shall be accepted. Otherwise, the Request will not be accepted, and the inmate shall be advised in writing of that determination, without a return of the Request. The inmate may pursue the matter by submitting an Administrative Remedy Request locally to the Warden. The Warden shall allow a reasonable extension of time for such a resubmission.

When may an inmate submit a Request directly to the Regional Director instead of at the institution?
options: When the Warden is away from the institution for more than five days
When he is dissatisfied with the response from the unit officer
When he has already filed a Request about the same matter at the institution
When he reasonably believes the issue is sensitive and his safety or well-being would be in danger if the Request became known at the institution
questions.rationale: "If the inmate reasonably believes the issue is sensitive and the inmate's safety or well-being would be placed in danger if the Request became known at the institution, the inmate may submit the Request directly to the appropriate Regional Director," marking it "Sensitive."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 542.14 (Initial filing), then answer the question.

(2) DHO appeals. DHO appeals shall be submitted initially to the Regional Director for the region where the inmate is currently located.

To whom are DHO appeals initially submitted?
options: The Regional Director for the region where the inmate is currently located
The Warden of the institution where the incident report was issued, unless an emergency requires otherwise
The General Counsel
The Unit Discipline Committee that referred the incident report
questions.rationale: "DHO appeals shall be submitted initially to the Regional Director for the region where the inmate is currently located."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 542.15 (Appeals), then answer the question.

(a) Submission. An inmate who is not satisfied with the Warden's response may submit an Appeal on the appropriate form (BP-10) to the appropriate Regional Director within 20 calendar days of the date the Warden signed the response. An inmate who is not satisfied with the Regional Director's response may submit an Appeal on the appropriate form (BP-11) to the General Counsel within 30 calendar days of the date the Regional Director signed the response. When the inmate demonstrates a valid reason for delay, these time limits may be extended. Valid reasons for delay include those situations described in § 542.14(b) of this part. Appeal to the General Counsel is the final administrative appeal.

If an inmate is not satisfied with the Warden's response, what is the appeal deadline and to whom is the appeal made?
options: Within 30 calendar days of the date the Warden signed the response, to the General Counsel on form BP-11
Within 20 calendar days of the date the Warden signed the response, to the Regional Director on form BP-10
Within 30 calendar days of the date the Warden signed the response, to the Regional Director on form BP-10
Within 20 calendar days of the date the Warden signed the response, to the General Counsel on form BP-11
questions.rationale: An inmate not satisfied with the Warden's response "may submit an Appeal on the appropriate form (BP-10) to the appropriate Regional Director within 20 calendar days of the date the Warden signed the response." The General Counsel appeal (BP-11) follows the Regional Director's response, within 30 days.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 542.15 (Appeals), then answer the question.

(2) An inmate may not raise in an Appeal issues not raised in the lower level filings. An inmate may not combine Appeals of separate lower level responses (different case numbers) into a single Appeal.

Which of the following is NOT permitted in an Appeal?
options: Appealing a response from a single case number
Stating specifically the reason for the appeal
Attaching a copy of the institution Request and response, based on the information available at the time
Raising issues that were not raised in the lower level filings
questions.rationale: "An inmate may not raise in an Appeal issues not raised in the lower level filings. An inmate may not combine Appeals of separate lower level responses (different case numbers) into a single Appeal."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 542.18 (Response time), then answer the question.

If accepted, a Request or Appeal is considered filed on the date it is logged into the Administrative Remedy Index as received. Once filed, response shall be made by the Warden or CCM within 20 calendar days; by the Regional Director within 30 calendar days; and by the General Counsel within 40 calendar days. If the Request is determined to be of an emergency nature which threatens the inmate's immediate health or welfare, the Warden shall respond not later than the third calendar day after filing. If the time period for response to a Request or Appeal is insufficient to make an appropriate decision, the time for response may be extended once by 20 days at the institution level, 30 days at the regional level, or 20 days at the Central Office level. Staff shall inform the inmate of this extension in writing. Staff shall respond in writing to all filed Requests or Appeals. If the inmate does not receive a response within the time allotted for reply, including extension, the inmate may consider the absence of a response to be a denial at that level.

Within how many calendar days must the Warden respond to a filed Request, the Regional Director to an Appeal, and the General Counsel to an Appeal?
options: 20, 20, and 20 days
20, 30, and 40 days
30, 40, and 50 days
10, 20, and 30 days
questions.rationale: "Once filed, response shall be made by the Warden or CCM within 20 calendar days; by the Regional Director within 30 calendar days; and by the General Counsel within 40 calendar days."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 542.18 (Response time), then answer the question.

If accepted, a Request or Appeal is considered filed on the date it is logged into the Administrative Remedy Index as received. Once filed, response shall be made by the Warden or CCM within 20 calendar days; by the Regional Director within 30 calendar days; and by the General Counsel within 40 calendar days. If the Request is determined to be of an emergency nature which threatens the inmate's immediate health or welfare, the Warden shall respond not later than the third calendar day after filing. If the time period for response to a Request or Appeal is insufficient to make an appropriate decision, the time for response may be extended once by 20 days at the institution level, 30 days at the regional level, or 20 days at the Central Office level. Staff shall inform the inmate of this extension in writing. Staff shall respond in writing to all filed Requests or Appeals. If the inmate does not receive a response within the time allotted for reply, including extension, the inmate may consider the absence of a response to be a denial at that level.

An inmate files a Request claiming a threat to his immediate health or welfare. By when must the Warden respond if the Request is determined to be an emergency?
options: Within 30 calendar days after the Warden's signature
Within 24 hours of the end of the inmate's shift
Not later than the third calendar day after filing
Within 20 calendar days after filing
questions.rationale: "If the Request is determined to be of an emergency nature which threatens the inmate's immediate health or welfare, the Warden shall respond not later than the third calendar day after filing."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 548.10 (Purpose and scope), then answer the question.

(b) When considered necessary for the security or good order of the institution, the Warden may limit attendance at or discontinue a religious activity. Opportunities for religious activities are open to the entire inmate population, without regard to race, color, nationality, or ordinarily, creed. The Warden, after consulting with the institution chaplain, may limit participation in a particular religious activity or practice to the members of that religious group. Ordinarily, when the nature of the activity or practice (e.g., religious fasts, wearing of headwear, work proscription, ceremonial meals) indicates a need for such a limitation, only those inmates whose files reflect the pertinent religious preference will be included.

When may the Warden limit attendance at or discontinue a religious activity?
options: When considered necessary for the security or good order of the institution
When an inmate requests a different activity
When the chaplain is away from the institution
When fewer than five inmates attend the activity
questions.rationale: "When considered necessary for the security or good order of the institution, the Warden may limit attendance at or discontinue a religious activity."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 548.16 (Inmate religious property), then answer the question.

(a) Inmate religious property includes but is not limited to rosaries and prayer beads, oils, prayer rugs, phylacteries, medicine pouches, and religious medallions. Such items, which become part of an inmate's personal property, are subject to normal considerations of safety and security. If necessary, their religious significance shall be verified by the chaplain prior to the Warden's approval.
(b) An inmate ordinarily shall be allowed to wear or use personal religious items during religious services, ceremonies, and meetings in the chapel, unless the Warden determines that the wearing or use of such items would threaten institution security, safety, or good order. Upon request of the inmate, the Warden may allow the wearing or use of certain religious items throughout the institution, consistent with considerations of security, safety, or good order. The Warden may request the chaplain to obtain direction from representatives of the inmate's faith group or other appropriate sources concerning the religious significance of the items.

When may an inmate ordinarily wear or use personal religious items?
options: During religious services, ceremonies, and meetings in the chapel, unless the Warden determines it would threaten security, safety, or good order
Only on days of religious observance, in the chapel, and only if the Warden has given written approval in advance
During religious services in the chapel, but only if the chaplain has verified the religious significance of each item, once the shift lieutenant has been informed
At any time in any part of the institution, unless a staff member objects that the item may be unsafe
questions.rationale: "An inmate ordinarily shall be allowed to wear or use personal religious items during religious services, ceremonies, and meetings in the chapel, unless the Warden determines that the wearing or use of such items would threaten institution security, safety, or good order."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 548.18 (Observance of religious holy days), then answer the question.

Consistent with maintaining security, safety, and good order in the institution, the Warden shall endeavor to facilitate the observance of important religious holy days which involve special fasts, dietary regulations, worship, or work proscription. The inmate must submit a written request to the chaplain for time off from work to observe a religious holy day. The Warden may request the chaplain to consult with community representatives of the inmate's faith group and/or other appropriate sources to verify the religious significance of the requested observance. The chaplain will work with requesting inmates to accommodate a proper observance of the holy day. The Warden will ordinarily allow an inmate to take earned vacation days, or to make up for missed work, or to change work assignments in order to facilitate the observance of the religious holy day.

What must an inmate do to take time off from work to observe a religious holy day?
options: Submit a written request to the Regional Director
Submit a written request to the chaplain
Submit a petition signed by five other inmates of his faith
Submit a verbal request to his work supervisor
questions.rationale: "The inmate must submit a written request to the chaplain for time off from work to observe a religious holy day."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 548.20 (Dietary practices), then answer the question.

(a) The Bureau provides inmates requesting a religious diet reasonable and equitable opportunity to observe their religious dietary practice within the constraints of budget limitations and the security and orderly running of the institution and the Bureau through a religious diet menu. The inmate will provide a written statement articulating the religious motivation for participation in the religious diet program.
(b) An inmate who has been approved for a religious diet menu must notify the chaplain in writing if the inmate wishes to withdraw from the religious diet. Approval for an inmate's religious diet may be withdrawn by the chaplain if the inmate is documented as being in violation of the terms of the religious diet program to which the inmate has agreed in writing. In order to preserve the integrity and orderly operation of the religious diet program and to prevent fraud, inmates who withdraw (or are removed) may not be immediately reestablished back into the program. The process of reapproving a religious diet for an inmate who voluntarily withdraws or who is removed ordinarily may extend up to thirty days. Repeated withdrawals (voluntary or otherwise), however, may result in inmates being subjected to a waiting period of up to one year.

Which statement about a religious diet is supported by paragraphs (a) and (b)?
options: An inmate must obtain the Warden's signature, and he may be removed only by the Warden
An inmate may withdraw verbally, and the chaplain may approve a return the next day
An inmate must provide a written statement of his religious motivation, and one who withdraws or is removed may not be immediately re-established in the program
An inmate may begin a religious diet by verbal request, and he may return to the program at any time
questions.rationale: The inmate "will provide a written statement articulating the religious motivation," and inmates who withdraw or are removed "may not be immediately reestablished back into the program"; reapproval ordinarily may take up to thirty days.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 548.20 (Dietary practices), then answer the question.

(c) The chaplain may arrange for inmate religious groups to have one appropriate ceremonial or commemorative meal each year for their members as identified by the religious preference reflected in the inmate's file. An inmate may attend one religious ceremonial meal in a calendar year.

How many religious ceremonial meals may an inmate attend each calendar year?
options: Two
Four
Twelve
One
questions.rationale: "An inmate may attend one religious ceremonial meal in a calendar year."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 543.11 (Legal research and preparation of legal documents), then answer the question.

(f)(1) Except as provided for in paragraph (f)(4) of this section, an inmate may assist another inmate in the same institution during his or her leisure time (as defined in paragraph (a) of this section) with legal research and the preparation of legal documents for submission to a court or other judicial body.

An inmate wants to help another inmate in the same institution prepare a court filing. When may he do this, according to paragraph (f)(1)?
options: During his work assignment, since legal help is a form of work
Only with the written permission of the other inmate's attorney
At any time, since the Warden may not limit this assistance in any way
During his leisure time, unless the Warden has imposed limitations in the interest of security, good order, or discipline
questions.rationale: An inmate "may assist another inmate in the same institution during his or her leisure time... with legal research and the preparation of legal documents," and the Warden "may impose limitations on an inmate's assistance to another inmate in the interest of institution security, good order, or discipline."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 543.11 (Legal research and preparation of legal documents), then answer the question.

(i) The assisting inmate may not remove another inmate's legal materials, including copies of the legal materials, from the law library or other designated location. An assisting inmate is permitted to make handwritten notes and to remove those notes from the library or other designated location if the notes do not contain a case caption or document title or the name(s) of any inmate(s). The assisting inmate may also develop and possess handwritten drafts of pleadings, so long as the draft pleadings do not contain a case caption or document title or the name(s) of any inmate(s). These notes and drafts are not considered to be the assisting inmate's legal property, and when the assisting inmate has these documents outside the law library or other designated location, they are subject to the property limitations in § 553.11(a) of this chapter.

What may an assisting inmate remove from the law library about another inmate's case?
options: Handwritten notes that do not contain a case caption, a document title, or the name of any inmate
Photocopies of the other inmate's legal materials, if the Warden approves, in accordance with the posted schedule
Nothing at all, including handwritten notes of any kind
The other inmate's pleadings, as long as he returns them the same day
questions.rationale: The assisting inmate "may not remove another inmate's legal materials, including copies... from the law library." He "is permitted to make handwritten notes and to remove those notes... if the notes do not contain a case caption or document title or the name(s) of any inmate(s)."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 543.11 (Legal research and preparation of legal documents), then answer the question.

(i) The Warden shall give special time allowance for research and preparation of documents to an inmate who demonstrates a requirement to meet an imminent court deadline. Otherwise, each inmate shall continue his regular institutional activities without undue disruption by legal activities.

An inmate demonstrates that he must meet an imminent court deadline. What does the excerpt require of the Warden?
options: Excuse the inmate from all work assignments for the rest of the month
Require the inmate to prepare the documents during the next scheduled leisure period
Give the inmate a special time allowance for research and preparation of documents
Assign a staff attorney to prepare the documents for the inmate
questions.rationale: "The Warden shall give special time allowance for research and preparation of documents to an inmate who demonstrates a requirement to meet an imminent court deadline. Otherwise, each inmate shall continue his regular institutional activities without undue disruption."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 543.11 (Legal research and preparation of legal documents), then answer the question.

(j) With consideration of the needs of other inmates and the availability of staff and other resources, the Warden shall provide an inmate confined in disciplinary segregation or administrative detention a means of access to legal materials, along with an opportunity to prepare legal documents. The Warden shall allow an inmate in segregation or detention a reasonable amount of personal legal materials. In no case shall the amount of personal legal materials be such as to pose a fire, sanitation, security, or housekeeping hazard.

What must the Warden provide to an inmate confined in disciplinary segregation or administrative detention?
options: A private office in which to meet with other inmates about legal issues
Access to the main law library at any time the inmate requests
Unlimited legal materials, even if they present a fire or sanitation hazard, with the approval of a supervisor on duty
A means of access to legal materials and an opportunity to prepare legal documents, as resources allow
questions.rationale: "The Warden shall provide an inmate confined in disciplinary segregation or administrative detention a means of access to legal materials, along with an opportunity to prepare legal documents," but the amount of personal legal materials may not pose a fire, sanitation, security, or housekeeping hazard.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 543.13 (Visits by attorneys), then answer the question.

(d) The Warden may require an attorney to indicate where he is licensed as an attorney and how that fact may be verified. Prior to each appointment or visit, the Warden shall require each attorney to identify himself and to confirm that he wishes to visit an inmate who has requested his visit or whom he represents or whom he wishes to interview as a witness. The Warden may not ask the attorney to state the subject matter of the law suit or interview. If there is any question about the identity of the visitor or his qualification as an attorney in good standing, the Warden shall refer the matter to the Regional Counsel.

What may the Warden NOT ask an attorney to state before a visit?
options: The place where the attorney is licensed, based on the information available at the time
The attorney's name
The subject matter of the law suit or interview
Whether the inmate requested the visit
questions.rationale: The Warden may require the attorney to indicate where he is licensed and to identify himself, but "The Warden may not ask the attorney to state the subject matter of the law suit or interview."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 543.13 (Visits by attorneys), then answer the question.

(e) Staff shall not subject visits between an attorney and an inmate to auditory supervision. The Warden may permit tape recordings to be used by an attorney during the course of a visit only if the attorney states in writing in advance of the interview that the sole purpose of the recording is to facilitate the attorney-client or attorney-witness relationship.

Which statement about supervision of attorney visits is supported by paragraph (e)?
options: Staff shall subject the visit to auditory supervision, but the attorney may use a tape recorder if he states in writing in advance that it is for the visit
Staff shall not subject the visit to auditory supervision, and the attorney may not use a tape recorder under any circumstances
Staff may subject the visit to auditory supervision with the Warden's approval, and the attorney may use a tape recorder with verbal permission
Staff shall not subject the visit to auditory supervision, and the attorney may use a tape recorder only if he states in writing in advance that its sole purpose is the attorney-client relationship
questions.rationale: "Staff shall not subject visits between an attorney and an inmate to auditory supervision. The Warden may permit tape recordings to be used by an attorney... only if the attorney states in writing in advance of the interview that the sole purpose of the recording is to facilitate the attorney-client or attorney-witness relationship."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 543.14 (Limitation or denial of attorney visits and correspondence), then answer the question.

(a) An act by an attorney which violates Bureau regulations or institution guidelines and which threatens the security, good order, or discipline of the institution is grounds for limitation or denial by the Warden of the attorney's privileged visitation and correspondence rights. Acts by an attorney which may warrant such limitation or denial include, for example the following:
(1) A false statement as to the attorney's identity or qualifications;
(2) A plan, attempt, or act to introduce contraband into the institution;
(3) A conspiracy to commit, an attempt to commit, or the actual commission of an act of violence within an institution; and
(4) Encouraging an inmate to violate the law, Bureau of Prisons rules, or local implementing guidelines.

Select ALL of the acts the excerpt gives as examples that may warrant limitation or denial of an attorney's privileged visitation and correspondence.
options: Arriving at the institution after the scheduled time
Asking staff to explain the visiting procedures
Encouraging an inmate to violate the law, Bureau rules, or local guidelines
A plan, attempt, or act to introduce contraband into the institution
A false statement as to the attorney's identity or qualifications
questions.rationale: Examples include a false statement about identity or qualifications, a plan or act to introduce contraband, conspiring to commit violence within an institution, and encouraging an inmate to violate the law or rules. Being late or asking questions is not listed.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 543.14 (Limitation or denial of attorney visits and correspondence), then answer the question.

(b) Unless the breach of regulations is extreme or repeated, limitation rather than a denial of visitation or correspondence rights is proper, especially where the inmate is represented by the attorney and is confronted with a court deadline. For example, the Warden may subject an attorney to a search of his person and belongings or may permit the attorney only non-privileged correspondence. The Warden shall also consider referral of the matter to the state agency regulating the attorney's professional conduct.

Unless the breach of regulations is extreme or repeated, which action is described as proper?
options: Denial of all visitation and correspondence rights
Permanent removal of the attorney from the inmate's case
Limitation rather than denial of visitation or correspondence rights
Immediate referral to the Regional Director for sentencing
questions.rationale: "Unless the breach of regulations is extreme or repeated, limitation rather than a denial of visitation or correspondence rights is proper, especially where the inmate is represented by the attorney and is confronted with a court deadline."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 543.14 (Limitation or denial of attorney visits and correspondence), then answer the question.

(c) An act by an inmate in violation of Bureau regulations or institution guidelines warrants a limitation by the Warden of the inmate's correspondence or visiting rights with attorneys only if necessary to protect institution security, good order, or discipline. The Warden may not deny correspondence or visiting rights with attorneys generally.

What may the Warden NOT do when an inmate violates regulations?
options: Consider the inmate's court deadlines in limiting rights
Refer the violation for disciplinary action
Limit the inmate's correspondence or visiting rights with attorneys if necessary to protect security
Deny the inmate's correspondence or visiting rights with attorneys generally
questions.rationale: An inmate's violation warrants a limitation "only if necessary to protect institution security, good order, or discipline. The Warden may not deny correspondence or visiting rights with attorneys generally."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 545.21 (Definitions), then answer the question.

(h) Light duty work assignment. A work assignment in which an inmate may, because of physical limitations, temporary or otherwise, only perform limited work functions, e.g., sedentary work, no prolonged standing, no lifting over 25 lbs., etc.

What is a "light duty work assignment"?
options: A work assignment given to an inmate who is medically unable to be assigned to any work program
A work assignment that contributes to the day-to-day operation of the institution, such as carpentry
A work assignment performed for only a portion of the scheduled work day
A work assignment in which an inmate may, because of physical limitations, only perform limited work functions, e.g., sedentary work or no lifting over 25 lbs.
questions.rationale: "Light duty work assignment. A work assignment in which an inmate may, because of physical limitations, temporary or otherwise, only perform limited work functions, e.g., sedentary work, no prolonged standing, no lifting over 25 lbs., etc."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 545.23 (Inmate work/program assignment), then answer the question.

(b) A pretrial inmate may not be required to work in any assignment or area other than housekeeping tasks in the inmate's own cell and in the community living area, unless the pretrial inmate has signed a waiver of his or her right not to work (see 28 CFR part 551, subpart J).

A pretrial inmate has not signed a waiver of his right not to work. To what work may he be required to perform?
options: Assignments in Federal Prison Industries
Housekeeping tasks in his own cell and in the community living area
Any assignment in the food service department
Any assignment that the Warden finds necessary for operation, once the shift lieutenant has been informed
questions.rationale: "A pretrial inmate may not be required to work in any assignment or area other than housekeeping tasks in the inmate's own cell and in the community living area, unless the pretrial inmate has signed a waiver of his or her right not to work."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 545.25 (Eligibility for performance pay), then answer the question.

(e) Inmates receiving performance pay who are found through the disciplinary process (part 541 of this subchapter) to have committed a level 100 or 200 series drug- or alcohol-related prohibited act will automatically have their performance pay reduced to maintenance pay level and will be removed from any assigned work detail outside the secure perimeter of the institution. This reduction to maintenance pay level, and removal from assigned work detail outside the secure perimeter of the institution, will ordinarily remain in effect for one year, unless otherwise authorized by the Warden.

An inmate receiving performance pay is found through the disciplinary process to have committed a level 100 series drug-related prohibited act. What will happen?
options: His performance pay will remain at the same level, but he will lose commissary privileges
His performance pay will be cancelled permanently, and he will be transferred
His performance pay will be suspended for one month, and he will be reassigned to a different housing unit, once the shift lieutenant has been informed, pending review by the appropriate official
His performance pay will automatically be reduced to maintenance pay level, and he will be removed from outside work details, ordinarily for one year
questions.rationale: Such inmates "will automatically have their performance pay reduced to maintenance pay level and will be removed from any assigned work detail outside the secure perimeter... This reduction... will ordinarily remain in effect for one year, unless otherwise authorized by the Warden."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 545.26 (Performance pay provisions), then answer the question.

(a) The Warden shall ensure that all institution work assignments have standardized work descriptions. Each inmate work position is assigned one of four pay grade levels. Factors to consider in assigning a grade level to the specific work position include the position's educational and vocational requirements, physical demands, working conditions (exposed to dusts, odors, etc.), and the degree of responsibility held by the inmate worker. The inmate assigned to a specific work position shall sign, and, if requested, receive a copy of, that position description.

How many pay grade levels does each inmate work position have, and what factors are considered in assigning a grade?
options: Four; educational and vocational requirements, physical demands, working conditions, and the degree of responsibility
Five; seniority, education, and work supervisor's recommendation
Two; hours worked, attendance, and the inmate's religious preference
Three; length of sentence, age, and security level of the inmate
questions.rationale: "Each inmate work position is assigned one of four pay grade levels. Factors to consider... include the position's educational and vocational requirements, physical demands, working conditions (exposed to dusts, odors, etc.), and the degree of responsibility held by the inmate worker."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 545.26 (Performance pay provisions), then answer the question.

Grade 1—5% of the institution's allotted inmate work assignments; Grade 2—15% of the institution's allotted inmate work assignments; Grade 3—25% of the institution's allotted inmate work assignments; Grade 4—55% of the institution's allotted inmate work assignments.

Using the percentages in the excerpt, which grade level is assigned to the largest share of an institution's inmate work assignments?
options: Grade 2, at 15%
Grade 4, at 55%
Grade 1, at 5%
Grade 3, at 25%
questions.rationale: Grade 1 is 5%, Grade 2 is 15%, Grade 3 is 25%, and Grade 4 is 55%. Grade 4 holds the largest share (Grade 1 is the highest pay).

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 545.26 (Performance pay provisions), then answer the question.

(c) An inmate may receive performance pay only for that portion of the month that the inmate was working. Performance pay may not be awarded retroactively.
(d) An inmate is eligible to receive performance pay only for those hours during which the inmate is actually performing satisfactory work or actively participating in an education or vocational training program. Absences from an inmate's scheduled assignment for such reasons as call-outs, visits, sick call, interviews, or making telephone calls shall be deducted from the monthly number of hours worked and will accordingly reduce the amount of pay received by the inmate. Any exception to such reduction in pay must be approved by the Assistant Director, Correctional Programs Division, Central Office.

Which absence is described as reducing the monthly hours worked and the pay an inmate receives?
options: Absences for approved vacation days that the inmate has earned, where the circumstances reasonably call for it
Absences of less than five minutes for water breaks
Absences for call-outs, visits, sick call, interviews, or making telephone calls
Absences for time spent working on overtime projects
questions.rationale: "Absences from an inmate's scheduled assignment for such reasons as call-outs, visits, sick call, interviews, or making telephone calls shall be deducted from the monthly number of hours worked and will accordingly reduce the amount of pay received."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 549.12 (Testing), then answer the question.

(a) Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV)—(1) Clinically indicated. The Bureau tests inmates who have sentences of six months or more if health services staff determine, taking into consideration the risk as defined by the Centers for Disease Control guidelines, that the inmate is at risk for HIV infection. If the inmate refuses testing, staff may initiate an incident report for refusing to obey an order.

Which statement about HIV exposure incident testing is supported by the excerpt?
options: The Bureau tests an inmate regardless of sentence length or pretrial status when there is a well-founded reason to believe he may have transmitted HIV to employees or other non-inmates, and consent is not required
The Bureau tests an inmate only if his sentence is six months or more and he gives written consent after counseling
The Bureau tests an inmate only if he has requested a test within the past twelve months and the health services staff approve it
The Bureau tests an inmate only if a staff member requests the test and the Warden gives approval in writing
questions.rationale: "The Bureau tests an inmate, regardless of the length of sentence or pretrial status, when there is a well-founded reason to believe that the inmate may have transmitted the HIV infection... Exposure incident testing does not require the inmate's consent."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 549.12 (Testing), then answer the question.

(4) An inmate who refuses TB screening may be subject to an incident report for refusing to obey an order. If an inmate refuses skin testing, and there is no contraindication to tuberculin skin testing, then, institution medical staff will test the inmate involuntarily.

An inmate refuses TB skin testing and there is no contraindication to tuberculin skin testing. What may happen?
options: He will be placed in segregation until he agrees to testing, where the circumstances reasonably call for it
He will be excused from testing for thirty days
He will be required to sign a waiver and will not be tested
He may be subject to an incident report, and institution medical staff will test him involuntarily
questions.rationale: "An inmate who refuses TB screening may be subject to an incident report for refusing to obey an order. If an inmate refuses skin testing, and there is no contraindication to tuberculin skin testing, then, institution medical staff will test the inmate involuntarily."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 549.13 (Programming, duty, and housing restrictions), then answer the question.

(c) If an inmate tests positive for an infectious disease, that test alone does not constitute sole grounds for disciplinary action. Disciplinary action may be considered when coupled with a secondary action that could lead to transmission of an infectious agent. Inmates testing positive for infectious disease are subject to the same disciplinary policy that applies to all inmates (see 28 CFR part 541, subpart B). Except as provided for in our disciplinary policy, no special or separate housing units may be established for HIV-positive inmates.

Which statement about an inmate who tests positive for an infectious disease is supported by the excerpt?
options: The positive test alone is not grounds for disciplinary action, which may be considered only with a secondary action that could lead to transmission
The positive test alone is grounds for disciplinary action, and a secondary action is considered only to increase the sanction, where the circumstances reasonably call for it
The positive test alone requires placement in a special housing unit established for HIV-positive inmates
The positive test alone is not grounds for discipline, but the inmate must be removed from all work assignments permanently
questions.rationale: "If an inmate tests positive for an infectious disease, that test alone does not constitute sole grounds for disciplinary action. Disciplinary action may be considered when coupled with a secondary action that could lead to transmission." No special housing units may be established for HIV-positive inmates.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 549.14 (Confidentiality of information), then answer the question.

Any disclosure of test results or medical information is made in accordance with:
(a) The Privacy Act of 1974, under which the Bureau publishes routine uses of such information in the Department of Justice Privacy Act System of Records Notice entitled “Inmate Physical and Mental Health Record System, JUSTICE/BOP-007”; and
(b) The Correction Officers Health and Safety Act of 1998 (codified at 18 U.S.C. 4014), which provides that test results must be communicated to a person requesting the test, the person tested, and, if the results of the test indicate the presence of HIV, to correctional facility personnel consistent with Bureau policy.

Which laws govern the disclosure of test results or medical information, according to the excerpt?
options: The Fair Credit Reporting Act and the Freedom of Information Act
The Privacy Act of 1974 and the Correction Officers Health and Safety Act of 1998
The Americans with Disabilities Act and the Family Medical Leave Act
The Prison Litigation Reform Act and the Violent Crime Control Act
questions.rationale: Disclosures are made in accordance with "The Privacy Act of 1974" and "The Correction Officers Health and Safety Act of 1998 (codified at 18 U.S.C. 4014)."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 549.65 (Refusal to accept treatment), then answer the question.

(a) When, as a result of inadequate intake or abnormal output, a physician determines that the inmate's life or health will be threatened if treatment is not initiated immediately, the physician shall give consideration to forced medical treatment of the inmate.
(b) Prior to medical treatment being administered against the inmate's will, staff shall make reasonable efforts to convince the inmate to voluntarily accept treatment. Medical risks faced by the inmate if treatment is not accepted shall also be explained to the inmate. Staff shall document their treatment efforts in the medical record of the inmate.
