(c) When, after reasonable efforts, or in an emergency preventing such efforts, a medical necessity for immediate treatment of a life or health threatening situation exists, the physician may order that treatment be administered without the consent of the inmate. Staff shall document their treatment efforts in the medical record of the inmate.

Before medical treatment is administered against an inmate's will, what must staff do?
options: Obtain a court order, explain the medical risks, and notify the inmate's family
Ask another inmate to speak with the inmate, and document the conversation
Wait forty-eight hours, explain the medical risks, and obtain the Warden's signature
Make reasonable efforts to convince the inmate to accept treatment, explain the medical risks, and document their efforts in the medical record
questions.rationale: "Prior to medical treatment being administered against the inmate's will, staff shall make reasonable efforts to convince the inmate to voluntarily accept treatment. Medical risks faced by the inmate if treatment is not accepted shall also be explained... Staff shall document their treatment efforts in the medical record."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 551.13 (Application to marry), then answer the question.

(a) A federal inmate confined in a Bureau institution who wants to get married shall submit a request to marry to the inmate's unit team. The unit team shall evaluate the request based on the criteria identified in § 551.12. A written report of the unit team's findings, and its recommendation, shall be forwarded to the Warden for a final decision.
(b) The Warden shall notify the inmate in writing whether the inmate's request to marry is approved or disapproved. A copy of this notification shall be placed in the inmate's central file. When the Warden's decision is to disapprove the inmate's request, the notification to the inmate shall include a statement of reason(s) for that action. The Warden shall advise the inmate that the decision may be appealed through the Administrative Remedy Procedure.

Which sequence describes how a request to marry is handled?
options: The inmate submits the request to his unit team, the team forwards a written report and recommendation to the Warden, and the Warden notifies the inmate in writing
The inmate submits the request to the Warden, the unit team gives a recommendation, and the chaplain decides, in accordance with the posted schedule, when staff resources allow
The inmate submits the request to his family, the unit team forwards it, and the Regional Director decides
The inmate submits the request to the chaplain, the Warden gives a recommendation, and the unit team decides
questions.rationale: The inmate "shall submit a request to marry to the inmate's unit team," which evaluates it and forwards "a written report of the unit team's findings, and its recommendation, to the Warden for a final decision." The Warden notifies the inmate in writing.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 551.31 (Approval of an organization), then answer the question.

(a) An inmate must submit a request for recognition of a proposed inmate organization to the Warden. The organization may not become active without the Warden's approval.
(b) The Warden may approve an inmate organization upon determining that:
(1) The organization has a constitution and bylaws duly approved by its members; the constitution and bylaws must include the organization's purpose and objectives, the duties and responsibilities of its officer(s), and the requirements for activities reporting and operational review; and
(2) The organization does not operate in opposition to the security, good order, or discipline of the institution.

Under what conditions may the Warden approve an inmate organization?
options: The organization has a written budget and has operated for at least one year
The organization has at least ten members and a faculty sponsor from outside the institution
The organization has a constitution and bylaws approved by its members and does not operate in opposition to security, good order, or discipline
The organization has the support of the chaplain and does not require staff supervision
questions.rationale: The Warden may approve an organization on determining that it "has a constitution and bylaws duly approved by its members" and "does not operate in opposition to the security, good order, or discipline of the institution."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 551.34 (Organization activities), then answer the question.

(a) An officer of the inmate organization must submit a written request for approval of an activity to the Warden or designee. Activities include, but are not limited to, meetings, guest speakers, sports competitions, banquets, or community programs. Activities may not include fund-raising projects. The request must specifically include:

Which of the following may NOT be part of an inmate organization's activities?
options: Guest speakers
Sports competitions
Meetings
Fund-raising projects
questions.rationale: Activities include "meetings, guest speakers, sports competitions, banquets, or community programs. Activities may not include fund-raising projects."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.5 (General definitions), then answer the question.

Unsubstantiated allegation means an allegation that was investigated and the investigation produced insufficient evidence to make a final determination as to whether or not the event occurred.

An investigation of an allegation ends with insufficient evidence to decide whether the event occurred. How does the excerpt classify it?
options: Unsubstantiated
Substantiated
Exigent
Unfounded
questions.rationale: "Unsubstantiated allegation means an allegation that was investigated and the investigation produced insufficient evidence to make a final determination as to whether or not the event occurred."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.5 (General definitions), then answer the question.

Contractor means a person who provides services on a recurring basis pursuant to a contractual agreement with the agency.
Volunteer means an individual who donates time and effort on a recurring basis to enhance the activities and programs of the agency.

What is the difference between a "contractor" and a "volunteer" in the excerpt?
options: A contractor donates time without pay, while a volunteer is paid by the agency
A contractor serves one day a year, while a volunteer serves every day
A contractor provides services on a recurring basis under a contractual agreement, while a volunteer donates time and effort on a recurring basis
A contractor works directly for the facility, while a volunteer works only for religious groups, unless local procedures say otherwise, in accordance with the posted schedule
questions.rationale: "Contractor means a person who provides services on a recurring basis pursuant to a contractual agreement with the agency." "Volunteer means an individual who donates time and effort on a recurring basis to enhance the activities and programs of the agency."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.5 (General definitions), then answer the question.

Jail means a confinement facility of a Federal, State, or local law enforcement agency whose primary use is to hold persons pending adjudication of criminal charges, persons committed to confinement after adjudication of criminal charges for sentences of one year or less, or persons adjudicated guilty who are awaiting transfer to a correctional facility.
Prison means an institution under Federal or State jurisdiction whose primary use is for the confinement of individuals convicted of a serious crime, usually in excess of one year in length, or a felony.

According to the definitions, how is a "jail" different from a "prison"?
options: A jail is a facility run by a Federal agency that holds only juveniles; a prison is a facility run by a State agency that holds only adults

A jail primarily holds persons convicted of felonies, usually over a year; a prison primarily holds persons pending adjudication or serving sentences of one year or less, as determined by the shift supervisor
A jail is a facility run by a local agency that holds only persons awaiting transfer; a prison is a facility that holds only persons awaiting trial
A jail primarily holds persons pending adjudication or serving sentences of one year or less; a prison primarily holds persons convicted of serious crimes, usually over a year
questions.rationale: A jail's primary use is "to hold persons pending adjudication of criminal charges" or sentenced to one year or less; a prison is for "individuals convicted of a serious crime, usually in excess of one year in length, or a felony."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.5 (General definitions), then answer the question.

Lockup means a facility that contains holding cells, cell blocks, or other secure enclosures that are:
(1) Under the control of a law enforcement, court, or custodial officer; and
(2) Primarily used for the temporary confinement of individuals who have recently been arrested, detained, or are being transferred to or from a court, jail, prison, or other agency.

What is a "lockup" as defined in the excerpt?
options: A facility with holding cells under the control of a law enforcement, court, or custodial officer, primarily used for temporary confinement of persons recently arrested or being transferred
A facility with secure enclosures under the control of the juvenile justice system, primarily used for confinement of juveniles
A facility with cell blocks under the control of a Federal agency, primarily used for confinement of persons convicted of felonies for more than a year, after a supervisor has reviewed the matter
A facility with dormitories under the control of a nonprofit authority, primarily used for treatment of persons with substance abuse problems
questions.rationale: A lockup contains holding cells or secure enclosures "under the control of a law enforcement, court, or custodial officer" and "primarily used for the temporary confinement of individuals who have recently been arrested, detained, or are being transferred."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.5 (General definitions), then answer the question.

Juvenile means any person under the age of 18, unless under adult court supervision and confined or detained in a prison or jail.

Who is a "juvenile" for the purposes of this part?
options: Any person under the age of 18, including those under adult court supervision in a jail
Any person under the age of 18, unless under adult court supervision and confined or detained in a prison or jail
Any person under the age of 16, unless held in a juvenile facility
Any person under the age of 21, whether or not under adult court supervision
questions.rationale: "Juvenile means any person under the age of 18, unless under adult court supervision and confined or detained in a prison or jail." Those under adult court supervision in a prison or jail are "youthful inmates."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.5 (General definitions), then answer the question.

Full compliance means compliance with all material requirements of each standard except for de minimis violations, or discrete and temporary violations during otherwise sustained periods of compliance.

What does "full compliance" mean under the definitions?
options: Compliance with a majority of the standards, as decided by an outside auditor
Compliance with every requirement of every standard with no exceptions of any kind
Compliance with the standards at the Warden's discretion, based on local conditions
Compliance with all material requirements of each standard except for de minimis violations or discrete and temporary violations during otherwise sustained compliance
questions.rationale: "Full compliance means compliance with all material requirements of each standard except for de minimis violations, or discrete and temporary violations during otherwise sustained periods of compliance."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.5 (General definitions), then answer the question.

Medical practitioner means a health professional who, by virtue of education, credentials, and experience, is permitted by law to evaluate and care for patients within the scope of his or her professional practice. A “qualified medical practitioner” refers to such a professional who has also successfully completed specialized training for treating sexual abuse victims.

What makes a "qualified medical practitioner" different from a "medical practitioner"?
options: The qualified practitioner has also successfully completed specialized training for treating sexual abuse victims
The qualified practitioner is also licensed to practice in more than one state
The qualified practitioner is also authorized to supervise other practitioners
The qualified practitioner has also been employed by the agency for at least five years, after a supervisor has reviewed the matter
questions.rationale: "A 'qualified medical practitioner' refers to such a professional who has also successfully completed specialized training for treating sexual abuse victims."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.6 (Definitions related to sexual abuse), then answer the question.

Sexual harassment includes—
(1) Repeated and unwelcome sexual advances, requests for sexual favors, or verbal comments, gestures, or actions of a derogatory or offensive sexual nature by one inmate, detainee, or resident directed toward another; and
(2) Repeated verbal comments or gestures of a sexual nature to an inmate, detainee, or resident by a staff member, contractor, or volunteer, including demeaning references to gender, sexually suggestive or derogatory comments about body or clothing, or obscene language or gestures.

According to the definition of sexual harassment, what is required of inmate-on-inmate conduct?
options: A single incident of physical contact that the other inmate reports to staff, after a supervisor has reviewed the matter, during normal operating hours
Repeated and unwelcome sexual advances, requests for sexual favors, or derogatory or offensive sexual comments, gestures, or actions
Any conversation about sexual topics held in a housing unit
Any physical contact that the other inmate later says was unwanted
questions.rationale: Sexual harassment by an inmate includes "repeated and unwelcome sexual advances, requests for sexual favors, or verbal comments, gestures, or actions of a derogatory or offensive sexual nature."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.6 (Definitions related to sexual abuse), then answer the question.

Sexual abuse of an inmate, detainee, or resident by a staff member, contractor, or volunteer includes any of the following acts, with or without consent of the inmate, detainee, or resident:

The excerpt says sexual abuse of an inmate by a staff member includes certain acts "with or without consent of the inmate." What does this suggest?
options: An inmate's consent matters only if it is in writing
An inmate's consent is required for staff-inmate contact to be allowed
An inmate's apparent consent does not make sexual contact with staff acceptable
An inmate's consent is not relevant to abuse by another inmate
questions.rationale: For abuse by staff, contractors, or volunteers, the definition applies "with or without consent." By contrast, for inmate-on-inmate abuse the acts count if the victim does not consent, is coerced, or cannot consent.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.6 (Definitions related to sexual abuse), then answer the question.

Sexual abuse of an inmate, detainee, or resident by another inmate, detainee, or resident includes any of the following acts, if the victim does not consent, is coerced into such act by overt or implied threats of violence, or is unable to consent or refuse:

Under what conditions do the listed acts between inmates count as sexual abuse?
options: If the acts are reported by a staff member within 24 hours
If the acts occur anywhere in the facility, regardless of consent, after a supervisor has reviewed the matter, as long as the unit team is notified
If the acts are witnessed by at least two other inmates
If the victim does not consent, is coerced by overt or implied threats of violence, or is unable to consent or refuse
questions.rationale: The acts count as sexual abuse of an inmate by another inmate "if the victim does not consent, is coerced into such act by overt or implied threats of violence, or is unable to consent or refuse."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.6 (Definitions related to sexual abuse), then answer the question.

Voyeurism by a staff member, contractor, or volunteer means an invasion of privacy of an inmate, detainee, or resident by staff for reasons unrelated to official duties, such as peering at an inmate who is using a toilet in his or her cell to perform bodily functions; requiring an inmate to expose his or her buttocks, genitals, or breasts; or taking images of all or part of an inmate's naked body or of an inmate performing bodily functions.

Which example of voyeurism by staff is given in the excerpt?
options: Peering at an inmate who is using a toilet in his or her cell to perform bodily functions
Observing an inmate from the control room during a scheduled count
Checking on an inmate who is sleeping during a security round
Reading an inmate's mail as part of a mail inspection
questions.rationale: Voyeurism is "an invasion of privacy... for reasons unrelated to official duties, such as peering at an inmate who is using a toilet in his or her cell," requiring an inmate to expose body parts, or taking images of an inmate's naked body.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.6 (Definitions related to sexual abuse), then answer the question.

(7) Any display by a staff member, contractor, or volunteer of his or her uncovered genitalia, buttocks, or breast in the presence of an inmate, detainee, or resident, and

Which of the following is listed as sexual abuse by a staff member, contractor, or volunteer?
options: Medical examinations conducted by a licensed practitioner as part of official duties
Any display of uncovered genitalia, buttocks, or breast in the presence of an inmate
Routine pat-down searches conducted according to agency policy
Escorting an inmate to a medical appointment
questions.rationale: The list includes "any display by a staff member, contractor, or volunteer of his or her uncovered genitalia, buttocks, or breast in the presence of an inmate, detainee, or resident."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.2 (Definitions), then answer the question.

(b) Representatives of the news media means persons whose principal employment is to gather or report news for:
(2) A news magazine which has a national circulation and is sold by newsstands and by mail subscription to the general public;

Which of the following qualifies as a news magazine under the definition of "representatives of the news media"?
options: A news magazine with national circulation sold by newsstands and mail subscription to the general public
A newsletter published monthly by a local club for its members
A magazine published for employees of a single company
A blog written by one individual for a small group of readers
questions.rationale: A qualifying news magazine is one "which has a national circulation and is sold by newsstands and by mail subscription to the general public."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.62 (Institutional visits), then answer the question.

(b) When media representatives visit the institutions, photographs of programs and activities may be taken, and media representatives may meet with groups of inmates engaged in authorized programs and activities. An inmate has the right not to be photographed and not to have his or her voice recorded by the media. A visiting representative of the media is required to obtain written permission from an inmate before photographing or recording the voice of an inmate participating in authorized programs and activities.

What must a visiting media representative obtain before photographing or recording the voice of an inmate who is participating in an authorized program?
options: Written permission from the inmate's family
Written permission from the inmate
Written permission from the Warden alone
Verbal permission from the housing unit officer
questions.rationale: "An inmate has the right not to be photographed and not to have his or her voice recorded by the media. A visiting representative of the media is required to obtain written permission from an inmate before photographing or recording the voice of an inmate."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.72 (Statutory restrictions requiring return of commercially published information or material which is sexually explicit or features nudity), then answer the question.

(2) Nudity means a pictorial depiction where genitalia or female breasts are exposed.
(4) Sexually explicit means a pictorial depiction of actual or simulated sexual acts including sexual intercourse, oral sex, or masturbation.

How does the excerpt define "sexually explicit" and "nudity"?
options: Sexually explicit is any depiction of a medical procedure; nudity is any depiction in a classroom
Sexually explicit is any written reference to a sexual act; nudity is any depiction of a person without a shirt
Sexually explicit is any depiction of kissing; nudity is any depiction of bare shoulders
Sexually explicit is a pictorial depiction of actual or simulated sexual acts; nudity is a pictorial depiction where genitalia or female breasts are exposed
questions.rationale: "Nudity means a pictorial depiction where genitalia or female breasts are exposed" and "Sexually explicit means a pictorial depiction of actual or simulated sexual acts including sexual intercourse, oral sex, or masturbation."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.72 (Statutory restrictions requiring return of commercially published information or material which is sexually explicit or features nudity), then answer the question.

(3) Features means the publication contains depictions of nudity or sexually explicit conduct on a routine or regular basis or promotes itself based upon such depictions in the case of individual one-time issues. Publications containing nudity illustrative of medical, educational, or anthropological content may be excluded from this definition.

Which publications may be excluded from the definition of a publication that "features" nudity?
options: Publications containing nudity illustrative of medical, educational, or anthropological content
Publications that are sent from a commercial publisher
Publications that contain nudity on a regular basis
Publications that promote themselves based on such depictions, according to the institution's local guidelines
questions.rationale: "Publications containing nudity illustrative of medical, educational, or anthropological content may be excluded from this definition."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 551.101 (Definitions), then answer the question.

(3) Concurrent federal and state sentences. For purpose of this rule, an inmate in a status described in paragraph (a) introductory text, (a)(1), or (a)(2) of this section and who is at the same time serving a state or federal sentence is not considered a pretrial inmate.

An inmate committed as a material witness is also serving a federal sentence at the same time. How does the excerpt treat him?
options: He is treated as a youthful inmate, according to the institution's local guidelines
He is treated as a juvenile
He is not considered a pretrial inmate
He is considered a pretrial inmate
questions.rationale: A person in a pretrial-type status "who is at the same time serving a state or federal sentence is not considered a pretrial inmate."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 551.115 (Recreation), then answer the question.

(e) Provisions of paragraphs (b) and (c) of this section must be carried out unless compelling security or safety reasons dictate otherwise. Institution staff shall document these reasons.

When may staff depart from the minimum recreation provisions for a pretrial inmate?
options: When the number of inmates exceeds the capacity of the recreation yard, when staff resources allow
When the pretrial inmate refuses to work
When the Warden is away from the institution
When compelling security or safety reasons dictate otherwise, and staff document those reasons
questions.rationale: The provisions "must be carried out unless compelling security or safety reasons dictate otherwise. Institution staff shall document these reasons."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 551.118 (Property), then answer the question.

(a) A pretrial inmate may retain personal property as authorized for convicted inmates housed in administrative detention units. (See 28 CFR part 541, subpart B.)
(b) Staff may store the pretrial inmate's unauthorized personal property until the individual is released, transferred to another facility, or sentenced and committed to a federal institution.

What may staff do with a pretrial inmate's unauthorized personal property?
options: Return it to the sender at the inmate's expense, unless the Warden has approved the cost
Destroy it after thirty days, with written documentation of the destruction kept for two years
Store it until the individual is released, transferred, or sentenced and committed to a federal institution
Store it until the end of the current fiscal year, and then dispose of it by approved methods
questions.rationale: "Staff may store the pretrial inmate's unauthorized personal property until the individual is released, transferred to another facility, or sentenced and committed to a federal institution."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.14 (Youthful inmates), then answer the question.

(b) In areas outside of housing units, agencies shall either:
(1) Maintain sight and sound separation between youthful inmates and adult inmates, or
(2) Provide direct staff supervision when youthful inmates and adult inmates have sight, sound, or physical contact.

In areas outside housing units, what must agencies do about youthful inmates and adult inmates?
options: Maintain sight and sound separation, or provide direct staff supervision when they have sight, sound, or physical contact
Place youthful inmates in isolation to avoid contact
Allow unsupervised contact if the youthful inmate agrees
Prohibit all contact between youthful and adult inmates in every area, when staff resources allow, after a supervisor has reviewed the matter
questions.rationale: Agencies "shall either: (1) maintain sight and sound separation between youthful inmates and adult inmates, or (2) provide direct staff supervision when youthful inmates and adult inmates have sight, sound, or physical contact."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.14 (Youthful inmates), then answer the question.

(c) Agencies shall make best efforts to avoid placing youthful inmates in isolation to comply with this provision. Absent exigent circumstances, agencies shall not deny youthful inmates daily large-muscle exercise and any legally required special education services to comply with this provision. Youthful inmates shall also have access to other programs and work opportunities to the extent possible.

What does paragraph (c) say about placing youthful inmates in isolation to comply with separation requirements?
options: Agencies may deny daily large-muscle exercise to youthful inmates in isolation, but shall provide special education
Agencies shall make best efforts to avoid it and, absent exigent circumstances, shall not deny daily large-muscle exercise or legally required special education
Agencies shall use isolation as the main method of separation, and shall provide daily exercise only on request
Agencies may deny special education to youthful inmates in isolation, but shall provide daily large-muscle exercise
questions.rationale: "Agencies shall make best efforts to avoid placing youthful inmates in isolation to comply with this provision. Absent exigent circumstances, agencies shall not deny youthful inmates daily large-muscle exercise and any legally required special education services."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.16 (Inmates with disabilities and inmates who are limited English proficient), then answer the question.

(a) The agency shall take appropriate steps to ensure that inmates with disabilities (including, for example, inmates who are deaf or hard of hearing, those who are blind or have low vision, or those who have intellectual, psychiatric, or speech disabilities), have an equal opportunity to participate in or benefit from all aspects of the agency's efforts to prevent, detect, and respond to sexual abuse and sexual harassment. Such steps shall include, when necessary to ensure effective communication with inmates who are deaf or hard of hearing, providing access to interpreters who can interpret effectively, accurately, and impartially, both receptively and expressively, using any necessary specialized vocabulary. In addition, the agency shall ensure that written materials are provided in formats or through methods that ensure effective communication with inmates with disabilities, including inmates who have intellectual disabilities, limited reading skills, or who are blind or have low vision. An agency is not required to take actions that it can demonstrate would result in a fundamental alteration in the nature of a service, program, or activity, or in undue financial and administrative burdens, as those terms are used in regulations promulgated under title II of the Americans With Disabilities Act, 28 CFR 35.164.

What must the agency ensure for inmates with disabilities regarding sexual abuse prevention efforts?
options: Access to a separate and less intensive version of the agency's efforts to prevent, detect, and respond
The ability to opt out of the agency's efforts to prevent, detect, and respond, with a signed waiver
An equal opportunity to participate in or benefit from all aspects of the agency's efforts to prevent, detect, and respond
A written notice of the agency's efforts to prevent, detect, and respond, with no interpreter provided
questions.rationale: The agency "shall take appropriate steps to ensure that inmates with disabilities... have an equal opportunity to participate in or benefit from all aspects of the agency's efforts to prevent, detect, and respond to sexual abuse and sexual harassment."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.17 (Hiring and promotion decisions), then answer the question.

(c) Before hiring new employees who may have contact with inmates, the agency shall:
(1) Perform a criminal background records check; and
(2) Consistent with Federal, State, and local law, make its best efforts to contact all prior institutional employers for information on substantiated allegations of sexual abuse or any resignation during a pending investigation of an allegation of sexual abuse.

Before hiring new employees who may have contact with inmates, what must the agency do?
options: Perform a criminal background records check, and contact local police departments in the applicant's home state, provided that the action is documented, under the direction of the senior officer present
Perform a criminal background records check and a credit check, and contact the applicant's personal references
Perform a medical and psychological examination, and contact the applicant's most recent employer only
Perform a criminal background records check and make best efforts to contact all prior institutional employers about substantiated sexual abuse allegations
questions.rationale: The agency shall "perform a criminal background records check" and "make its best efforts to contact all prior institutional employers for information on substantiated allegations of sexual abuse or any resignation during a pending investigation."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.34 (Specialized training: Investigations), then answer the question.

(a) In addition to the general training provided to all employees pursuant to § 115.31, the agency shall ensure that, to the extent the agency itself conducts sexual abuse investigations, its investigators have received training in conducting such investigations in confinement settings.
(b) Specialized training shall include techniques for interviewing sexual abuse victims, proper use of Miranda and Garrity warnings, sexual abuse evidence collection in confinement settings, and the criteria and evidence required to substantiate a case for administrative action or prosecution referral.

What special training must agency investigators have?
options: Training in forensic medical examination, including how to collect samples from victims of abuse
Training in the use of force and restraints, including the application of the Use of Force Team Technique
Training in conducting such investigations in confinement settings, including interviewing victims and evidence collection
General investigative training given to all employees, including how to conduct counts and document incidents, provided that the action is documented
questions.rationale: Investigators must have "received training in conducting such investigations in confinement settings," and specialized training includes interviewing sexual abuse victims, proper use of Miranda and Garrity warnings, and evidence collection.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.35 (Specialized training: Medical and mental health care), then answer the question.

(a) The agency shall ensure that all full- and part-time medical and mental health care practitioners who work regularly in its facilities have been trained in:
(1) How to detect and assess signs of sexual abuse and sexual harassment;
(2) How to preserve physical evidence of sexual abuse;
(3) How to respond effectively and professionally to victims of sexual abuse and sexual harassment; and
(4) How and to whom to report allegations or suspicions of sexual abuse and sexual harassment.

What topics must training for full- and part-time medical and mental health care practitioners cover?
options: How to administer discipline, impose sanctions, and review inmate appeals through the Administrative Remedy Program
How to supervise inmates in housing units, conduct counts, and respond to emergencies in the dining hall
How to prepare incident reports, document the use of force, and review restraint placements every two hours
How to detect and assess signs of sexual abuse and sexual harassment, preserve physical evidence, and respond effectively and professionally to victims
questions.rationale: Practitioners must be trained in how to detect and assess signs of sexual abuse and sexual harassment, how to preserve physical evidence, how to respond effectively and professionally to victims, and how and to whom to report allegations.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.87 (Data collection), then answer the question.

(a) The agency shall collect accurate, uniform data for every allegation of sexual abuse at facilities under its direct control using a standardized instrument and set of definitions.
(b) The agency shall aggregate the incident-based sexual abuse data at least annually.

What does the agency collect under the data collection standard?
options: Accurate data for allegations of sexual abuse involving staff only, using definitions chosen by each facility
Accurate, uniform data for every allegation of sexual abuse at facilities under its direct control, using a standardized instrument and set of definitions
Accurate data for every allegation of sexual abuse, collected by each inmate in a daily log and reviewed by the Warden
Accurate, uniform data for every substantiated allegation of sexual abuse at its largest facility, using a standardized instrument, provided that the action is documented
questions.rationale: Section 115.87 requires data collection "for every allegation of sexual abuse at facilities under its direct control using a standardized instrument and set of definitions."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.88 (Data review for corrective action), then answer the question.

(a) The agency shall review data collected and aggregated pursuant to § 115.87 in order to assess and improve the effectiveness of its sexual abuse prevention, detection, and response policies, practices, and training, including by:
(1) Identifying problem areas;

What does the agency do with the sexual abuse data it collects?
options: Destroys it after thirty days to protect the privacy of the alleged victims and the accused
Reviews it only to decide which individual staff members should be disciplined for sexual abuse allegations
Reviews it to assess and improve the effectiveness of its sexual abuse prevention, detection, and response policies, practices, and training
Sends it to the news media each quarter, with the names of the alleged victims and abusers removed
questions.rationale: The agency "shall review data collected and aggregated pursuant to § 115.87 in order to assess and improve the effectiveness of its sexual abuse prevention, detection, and response policies, practices, and training."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 115.89 (Data storage, publication, and destruction), then answer the question.

(c) Before making aggregated sexual abuse data publicly available, the agency shall remove all personal identifiers.

What must the agency do with sexual abuse data before making it publicly available?
options: Add the names of the accused staff
Add the inmates' register numbers
Add the cell number of the victim
Remove all personal identifiers
questions.rationale: Paragraph (c) states: "Before making aggregated sexual abuse data publicly available, the agency shall remove all personal identifiers."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.71 (Procedures), then answer the question.

(2) At medium security, high security, and administrative institutions, an inmate may receive softcover publications (for example, paperback books, newspaper, clippings, magazines, and other similar items) only from the publisher, from a book club, or from a bookstore.
(3) At minimum security and low security institutions, an inmate any receive softcover publications (other than newspapers) from any source.

How do the rules for softcover publications differ between medium security and minimum security institutions?
options: Medium security institutions allow softcover publications from any source; minimum and low security allow them only from a bookstore
Medium security institutions allow softcover publications only from the publisher, book club, or bookstore; minimum and low security allow them (other than newspapers) from any source
Medium security institutions allow only newspapers; minimum and low security allow only paperback books
Both types of institution allow softcover publications from any source, but minimum security requires prior approval
questions.rationale: At medium, high, and administrative institutions softcover publications come only from a publisher, book club, or bookstore; at minimum and low security institutions an inmate may receive softcover publications (other than newspapers) from any source.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.71 (Procedures), then answer the question.

(4) The Unit Manager may make an exception to the provisions of paragraphs (a)(1) and (2) of this section of the publication is no longer available from the publisher, book club, or bookstore. The Unit Manager shall require that the inmate provide written documentation that the publication is no longer available from these sources. The approval or disapproval of any request for an exception is to be documented, in writing, on an Authorization to Receive a Package form which will be used to secure the item.

Who may make an exception to the source restrictions if a publication is no longer available, and what must the inmate provide?
options: The Warden, who requires a letter from the author explaining that the work is out of print
The chaplain, who requires the inmate to submit a request through the Administrative Remedy Program, as long as the unit team is notified
The Unit Manager, who requires the inmate to provide written documentation that the publication is no longer available
The Captain, who requires the inmate to pay for the replacement of the publication
questions.rationale: "The Unit Manager may make an exception... The Unit Manager shall require that the inmate provide written documentation that the publication is no longer available from these sources."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.71 (Procedures), then answer the question.

(c) The Warden may not establish an excluded list of publications. This means the Warden shall review the individual publication prior to the rejection of that publication. Rejection of several issues of a subscription publication is not sufficient reason to reject the subscription publication in its entirety.

Which statement about an excluded list of publications is supported by paragraph (c)?
options: The Warden may reject a whole subscription after several issues have been rejected
The Warden may not establish an excluded list and must review each individual publication before rejecting it
The Warden may establish an excluded list if the Regional Director approves it
The Warden may establish an excluded list limited to publications of a violent nature, unless local procedures say otherwise
questions.rationale: "The Warden may not establish an excluded list of publications... Rejection of several issues of a subscription publication is not sufficient reason to reject the subscription publication in its entirety."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.71 (Procedures), then answer the question.

(d) Where a publication is found unacceptable, the Warden shall promptly advise the inmate in writing of the decision and the reasons for it. The notice must contain reference to the specific article(s) or material(s) considered objectionable. The Warden shall permit the inmate an opportunity to review this material for purposes of filing an appeal under the Administrative Remedy Program unless such review may provide the inmate with information of a nature which is deemed to pose a threat or detriment to the security, good order or discipline of the institution or to encourage or instruct in criminal activity.

What must the Warden's notice to the inmate about an unacceptable publication contain?
options: The decision and a copy of the rejected publication, which the inmate may keep during any appeal, according to the institution's local guidelines
The decision and reasons, with a general statement that the publication was unsuitable
The decision and reasons, with reference to the specific article(s) or material(s) considered objectionable
The decision only, without the reasons, to avoid repeating the objectionable material
questions.rationale: "The Warden shall promptly advise the inmate in writing of the decision and the reasons for it. The notice must contain reference to the specific article(s) or material(s) considered objectionable."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.71 (Procedures), then answer the question.

(e) The Warden shall provide the publisher or sender of an unacceptable publication a copy of the rejection letter. The Warden shall advise the publisher or sender that he may obtain an independent review of the rejection by writing to the Regional Director within 20 days of receipt of the rejection letter. The Warden shall return the rejected publication to the publisher or sender of the material unless the inmate indicates an intent to file an appeal under the Administrative Remedy Program, in which case the Warden shall retain the rejected material at the institution for review. In case of appeal, if the rejection is sustained, the rejected publication shall be returned when appeal or legal use is completed.

How may a publisher or sender obtain an independent review of the rejection of a publication?
options: By writing to the Warden within 20 days of the date of the rejection letter
By writing to the General Counsel within 30 days of receiving the rejection letter
By writing to the Regional Director within 60 days of the publication's arrival at the institution
By writing to the Regional Director within 20 days of receiving the rejection letter
questions.rationale: The Warden "shall advise the publisher or sender that he may obtain an independent review of the rejection by writing to the Regional Director within 20 days of receipt of the rejection letter."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.64 (Press pools), then answer the question.

(c) All members of the press pool are selected by their peers and consist of not more than one representative from each of the following groups:
(1) The national and international news services;
(2) The television and radio networks and outlets;
(3) The news magazines and newspapers; and
(4) All media in the local community where the institution is located. If no interest has been expressed by one or more of these groups, no representative from such group need be selected.

How are the members of a press pool chosen?
options: They are selected by the inmate population, with not more than one representative from the local community
They are selected by the Warden, with not more than one representative from each news organization
They are selected by their peers, with not more than one representative from each of four groups
They are selected by lottery, with not more than two representatives from each of three groups
questions.rationale: "All members of the press pool are selected by their peers and consist of not more than one representative from each" of national and international news services, television and radio, news magazines and newspapers, and local community media.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.64 (Press pools), then answer the question.

(d) All news material generated by such a press pool is made available to all media without right of first publication or broadcast.

What happens to news material generated by a press pool?
options: It is held by the pool members for twenty-four hours before it is shared with other media
It is made available only to the national and international news services
It is made available to the Warden first and then released to the pool members
It is made available to all media without right of first publication or broadcast
questions.rationale: "All news material generated by such a press pool is made available to all media without right of first publication or broadcast."

options: The inmate's place of incarceration
The inmate's general institutional assignments
The inmate's medical history
The inmate's register number
The inmate's disciplinary record
questions.rationale: Public-record information limited to name, register number, place of incarceration, age, race, conviction and sentencing data, past movement, and general institutional assignments. Medical and disciplinary records are not on the list.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.65 (Release of information), then answer the question.

(c) Information in paragraphs (b)(1) through (8) of this section may not be released if confidential for protection cases.
(d) A request for additional information concerning an inmate by a representative of the news media is referred to the Public Information Officer, Central Office, Washington, DC.

Where is a request by the news media for additional information concerning an inmate referred?
options: To the Regional Director in the region where the inmate is housed
To the inmate's unit team for approval and a written response
To the Public Information Officer, Central Office, Washington, DC
To the Warden, who may release any information the Warden considers appropriate
questions.rationale: "A request for additional information concerning an inmate by a representative of the news media is referred to the Public Information Officer, Central Office, Washington, DC." Information may also not be released for protection cases.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.41 (Institutional referral), then answer the question.

(a) The Warden shall submit a recommendation for referral of an inmate for placement in a control unit to the Regional Director in the region where the inmate is located.
(b) The Warden shall consider the following factors in a recommendation for control unit placement.

Who submits a recommendation for referral of an inmate for placement in a control unit, and to whom?
options: The Warden submits it to the Regional Director in the region where the inmate is located
The Captain submits it to the Warden of the institution where the inmate is located, in accordance with the posted schedule
The unit team submits it to the Discipline Hearing Officer for a hearing
The Regional Director submits it to the General Counsel for a final decision
questions.rationale: "The Warden shall submit a recommendation for referral of an inmate for placement in a control unit to the Regional Director in the region where the inmate is located."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.41 (Institutional referral), then answer the question.

(1) Any incident during confinement in which the inmate has caused injury to other persons.
(2) Any incident in which the inmate has expressed threats to the life or well-being of other persons.
(3) Any incident involving possession by the inmate of deadly weapons or dangerous drugs.
(4) Any incident in which the inmate is involved in a disruption of the orderly operation of a prison, jail or other correctional institution.
(5) An escape from a correctional institution.
(6) An escape attempt. Depending on the circumstances, an escape attempt, considered alone or together with an inmate's prior history, may warrant consideration for a control unit placement.
(7) The nature of the offense for which committed. An inmate may not be considered solely on the nature of the crime which resulted in that inmate's incarceration; however, the nature of the crime may be considered in combination with other factor(s) as described in paragraph (b) of this section.

Select ALL of the factors the Warden shall consider in a recommendation for control unit placement.
options: An escape from a correctional institution
The inmate's religious affiliation
Any incident involving possession of deadly weapons or dangerous drugs
The inmate's educational level
Any incident in which the inmate caused injury to other persons
questions.rationale: Factors include incidents causing injury, threats to life, possession of deadly weapons or dangerous drugs, disruption of orderly operation, escape, escape attempt, and the nature of the offense (in combination with other factors). Religion and education are not listed.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.41 (Institutional referral), then answer the question.

(7) The nature of the offense for which committed. An inmate may not be considered solely on the nature of the crime which resulted in that inmate's incarceration; however, the nature of the crime may be considered in combination with other factor(s) as described in paragraph (b) of this section.

What does paragraph (b)(7) imply about the nature of the offense for which an inmate was committed?
options: It may never be considered under any circumstances
It may be considered alone, since it shows the inmate's dangerousness, for the duration of the incident
It may be considered only in combination with other factors, and not alone
It may be considered only if the offense involved a weapon
questions.rationale: "An inmate may not be considered solely on the nature of the crime which resulted in that inmate's incarceration; however, the nature of the crime may be considered in combination with other factor(s)."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.41 (Institutional referral), then answer the question.

(c) The Warden may not refer an inmate for placement in a control unit:
(1) If the inmate shows evidence of significant mental disorder or major physical disabilities as documented in a mental health evaluation or a physical examination;
(2) On the basis that the inmate is a protection case, e.g., a homosexual, an informant, etc., unless the inmate meets other criteria as described in paragraph (b) of this section.

In which situation may the Warden NOT refer an inmate for placement in a control unit?
options: The inmate has been involved in an escape attempt that was prevented by staff, where the circumstances reasonably call for it, in most circumstances
The inmate has expressed threats to the well-being of other persons
The inmate was found in possession of dangerous drugs in a housing unit
The inmate shows evidence of significant mental disorder or major physical disabilities documented in an evaluation or examination
questions.rationale: The Warden may not refer an inmate "if the inmate shows evidence of significant mental disorder or major physical disabilities as documented in a mental health evaluation or a physical examination," or solely because he is a protection case.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.46 (Programs and services), then answer the question.

(i) Mental health services. During the first 30-day period in a control unit, staff shall schedule the control unit inmate for a psychological evaluation conducted by a psychologist. Additional individual evaluations shall occur every 30 days. The psychologist shall perform and/or supervise needed psychological services. Psychiatric services will be provided when necessary. Inmates requiring prescribed psychotropic medication are not ordinarily housed in a control unit.

What mental health schedule applies to control unit inmates?
options: A psychological evaluation before admission, and additional evaluations only after an incident
A psychological evaluation on request only, and additional evaluations every year
A psychological evaluation during the first 30-day period, and additional individual evaluations every 30 days
A psychological evaluation during the first 7 days, and additional evaluations every 90 days
questions.rationale: "During the first 30-day period in a control unit, staff shall schedule the control unit inmate for a psychological evaluation conducted by a psychologist. Additional individual evaluations shall occur every 30 days."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.46 (Programs and services), then answer the question.

(j) Religion. Staff shall issue religious materials upon request, limited by security consideration and housekeeping rules in the unit. This material may come from an inmate's personal property or from the chaplain's office. The institutional chaplains shall make at least weekly visits to the control unit. While individual prayer and/or worship is allowed in a control unit, religious assemblies or group meetings are not allowed.

Which statement about religion in a control unit is supported by the excerpt?
options: Individual prayer is not allowed, but religious materials may be issued at the chaplain's discretion
Group worship is allowed once a week in the unit's dayroom under staff supervision
Religious materials are not issued, but chaplains visit the unit once a month
Individual prayer or worship is allowed, but religious assemblies or group meetings are not allowed
questions.rationale: "While individual prayer and/or worship is allowed in a control unit, religious assemblies or group meetings are not allowed." Chaplains make at least weekly visits.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 541.46 (Programs and services), then answer the question.

(m) Visiting. Visits for inmates confined in a control unit are conducted in a controlled visiting area, separated from regular visiting facilities. Staff shall allot a minimum of four hours per month visiting time to a control unit inmate. The number of consecutive hours visiting on a particular day may be limited by the number of visitors waiting to visit. All visitors must be on the inmate's approved visiting list.

What is the minimum visiting time for a control unit inmate?
options: A minimum of four hours per month, in a controlled visiting area separated from regular visiting facilities
A minimum of four hours per week, in the regular visiting room when it is not crowded
A minimum of eight hours per month, in a controlled visiting area with no restrictions on visitors
A minimum of two hours per month, in the regular visiting room with extra supervision
questions.rationale: "Visits for inmates confined in a control unit are conducted in a controlled visiting area, separated from regular visiting facilities. Staff shall allot a minimum of four hours per month visiting time." All visitors must be on the approved visiting list.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 551.151 (Definitions), then answer the question.

(b) For purpose of this rule, witness is defined as someone who has information or evidence concerning a crime, and provides information regarding this knowledge to a law enforcement agency. Where the witness is a minor, the term “witness” includes an appropriate family member. The term “witness” does not include defense witnesses or those individuals involved in the crime as a perpetrator or accomplice.

Who is NOT included in the definition of a "witness" under the notification rule?
options: A person who provides information about a crime to a law enforcement agency, after a supervisor has reviewed the matter
An appropriate family member, where the witness is a minor
A person who has information or evidence concerning a crime
Defense witnesses and individuals involved in the crime as a perpetrator or accomplice
questions.rationale: A witness provides information to law enforcement; "The term 'witness' does not include defense witnesses or those individuals involved in the crime as a perpetrator or accomplice."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 551.152 (Procedures), then answer the question.

(a) A victim and/or witness of a serious crime who wants to be notified of a specific inmate's release must make this request to the United States Attorney in the district where the prosecution occurred. Requests for notification received by the Bureau of Prisons directly from a victim and/or witness will be referred to the U.S. Attorney in the district of prosecution for approval.

To whom must a victim or witness of a serious crime make a request to be notified of an inmate's release?
options: The United States Attorney in the district where the prosecution occurred
The Warden of the institution where the inmate is housed
The Public Information Officer at the Central Office
The Regional Director in the region where the inmate is located, in accordance with the posted schedule
questions.rationale: "A victim and/or witness of a serious crime who wants to be notified of a specific inmate's release must make this request to the United States Attorney in the district where the prosecution occurred." Requests made to the Bureau are referred there.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.20 (Inmate correspondence with representatives of the news media), then answer the question.

(a) An inmate may write through “special mail” to representatives of the news media specified by name or title (see § 540.2(b)).
(b) The inmate may not receive compensation or anything of value for correspondence with the news media. The inmate may not act as reporter.
(c) Representatives of the news media may initiate correspondence with an inmate. Staff shall open incoming correspondence from representatives of the media and inspect for contraband, for its qualification as media correspondence, and for content which is likely to promote either illegal activity or conduct contrary to Bureau regulations.

Which statement about inmate correspondence with news media is supported by the excerpt?
options: An inmate may write through special mail to the media only if the Warden approves each letter, provided that the action is documented
An inmate may write through general mail to the media and may receive payment for articles
An inmate may write through special mail to the media but may not receive compensation or act as a reporter
An inmate may not write to the media but may receive mail from news representatives
questions.rationale: An inmate "may write through 'special mail' to representatives of the news media," but "may not receive compensation or anything of value" and "may not act as reporter." Staff inspect incoming media mail for contraband and illegal content.

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.21 (Payment of postage), then answer the question.

(d) An inmate who has neither funds nor sufficient postage and who wishes to mail legal mail (includes courts and attorneys) or Administrative Remedy forms will be provided the postage stamps for such mailing. To prevent abuses of this provision, the Warden may impose restrictions on the free legal and administrative remedy mailings.

Under what circumstances will an inmate with neither funds nor sufficient postage be provided stamps?
options: To mail letters to the news media, at the Warden's discretion
To mail packages only, once each month
To mail any number of personal letters, with no restrictions
To mail legal mail (to courts or attorneys) or Administrative Remedy forms, subject to restrictions to prevent abuse
questions.rationale: "An inmate who has neither funds nor sufficient postage and who wishes to mail legal mail (includes courts and attorneys) or Administrative Remedy forms will be provided the postage stamps for such mailing. To prevent abuses of this provision, the Warden may impose restrictions."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.21 (Payment of postage), then answer the question.

(j) Inmates may not be permitted to receive stamps or stamped items (e.g., envelopes embossed with stamps, postal cards with postage affixed) other than by issuance from the institution or by purchase from commissary.

How may an inmate obtain stamps or stamped items?
options: From any source, as long as the stamps are inspected first
Only by issuance from the institution or by purchase from the commissary
From family members, who may mail stamped envelopes to the inmate
From other inmates, with the approval of the unit officer
questions.rationale: "Inmates may not be permitted to receive stamps or stamped items... other than by issuance from the institution or by purchase from commissary."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.22 (Special postal services), then answer the question.

(a) An inmate, at no cost to the government, may send correspondence by registered, certified, or insured mail, and may request a return receipt.
(c) Certified mail is sent first class at the inmate's expense.
(d) An inmate may not be provided such services as express mail, COD, private carriers, or stamp collecting while confined.

Which mail services may an inmate NOT be provided while confined?
options: Insurance on outgoing personal correspondence, unless an emergency requires otherwise
Registered, certified, or insured mail
Express mail, COD, private carriers, or stamp collecting
A return receipt on registered mail
questions.rationale: An inmate may send registered, certified, or insured mail at no cost to the government and request a return receipt, but "may not be provided such services as express mail, COD, private carriers, or stamp collecting while confined."

questions.stem:
Read the following excerpt from 28 CFR § 540.25 (Change of address and forwarding of mail for inmates), then answer the question.

(d) Except as provided in paragraphs (e) through (g) of this section, all mail received for a released or transferred inmate will be returned to the U.S. Postal Service for disposition in accordance with U.S. Postal Service regulations.
(e) Staff shall use all means practicable to forward special mail.
(f) Staff shall forward inmate general correspondence to the new address for a period of 30 days.

How is mail handled for an inmate who has been transferred?
options: General correspondence is forwarded for 30 days, and special mail is held at the institution until requested, as determined by the shift supervisor
All mail is returned to the U.S. Postal Service for disposition, with no forwarding
Special mail is returned to the sender, and general correspondence is forwarded for 90 days
Special mail is forwarded by all means practicable, and general correspondence is forwarded to the new address for 30 days
questions.rationale: "Staff shall use all means practicable to forward special mail. Staff shall forward inmate general correspondence to the new address for a period of 30 days." Other mail is returned to the U.S. Postal Service.

questions.stem:
After an inmate insults Officer Brandt in front of the unit, a senior officer says, "Cuff him to the cell door for an hour. That will teach him." The inmate is now calm and sitting on his bunk.

What is the correct response?
options: Comply, because a senior officer has authority over unit discipline
Decline, but only if the Warden has not already approved the action
Decline, because force and restraints may not be used to punish an inmate
Comply, but shorten the time to thirty minutes and note it in the log
questions.rationale:
Restraints and force are for control and safety, never punishment, and securing an inmate to a fixed object such as a cell door is specifically prohibited.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.22: “(b) Force may not be used to punish an inmate.”
28 CFR § 552.22: “(1) As a method of punishing an inmate.”

questions.stem:
After a brief struggle, Officer Hale applies restraints. The inmate says he is "fine" and refuses to go to the infirmary. No injuries are visible.

What is Officer Hale's responsibility?
options: Accept the inmate's statement and note it in the log, as determined by the shift supervisor, based on the information available at the time
Wait until the next scheduled sick call, a day later
Make sure the inmate is examined by qualified health personnel, and that any injuries are immediately treated
Ask a supervisor whether an exam is convenient
questions.rationale:
An examination by qualified health personnel is required after any use of force or forcible application of restraints, regardless of what the inmate says.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.26: “(b) After any use of force or forcible application of restraints, the inmate shall be examined by qualified health personnel, and any injuries noted, immediately treated.”

questions.stem:
Officer Lindqvist used chemical agents on a barricaded inmate, and no one was hurt. A coworker suggests skipping the report because "nothing happened."

What should Officer Lindqvist do?
options: Skip the report, since it is needed only when someone is injured
Record it only in the shift log, which is enough without a report
Wait for the inmate to complain before writing a report
Document the incident, because the use of chemical agents must be documented, and a copy goes in the inmate's central file
questions.rationale:
All incidents involving use of force, chemical agents, or less-than-lethal weapons must be documented, with a copy in the central file.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.27: “Staff shall appropriately document all incidents involving the use of force, chemical agents, or less-than-lethal weapons. Staff shall also document, in writing, the use of restraints on an inmate who becomes violent or displays signs of imminent violence. A copy of the report shall be placed in the inmate's central file.”

questions.stem:
Officer Wells is an observer on a suicide watch. Midway through the shift, the inmate paces, mutters, and tears a blanket into strips.

What must Officer Wells do with that information?
options: Wait until the end of the shift to remember what happened
Document significant observed behavior in the suicide watch log book
Record it in the inmate's visiting file
Tell the inmate's cellmate to keep an eye on him
questions.rationale:
Observers are to document significant observed behavior in a log book.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.42: “(c) Suicide watch log. Observers are to document significant observed behavior in a log book.”

questions.stem:
A hostage incident has begun in a housing unit. A new officer asks what the Bureau's primary goals are.

What is the correct answer?
options: To capture the hostage takers alive for prosecution
To negotiate a settlement of the inmates' grievances
To protect the institution's reputation by limiting media attention
To safely free the hostage(s) and regain control of the institution
questions.rationale:
The primary objectives in all hostage situations are to safely free the hostage(s) and regain control of the institution.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.30: “The Bureau of Prisons primary objectives in all hostage situations are to safely free the hostage(s) and to regain control of the institution.”

questions.stem:
At 2:00 p.m., Officer Kowalski sees an inmate pass a weapon to another inmate in the yard. He is sure the act is a prohibited act.

What starts the formal discipline process?
options: Referring the matter directly to the Discipline Hearing Officer
Asking the inmate to sign a statement admitting the act
Issuing the inmate an incident report describing the incident and the prohibited acts charged
Placing the inmate in the Special Housing Unit before any paperwork is completed, pending review by the appropriate official
questions.rationale:
The discipline process begins when staff witness or reasonably believe a prohibited act occurred, and a staff member issues an incident report.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.5: “(a) Incident report. The discipline process starts when staff witness or reasonably believe that you committed a prohibited act. A staff member will issue you an incident report describing the incident and the prohibited act(s) you are charged with committing. You will ordinarily receive the incident report within 24 hours of staff becoming aware of your involvement in the incident.”

questions.stem:
A mailroom officer receives a letter for an inmate. The envelope carries a law firm's return address and the front is marked "Special Mail—Open only in the presence of the inmate."

How should the letter be opened?
options: By the Warden, after the contents have been copied
Only in the inmate's presence, to check for physical contraband and qualifying enclosures, without reading or copying it
In the mailroom, then read for threats before delivery
In the housing unit by the unit officer, without the inmate present, subject to the Warden's discretion, as long as no other inmate is affected
questions.rationale:
Properly identified and marked special mail is opened only in the inmate's presence, inspected for contraband, and not read or copied.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.18: “(a) The Warden shall open incoming special mail only in the presence of the inmate for inspection for physical contraband and the qualification of any enclosures as special mail. The correspondence may not be read or copied if the sender is adequately identified on the envelope, and the front of the envelope is marked “Special Mail—Open only in the presence of the inmate”.”

questions.stem:
Family members ask how much visiting time a general population inmate is guaranteed each month.

What is the minimum?
options: Four hours
Two hours
Twelve hours
Eight hours
questions.rationale:
The Warden must allow each inmate at least four hours of visiting time per month, limiting only to avoid chronic overcrowding.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.43: “The Warden shall allow each inmate a minimum of four hours visiting time per month. The Warden may limit the length or frequency of visits only to avoid chronic overcrowding. The Warden may establish a guideline for the maximum number of persons who may visit an inmate at one time, to prevent overcrowding in the visiting room or unusual difficulty in supervising a visit. Exceptions may be made to any local guideline when indicated by special circumstances, such as distance the visitor must travel, frequency of the inmate's visits, or health problems of the inmate or visitor.”

questions.stem:
A new officer asks a Lieutenant what separates administrative detention from disciplinary segregation in a Special Housing Unit.

What is the correct explanation?
options: Administrative detention is punitive and imposed by the Warden; disciplinary segregation is non-punitive and imposed by the DHO
Both are non-punitive statuses, but administrative detention is for protection and disciplinary segregation is for transfers
Administrative detention is non-punitive; disciplinary segregation is a punitive status imposed only by a DHO as a sanction
Both are punitive statuses, but administrative detention can be imposed by the unit team and segregation by the DHO
questions.rationale:
Administrative detention removes an inmate from the general population for safety or security reasons and is non-punitive, while disciplinary segregation is punitive and imposed only by a DHO.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.22: “(a) Administrative detention status. Administrative detention status is an administrative status which removes you from the general population when necessary to ensure the safety, security, and orderly operation of correctional facilities, or protect the public. Administrative detention status is non-punitive, and can occur for a variety of reasons.”
28 CFR § 541.22: “(b) Disciplinary segregation status. Disciplinary segregation status is a punitive status imposed only by a Discipline Hearing Officer (DHO) as a sanction for committing a prohibited act(s).”

questions.stem:
Officer Adeyemi is working a housing unit. An inmate locked in his cell refuses to come out for a scheduled transfer. He is not threatening anyone and has no weapon. The shift supervisor says the transfer is not urgent.

What should happen before any decision to use force is made?
options: The officer leaves the inmate alone for the shift and writes an incident report without further steps
The ranking custodial official, a mental health professional, and others confer, then someone is chosen to seek the inmate's voluntary cooperation
The officer orders the inmate to submit to restraints through the food slot and reports a refusal if he does not comply, under the direction of the senior officer present
The Use of Force Team enters at once in protective gear to prevent the situation from getting worse
questions.rationale:
Because the inmate is in an area that can be isolated and poses no immediate threat, any force would be "calculated." Before a calculated use of force, officials must gather information and identify staff to seek voluntary cooperation.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.23: “Prior to any calculated use of force, the ranking custodial official (ordinarily the Captain or shift Lieutenant), a designated mental health professional, and others shall confer and gather pertinent information about the inmate and the immediate situation. Based on their assessment of that information, they shall identify a staff member(s) to attempt to obtain the inmate's voluntary cooperation and, using the knowledge they have gained about the inmate and the incident, determine if use of force is necessary.”

questions.stem:
Officer Carrow responds to a fight in the yard and applies handcuffs to an inmate who was swinging at others. The inmate is now under physical control.

According to policy, who must be notified immediately, and for what purpose?
options: The inmate's unit team, for a decision on how the incident report will be classified
The Regional Director, for a decision on whether the inmate should be transferred
The health services administrator, for a decision on whether the inmate needs surgery
The Warden or designee, for a decision on whether the restraints should continue
questions.rationale:
Temporary restraints may be applied to prevent harm, but after control is gained the Warden or designee decides whether they continue.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.22: “(d) Where immediate use of restraints is indicated, staff may temporarily apply such restraints to an inmate to prevent that inmate from hurting self, staff, or others, and/or to prevent serious property damage. When the temporary application of restraints is determined necessary, and after staff have gained control of the inmate, the Warden or designee is to be notified immediately for a decision on whether the use of restraints should continue.”

questions.stem:
A supervisor is reviewing how restraints were used on four inmates today. Which of the four uses breaks the rules on restraint equipment?

Which use is prohibited?
options: Handcuffs were fastened to a cell door grill to keep a calm inmate in place for the night
Handcuffs were kept on an inmate who continued to resist after control was gained
Handcuffs were applied temporarily to stop an inmate from injuring himself
Soft restraints were applied by the Use of Force Team after other means had failed, where the circumstances reasonably call for it
questions.rationale:
Restraint equipment may be used temporarily to prevent injury and on inmates who continue to resist, but may not be used to secure an inmate to a fixed object (except under the four-point restraint rule).

Source — 28 CFR § 552.22: “(4) To secure an inmate to a fixed object, such as a cell door or cell grill, except as provided in § 552.24.”

questions.stem:
An inmate has been placed in four-point restraints on a bed. Officer Ng has been checking him every 30 minutes because the unit is short-staffed.

What should a supervisor tell Officer Ng?
options: Staff may check the inmate every 30 minutes if a camera is in the room
Staff must check the inmate at least every two hours, along with the Lieutenant
Staff must check the inmate at least every 15 minutes
Staff must check the inmate at least once every hour
questions.rationale:
Frequent checks protect circulation and welfare; the 15-minute interval is a minimum.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.24: “(d) Staff shall check the inmate at least every 15 minutes, both to ensure that the restraints are not hampering circulation and for the general welfare of the inmate. When an inmate is restrained to a bed, staff shall periodically rotate the inmate's position to avoid soreness or stiffness.”

questions.stem:
Lieutenant Morales is conducting the two-hour review of an inmate in four-point restraints. The inmate is quiet, says he needs the toilet, and has not resisted since being placed.
