What does the policy require at this review?
options: The inmate is moved to a segregation cell until the next review
The inmate is asked to sign a statement that he is calm
The inmate is released from all restraints regardless of his condition
The inmate is given the opportunity to use the toilet
questions.rationale:
At every two-hour review the inmate must be afforded the opportunity to use the toilet unless he is actively resisting or violent while being released.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.24: “(e) A review of the inmate's placement in four-point restraints shall be made by a Lieutenant every two hours to determine if the use of restraints has had the required calming effect and so that the inmate may be released from these restraints (completely or to lesser restraints) as soon as possible. At every two-hour review, the inmate will be afforded the opportunity to use the toilet, unless the inmate is continuing to actively resist or becomes violent while being released from the restraints for this purpose.”

questions.stem:
An inmate who was restrained after a violent episode now refuses to walk to the Special Housing Unit. Officers are tempted to drag him by his arms.

What does the policy allow staff to do?
options: Drag the inmate by his restraints to save time
Physically move the inmate by lifting and carrying him to the appropriate destination
Strike the inmate until he agrees to walk
Leave the inmate in the hallway until his shift ends, based on the information available at the time
questions.rationale:
If an inmate in a forcible restraint situation refuses to move on his own, staff may lift and carry him to the destination.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.22: “(e) Staff may apply restraints (for example, handcuffs) to the inmate who continues to resist after staff achieve physical control of that inmate, and may apply restraints to any inmate who is placed under control by the Use of Force Team Technique. If an inmate in a forcible restraint situation refuses to move to another area on his own, staff may physically move that inmate by lifting and carrying the inmate to the appropriate destination.”

questions.stem:
A nurse offers to give an agitated inmate a sedative so that the night shift can have a quiet unit. The inmate has not been assessed by a physician.

What does policy say about this plan?
options: It is acceptable if the nurse agrees and the Lieutenant is notified
It is acceptable if soft restraints are not available
Medication may not be used as a restraint solely for security purposes
It is acceptable if the inmate has a history of violence
questions.rationale:
A sedative given only to control behavior for security reasons is medication used as a restraint, which is prohibited.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.22: “(i) Medication may not be used as a restraint solely for security purposes.”

questions.stem:
An inmate returns to the institution after a contact visit in the visiting room. A new officer asks whether a visual search is permitted without any further suspicion.

What is the correct answer?
options: Yes; re-entry after a contact visit is sufficient to justify a visual search, which must be made in a manner that assures as much privacy as practicable
No; a visual search is permitted only after finding contraband in a pat search
Yes; but the officer must conduct the search in the visiting room in front of the visitors, as long as the unit team is notified, provided that the action is documented
No; a visual search requires the Warden's written approval each time
questions.rationale:
Re-entry after a contact visit is one of the examples the regulation gives as enough to justify a visual search, and privacy must be assured as much as practicable.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.11: “(1) Staff may conduct a visual search where there is reasonable belief that contraband may be concealed on the person, or a good opportunity for concealment has occured. For example, placement in a special housing unit (see 28 CFR part 541, subpart B), leaving the institution, or re-entry into an institution after contact with the public (after a community trip, court transfer, or after a “contact” visit in a visiting room) is sufficient to justify a visual search. The visual search shall be made in a manner designed to assure as much privacy to the inmate as practicable.”

questions.stem:
Officer Vance is about to search an inmate's housing area. An inmate asks, "Don't you have to give me notice and let me watch?"

What is the correct response?
options: Yes; staff must have a supervisor approve the search and have the inmate present to observe it
Yes; staff must give the inmate 24-hour notice and allow him to be present, and then leave the area in order, after a supervisor has reviewed the matter
No; staff may search without notice or approval, but need not restore the area to its original order
No; staff may search without notice, approval, or the inmate present, but should leave the area as nearly as practicable in its original order
questions.rationale:
Staff may search an inmate's housing and work area without notice or prior approval and without the inmate present, and must leave it as nearly as practicable in its original order.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.14: “(a) Staff may search an inmate's housing and work area, and personal items contained within those areas, without notice to or prior approval from the inmate and without the inmate's presence.”
28 CFR § 552.14: “(b) Staff conducting the search shall leave the housing or work area as nearly as practicable in its original order.”

questions.stem:
During a cell search, Officer Rowan finds a homemade knife, a stack of old newspapers that is a fire hazard, and a tray of spoiled food.

Which item is hard contraband?
options: The tray of spoiled food
The stack of old newspapers
The homemade knife
None of the items
questions.rationale:
Hard contraband is an item that threatens safety or security and is ordinarily not approved, such as a weapon. Excess newspapers and spoiled food are nuisance contraband.

Source — 28 CFR § 553.12: “(1) Staff shall consider as hard contraband any item which threatens the safety, security, or good order of the facility or protection of the public and which ordinarily is not approved for possession by an inmate or for admission into the institution. Examples of hard contraband include weapons, intoxicants, and currency (where prohibited).”
28 CFR § 553.12: “(2) Staff shall consider as nuisance contraband any item other than hard contraband, which has never been authorized, or which may be, or which previously has been authorized for possession by an inmate, but whose possession is prohibited when it presents a threat to safety, security, or good order of the facility or protection of the public, or its condition or excessive quantities of it present a health, fire, or housekeeping hazard. Examples of nuisance contraband include: personal property no longer permitted for admission to the institution or permitted for sale in the commissary; altered personal property; excessive accumulation of commissary, newspapers, letters, or magazines which cannot be stored neatly and safely in the designated area; food items which are spoiled or retained beyond the point of safe consumption; government-issued items which have been altered, or other items made from government property without staff authorization.”

questions.stem:
An inmate buys a radio from another inmate without staff authorization. It is found in his locker, and he claims he owns it.

How will his claim of ownership ordinarily be treated?
options: It will be accepted if he can name the seller
It will be accepted if the radio is in good condition
It will be accepted if he pays a fine
It ordinarily will not be accepted, because the item may be considered nuisance contraband
questions.rationale:
Items obtained from another inmate without staff authorization may be considered nuisance contraband, for which a claim of ownership is ordinarily not accepted.

Source — 28 CFR § 553.13: “(ii) The inmate shall have seven days following receipt of the inventory to provide staff with evidence of ownership of the listed items. A claim of ownership may not be accepted for an item made from the unauthorized use of government property. Items obtained from another inmate (for example, through purchase, or as a gift) without staff authorization may be considered nuisance contraband for which a claim of ownership is ordinarily not accepted.”

questions.stem:
Officer Santos confiscates a box of personal property that may be contraband and completes an inventory. The inmate wants to know what happens next.

Which steps does the regulation require?
options: Give the inmate a copy of the inventory as soon as practicable, put a copy in the central file, and allow seven days to show ownership
Give the inmate a verbal summary of the inventory, keep the original with the officer, and allow thirty days to show ownership
Give the inmate a copy of the inventory within thirty days, put a copy in the central file, and allow seven days to show ownership, according to the institution's local guidelines
Give the inmate a copy of the inventory only if he files an appeal, and allow seven days to show ownership
questions.rationale:
After inventory, staff provide the inmate a copy as soon as practicable, place a copy in the central file, and allow seven days following receipt for evidence of ownership.

Source — 28 CFR § 553.13: “(i) Staff shall provide the inmate with a copy of the inventory as soon as practicable. A copy of this inventory shall also be placed in the inmate's central file.”
28 CFR § 553.13: “(ii) The inmate shall have seven days following receipt of the inventory to provide staff with evidence of ownership of the listed items. A claim of ownership may not be accepted for an item made from the unauthorized use of government property. Items obtained from another inmate (for example, through purchase, or as a gift) without staff authorization may be considered nuisance contraband for which a claim of ownership is ordinarily not accepted.”

questions.stem:
Officer Patel overhears an inmate say he cannot go on and has been giving away his belongings. The inmate's behavior has changed this week. The officer is not medical staff.

What should Officer Patel do?
options: Document the comment and discuss it at the next shift change
Wait for the next medical screening before taking any action
Ask the inmate to promise he will not hurt himself and return to post, with the approval of a supervisor on duty, once the shift lieutenant has been informed
Report it so the inmate is placed on suicide watch, since any staff member may identify an at-risk inmate based on observed behavior
questions.rationale:
Staff, medical or non-medical, may identify an inmate at risk at any time based on observed behavior, and the identified inmate is placed on suicide watch.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.41: “(2) Staff (whether medical or non-medical) may make an identification at any time based upon the inmate's observed behavior.”
28 CFR § 552.41: “(d) Referral. Staff who identify an inmate to be at risk for suicide will have the inmate placed on suicide watch.”

questions.stem:
An inmate has been placed on suicide watch. The watch is being staffed on a schedule, and a trained inmate observer is proposed as one of the observers.

Who may authorize the use of inmate observers?
options: Only the Warden
The Captain
The psychologist assigned to the watch
The Program Coordinator
questions.rationale:
Staff or trained inmate observers keep the inmate under constant observation, but only the Warden may authorize inmate observers.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.42: “(2) Only the Warden may authorize the use of inmate observers.”

questions.stem:
During a hostage incident, the hostage taker demands a weapon and immunity from prosecution. A negotiator asks the command center whether to agree to either demand to win the hostage's release.

What is the correct guidance?
options: The weapon may be granted but immunity may not
Both items may be granted if the Warden approves, once the shift lieutenant has been informed
Both items are non-negotiable, and negotiators have no decision-making authority
Immunity may be granted but the weapon may not
questions.rationale:
The release of captors, providing weapons, exchange of hostages, and immunity from prosecution are non-negotiable, and negotiators serve only as intermediaries without decision-making authority.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.31: “(a) Negotiators have no decision-making authority in hostage situations, but rather serve as intermediaries between hostage takers and command center staff.”
28 CFR § 552.31: “(b) During the negotiation process, the following items are non-negotiable: release of captors from custody, providing of weapons, exchange of hostages, and immunity from prosecution.”

questions.stem:
An inmate is placed in four-point restraints in a cold room, wearing only a thin shirt, and with no blanket. The officer says it is quicker that way.

Which requirement is being ignored?
options: Inmates are to be moved to a heated cell within thirty minutes, with a mattress and a pillow provided
Inmates are to be dressed in institution clothing at all times, with the mattress removed for safety
Inmates are to be given a hot meal every two hours, with a blanket provided at the inmate's request
Inmates are to be dressed in clothing appropriate to the temperature, with a mattress, and a blanket or sheet provided
questions.rationale:
Four-point restraint procedures require clothing appropriate to the temperature, a mattress covering the bed, and a blanket or sheet.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.24: “(b) Inmates will be dressed in clothing appropriate to the temperature.”
28 CFR § 552.24: “(c) Beds will be covered with a mattress, and a blanket/sheet will be provided to the inmate.”

questions.stem:
An inmate is placed on close observation for suspected ingestion of contraband. A staff member asks what the inmate must provide within two hours of placement.

What is the answer?
options: A urine sample, with a second sample before release
A written statement of what he swallowed
A signed consent for a body cavity search, as long as no other inmate is affected
A stool sample every two hours
questions.rationale:
The inmate must provide a urine sample within two hours of placement and a second sample before being released from close observation.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.12: “(1) The inmate shall be required to provide a urine sample within two hours of placement under close observation in accordance with the provisions of § 550.30 of this chapter on urine surveillance. A second urine sample is required prior to releasing the inmate from close observation.”

questions.stem:
An inmate on close observation needs to defecate. A new officer is unsure what is allowed.

What should the officer provide?
options: A trip to the infirmary toilet, unsupervised
An empty hospital bed pan
Access to the dayroom restroom, with an officer outside the door
A plastic bag, to be inspected by the shift supervisor
questions.rationale:
When the inmate needs to urinate or defecate, the inmate is furnished an empty hospital bed pan so staff can see whether contraband is voided.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.12: “(9) When the inmate needs to urinate and/or defecate, the inmate will be furnished an empty hospital bed pan.”

questions.stem:
An officer finds an item identified as contraband in a common area (the dayroom) rather than in any inmate's possession. A coworker says staff cannot seize it because no one owns it.

What is the correct response?
options: Staff shall seize any item identified as contraband, whether found on an inmate, in his living quarters, or in common areas
Staff shall seize contraband found on an inmate or in his living quarters, but not in common areas
Staff may seize the item only if an inmate claims it or the Warden gives permission in writing
Staff should leave the item in place and monitor the area to learn which inmate comes to collect it, as long as no other inmate is affected
questions.rationale:
Staff must seize identified contraband wherever it is found: on an inmate, in his quarters, or in common areas.

Source — 28 CFR § 553.13: “(a) Staff shall seize any item in the institution which has been identified as contraband whether the item is found in the physical possession of an inmate, in an inmate's living quarters, or in common areas of the institution.”

questions.stem:
An investigator is questioning an inmate after an incident report. The inmate says nothing and stares at the wall. The investigator tells a colleague, "His silence proves he did it."

What is wrong with the investigator's statement?
options: Silence may never be considered at any stage of the process
Silence may be used only at the Discipline Hearing Officer stage, based on the information available at the time, as long as the unit team is notified
Silence is the same as a confession in a discipline case
Silence may be used to draw an adverse inference, but silence alone cannot be the basis for finding the inmate committed the act
questions.rationale:
The inmate may remain silent. His silence may support an adverse inference, but it cannot be the sole basis for a finding.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.5: “(B) that you may remain silent at all stages of the discipline process, but that your silence may be used to draw an adverse inference against you at any stage of the process. Your silence alone, however, cannot be the basis for finding you committed the prohibited act(s).”

questions.stem:
An inmate is charged with a Greatest severity prohibited act. The UDC chair wonders whether the UDC can decide the matter itself and impose sanctions.

What does the regulation require?
options: The UDC may decide the matter if the inmate agrees
The UDC will automatically refer the incident report to the DHO for further review
The UDC may decide the matter and impose any sanction in the tables
The UDC may decide the matter if the Warden approves
questions.rationale:
Greatest or High severity charges are automatically referred to the DHO.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.7: “(4) If you are charged with a Greatest or High severity prohibited act, or are an inmate covered by § 541.4, the UDC will automatically refer the incident report to the DHO for further review.”

questions.stem:
An inmate refuses to attend his UDC review and tells the staff, "Do what you want without me."

What happens?
options: The review is postponed until he agrees to attend
The review is conducted by the DHO instead
The review is cancelled and the incident report is dismissed, pending review by the appropriate official
The inmate may waive his appearance, and the UDC reviews the incident report in his absence
questions.rationale:
An inmate may waive his appearance before the UDC, and the review proceeds in his absence.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.7: “(2) You may waive your appearance before the UDC. If you waive your appearance, the UDC will review the incident report in your absence.”

questions.stem:
Two staff members give conflicting accounts at a UDC review. One says the inmate threw the first punch, and the inmate's witness says otherwise.

What standard guides the decision?
options: The decision will be based on at least some facts and, with conflicting evidence, on the greater weight of the evidence
The decision must favor the statement of the reporting officer
The decision must be unanimous
The decision must be based on proof beyond a reasonable doubt
questions.rationale:
The UDC's decision is based on at least some facts, and when evidence conflicts, the greater weight of the evidence.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.7: “(e) Evidence. You are entitled to make a statement and present documentary evidence to the UDC on your own behalf. The UDC will consider all evidence presented during its review. The UDC's decision will be based on at least some facts and, if there is conflicting evidence, on the greater weight of the evidence.”

questions.stem:
A DHO hearing is scheduled for 10:00 a.m. tomorrow. The inmate received the written notice of the charges at 3:00 p.m. today (19 hours earlier) and did not waive the notice requirement.

What is the problem?
options: The inmate must receive notice at the hearing itself
The inmate must receive written notice at least 24 hours before the hearing unless he waives it
The inmate must receive notice at least 72 hours before the hearing, when staff resources allow, as determined by the shift supervisor
The inmate must receive notice at least one week before the hearing
questions.rationale:
Written notice must be received at least 24 hours before the DHO's hearing. The inmate may waive it, but he did not.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.8: “(c) Timing. You will receive written notice of the charge(s) against you at least 24 hours before the DHO's hearing. You may waive this requirement, in which case the DHO's hearing can be conducted sooner.”

questions.stem:
The DHO has found an inmate committed a prohibited act. The inmate asks whether a word-for-word transcript of the hearing will be provided.

What should staff tell him?
options: He will receive a complete verbatim transcript within seven days, during normal operating hours
He will receive a written report, but the DHO is not required to prepare a verbatim record
He will receive a transcript only if he appeals
He will receive nothing in writing, only an oral summary
questions.rationale:
The DHO is not required to prepare a verbatim record, but the inmate receives a written copy of the decision documenting rights, evidence, decision, sanction, and reasons.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.8: “(h) Written Report. You will receive a written copy of the DHO's decision following the hearing. The DHO is not required to prepare a verbatim record of the hearing. The DHO's written report will document the following:”

questions.stem:
A staff member observes an inmate who seems confused and talks about hearing voices during the discipline process.

What does the regulation require?
options: The proceedings must continue unchanged, since mental illness is not relevant
The charges are dismissed automatically
The inmate will be examined by mental health staff if it appears he is mentally ill at any stage of the discipline process
The inmate is placed in disciplinary segregation until he is stable
questions.rationale:
If it appears the inmate is mentally ill at any stage, mental health staff examine him, and proceedings may be postponed or conduct excused based on the evidence.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.6: “If it appears you are mentally ill at any stage of the discipline process, you will be examined by mental health staff.”

questions.stem:
An inmate wants to appeal the UDC's decision. He asks staff where to file.

What is the correct answer?
options: Through the Administrative Remedy Program, 28 CFR part 542, subpart B
By submitting a request to the inmate's case manager, when staff resources allow
By writing to the sentencing court
By asking the UDC to reconsider in a new hearing
questions.rationale:
Both UDC and DHO actions are appealed through the Administrative Remedy Program.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.7: “(i) Appeals. You may appeal the UDC's action(s) through the Administrative Remedy Program, 28 CFR part 542, subpart B.”

questions.stem:
When is the incident report ordinarily delivered after staff learn of the inmate's involvement? Officer Tate learned of the involvement at 8:00 a.m. Monday and plans to deliver the report Thursday afternoon.

What is the issue with this timeline?
options: The report must be delivered within 5 work days
The inmate will ordinarily receive the incident report within 24 hours of staff becoming aware of his involvement
The report may be delivered at any time before the hearing
The report must be delivered within 72 hours of the incident
questions.rationale:
The ordinary time frame is within 24 hours of staff becoming aware.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.5: “(a) Incident report. The discipline process starts when staff witness or reasonably believe that you committed a prohibited act. A staff member will issue you an incident report describing the incident and the prohibited act(s) you are charged with committing. You will ordinarily receive the incident report within 24 hours of staff becoming aware of your involvement in the incident.”

questions.stem:
A teacher is the first staff member to hear an inmate report a recent sexual abuse. The teacher is not security staff.

What must the teacher do?
options: Escort the alleged victim to the medical unit without notifying security staff, to avoid delay
Interview the alleged victim in detail in the classroom, and then notify security staff at the end of the period, unless an emergency requires otherwise
Separate the alleged victim and abuser, and then wait for security staff to ask for a written account
Request that the alleged victim not take any actions that could destroy physical evidence, and then notify security staff
questions.rationale:
A non-security first responder must ask the victim to preserve evidence and then notify security.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.64: “(b) If the first staff responder is not a security staff member, the responder shall be required to request that the alleged victim not take any actions that could destroy physical evidence, and then notify security staff.”

questions.stem:
Officer Reddy hears a coworker say that something happened to an inmate at another correctional facility run by a different agency. She is not sure it is true.

What must she do?
options: Report immediately and according to agency policy any knowledge, suspicion, or information, whether or not the facility is part of the agency
Wait until she can confirm the rumor with the other facility, and then report it to her supervisor
Report it only if the facility named is part of her own agency, since other agencies have their own duties
Tell the inmates in her unit to be careful, and report it only if an inmate asks her to
questions.rationale:
Staff must report any knowledge, suspicion, or information regarding sexual abuse that occurred in a facility, whether or not it is part of the agency.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.61: “(a) The agency shall require all staff to report immediately and according to agency policy any knowledge, suspicion, or information regarding an incident of sexual abuse or sexual harassment that occurred in a facility, whether or not it is part of the agency; retaliation against inmates or staff who reported such an incident; and any staff neglect or violation of responsibilities that may have contributed to an incident or retaliation.”

questions.stem:
After reporting a sexual abuse allegation, Officer Fisher tells several coworkers in the break room the details of the case.

What does the standard say?
options: Staff may share the details with any employee on the same shift so that everyone stays aware of the situation
Staff shall not reveal information related to a sexual abuse report except as necessary for treatment, investigation, and security and management decisions
Staff may share the details with the alleged abuser's family so that they can support the person
Staff may share the details with other inmates in the unit to stop rumors from spreading further
questions.rationale:
Apart from designated officials, staff may reveal information only as needed to make treatment, investigation, and other security and management decisions.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.61: “(b) Apart from reporting to designated supervisors or officials, staff shall not reveal any information related to a sexual abuse report to anyone other than to the extent necessary, as specified in agency policy, to make treatment, investigation, and other security and management decisions.”

questions.stem:
An inmate's mother calls the facility and anonymously reports that her son was sexually abused. A staff member says third-party and anonymous reports are not accepted.

What is the correct response?
options: Staff shall accept reports made verbally and in writing, and anonymous reports only if the caller gives a name later, based on the information available at the time
Staff shall accept reports made by the alleged victim only, and ask third parties to submit a written complaint
Staff shall accept reports made verbally, in writing, anonymously, and from third parties, and promptly document verbal reports
Staff shall accept reports made in writing and from third parties, but verbal and anonymous reports are not accepted
questions.rationale:
Reports are accepted in all of these forms, and verbal ones must be promptly documented.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.51: “(c) Staff shall accept reports made verbally, in writing, anonymously, and from third parties and shall promptly document any verbal reports.”

questions.stem:
A male officer is about to enter a housing unit for female inmates during the evening.

What must he do?
options: Enter quietly to avoid disturbing the inmates, provided that the action is documented
Announce his presence when entering the housing unit
Wait for a female officer to open the door
Sign a log at the control room only
questions.rationale:
Policies must require staff of the opposite gender to announce their presence when entering an inmate housing unit.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.15: “(d) The facility shall implement policies and procedures that enable inmates to shower, perform bodily functions, and change clothing without nonmedical staff of the opposite gender viewing their breasts, buttocks, or genitalia, except in exigent circumstances or when such viewing is incidental to routine cell checks. Such policies and procedures shall require staff of the opposite gender to announce their presence when entering an inmate housing unit.”

questions.stem:
A sexual abuse victim says she does not want to name her abuser or cooperate with the investigation. She asks if she can still see a nurse.

What does the standard say?
options: Treatment services shall be provided only after the investigation has concluded and the allegation is substantiated, as long as the unit team is notified
Treatment services shall be provided at the victim's cost unless the abuser is a staff member
Treatment services shall be provided without financial cost, but only if she names the abuser and cooperates
Treatment services shall be provided without financial cost and regardless of whether she names the abuser or cooperates
questions.rationale:
Victims receive treatment services free of charge and regardless of cooperation.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.82: “(d) Treatment services shall be provided to the victim without financial cost and regardless of whether the victim names the abuser or cooperates with any investigation arising out of the incident.”

questions.stem:
At the start of services, a nurse wants to assure an inmate that everything he says will remain completely confidential.

What must the nurse tell the inmate instead?
options: The nurse's duty to report sexual abuse and the limitations of confidentiality
That the nurse must report to the inmate's family
That the nurse will keep every disclosure private from everyone, with the approval of a supervisor on duty
That the nurse will report only if the inmate names the abuser
questions.rationale:
Practitioners must inform inmates of their duty to report and the limits of confidentiality at the initiation of services.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.61: “(c) Unless otherwise precluded by Federal, State, or local law, medical and mental health practitioners shall be required to report sexual abuse pursuant to paragraph (a) of this section and to inform inmates of the practitioner's duty to report, and the limitations of confidentiality, at the initiation of services.”

questions.stem:
A new inmate arrives. Staff conduct the intake screening for risk of victimization after he has been in the facility for 10 days.

What does the standard say about timing?
options: Intake screening shall take place within 30 days of arrival
Intake screening shall ordinarily take place within 72 hours of arrival
Intake screening shall take place within 24 hours of arrival, unless local procedures say otherwise
Intake screening shall take place within 10 days of arrival
questions.rationale:
Intake screening ordinarily takes place within 72 hours, with a reassessment within 30 days.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.41: “(b) Intake screening shall ordinarily take place within 72 hours of arrival at the facility.”

questions.stem:
A supervisor reviews staff training records and finds that an officer has not received refresher training for four years.

What does the standard require?
options: Refresher training every two years, with refresher information in the years between
Refresher training only when policies change
Refresher training only for new officers
Refresher training every five years
questions.rationale:
The agency provides refresher training every two years and refresher information in the intervening years.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.31: “(c) All current employees who have not received such training shall be trained within one year of the effective date of the PREA standards, and the agency shall provide each employee with refresher training every two years to ensure that all employees know the agency's current sexual abuse and sexual harassment policies and procedures. In years in which an employee does not receive refresher training, the agency shall provide refresher information on current sexual abuse and sexual harassment policies.”

questions.stem:
A newly arrived inmate has not yet been told how to report sexual abuse. Staff say they will cover it "someday in the first year."

What does the standard require?
options: At intake, inmates receive the zero-tolerance policy only, and education on reporting is given within one year
At intake, inmates receive information on the zero-tolerance policy and how to report, and comprehensive education within 30 days
Within 30 days, inmates receive information on the zero-tolerance policy, and education is given within one year, in accordance with the posted schedule
At intake, information is provided only on request, and comprehensive education is given within 72 hours
questions.rationale:
At intake inmates receive the zero-tolerance policy and reporting information, and comprehensive education is provided within 30 days.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.33: “(a) During the intake process, inmates shall receive information explaining the agency's zero-tolerance policy regarding sexual abuse and sexual harassment and how to report incidents or suspicions of sexual abuse or sexual harassment.”
28 CFR § 115.33: “(b) Within 30 days of intake, the agency shall provide comprehensive education to inmates either in person or through video regarding their rights to be free from sexual abuse and sexual harassment and to be free from retaliation for reporting such incidents, and regarding agency policies and procedures for responding to such incidents.”

questions.stem:
A staff member learns that an inmate is subject to a substantial risk of imminent sexual abuse.

What does the agency have to do?
options: Take immediate action to protect the inmate
Notify the inmate's family first
Wait for the inmate to file a formal grievance
Document the concern and review it at the next meeting
questions.rationale:
When an agency learns of a substantial risk of imminent sexual abuse, it must take immediate action to protect the inmate.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.62: “When an agency learns that an inmate is subject to a substantial risk of imminent sexual abuse, it shall take immediate action to protect the inmate.”

questions.stem:
The standard of proof for finding an allegation of sexual abuse substantiated in an administrative investigation is being discussed at a training session.

What is the highest standard the agency may impose?
options: Clear and convincing evidence
A preponderance of the evidence
A signed confession
Proof beyond a reasonable doubt
questions.rationale:
The agency shall impose no standard higher than a preponderance of the evidence.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.72: “The agency shall impose no standard higher than a preponderance of the evidence in determining whether allegations of sexual abuse or sexual harassment are substantiated.”

questions.stem:
A report of recent sexual abuse is made at 3:00 a.m. when no qualified medical or mental health practitioner is on duty.

What must the security first responders do?
options: Wait until the morning shift arrives and then inform medical staff, while keeping the victim in a holding cell, as determined by the shift supervisor
Examine the victim themselves to document injuries, and then notify the practitioners at the end of the shift
Take preliminary steps to protect the victim and immediately notify the appropriate medical and mental health practitioners
Return the victim to the housing unit and notify the practitioners only if the victim asks to see them
questions.rationale:
When no practitioners are on duty, security first responders protect the victim and immediately notify the appropriate practitioners.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.82: “(b) If no qualified medical or mental health practitioners are on duty at the time a report of recent abuse is made, security staff first responders shall take preliminary steps to protect the victim pursuant to § 115.62 and shall immediately notify the appropriate medical and mental health practitioners.”

questions.stem:
A letter from a law firm arrives for an inmate. The firm's name is on the envelope, but there is no "Special Mail" marking on the front.

How may staff handle it?
options: As special mail, opened only in the inmate's presence, based on the information available at the time
As contraband, destroyed immediately
As general correspondence, which they may open, inspect, and read
As rejected mail, returned to the sender unopened
questions.rationale:
Without adequate identification or the special mail marking, staff may treat the mail as general correspondence.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.18: “(b) In the absence of either adequate identification or the “special mail” marking indicated in paragraph (a) of this section appearing on the envelope, staff may treat the mail as general correspondence and may open, inspect, and read the mail.”

questions.stem:
An inmate in a minimum security institution seals an outgoing letter to his cousin. The envelope has a complete return address, and nothing about the letter looks suspicious.

How is the letter handled?
options: It is held for 72 hours for review by the Warden
It is opened and read by the mailroom before sending
It is returned to the inmate to be mailed unsealed
It is sent out unopened and uninspected, unless an exception applies
questions.rationale:
Outgoing mail from a sentenced inmate in a minimum or low security institution may be sealed and sent unopened, except in specified situations.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.14: “(c)(1) Outgoing mail from a sentenced inmate in a minimum or low security level institution may be sealed by the inmate and, except as provided for in paragraphs (c)(1)(i) through (iv) of this section, is sent out unopened and uninspected. Staff may open a sentenced inmate's outgoing general correspondence:”

questions.stem:
An outgoing letter from an inmate in a medium security institution is sealed. The mailroom officer wants to know if it can be read.

What is the rule?
options: Outgoing mail from medium or high security institutions may not be sealed, but staff may read it only with a court order
Except for special mail, outgoing mail from medium or high security institutions may not be sealed and may be read and inspected
Outgoing mail from medium or high security institutions may be sealed, but staff may read it with the Warden's approval
Except for special mail, outgoing mail from medium or high security institutions may be sealed and is sent unopened unless a reason exists
questions.rationale:
At medium and high security level institutions (and administrative ones), outgoing general mail may not be sealed and may be read and inspected.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.14: “(2) Except for “special mail,” outgoing mail from a sentenced inmate in a medium or high security level institution, or an administrative institution may not be sealed by the inmate and may be read and inspected by staff.”

questions.stem:
The Warden rejects a letter to an inmate because it contains a coded message. The inmate and the sender both want to challenge the decision.

What does the regulation require regarding notice and appeal?
options: Written notice to the inmate only, with the right to appeal to the Regional Director
Verbal notice to the sender and the inmate, with the right to appeal to a different official
Written notice to the sender only, with the right to appeal to the same official who rejected the letter, based on the information available at the time
Written notice to the sender and the inmate with reasons and the right to appeal, with the appeal going to a different official
questions.rationale:
The Warden notifies both the sender and the inmate in writing of the rejection, reasons, and right to appeal, and refers the appeal to a different official.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.13: “When correspondence is rejected, the Warden shall notify the sender in writing of the rejection and the reasons for the rejection. The Warden shall also give notice that the sender may appeal the rejection. The Warden shall also notify an inmate of the rejection of any letter addressed to that inmate, along with the reasons for the rejection and shall notify the inmate of the right to appeal the rejection. The Warden shall refer an appeal to an official other than the one who originally disapproved the correspondence. The Warden shall return rejected correspondence to the sender unless the correspondence includes plans for or discussion of commission of a crime or evidence of a crime, in which case there is no need to return the correspondence or give notice of the rejection, and the correspondence should be referred to appropriate law enforcement authorities. Also, contraband need not be returned to the sender.”

questions.stem:
A pretrial inmate seals an outgoing letter to his sister.

What is the correct handling?
options: Outgoing mail from a pretrial inmate other than special mail may not be sealed and may be read and inspected
Outgoing mail from a pretrial inmate may always be sealed
Outgoing mail from a pretrial inmate may not be sent
Outgoing mail from a pretrial inmate may be read only by the Warden
questions.rationale:
Except for special mail, outgoing mail from a pretrial inmate may not be sealed and may be read and inspected.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.14: “(b) Except for “special mail,” outgoing mail from a pretrial inmate may not be sealed by the inmate and may be read and inspected by staff.”

questions.stem:
An inmate writes a letter threatening the life of a judge. A mailroom officer is unsure whether this is just a disciplinary matter.

What can result from correspondence containing threats or extortion?
options: Referral to law enforcement only, since mail violations are not handled through discipline, when staff resources allow
Disciplinary action only, since the letter was stopped before it reached its recipient
Disciplinary action, copying of the writing, and referral to law enforcement for possible prosecution
A written reprimand and a copy of the letter placed in the inmate's visiting file
questions.rationale:
Such correspondence may result in prosecution, disciplinary action, copying, and referral of all material to law enforcement.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.12: “(c) Staff shall inform an inmate that letters placed in the U.S. Mail are placed there at the request of the inmate and the inmate must assume responsibility for the contents of each letter. Correspondence containing threats, extortion, etc., may result in prosecution for violation of federal laws. When such material is discovered, the inmate may be subject to disciplinary action, the written material may be copied, and all material may be referred to the appropriate law enforcement agency for prosecution.”

questions.stem:
A new inmate asks what the institution's rules for handling his mail are and whether staff may open all of it.

What must staff tell him?
options: Staff may open only the mail that comes from outside the state, and all other mail is delivered sealed, under the direction of the senior officer present
Staff may open all mail, including special mail, outside his presence, but may not read special mail
Staff may open general mail before delivery, but may read special mail only with the Warden's approval
Staff may open all mail before delivery, but special mail may be opened only in his presence to check for contraband
questions.rationale:
The rules notice states that staff may open all mail before delivery, while special mail may be opened only in the inmate's presence.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.12: “The staff of each institution of the Bureau of Prisons has the authority to open all mail addressed to you before it is delivered to you. “Special Mail” (mail from the President and Vice President of the U.S., attorneys, Members of the U.S. Congress, Embassies and Consulates, the U.S. Department of Justice (excluding the Bureau of Prisons but including U.S. Attorneys), other Federal law enforcement officers, State Attorneys General, Prosecuting Attorneys, Governors, U.S. Courts (including U.S. Probation Officers), and State Courts) may be opened only in your presence to be checked for contraband. This procedure occurs only if the sender is adequately identified on the envelope and the front of the envelope is marked “Special Mail—Open only in the presence of the inmate.” Other mail may be opened and read by the staff. If you do not want your general correspondence opened and read, the Bureau will return it to the Postal Service. This means that you will not receive such mail. You may choose whether you want your general correspondence delivered to you subject to the above conditions, or returned to the Postal Service. Whatever your choice, special mail will be delivered to you, after it is opened in your presence and checked for contraband. You can make your choice by signing part I or part II. Part I—General Correspondence to be Returned to the Postal Service I have read or had read to me the foregoing notice regarding mail. I do not want my general correspondence opened and read. I REQUEST THAT THE BUREAU OF PRISONS RETURN MY GENERAL CORRESPONDENCE TO THE POSTAL SERVICE. I understand that special mail will be delivered to me, after it is opened in my presence and checked for contraband. (Name) (Reg. No.) (Date) Part II—General Correspondence to be Opened, Read, and Delivered I have read or had read to me the foregoing notice regarding mail, I WISH TO RECEIVE MY GENERAL CORRESPONDENCE. I understand that the Bureau of Prisons may open and read my general correspondence if I choose to receive same. I also understand that special mail will be delivered to me, after it is opened in my presence and checked for contraband. (Name) (Reg. No.) (Date) Inmate (Name), (Reg. No.), refused to sign this form. He (she) was advised by me that the Bureau of Prisons retains the authority to open and read all general correspondence. The inmate was also advised that his (her) refusal to sign this form will be interpreted as an indication that he (she) wishes to receive general correspondence subject to the conditions in part II above. Staff Member's Signature Date”

questions.stem:
An inmate who has no family visits wants his former employer to visit to help with release planning.

How is this visitor treated?
options: As a special visitor; the requirement of an established pre-confinement relationship does not apply to former or prospective employers
As a special visitor; the requirement of an established pre-confinement relationship applies and the visits must recur
As a regular visitor; the requirement of an established pre-confinement relationship applies to former or prospective employers, during normal operating hours
As a regular visitor; the visits are limited to immediate family and so the employer is not approved
questions.rationale:
Clergy, former or prospective employers, sponsors, and parole advisors qualify as special visitors, and the established-relationship requirement does not apply.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.45: “(d) Clergy, former or prospective employers, sponsors, and parole advisors. Visitors in this category ordinarily provide assistance in release planning, counseling, and discussion of family problems. The requirement for the existence of an established relationship prior to confinement for visitors does not apply to visitors in this category.”

questions.stem:
A visitor is caught trying to pass a small package to an inmate in the visiting room.

What may result?
options: Disciplinary action against the inmate only, with no prosecution because the package was seized
Disciplinary action against the inmate including denial of future visits, and criminal prosecution of the visitor, the inmate, or both
Disciplinary action against the visitor only, including denial of future visits, with no action against the inmate, where the circumstances reasonably call for it
Criminal prosecution of the visitor only, with the inmate's visits continuing as before
questions.rationale:
Violation of visiting guidelines may result in discipline including extended denial of visits, and criminal prosecution of the visitor, inmate, or both.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.52: “Any act or effort to violate the visiting guidelines of an institution may result in disciplinary action against the inmate, which may include the denial of future visits, possibly over an extended period of time. Moreover, criminal prosecution may be initiated against the visitor, the inmate, or both, in the case of criminal violations.”

questions.stem:
The Warden wants to limit visits on weekends because the visiting room is crowded. A family says it will be unfair if they can attend only one of the two weekend days.

What does the regulation say?
options: The Warden must allow every visitor both days
The Warden may not limit weekend visits at all
The Warden may limit visits to Saturday or Sunday but not both, and no one is guaranteed both days
The Warden may limit visits only on holidays
questions.rationale:
The Warden may limit the visiting period; there is no requirement that every visitor or inmate have both days of the weekend.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.42: “(b) Consistent with available resources, such as space limitations and staff availability, and with concerns of institution security, the Warden may limit the visiting period. With respect to weekend visits, for example, some or all inmates and visitors may be limited to visiting on Saturday or on Sunday, but not on both days, in order to accommodate the volume of visitors. There is no requirement that every visitor has the opportunity to visit on both days of the weekend, nor that every inmate has the opportunity to have visits on both days of the weekend.”

questions.stem:
A visitor wants to know on which days the Warden must at least set visiting hours.

What is the answer?
options: Tuesdays and Thursdays
Fridays only
Weekday evenings
Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays
questions.rationale:
At a minimum the Warden establishes visiting hours on Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.42: “(a) Each Warden shall establish a visiting schedule for the institution. At a minimum, the Warden shall establish visiting hours at the institution on Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays. The restriction of visiting to these days may be a hardship for some families and arrangements for other suitable hours shall be made to the extent practicable. Where staff resources permit, the Warden may establish evening visiting hours.”

questions.stem:
An inmate uses another inmate's telephone access code to call his family. Later, he tells staff the code was "given" to him.

What does the regulation say about telephone access codes?
options: An inmate may not possess another inmate's code or give his own code to another inmate, and must report a compromised code immediately to unit staff
An inmate may share his code with a cellmate, but must report a compromised code to unit staff immediately
An inmate may possess another inmate's code if the other inmate has written permission from the Associate Warden
An inmate may not give his code to another inmate, but need not report if the code is used without his knowledge
questions.rationale:
An inmate may not possess another inmate's access code or give his own to another inmate, and must report a compromised code immediately.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.101: “(c) Telephone access codes. An inmate may not possess another inmate's telephone access code number. An inmate may not give his or her telephone access code number to another inmate, and is to report a compromised telephone access code number immediately to unit staff.”

questions.stem:
An inmate asks his cellmate to place a three-way call so that a friend can be added without being on the telephone list. Staff note that a call was transferred to a third party.

What does the regulation say about this?
options: Third-party transfers are allowed if the friend pays, according to the institution's local guidelines
Third-party transfers are allowed for family only
Third party billing and electronic transfer of a call to a third party are prohibited
Third-party transfers are allowed on weekends
questions.rationale:
Third party billing and electronic transfer of a call to a third party are prohibited.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.105: “(a) An inmate is responsible for the expenses of inmate telephone use. Such expenses may include a fee for replacement of an inmate's telephone access code that is used in an institution which has implemented debit billing for inmate telephone calls. Each inmate is responsible for staying aware of his or her account balance through the automated process provided by the system. Third party billing and electronic transfer of a call to a third party are prohibited.”

questions.stem:
A new inmate asks how many numbers can be on his phone list.

What is the ordinary limit?
options: Up to 30 numbers, with the Associate Warden able to authorize more based on the inmate's situation
Up to 30 numbers, with the Warden alone able to authorize more based on the inmate's situation
Up to 15 numbers, with the Associate Warden able to authorize more based on the inmate's situation
Up to 50 numbers, with the Captain able to authorize more based on the inmate's situation
questions.rationale:
The list ordinarily may contain up to 30 numbers, and the Associate Warden may authorize more.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.101: “(a) Telephone list preparation. An inmate telephone call shall ordinarily be made to a number identified on the inmate's official telephone list. This list ordinarily may contain up to 30 numbers. The Associate Warden may authorize the placement of additional numbers on an inmate's telephone list based on the inmate's individual situation, e.g., size of family.”

questions.stem:
An inmate is helping another inmate research a court filing in the law library during his leisure time. He asks to take the other inmate's legal papers back to his cell.

What does the regulation say?
options: The assisting inmate may remove copies of another inmate's materials but not the originals
The assisting inmate may remove another inmate's legal materials during evening hours only
The assisting inmate may not remove another inmate's legal materials from the law library or other designated location
The assisting inmate may remove another inmate's legal materials if the other inmate signs a note, as long as the unit team is notified
questions.rationale:
The assisting inmate may not remove another inmate's legal materials, including copies, from the library or designated location.

Source — 28 CFR § 543.11: “(i) The assisting inmate may not remove another inmate's legal materials, including copies of the legal materials, from the law library or other designated location. An assisting inmate is permitted to make handwritten notes and to remove those notes from the library or other designated location if the notes do not contain a case caption or document title or the name(s) of any inmate(s). The assisting inmate may also develop and possess handwritten drafts of pleadings, so long as the draft pleadings do not contain a case caption or document title or the name(s) of any inmate(s). These notes and drafts are not considered to be the assisting inmate's legal property, and when the assisting inmate has these documents outside the law library or other designated location, they are subject to the property limitations in § 553.11(a) of this chapter.”

questions.stem:
An inmate asks for copies of a court filing. He says he must submit more than one copy and cannot use carbon paper.

Who bears the cost and when may staff waive it?
options: The institution; staff may charge him only if the number of copies is large or excessive, when staff resources allow
The inmate's attorney; staff may waive the cost if the attorney is a public defender
The inmate; the cost may be waived only if the Warden gives approval in advance
The inmate; staff may waive the cost if he is without funds or the copying is minimal and not excessive
questions.rationale:
The inmate bears the duplication cost, but staff may waive it if the inmate lacks funds or the requests are minimal.

Source — 28 CFR § 543.11: “(g) The institution staff shall, upon an inmate's request and at times scheduled by staff, duplicate legal documents if the inmate demonstrates that more than one copy must be submitted to court and that the duplication cannot be accomplished by use of carbon paper. The inmate shall bear the cost, and the duplication shall be done so as not to interfere with regular institution operations. Staff may waive the cost if the inmate is without funds or if the material to be duplicated is minimal, and the inmate's requests for duplication are not large or excessive.”

questions.stem:
An inmate wants to file a formal complaint about his cell conditions. He has not yet talked with staff about the problem.

What must ordinarily happen first?
options: The inmate presents the issue informally to staff, and staff attempt to resolve it
The inmate waits 60 days
The inmate asks a family member to write the Warden, as long as the unit team is notified
The inmate files directly with the General Counsel
questions.rationale:
An inmate shall first present an issue informally to staff before submitting a Request for Administrative Remedy.

Source — 28 CFR § 542.13: “(a) Informal resolution. Except as provided in § 542.13(b), an inmate shall first present an issue of concern informally to staff, and staff shall attempt to informally resolve the issue before an inmate submits a Request for Administrative Remedy. Each Warden shall establish procedures to allow for the informal resolution of inmate complaints.”

questions.stem:
An inmate asks how long he has to appeal the Warden's response to the Regional Director.

What is the answer?
options: 60 calendar days from the date the Warden signed the response
30 calendar days from the date the Warden signed the response
10 calendar days from the date the Warden signed the response
20 calendar days from the date the Warden signed the response
questions.rationale:
An appeal to the Regional Director (BP-10) must be submitted within 20 calendar days of the date the Warden signed the response.

Source — 28 CFR § 542.15: “(a) Submission. An inmate who is not satisfied with the Warden's response may submit an Appeal on the appropriate form (BP-10) to the appropriate Regional Director within 20 calendar days of the date the Warden signed the response. An inmate who is not satisfied with the Regional Director's response may submit an Appeal on the appropriate form (BP-11) to the General Counsel within 30 calendar days of the date the Regional Director signed the response. When the inmate demonstrates a valid reason for delay, these time limits may be extended. Valid reasons for delay include those situations described in § 542.14(b) of this part. Appeal to the General Counsel is the final administrative appeal.”

questions.stem:
A Lieutenant wants to place an inmate in disciplinary segregation for the weekend after an argument, pending the DHO's hearing next week.

What does the regulation say?
options: The Warden may impose disciplinary segregation without a hearing
The Lieutenant may place the inmate in disciplinary segregation for up to seven days, unless local procedures say otherwise
The unit team may impose disciplinary segregation
Disciplinary segregation status may be imposed only by the DHO as a disciplinary sanction
questions.rationale:
Only a DHO may place an inmate in disciplinary segregation status as a sanction. Pending a hearing, administrative detention may be available when the inmate is under investigation or awaiting a hearing.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.24: “You may be placed in disciplinary segregation status only by the DHO as a disciplinary sanction.”

questions.stem:
An inmate is under investigation for possibly violating a federal law, and staff believe his presence in the general population poses a threat to the institution.

Which status is appropriate?
options: Administrative detention status
Protective custody under PREA only
Close observation
Disciplinary segregation status
questions.rationale:
An inmate who is under investigation or awaiting a hearing, and whose presence poses a threat, may be placed in administrative detention.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.23: “(c) Removal from general population. Your presence in the general population poses a threat to life, property, self, staff, other inmates, the public, or to the security or orderly running of the institution and: (1) Investigation. You are under investigation or awaiting a hearing for possibly violating a Bureau regulation or criminal law;”

questions.stem:
An inmate is placed in administrative detention and asks when he will receive a copy of the order detailing the reasons for his placement.

What is the ordinary time frame?
options: Within 7 days
Within 24 hours
Within 3 work days
At the next 30-day review
questions.rationale:
He will ordinarily receive the administrative detention order within 24 hours (except when pending classification or in holdover status).

Source — 28 CFR § 541.25: “(a) Administrative detention status. When placed in administrative detention status, you will receive a copy of the administrative detention order, ordinarily within 24 hours, detailing the reason(s) for your placement. However, when placed in administrative detention status pending classification or while in holdover status, you will not receive an administrative detention order.”

questions.stem:
An inmate in the SHU claims his placement was unfair and asks how to challenge it.

What can he do?
options: Submit a formal grievance through the Administrative Remedy Program
Write the sentencing judge
Wait for the next review without taking action, as long as no other inmate is affected
Ask the SHU officer to release him
questions.rationale:
An inmate can challenge his placement in the SHU through the Administrative Remedy Program.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.26: “(d) Administrative remedy program. You can submit a formal grievance challenging your placement in the SHU through the Administrative Remedy Program, 28 CFR part 542, subpart B.”

questions.stem:
A health services staff member tells a SHU officer that medical staff will visit inmates in the SHU "when requested."

What does the regulation require?
options: A health services staff member will visit only on request, as long as no other inmate is affected
A health services staff member will visit weekly
A health services staff member will visit daily to provide necessary medical care
A health services staff member will visit monthly
questions.rationale:
A health services staff member visits SHU inmates daily, and emergency care is always available.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.32: “(a) Medical Care. A health services staff member will visit you daily to provide necessary medical care. Emergency medical care is always available.”

questions.stem:
An inmate has been in the SHU for 30 continuous calendar days.

What must occur?
options: The unit team must hold a formal hearing that the inmate can attend, unless local procedures say otherwise
The Warden must review his file and decide whether he is released
A chaplain must interview him and report the results to the SRO
Mental health staff must examine him, including a personal interview
questions.rationale:
After every 30 calendar days of continuous placement, mental health staff examine the inmate, including a personal interview.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.32: “(b) Mental Health Care. After every 30 calendar days of continuous placement in either administrative detention or disciplinary segregation status, mental health staff will examine you, including a personal interview. Emergency mental health care is always available.”

questions.stem:
A young inmate under 18 arrives at an adult prison. Staff suggest placing him in the same dayroom as adult inmates.

What does the standard say?
options: A youthful inmate may be placed with adult inmates if the adult inmates have no history of violence
A youthful inmate shall not share sleeping quarters with adult inmates, but may share showers and dayrooms
A youthful inmate may share a dayroom with adult inmates if direct staff supervision is provided
A youthful inmate shall not be placed where he will have sight, sound, or physical contact with any adult inmate in a shared dayroom, shower, or sleeping quarters
questions.rationale:
Youthful inmates are not placed where they would have sight, sound, or physical contact with adult inmates in a shared dayroom, shower area, or sleeping quarters.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.14: “(a) A youthful inmate shall not be placed in a housing unit in which the youthful inmate will have sight, sound, or physical contact with any adult inmate through use of a shared dayroom or other common space, shower area, or sleeping quarters.”

questions.stem:
A deaf inmate wants to report an incident. The only person available to interpret is another inmate.

What does the standard say?
options: The agency shall not rely on inmate interpreters except in limited circumstances where a delay in obtaining an effective interpreter could compromise safety, first-response duties, or the investigation

The agency shall not rely on inmate interpreters under any circumstances, even where safety is at risk, unless an emergency requires otherwise, once the shift lieutenant has been informed, for the duration of the incident
The agency may rely on inmate interpreters if the inmate being interpreted for agrees in writing
The agency may rely on inmate interpreters whenever staff interpreters are unavailable on the shift
questions.rationale:
The agency may rely on inmate interpreters only where an extended delay could compromise the inmate's safety, first-response duties, or the investigation.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.16: “(c) The agency shall not rely on inmate interpreters, inmate readers, or other types of inmate assistants except in limited circumstances where an extended delay in obtaining an effective interpreter could compromise the inmate's safety, the performance of first-response duties under § 115.64, or the investigation of the inmate's allegations.”

questions.stem:
A transgender inmate asks to shower separately from other inmates.

What does the standard say?
options: Transgender and intersex inmates shall be given the opportunity to shower separately from other inmates
Transgender and intersex inmates shall be given a separate shower only after an incident
Transgender and intersex inmates may shower separately only if a medical practitioner writes an order
Transgender and intersex inmates shall shower with other inmates but at a time when staff are not present
questions.rationale:
The standard gives transgender and intersex inmates the opportunity to shower separately.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.42: “(f) Transgender and intersex inmates shall be given the opportunity to shower separately from other inmates.”

questions.stem:
An inmate who reported sexual abuse asks to speak with a victim advocate.

What must the facility provide?
options: Telephone numbers of victim advocacy organizations, with calls placed only by staff on the inmate's behalf
Mailing addresses of victim advocacy organizations, with all communication reviewed in advance by the PREA coordinator
Mailing addresses and telephone numbers of local, State, or national victim advocacy or rape crisis organizations, with reasonably confidential communication
Mailing addresses and telephone numbers of the facility's own staff counselors, with communication through the unit team
questions.rationale:
The facility provides contact information for outside victim advocates and enables reasonable communication as confidentially as possible.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.53: “(a) The facility shall provide inmates with access to outside victim advocates for emotional support services related to sexual abuse by giving inmates mailing addresses and telephone numbers, including toll-free hotline numbers where available, of local, State, or national victim advocacy or rape crisis organizations, and, for persons detained solely for civil immigration purposes, immigrant services agencies. The facility shall enable reasonable communication between inmates and these organizations and agencies, in as confidential a manner as possible.”

questions.stem:
A facility did not follow its staffing plan on the night shift because of a flu outbreak and did not record the reason.

What does the standard require?
options: A rewrite of the plan within a day, pending review by the appropriate official
Notification to the family
Nothing, if the shift was short
The facility shall document and justify all deviations from the plan
questions.rationale:
Where the staffing plan is not complied with, the facility must document and justify all deviations.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.13: “(b) In circumstances where the staffing plan is not complied with, the facility shall document and justify all deviations from the plan.”

questions.stem:
A male officer on the night shift must conduct a search of a female inmate. No exigent circumstances exist.

What does the standard say about cross-gender pat-down searches of female inmates?
options: The facility shall not permit cross-gender pat-down searches of female inmates absent exigent circumstances, and shall not restrict their programming to comply
The facility may permit cross-gender pat-down searches of female inmates if they are documented and a supervisor is present, unless local procedures say otherwise
The facility shall not permit cross-gender pat-downs of female inmates, and may limit their programming to comply
The facility may permit cross-gender pat-down searches of female inmates whenever same-gender staff are not on shift
questions.rationale:
Cross-gender pat-downs of female inmates are not permitted absent exigent circumstances, and facilities may not restrict female inmates' programming opportunities to comply.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.15: “(b) As of August 20, 2015, or August 21, 2017 for a facility whose rated capacity does not exceed 50 inmates, the facility shall not permit cross-gender pat-down searches of female inmates, absent exigent circumstances. Facilities shall not restrict female inmates' access to regularly available programming or other out-of-cell opportunities in order to comply with this provision.”

questions.stem:
Hassan asks his work supervisor for time off to observe a religious holy day that requires a fast and special worship. He did not tell anyone else.

What must Hassan do under the regulation?
options: Submit a written request to the chaplain for time off from work
Tell his work supervisor in person and leave on the day, provided that the action is documented
Ask a fellow inmate of his faith to speak for him
Submit a written request to the Regional Director
questions.rationale:
An inmate must submit a written request to the chaplain for time off from work to observe a religious holy day.

Source — 28 CFR § 548.18: “Consistent with maintaining security, safety, and good order in the institution, the Warden shall endeavor to facilitate the observance of important religious holy days which involve special fasts, dietary regulations, worship, or work proscription. The inmate must submit a written request to the chaplain for time off from work to observe a religious holy day. The Warden may request the chaplain to consult with community representatives of the inmate's faith group and/or other appropriate sources to verify the religious significance of the requested observance. The chaplain will work with requesting inmates to accommodate a proper observance of the holy day. The Warden will ordinarily allow an inmate to take earned vacation days, or to make up for missed work, or to change work assignments in order to facilitate the observance of the religious holy day.”

questions.stem:
Inmate Alvarez wishes to wear a religious medallion and prayer beads throughout the institution, not only in the chapel. The Warden has no security concerns about the items.

What does the regulation say about wearing religious items outside the chapel?
options: Religious items may be worn anywhere in the institution without approval, unless a staff member objects
Upon the inmate's request, the Warden may allow wearing or use of certain religious items throughout the institution, consistent with security, safety, and good order

Upon the inmate's request, the chaplain alone may allow wearing or use of religious items throughout the institution, subject to the Warden's discretion, based on the information available at the time
Religious items may be worn only in the chapel, and the Warden may not allow them elsewhere in the institution
questions.rationale:
Inmates ordinarily may wear or use religious items during services in the chapel, and the Warden may allow wearing throughout the institution on request.

Source — 28 CFR § 548.16: “(b) An inmate ordinarily shall be allowed to wear or use personal religious items during religious services, ceremonies, and meetings in the chapel, unless the Warden determines that the wearing or use of such items would threaten institution security, safety, or good order. Upon request of the inmate, the Warden may allow the wearing or use of certain religious items throughout the institution, consistent with considerations of security, safety, or good order. The Warden may request the chaplain to obtain direction from representatives of the inmate's faith group or other appropriate sources concerning the religious significance of the items.”

questions.stem:
An inmate lists no religious preference at his intake screening and later wants to list a religion.

What does the regulation say about changing a religious preference?
options: An inmate may request a change at any time, but only by submitting the request to the Warden for approval
An inmate may not change a preference after the initial team screening, except at the Warden's discretion
An inmate may request a change once each year by notifying the chaplain in writing, and the change is effective at the next review, where the circumstances reasonably call for it
An inmate may request a change at any time by notifying the chaplain in writing, and the change will be effected in a timely fashion
questions.rationale:
The Bureau does not require an inmate to profess a belief; he may designate any or no preference and change it at any time by notifying the chaplain in writing.

Source — 28 CFR § 548.10: “(c) The Bureau of Prisons does not require an inmate to profess a religious belief. An inmate may designate any or no religious preference at his/her initial team screening. By notifying the chaplain in writing, an inmate may request to change this designation at any time, and the change will be effected in a timely fashion.”

questions.stem:
A pretrial detainee who has not signed a waiver is told to work in the kitchen. He objects.

What is the correct position?
options: A pretrial inmate may be required to do only housekeeping in his own cell and the community living area, unless he signed a waiver
A pretrial inmate may be required to work in any assignment that the work supervisor considers necessary
A pretrial inmate may be required to work in food service, but not in any area that is outside the security perimeter, unless an emergency requires otherwise
A pretrial inmate may be required to work in any assignment, if the unit team documents a shortage of workers
questions.rationale:
A pretrial inmate may not be required to work other than in housekeeping tasks in his own cell and the community living area unless he has signed a waiver of his right not to work.

Source — 28 CFR § 545.23: “(b) A pretrial inmate may not be required to work in any assignment or area other than housekeeping tasks in the inmate's own cell and in the community living area, unless the pretrial inmate has signed a waiver of his or her right not to work (see 28 CFR part 551, subpart J).”

questions.stem:
An inmate is injured on his work detail but is afraid he'll be disciplined if he reports it.

What is he expected to do?
options: Wait until the next sick call, and tell the health services staff about the injury at that time
Notify the work supervisor so that appropriate action, such as medical attention and necessary reports, may be taken
Notify the housing unit officer after the shift, so that a report can be added to the daily count record
Tell the work detail supervisor only if the injury leaves a visible mark or prevents him from working
questions.rationale:
In the event of any work related injury the inmate shall notify the work supervisor so medical attention and reports can follow.

Source — 28 CFR § 545.24: “(e) An inmate is expected to perform the work assignment in a safe manner, using safety equipment as instructed by the work supervisor. In the event of any work related injury, the inmate shall notify the work supervisor so that appropriate action (for example, medical attention, and submission of necessary reports) may be taken.”

questions.stem:
A new inmate asks how long his scheduled work day will be.

What is the ordinary minimum?
options: Seven hours
Twelve hours
Ten hours
Four hours
questions.rationale:
The scheduled work day ordinarily consists of a minimum of seven hours.

Source — 28 CFR § 545.24: “(a) The scheduled work day for an inmate in a federal institution ordinarily consists of a minimum of seven hours.”

questions.stem:
A medical staff member must test an inmate for HIV after the inmate bit a staff member and broke the skin. The inmate refuses to consent.

What does the regulation say about exposure incident testing?
options: Testing is allowed only if the sentence is over six months
Testing requires written consent
Exposure incident testing does not require the inmate's consent
Testing is allowed only for pretrial inmates
questions.rationale:
The Bureau tests an inmate when there is well-founded reason to believe he may have transmitted HIV to employees or others lawfully present, and consent is not required.

Source — 28 CFR § 549.12: “(2) Exposure incidents.
