The Bureau tests an inmate, regardless of the length of sentence or pretrial status, when there is a well-founded reason to believe that the inmate may have transmitted the HIV infection, whether intentionally or unintentionally, to Bureau employees or other non-inmates who are lawfully present in a Bureau institution. Exposure incident testing does not require the inmate's consent.”

questions.stem:
An inmate has just been admitted. Staff want to know when the TB screening must happen.

What is the requirement?
options: Within the first year, as part of the annual health review
Within seven calendar days of initial incarceration
Within thirty calendar days of initial incarceration
Within two calendar days of initial incarceration
questions.rationale:
The Bureau screens each inmate for TB within two calendar days of initial incarceration.

Source — 28 CFR § 549.12: “(b) Tuberculosis (TB). (1) The Bureau screens each inmate for TB within two calendar days of initial incarceration.”

questions.stem:
An inmate with no funds asks for over-the-counter pain medication.

What must the Warden's procedures provide?
options: Up to four OTC medications per week for an inmate without funds, with no restrictions
Up to two OTC medications per month for an inmate without funds
Only one OTC medication each week, and only after a visit to sick call
Up to two OTC medications per week for an inmate without funds
questions.rationale:
The Warden must establish procedures to provide up to two OTC medications per week for an inmate without funds.

Source — 28 CFR § 549.31: “(a) The Warden must establish procedures to provide up to two OTC medications per week for an inmate without funds. An inmate without funds is an inmate who has not had a trust fund account balance of $6.00 for the past 30 days.”

questions.stem:
An inmate asks whether he will be charged a fee for a mental health visit.

What is the answer?
options: No; mental health care is among the services for which the Bureau does not charge a fee
Yes; mental health care is charged unless it is an emergency or the inmate is on suicide watch
Yes; mental health care is charged if the inmate requested the visit himself without a staff referral
No; but substance abuse treatment is charged to the inmate at the standard fee
questions.rationale:
No fee is charged for emergency services, prenatal care, mental health care, substance abuse treatment, preventive services, and others.

Source — 28 CFR § 549.72: “(a) Health care services based on staff referrals; (b) Staff-approved follow-up treatment for a chronic condition; (c) Preventive health care services; (d) Emergency services; (e) Prenatal care; (f) Diagnosis or treatment of chronic infectious diseases; (g) Mental health care; or (h) Substance abuse treatment.”

questions.stem:
A new inmate asks to keep his own civilian clothing in his locker.

What does the regulation say?
options: Civilian clothing is authorized for one week
Civilian clothing ordinarily is not authorized for retention by the inmate
Civilian clothing is authorized if the inmate pays, with the approval of a supervisor on duty
Civilian clothing is always authorized
questions.rationale:
Civilian clothing not issued by the Bureau or purchased from the commissary ordinarily is not authorized for retention.

Source — 28 CFR § 553.11: “(c) Clothing. Civilian clothing (i.e., clothing not issued to the inmate by the Bureau or purchased by the inmate from the commissary) ordinarily is not authorized for retention by the inmate. Civilian clothing which previously had been approved for retention may not be retained after August 6, 1999. Prerelease civilian clothing for an inmate may be retained by staff in the Receiving and Discharge area during the last 30 days of the inmate's confinement.”

questions.stem:
An inmate wants to have two approved radios in his locker.

What is the limit?
options: One approved radio and one approved watch at a time, without any proof of ownership required
One approved radio and two approved watches at a time, with proof of ownership
One approved radio and one approved watch at a time, with proof of ownership
Two approved radios and one approved watch at a time, with proof of ownership
questions.rationale:
An inmate may possess only one approved radio and one approved watch at a time and must be able to demonstrate proof of ownership.

Source — 28 CFR § 553.11: “(f) Radios and Watches. An inmate may possess only one approved radio and one approved watch at a time. The inmate must be able to demonstrate proof of ownership. An inmate who purchases a radio or watch through a Bureau of Prisons commissary is ordinarily permitted the use of that radio or watch at any Bureau institution if the inmate is later transferred. If the inmate is not allowed to use the radio or watch at the new institution, the inmate shall be permitted to mail, at the receiving institution's expense, the radio or watch to a destination of the inmate's choice. Where the inmate refuses to provide a mailing address, the radio and/or watch may be disposed of through approved methods, including destruction of the property.”

questions.stem:
A food service inmate with a beard and long hair is about to start a shift.

What must the Warden require?
options: A beard covering for the inmate with a beard, and a cap or hair net for the inmate with long hair
A beard covering for the inmate with a beard, and a shorter haircut for the inmate with long hair
Nothing, since inmates may choose any hair style and wear a beard in any work area
That the inmate with a beard shave, and a cap or hair net for the inmate with long hair
questions.rationale:
The Warden requires a beard covering for an inmate with a beard, and a cap or hair net for long hair, when working in food service or where there is an increased likelihood of work injury.

Source — 28 CFR § 551.2: “An inmate may wear a mustache or beard or both. The Warden shall require an inmate with a beard to wear a beard covering when working in food service or where a beard could result in increased likelihood of work injury.”
28 CFR § 551.4: “(b) The Warden shall require an inmate with long hair to wear a cap or hair net when working in food service or where long hair could result in increased likelihood of work injury.”

questions.stem:
A supervisor orders an inmate to cut his hair to a uniform length. The inmate keeps his hair neat and clean.

What does the regulation say?
options: The Warden may restrict hair length if the unit team documents a security concern
The Warden may not restrict hair length if the inmate keeps it neat and clean
The Warden may restrict hair length to above the collar for all inmates in food service
The Warden may restrict hair length only for inmates who are housed in a special housing unit
questions.rationale:
The Warden may not restrict hair length if the inmate keeps it neat and clean.

Source — 28 CFR § 551.4: “(a) The Warden may not restrict hair length if the inmate keeps it neat and clean.”

questions.stem:
An inmate's family asks who pays the costs for a marriage license.

What does the regulation say?
options: The chaplain pays from the religious services fund, and the inmate and spouse repay the cost later
The Regional Office pays for the license, and the inmate repays the cost over the next twelve months
The institution pays for the license and ceremony from the inmate welfare fund, but not from appropriated funds, once the shift lieutenant has been informed
The inmate, the intended spouse, the inmate's family, or another source approved by the Warden pays; appropriated funds may not be used
questions.rationale:
All expenses are paid by the inmate, the intended spouse, family, or other approved source; appropriated funds may not be used.

Source — 28 CFR § 551.13: “(c) All expenses of the marriage (for example, a marriage license) shall be paid by the inmate, the inmate's intended spouse, the inmate's family, or other appropriate source approved by the Warden. The Warden may not permit appropriated funds to be used for an inmate marriage.”

questions.stem:
A pretrial inmate refuses to attend his scheduled review with the unit team.

What must staff do?
options: Order the inmate to be disciplined for refusing, and note the discipline in the record of the meeting
Cancel the review and reschedule it after the inmate's next scheduled disciplinary hearing
Ask the court to compel his attendance and record the court's response in the review
Document the refusal and, if known, the reason for it, in the record of the meeting
questions.rationale:
Staff document the inmate's refusal and, if known, the reason.

Source — 28 CFR § 551.107: “(c) A pretrial inmate is expected to attend these reviews. If the inmate refuses to appear, staff shall document in the record of the meeting the inmate's refusal and, if known, the reason for refusal.”

questions.stem:
A pretrial inmate is scheduled for a review in two hours. He was told about it only now.

What does the regulation require?
options: The inmate must be notified at least 48 hours before the scheduled review
He must be notified 1 hour before, according to the institution's local guidelines
No notice is required
He must be notified 7 days before
questions.rationale:
The inmate shall be notified at least 48 hours prior to the scheduled review.

Source — 28 CFR § 551.107: “(b) The inmate shall be notified at least 48 hours prior to the inmate's scheduled review.”

questions.stem:
A pretrial inmate asks to call his attorney on a weekend.

What does the regulation say?
options: Staff shall allow the inmate to telephone his attorney once a week, and attorney visits must be available on weekdays
Staff shall allow the inmate to telephone his attorney as often as institution resources allow, and attorney visits must be available seven days a week
Staff shall allow the inmate to telephone his attorney only with a supervisor present, and visits must be available on weekends
Staff shall allow the inmate to telephone his attorney once a month, and attorney visits must be available during regular visiting hours, provided that the action is documented
questions.rationale:
The Warden provides pretrial inmate-attorney visits seven days a week, and staff allow calls to the attorney as often as resources allow.

Source — 28 CFR § 551.117: “(a) The Warden shall provide the opportunity for pretrial inmate-attorney visits on a seven-days-a-week basis. (c) Staff shall allow the pretrial inmate, upon the inmate's request, to telephone the inmate's attorney as often as resources of the institution allow.”

questions.stem:
A news crew arrives at the institution to photograph inmates in a vocational class. They have no appointment.

What does the regulation require?
options: A media representative shall make advance appointments for visits
Media may not visit at all
Media may visit if the Warden is absent, where the circumstances reasonably call for it
Media may visit without notice
questions.rationale:
A media representative shall make advance appointments for visits.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.62: “(a) A media representative shall make advance appointments for visits.”

questions.stem:
An inmate currently confined in the institution wants to write articles as a reporter for a local newspaper and be paid.

What does the regulation say?
options: An inmate currently confined may act as a reporter only for the institution's own newsletter
An inmate currently confined may act as a reporter if the Warden gives approval and the work is unpaid
An inmate currently confined may not be employed or act as a reporter
An inmate currently confined may act as a reporter if he has a clear disciplinary record for a year
questions.rationale:
An inmate currently confined in an institution may not be employed or act as a reporter.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.62: “(d) An inmate currently confined in an institution may not be employed or act as a reporter.”

questions.stem:
An inmate is lighting a cigarette in the dayroom, saying he is entitled to smoke.

What does the regulation say?
options: Smoking is generally prohibited in and on the grounds of Bureau institutions, with narrow exceptions such as an authorized inmate religious activity
Smoking is generally prohibited in housing units, but is permitted in the dayroom during evening hours
Smoking is generally permitted in cells, but prohibited in the dayroom, dining hall, and recreation yard
Smoking is generally prohibited for inmates under age forty, but permitted for older inmates in designated areas
questions.rationale:
Smoking is generally prohibited in and on the grounds of institutions, except as part of an authorized inmate religious activity and in smoking areas designated by the Warden for staff and official visitors.

Source — 28 CFR § 551.162: “Smoking is generally prohibited in and on the grounds of Bureau institutions and offices, with the following two exceptions: (a) Smoking is permitted as part of an authorized inmate religious activity; and (b) For Bureau staff and official visitors, smoking is permitted only in smoking areas designated by the Warden.”

questions.stem:
An inmate wants to submit a request on behalf of his cellmate, who is illiterate.

What does the regulation say about requests on behalf of others?
options: An inmate may submit an Appeal, but not a Request, on behalf of another inmate
An inmate may submit a Request on behalf of another inmate if both inmates sign the form
An inmate may not submit a Request or Appeal on behalf of another inmate
An inmate may submit a Request on behalf of another inmate if a staff member agrees to witness it
questions.rationale:
An inmate may not submit a Request or Appeal on behalf of another inmate.

Source — 28 CFR § 542.10: “(a) Purpose. The purpose of the Administrative Remedy Program is to allow an inmate to seek formal review of an issue relating to any aspect of his/her own confinement. An inmate may not submit a Request or Appeal on behalf of another inmate.”

questions.stem:
Each institution must name a person responsible for the suicide prevention program, and training for staff and inmate observers.

Who is responsible for ensuring appropriate training is available?
options: The chaplain
The Program Coordinator
The Captain only
The Warden only
questions.rationale:
Each institution has a Program Coordinator who is responsible for ensuring appropriate training is available to staff and to inmates selected as inmate observers.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.41: “(a) Program Coordinator. Each institution must have a Program Coordinator for the institution's suicide prevention program.”
28 CFR § 552.41: “(b) Training. The Program Coordinator is responsible for ensuring that appropriate training is available to staff and to inmates selected as inmate observers.”

questions.stem:
At the visiting room desk, Officer Navarro is checking in a visitor who says he forgot his wallet at home but is "well known to the Warden."

What does the regulation require before the visitor is admitted?
options: Staff verify the identity of each visitor through a driver's license, photo identification, or similar means
Staff accept the visitor's verbal assurance if he knows the inmate's register number
Staff accept the identification of any inmate who is on the visitor's approved list
Staff verify the visitor's identity only on the first visit, and not on later visits
questions.rationale:
Staff must verify the identity of each visitor prior to admission.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.51: “(d) Identification of visitors. Staff shall verify the identity of each visitor (through driver's license, photo identification, etc.) prior to admission of the visitor to the institution.”

questions.stem:
A visitor is handed the written visiting guidelines at check-in but refuses to sign the statement saying he has nothing in his possession that threatens security. He says it is "just a formality."

What may staff do?
options: Admit the visitor and note the refusal in the inmate's central file, based on the information available at the time
Deny the visiting privilege to a visitor who refuses to make the declaration
Admit the visitor if he agrees to a pat search and allow the visit
Admit the visitor but require a staff member to remain at the table
questions.rationale:
Visitors sign a statement acknowledging the guidelines and declaring that they have no threatening articles, and staff may deny the privilege to one who refuses.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.51: “(e) Notification to visitors. Staff shall make available to all visitors written guidelines for visiting the institution. Staff shall have the visitor sign a statement acknowledging that the guidelines were provided and declaring that the visitor does not have any articles in his/her possession which the visitor knows to be a threat to the security of the institution. Staff may deny the visiting privilege to a visitor who refuses to make such a declaration.”

questions.stem:
A visitor objects to being asked to empty his pockets and have his bag searched before a visit, saying he is a lawyer for another case.

What does the regulation say about searching visitors?
options: Staff may search a visitor only with a written order from the Regional Director
Staff may search a visitor only after the visit has ended and the visitor is leaving, as determined by the shift supervisor, for the duration of the incident
Staff may require a visitor to submit to a personal search, including personal property, as a condition of allowing or continuing a visit
Staff may search a visitor only if the visitor has a prior conviction on record
questions.rationale:
Staff may require a visitor to submit to a personal search, including personal property, as a condition of allowing or continuing a visit.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.51: “(f) Searching visitors. Staff may require a visitor to submit to a personal search, including a search of any items of personal property, as a condition of allowing or continuing a visit.”

questions.stem:
A visitor and an inmate hug and kiss briefly at the start of a visit. A new officer thinks that all physical contact should be prohibited.

What does the regulation say about limited physical contact?
options: Staff shall permit physical contact at any point during the visit, as long as it is brief
Staff shall permit limited contact such as handshaking, embracing, and kissing, unless there is clear and convincing evidence it would jeopardize safety or security
Staff shall permit physical contact only between an inmate and a spouse, and not other relatives
Staff shall prohibit all physical contact, since it creates an opportunity to pass contraband
questions.rationale:
Staff shall permit limited physical contact unless clear and convincing evidence shows that it would jeopardize safety or security; where contact visiting is provided, it is ordinarily permitted only at the beginning and end of the visit.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.51: “(2) Staff shall permit limited physical contact, such as handshaking, embracing, and kissing, between an inmate and a visitor, unless there is clear and convincing evidence that such contact would jeopardize the safety or security of the institution. Where contact visiting is provided, handshaking, embracing, and kissing are ordinarily permitted within the bounds of good taste and only at the beginning and at the end of the visit. The staff may limit physical contact to minimize opportunity for the introduction of contraband and to maintain the orderly operation of the visiting area.”

questions.stem:
An inmate wants to add a new visitor to his approved visiting list six months after admission. A staff member says the list can only be set at intake.

What does the regulation say?
options: An inmate's visiting list is set at intake and may not be changed unless the inmate transfers, under the direction of the senior officer present
An inmate's visiting list may be amended at any time in accordance with the procedures of the section
An inmate's visiting list may be amended only by adding immediate family members
An inmate's visiting list may be amended once each year with the Warden's approval
questions.rationale:
An inmate's visiting list may be amended at any time in accordance with the procedures of the section.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.51: “(5) An inmate's visiting list may be amended at any time in accordance with the procedures of this section.”

questions.stem:
A newly arrived inmate has no visiting list from a transferring institution and no way to verify his proposed visitors. A relative who is not immediate family asks to visit during the orientation period.

What may the Warden do?
options: Permit visits only from persons who live within 50 miles of the institution
Permit visits from any approved friends but not from relatives of any kind
Limit visits during the admission-orientation period to the immediate family of the inmate
Deny all visits for the first 30 days, including visits by immediate family
questions.rationale:
The Warden may limit visits during the admission-orientation period or for holdovers to the immediate family where there is neither a visiting list from a transferring institution nor other verification of proposed visitors.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.50: “(a) Admission and holdover status. The Warden may limit to the immediate family of the inmate visits during the admission-orientation period or for holdovers where there is neither a visiting list from a transferring institution nor other verification of proposed visitors.”

questions.stem:
An inmate with a history of threatening a government official is being considered for restricted general correspondence.

Which of these is a determining factor the regulation lists?
options: Having a spouse who lives in another state
Threatening a government official
Receiving a large number of letters each week
Using the commissary to buy writing paper
questions.rationale:
Determining factors include involvement in activities in 540.14(d), soliciting funds or items, being a security risk, threatening a government official, or having committed an offense involving the mail.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.15: “(a) The Warden may place an inmate on restricted general correspondence based on misconduct or as a matter of classification. Determining factors include the inmate's: (4) Threatening a government official; or”

questions.stem:
An inmate in disciplinary segregation asks whether he is allowed to write letters.

What does the regulation say?
options: The Warden shall permit an inmate in segregation to have full correspondence privileges unless he is placed on restricted general correspondence
The Warden shall suspend an inmate's correspondence privileges for the whole period of segregation, as determined by the shift supervisor, for the duration of the incident
The Warden shall permit an inmate in segregation to send but not to receive correspondence
The Warden shall limit an inmate in segregation to one letter a week to immediate family only
questions.rationale:
The Warden shall permit an inmate in segregation to have full correspondence privileges unless placed on restricted general correspondence.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.16: “(b) The Warden shall permit an inmate in segregation to have full correspondence privileges unless placed on restricted general correspondence under § 540.15.”

questions.stem:
A news reporter wants to visit the institution to conduct interviews and asks what she must do.

What does the regulation require of her?
options: Appear at the front desk with a photo identification and a signed letter from her editor
Apply in writing to the Warden, indicating that she is familiar with and agrees to comply with the institution's rules
Apply in writing to the Regional Director, and send a copy of her press credentials
Telephone the Public Information Officer in Washington, DC, and wait for a written authorization, during normal operating hours
questions.rationale:
A news media representative who desires to make a visit or conduct an interview must make application in writing to the Warden, indicating familiarity with the rules and agreement to comply.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.61: “(a) A news media representative who desires to make a visit or conduct an interview at an institution must make application in writing to the Warden, indicating that he or she is familiar with the rules and regulations of the institution and agrees to comply with them.”

questions.stem:
A press pool has been formed to cover a series of requests for interviews. One news network is chosen by the Warden, and the others object.

What does the regulation say about how members are chosen?
options: Members are selected by the inmates, with not more than one representative from each group
Members are selected by the Warden, with not more than two representatives from each group
Members are selected by the Public Information Officer, with not more than one representative from the national group
Members are selected by their peers, with not more than one representative from each of the four groups
questions.rationale:
All members of the press pool are selected by their peers and consist of not more than one representative from each listed group.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.64: “(c) All members of the press pool are selected by their peers and consist of not more than one representative from each of the following groups:”

questions.stem:
Inmate Foster subscribes to a political magazine. The mailroom supervisor wants to reject it because the magazine is critical of the government.

What does the regulation say?
options: The Warden may not reject a publication solely because its content is political, religious, social, or unpopular
The Warden may reject a publication if three staff members find it objectionable
The Warden may reject any publication that criticizes government policy
The Warden may reject political magazines at medium and high security institutions only
questions.rationale:
The Warden may reject a publication only if it is detrimental to security, good order, or discipline or might facilitate criminal activity, and may not reject one solely because of political, religious, philosophical, social, or sexual content or because it is unpopular or repugnant.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.71: “(b) The Warden may reject a publication only if it is determined detrimental to the security, good order, or discipline of the institution or if it might facilitate criminal activity. The Warden may not reject a publication solely because its content is religious, philosophical, political, social or sexual, or because its content is unpopular or repugnant. Publications which may be rejected by a Warden include but are not limited to publications which meet one of the following criteria:”

questions.stem:
A family member sends a paperback novel to an inmate in a minimum security institution from a department store, not a publisher.

Is it allowed?
options: No; softcover publications may be received only from the publisher, a book club, or a bookstore, for the duration of the incident, as long as no other inmate is affected
No; softcover publications may be received only from the family with the Warden's approval
Yes; but only if the Unit Manager gives an exception in writing
Yes; at minimum and low security institutions an inmate may receive softcover publications (other than newspapers) from any source
questions.rationale:
At minimum and low security institutions an inmate may receive softcover publications (other than newspapers) from any source.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.71: “(3) At minimum security and low security institutions, an inmate any receive softcover publications (other than newspapers) from any source.”

questions.stem:
A newly admitted control unit inmate asks what he is entitled to be told.

Which of these must staff provide?
options: The date on which his sentence will end
The names of the staff who recommended his placement
A copy of the psychological evaluations of other inmates in the unit
The criteria for release from the unit and how those criteria relate to his confinement
questions.rationale:
Staff provide notice of projected duration, allowable property, a summary of guidelines and disciplinary procedures, an explanation of activities, expectations of involvement, and the criteria for release and how they relate to his confinement.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.47: “Staff shall provide an inmate admitted to a control unit with: (f) The criteria for release from the unit, and how those criteria specifically relate to this confinement period in the unit and any specific requirements in the inmate's individual case.”

questions.stem:
A Lieutenant is briefing a team before the Use of Force Team Technique is used on an inmate in a locked cell who has refused to give up a piece of metal he broke from a fixture.

What does the regulation say the team ordinarily consists of?
options: Trained staff who spray a chemical agent through the door before entering the cell
Trained staff in protective gear who enter the inmate's area in tandem, each with a coordinated responsibility
Two untrained officers who enter the area in street clothes to speak with the inmate
A single officer in protective gear who restrains the inmate while others observe
questions.rationale:
The technique ordinarily involves trained staff, clothed in protective gear, who enter the inmate's area in tandem, each with a coordinated responsibility for helping achieve immediate control.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.21: “(c) Use of Force Team Technique. If use of force is determined to be necessary, and other means of gaining control of an inmate are deemed inappropriate or ineffective, then the Use of Force Team Technique shall be used to control the inmate and to apply soft restraints, to include ambulatory leg restraints. The Use of Force Team Technique ordinarily involves trained staff, clothed in protective gear, who enter the inmate's area in tandem, each with a coordinated responsibility for helping achieve immediate control of the inmate.”

questions.stem:
Staff have taken physical control of an inmate who attacked an officer. He is handcuffed but continues to kick and resist.

What does policy allow?
options: Staff may apply restraints, such as handcuffs, to an inmate who continues to resist after staff achieve physical control
Staff must remove all restraints once physical control is achieved
Staff may apply restraints only if the Warden is present at the scene
Staff may apply restraints only to the legs and not to the hands
questions.rationale:
Staff may apply restraints (for example, handcuffs) to an inmate who continues to resist after staff achieve physical control, and to any inmate placed under control by the Use of Force Team Technique.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.22: “(e) Staff may apply restraints (for example, handcuffs) to the inmate who continues to resist after staff achieve physical control of that inmate, and may apply restraints to any inmate who is placed under control by the Use of Force Team Technique. If an inmate in a forcible restraint situation refuses to move to another area on his own, staff may physically move that inmate by lifting and carrying the inmate to the appropriate destination.”

questions.stem:
Soft restraints are available, but an officer prefers to use metal restraints for four-point placement because they are "more secure." Soft restraints have not previously failed for this inmate.

What does the regulation require?
options: Either type may be used, at the discretion of the officer applying them, after a supervisor has reviewed the matter, when staff resources allow
Soft restraints must be used unless they previously proved ineffective for that inmate or prove ineffective during the initial application
Soft restraints are used only for juveniles and female inmates
Metal restraints are preferred whenever the inmate has been violent
questions.rationale:
Soft restraints (e.g., vinyl) must be used unless they previously proved ineffective with respect to that inmate or prove ineffective during the initial application procedure.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.24: “(a) Soft restraints (e.g., vinyl) must be used to restrain an inmate, unless: (1) Such restraints previously have proven ineffective with respect to that inmate, or (2) Such restraints are proven ineffective during the initial application procedure.”

questions.stem:
An inmate under close observation tells the officer he is hungry. The cook wants to send a special restricted diet to the cell.

What does the regulation say about meals?
options: The inmate is to be served the same meals as those served to the general population, unless medically contraindicated
The inmate is to be served a liquid diet to prevent concealment of contraband
The inmate is to be served only bread and water until the watch is over
The inmate is to be served meals chosen by the supervisor on duty
questions.rationale:
The inmate is to be served the same meals as those served to the general population, unless medically contraindicated.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.12: “(7) The inmate is to be served the same meals as those served to the general population, unless medically contraindicated.”

questions.stem:
A supervisor asks officers to explain when a pat search may be used on inmates in the dayroom.

What is the correct answer?
options: Staff may conduct a pat search only after the inmate has returned from a visit
Staff may conduct a pat search only after reasonable belief that the inmate has contraband, in accordance with the posted schedule, as long as the unit team is notified
Staff may conduct a pat search on a routine or random basis to control contraband, and it does not require the inmate to remove clothing
Staff may conduct a pat search only after the Warden has approved a search plan
questions.rationale:
Inspection of an inmate using the hands does not require the inmate to remove clothing, includes a search of clothing and personal effects, and may be conducted on a routine or random basis.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.11: “(b) Pat Search. Inspection of an inmate using the hands does not require the inmate to remove clothing. The inspection includes a search of the inmate's clothing and personal effects. Staff may conduct a pat search of an inmate on a routine or random basis to control contraband.”

questions.stem:
Staff plan a search of the inmates' work area and personal items in a locker, at a time when the inmates are in the dining hall.

Is notice or the inmate's presence required?
options: Yes; staff must give 24 hours' notice to every inmate affected by the search, provided that the action is documented
No; staff may search without notice to or prior approval from the inmate and without the inmate's presence
No; but a second officer must be present to count the inmate's belongings
Yes; the inmate must be present to prevent claims that property was taken
questions.rationale:
Staff may search an inmate's housing and work area, and personal items contained within those areas, without notice to or prior approval from the inmate and without the inmate's presence.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.14: “(a) Staff may search an inmate's housing and work area, and personal items contained within those areas, without notice to or prior approval from the inmate and without the inmate's presence.”

questions.stem:
A staff member finds a deck of cards that an inmate bought from the commissary last week and wonders whether to seize it as contraband.

What does the regulation say?
options: Items purchased from the commissary are contraband if they are used for gambling
Items purchased by the inmate from the commissary ordinarily are not considered contraband
Any item found in a locker is contraband until the inmate shows a receipt
Items purchased from the commissary are contraband after seven days
questions.rationale:
Items ordinarily are not considered contraband if the inmate was authorized to retain them on admission, they were issued by staff, purchased from the commissary, or received through approved channels.

Source — 28 CFR § 553.12: “(a) Contraband is defined in § 500.1(h) of this chapter. Items possessed by an inmate ordinarily are not considered to be contraband if the inmate was authorized to retain the item upon admission to the institution, the item was issued by authorized staff, purchased by the inmate from the commissary, or purchased or received through approved channels (to include approved for receipt by an authorized staff member or authorized by institution guidelines).”

questions.stem:
A new Unit Discipline Committee member asks how many days the UDC has to review an incident report.

What is the ordinary time frame?
options: Within five calendar days after the report is issued, counting weekends and holidays, in most circumstances, as long as no other inmate is affected
Within twenty-four hours after the report is issued
Within five work days after the report is issued, not counting the day it was issued, weekends, and holidays
Within ten work days after the hearing before the DHO
questions.rationale:
The UDC will ordinarily review the incident report within five work days after it is issued, not counting the day it was issued, weekends, and holidays.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.7: “(c) Timing. The UDC will ordinarily review the incident report within five work days after it is issued, not counting the day it was issued, weekends, and holidays. UDC review of the incident report may also be suspended if it is being investigated for possible criminal prosecution.”

questions.stem:
A DHO hearing is about to begin for an inmate charged with a prohibited act. The inmate asks who the DHO is allowed to be.

What does the regulation require?
options: The DHO will be the Warden or the Associate Warden, who knows the inmate's history
The DHO will be a member of the UDC who has already reviewed the incident report
The DHO will be the reporting officer's supervisor, who understands the incident report, under the direction of the senior officer present, after a supervisor has reviewed the matter
The DHO will be an impartial decision maker who was not a victim, witness, investigator, or otherwise significantly involved in the incident
questions.rationale:
The DHO will be an impartial decision maker who was not a victim, witness, investigator, or otherwise significantly involved in the incident.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.8: “(b) Discipline Hearing Officer. The DHO will be an impartial decision maker who was not a victim, witness, investigator, or otherwise significantly involved in the incident.”

questions.stem:
A volunteer chaplain's aide asks whether he needs to do anything if an inmate tells him about being sexually abused.

What do the standards require of volunteers and contractors who have contact with inmates?
options: They must keep the information confidential unless asked by the Warden
They must tell the inmate to file a grievance and take no other action
They must refer the inmate to a staff member but need not report it themselves, as long as the unit team is notified
They must be trained on the agency's zero-tolerance policy and on how to report incidents
questions.rationale:
The agency must train volunteers and contractors who have contact with inmates on their responsibilities under the sexual abuse prevention, detection, and response policies.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.32: “(a) The agency shall ensure that all volunteers and contractors who have contact with inmates have been trained on their responsibilities under the agency's sexual abuse and sexual harassment prevention, detection, and response policies and procedures.”

questions.stem:
A pretrial inmate asks his unit officer whether he can be granted a furlough to attend a family event.

What does the regulation say?
options: The Warden may grant a furlough of up to 48 hours with an escort
The Warden may not grant a furlough to a pretrial inmate
The Warden may grant a furlough with the consent of the U.S. Marshal
The Warden may grant a furlough if the inmate has no disciplinary reports
questions.rationale:
The Warden may not grant a furlough to a pretrial inmate. In an emergency, staff facilitate contact with the inmate's attorney of record, who may seek a court decision about release or an escorted trip.

Source — 28 CFR § 551.109: “(a) The Warden may not grant a furlough to a pretrial inmate (18 U.S.C. § 3622). (b) In an emergency, staff shall facilitate contact with the pretrial inmate's attorney of record, who may seek from the court a decision concerning release from custody or an escorted trip.”

questions.stem:
A pretrial inmate's mother is seriously ill, and he asks to attend her bedside. The institution wants to know the proper route.

What does the regulation direct staff to do in an emergency?
options: Allow the Warden to approve an escorted trip without any court involvement
Tell the inmate that no emergency exceptions are available
Facilitate contact with the pretrial inmate's attorney of record, who may seek a court decision about release or an escorted trip
Refer the inmate to the unit team to file a request for a temporary transfer
questions.rationale:
In an emergency, staff shall facilitate contact with the pretrial inmate's attorney of record, who may seek from the court a decision concerning release from custody or an escorted trip.

Source — 28 CFR § 551.109: “(b) In an emergency, staff shall facilitate contact with the pretrial inmate's attorney of record, who may seek from the court a decision concerning release from custody or an escorted trip.”

questions.stem:
A pretrial inmate asks for dental care. A staff member says pretrial detainees are not entitled to the same medical care as sentenced inmates.

What does the regulation say?
options: Staff shall provide the pretrial inmate with emergency medical care only
Staff shall provide the pretrial inmate with the same level of basic medical (including dental), psychiatric, and psychological care provided to convicted inmates
Staff shall provide the pretrial inmate with medical and dental care but not psychiatric care
Staff shall provide the pretrial inmate with care at his own expense
questions.rationale:
Staff shall provide the pretrial inmate with the same level of basic medical (including dental), psychiatric, and psychological care provided to convicted inmates.

Source — 28 CFR § 551.114: “(a) Staff shall provide the pretrial inmate with the same level of basic medical (including dental), psychiatric, and psychological care provided to convicted inmates.”

questions.stem:
A pretrial inmate is released from custody at 10:00 p.m., when the business office is closed.

What must the institution have in place?
options: A rule that funds and property are released only to the U.S. Marshal
A requirement that the inmate remain until the next business day
Procedures that allow for the release of funds and personal property to pretrial inmates released during other than normal business hours
A rule that funds and property are mailed to the inmate within thirty days, based on the information available at the time, with the approval of a supervisor on duty
questions.rationale:
Staff shall establish procedures which allow for release of funds and personal property to pretrial inmates released during other than normal business hours.

Source — 28 CFR § 551.119: “(a) Staff shall establish procedures which allow for the release of funds and personal property to pretrial inmates released during other than normal business hours.”

questions.stem:
A pretrial inmate asks how he will be supervised in terms of custody classification.

What does the regulation say?
options: Staff will supervise a pretrial inmate under the same custody as a convicted inmate in every case, unless an emergency requires otherwise, for the duration of the incident
Staff will supervise a pretrial inmate according to his own request
Staff will supervise a pretrial inmate as if classified "Out" custody at all times
Staff ordinarily will supervise a pretrial inmate as if classified "In" custody, and may use other custody procedures where circumstances warrant
questions.rationale:
Staff ordinarily supervise a pretrial inmate as if classified "In" custody, and where circumstances warrant, may supervise according to procedures for other custody levels.

Source — 28 CFR § 551.105: “(a) Staff ordinarily will supervise a pretrial inmate as if classified “In” custody. (b) Where circumstances warrant, staff may supervise a pretrial inmate according to procedures for other custody levels.”

questions.stem:
A pretrial inmate wants to attend chapel with sentenced inmates, but the Captain is worried about security.

What must staff ensure?
options: When consistent with security and good order, pretrial inmates may participate with convicted inmates; those who do not must have access to other religious programs
Pretrial inmates are not entitled to religious programs while awaiting trial
Pretrial inmates may never participate in religious programs with convicted inmates
Pretrial inmates must always participate with convicted inmates in religious programs
questions.rationale:
Pretrial inmates may be allowed to participate in religious programs with convicted inmates when consistent with institution security and good order, and staff must ensure that those who do not participate have access to other religious programs.

Source — 28 CFR § 551.110: “(a) When consistent with institution security and good order, pretrial inmates may be allowed the opportunity to participate in religious programs with convicted inmates. (b) Staff shall ensure that pretrial inmates who do not participate in religious programs with convicted inmates have access to other religious programs.”

questions.stem:
A law school clinic with Bureau approval sends a student to visit an inmate. The student is not yet an attorney.

What status does the regulation give a student in an approved legal aid program?
options: No status at all, since only licensed attorneys have privileged access
The same status as attorneys with respect to visiting and correspondence, except where specific exceptions are made
The same status as regular visitors, with no special visiting privileges
The same status as media representatives, with a requirement of written appointment, as long as the unit team is notified
questions.rationale:
The Warden shall give students or legal assistants working in legal aid programs the same status as attorneys with respect to visiting and correspondence, except where specific exceptions are made.

Source — 28 CFR § 543.15: “(b) In order to promote the inmate-program relationship, the Warden shall give those students or legal assistants working in legal aid programs the same status as attorneys with respect to visiting and correspondence except where specific exceptions are made in this section and in part 540 of this chapter.”

questions.stem:
An approved legal aid program is supervising law students who are meeting with inmates. The Warden wants to terminate the program because of a dispute with its director.

What does the regulation require?
options: The Warden may terminate the program on his own authority
The Warden may terminate the program after consulting the inmates involved
The Warden shall refer a request or decision to terminate or restrict a program, or individual participants, to the Regional Counsel
The Warden must obtain permission from the supervising attorney before restricting any participant, based on the information available at the time
questions.rationale:
The Warden shall refer a request or decision to terminate or restrict a legal aid program, or individual participants in it, to the Regional Counsel.

Source — 28 CFR § 543.15: “(a) A legal aid program which is funded or approved by the Bureau is expected to provide a broad range of legal assistance to inmates. Staff shall allow these programs generally to operate with the same independence as privately retained attorneys. The Warden shall refer a request or decision to terminate or restrict a program, or individual participants in a program, to the Regional Counsel.”

questions.stem:
An inmate who has worked full-time in an institution work assignment for twelve consecutive months asks about a paid vacation.

What is he eligible for?
options: A ten-day paid vacation at double his hourly rate, approved by the Warden, when staff resources allow, in most circumstances, with the approval of a supervisor on duty
A five-day unpaid vacation, approved by the work supervisor
A thirty-day paid vacation, approved by the Regional Director
A five-day paid vacation at his prevailing hourly rate, recommended by the work supervisor and approved by the Unit Team if performance qualifies
questions.rationale:
An inmate who has worked full-time for 12 consecutive months on an institution work assignment is eligible for a five-day paid vacation at his prevailing hourly rate, recommended by the supervisor through the Department Head to the Unit Team.

Source — 28 CFR § 545.27: “(a) An inmate who has worked full-time for 12 consecutive months on an institution work assignment is eligible to take a five-day paid vacation at the inmate's prevailing hourly rate. A recommendation for an inmate to receive vacation credit is made by the inmate's work supervisor, through the Department Head, to the Unit Team, who shall approve the request if the inmate's work performance qualifies for vacation credit.”

questions.stem:
An inmate completes the Literacy program and asks if there is any recognition for it.

What may the inmate be granted?
options: A reduction of his security level, with the approval of the Captain
An achievement award from performance pay funds, with the prior approval of the Education Department
A transfer to a lower-security institution, with the approval of the Warden
A bonus from the commissary fund, with the approval of the unit team
questions.rationale:
With prior approval of the Education Department, each inmate who completes the Literacy program, Vocational Training, or related trades classroom work part of a certified apprenticeship may be granted an achievement award from performance pay funds.

Source — 28 CFR § 545.28: “(a) With prior approval of the Education Department, each inmate who completes the Literacy program, Vocational Training, or related trades classroom work that is part of a certified apprenticeship program may be granted an achievement award from performance pay funds.”

questions.stem:
An inmate is seeking plastic surgery that the clinical director believes is part of the presently medically necessary standard of treatment.

What must the Clinical Director do?
options: Forward the request to the Warden for initial approval and the Regional Director for final approval
Forward the surgery request to the Office of Medical Designations and Transportation for approval
Deny the request automatically, since plastic surgery is never authorized
Approve the request himself and schedule the surgery
questions.rationale:
Where plastic surgery is a component of the presently medically necessary standard of treatment, the Clinical Director forwards the request to the Office of Medical Designations and Transportation for approval.

Source — 28 CFR § 549.51: “(a) In circumstances where plastic surgery is a component of the presently medically necessary standard of treatment, the Clinical Director shall forward the surgery request to the Office of Medical Designations and Transportation for approval.”

questions.stem:
Plastic surgery has been approved for an inmate, but he is unsure about going ahead.

What does the regulation say?
options: Approved procedures may be performed with the consent of a family member
Approved procedures may be performed without consent if the Warden agrees, based on the information available at the time
Approved plastic surgery procedures may not be performed without the informed consent of the inmate
Approved procedures must be performed as soon as they are scheduled
questions.rationale:
Approved plastic surgery procedures may not be performed without the informed consent of the inmate involved.

Source — 28 CFR § 549.52: “Approved plastic surgery procedures may not be performed without the informed consent of the inmate involved.”

questions.stem:
A supervisor wants to place a newly arrived inmate in administrative detention while classification is pending, and a staff member asks whether an administrative detention order must be issued.

What does the regulation say?
options: An administrative detention order is required only for protection cases, once the shift lieutenant has been informed, after a supervisor has reviewed the matter
An administrative detention order is required only after seven days
An administrative detention order is always required within 24 hours
When placed in administrative detention pending classification or in holdover status, the inmate will not receive an administrative detention order
questions.rationale:
Administrative detention orders are ordinarily provided within 24 hours, but when placed in administrative detention pending classification or in holdover status, the inmate will not receive one.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.25: “(a) Administrative detention status. When placed in administrative detention status, you will receive a copy of the administrative detention order, ordinarily within 24 hours, detailing the reason(s) for your placement. However, when placed in administrative detention status pending classification or while in holdover status, you will not receive an administrative detention order.”

questions.stem:
An inmate is placed in disciplinary segregation at the end of a DHO hearing. He asks how he will find out the reason.

What does the regulation say?
options: He will be informed by the DHO at the end of the discipline hearing
He will receive an order from the Warden within 24 hours
He will be told by the unit officer at the next count
He will be told only at the 30-day review
questions.rationale:
When an inmate is to be placed in disciplinary segregation as a sanction, he will be informed by the DHO at the end of the discipline hearing.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.25: “(b) Disciplinary segregation status. When you are to be placed in disciplinary segregation status as a sanction for violating Bureau regulations, you will be informed by the DHO at the end of your discipline hearing.”

questions.stem:
An inmate worries that he provided information to staff about other inmates, and fears for his safety in the general population.

Which protection-case circumstance applies?
options: Victim of inmate assault, because he has been hit
Staff concern based on a prior disciplinary record
Inmate informant: his safety is threatened because he provided or is perceived as having provided information to staff or law enforcement
Inmate refusal to enter general population for no reason
questions.rationale:
A protection case may be an inmate informant whose safety is threatened because he provided, or is perceived as having provided, information to staff or law enforcement about other inmates or persons in the community.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.27: “(b) Inmate informant. Your safety is threatened because you provided, or are perceived as having provided, information to staff or law enforcement authorities regarding other inmates or persons in the community.”

questions.stem:
An agency's policy documents do not show that volunteers understood their PREA training.

What does the standard require the agency to maintain?
options: A list of the volunteers who completed the training last year
A copy of the training outline only
Documentation confirming that volunteers and contractors understand the training they have received
A signed statement from the Warden that training occurred
questions.rationale:
The agency shall maintain documentation confirming that volunteers and contractors understand the training they have received.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.32: “(c) The agency shall maintain documentation confirming that volunteers and contractors understand the training they have received.”

questions.stem:
A contract is being renewed with a private company that will house inmates for the agency.

What must a new contract or renewal include?
options: The entity's obligation to adopt and comply with the PREA standards, and provision for agency contract monitoring
A requirement that the entity set its own standards for sexual abuse prevention
A requirement that the entity report to the agency only after an incident is substantiated, during normal operating hours
An exemption from the standards for facilities with fewer than 100 inmates
questions.rationale:
A public agency that contracts for confinement of its inmates shall include in any new contract or renewal the entity's obligation to adopt and comply with the PREA standards, and provide for agency contract monitoring.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.12: “(a) A public agency that contracts for the confinement of its inmates with private agencies or other entities, including other government agencies, shall include in any new contract or contract renewal the entity's obligation to adopt and comply with the PREA standards.”
28 CFR § 115.12: “(b) Any new contract or contract renewal shall provide for agency contract monitoring to ensure that the contractor is complying with the PREA standards.”

questions.stem:
A newly transferred inmate has already received PREA education at his previous facility. Staff ask whether further education is necessary.

What does the standard require?
options: Inmates receive education upon transfer to a different facility to the extent that the new facility's policies and procedures differ from those of the previous facility
No further education is required after the first facility
Education must be repeated in full at every facility
Education is required only if the inmate asks for it in writing
questions.rationale:
Current inmates shall receive education upon transfer to a different facility to the extent that the policies and procedures of the new facility differ from those of the previous facility.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.33: “(c) Current inmates who have not received such education shall be educated within one year of the effective date of the PREA standards, and shall receive education upon transfer to a different facility to the extent that the policies and procedures of the inmate's new facility differ from those of the previous facility.”

questions.stem:
A facility wants to rely on a single orientation video as proof that inmates have key PREA information, with nothing posted in the housing units.

What else does the standard require?
options: The agency shall ensure that key information is posted only in the visiting room
The agency shall ensure that key information is continuously and readily available or visible to inmates through posters, inmate handbooks, or other written formats
The agency shall ensure that key information is available only to staff
The agency shall ensure that key information is available only to inmates who request it
questions.rationale:
In addition to education, the agency shall ensure that key information is continuously and readily available or visible to inmates through posters, inmate handbooks, or other written formats.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.33: “(f) In addition to providing such education, the agency shall ensure that key information is continuously and readily available or visible to inmates through posters, inmate handbooks, or other written formats.”

questions.stem:
A facility's records do not show which inmates attended PREA education sessions.

What does the standard require?
options: The agency shall keep no records, to protect inmate privacy
The agency shall record only the sessions in which an incident was reported, in accordance with the posted schedule
The agency shall maintain documentation of inmate participation in these education sessions
The agency shall record participation for juvenile inmates only
questions.rationale:
The agency shall maintain documentation of inmate participation in these education sessions.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.33: “(e) The agency shall maintain documentation of inmate participation in these education sessions.”

questions.stem:
An inmate tells Officer Prieto he has no one to call and asks whether he can place a collect call because he just arrived at the institution.

What does the regulation say about collect calls for new arrivals?
options: The Warden may allow collect calls for good cause, and new arrivals, including new commitments and transfers, are given as an example
Collect calls are never allowed at any Bureau institution
Collect calls are allowed only after thirty days of good conduct
Collect calls are allowed only for inmates who have family emergencies, after a supervisor has reviewed the matter, in accordance with the posted schedule
questions.rationale:
The Warden may allow collect calls for good cause, such as new arrivals (new commitments and transfers), pretrial inmates, holdovers, inmates without funds, and family emergencies.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.101: “(e) Exception. The Warden may allow the placement of collect calls for good cause. Examples of good cause include, but are not limited to, inmates who are new arrivals to the institution, including new commitments and transfers; inmates confined at Metropolitan Correctional Centers, Metropolitan Detention Centers, or Federal Detention Centers; pretrial inmates; inmates in holdover status; inmates who are without funds (see § 540.105(b)); and in cases of family emergencies.”

questions.stem:
An inmate who ran a business before commitment asks to have a business partner visit to make a major decision that will substantially affect the business's assets.

What may the Warden do?
options: Deny all business visits, since inmates may never discuss business
Permit regular business visits each week with no limit
Permit a special business visit where a decision must be made that will substantially affect the assets or prospects of the business
Permit a business visit only if the Regional Director approves it
questions.rationale:
An inmate is expected to assign authority for a business to someone in the community, but the Warden may permit a special business visit when a decision must be made that will substantially affect the assets or prospects of the business.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.45: “(a) Business visitor. Except for pretrial inmates, an inmate is not permitted to engage actively in a business or profession. An inmate who was engaged in a business or profession prior to commitment is expected to assign authority for the operation of such business or profession to a person in the community. Pretrial inmates may be allowed special visitors for the purpose of protecting the pretrial inmate's business interests. In those instances where an inmate has turned over the operation of a business or profession to another person, there still may be an occasion where a decision must be made which will substantially affect the assets or prospects of the business. The Warden accordingly may permit a special business visit in such cases. The Warden may waive the requirement for the existence of an established relationship prior to confinement for visitors approved under this paragraph.”

questions.stem:
An inmate keeps a draft court pleading in his locker. The draft has his name and case caption prominently displayed on the first page. A new officer wonders whether it counts as legal material.

What does the regulation say?
options: Drafts of pleadings to be submitted to a court that contain the inmate's name or case caption prominently on the first page are included among legal materials

Drafts are contraband unless a staff member has approved them in advance, as determined by the shift supervisor, with the approval of a supervisor on duty, under the direction of the senior officer present
Only photocopies of legal reference books count as legal materials
Only documents already filed in court count as legal materials
questions.rationale:
An inmate's legal materials include pleadings filed in court, drafts of pleadings to be submitted that have his name or case caption prominently on the first page, documents pertaining to his administrative case, photocopies of legal reference materials, and certain legal reference materials.

Source — 28 CFR § 543.11: “(d) An inmate's legal materials include but are not limited to the inmate's pleadings and documents (such as a presentence report) that have been filed in court or with another judicial or administrative body, drafts of pleadings to be submitted by the inmate to a court or with other judicial or administrative body which contain the inmate's name and/or case caption prominently displayed on the first page, documents pertaining to an inmate's administrative case, photocopies of legal reference materials, and legal reference materials which are not available in the institution main law library (or basic law library in a satellite camp).”

questions.stem:
An inmate has been exposed to blood in a fight, and medical staff want to run a test to verify whether a bloodborne pathogen was transmitted. He refuses.

What does the regulation say?
options: The Bureau may test only if the inmate gives written consent
The Bureau may not test, since refusal ends the matter
The Bureau tests an inmate for an infectious disease when necessary to verify transmission following exposure, and an inmate who refuses is subject to an incident report
The Bureau may test only if the Warden approves it in writing
questions.rationale:
The Bureau tests an inmate for an infectious or communicable disease when the test is necessary to verify transmission following exposure to bloodborne pathogens or infectious body fluid, and an inmate who refuses is subject to an incident report for refusing to obey an order.

Source — 28 CFR § 549.12: “(c) Diagnostics. The Bureau tests an inmate for an infectious or communicable disease when the test is necessary to verify transmission following exposure to bloodborne pathogens or to infectious body fluid. An inmate who refuses diagnostic testing is subject to an incident report for refusing to obey an order.”

questions.stem:
A medically unassigned inmate is told he cannot do any work at all, including cleaning his own cell.

What does the regulation say?
options: Medically unassigned inmates may be required to work in food service
Medically unassigned inmates may be required, to the extent medically possible, to perform housekeeping tasks in their own cell and the community living area
Medically unassigned inmates may be required to work only outside the secure perimeter, in accordance with the posted schedule, with the approval of a supervisor on duty
Medically unassigned inmates may never be required to do any work
questions.rationale:
Medically unassigned inmates may be required, to the extent medically possible, to perform housekeeping tasks in the inmate's own cell and in the community living area.

Source — 28 CFR § 545.23: “(c) Medically unassigned inmates may be required, to the extent medically possible, to perform housekeeping tasks in the inmate's own cell and in the community living area.”

questions.stem:
An inmate leaves his work detail early to talk to a friend without telling the supervisor.

What does the regulation say?
options: An inmate may leave a work assignment if another inmate covers for him, as long as the unit team is notified, with the approval of a supervisor on duty
An inmate may leave a work assignment whenever the task is finished
An inmate may not leave an assignment without permission, and is expected to report to the place of assignment at the required time
An inmate may leave a work assignment during the last hour of the day
questions.rationale:
An inmate is expected to report to the place of assignment at the required time and may not leave an assignment without permission.

Source — 28 CFR § 545.24: “(b) An inmate is expected to report to the place of assignment at the required time. An inmate may not leave an assignment without permission.”

questions.stem:
An inmate is placed in holdover status while being transferred to a designated institution.

Which status is this inmate in, and why?
options: Close observation, because transfers carry a risk of concealed contraband, according to the institution's local guidelines
Disciplinary segregation, because he is moving between institutions
Protective custody, because all transferred inmates are protection cases
Administrative detention, because holdover status during transfer is one of the reasons for placement
questions.rationale:
An inmate may be placed in administrative detention for pending classification, holdover status during transfer, or removal from general population because of a threat.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.23: “(b) Holdover Status. You are in holdover status during transfer to a designated institution or other destination.”

questions.stem:
A psychologist assesses an inmate on suicide watch. A staff member asks who decides what happens next.

What does the regulation say?
options: The Warden decides the intervention after reading the assessment, during normal operating hours, with the approval of a supervisor on duty, as long as the unit team is notified
The inmate decides the intervention with his psychologist
Upon completion of the clinical assessment, the Program Coordinator or designee will determine the appropriate intervention that best meets the needs of the inmate
The unit team decides the intervention by majority vote
questions.rationale:
A psychologist clinically assesses each inmate placed on suicide watch, and upon completion the Program Coordinator or designee determines the appropriate intervention.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.41: “(e) Assessment. A psychologist will clinically assess each inmate placed on suicide watch. (f) Intervention. Upon completion of the clinical assessment, the Program Coordinator or designee will determine the appropriate intervention that best meets the needs of the inmate.”

questions.stem:
A suicide watch room is being designated at a new institution. The architect suggests a room that is isolated at the far end of a corridor with no sight line.

What must the designated room allow?
options: Staff to leave the inmate unobserved for fifteen minutes at a time
Staff to observe the inmate only through a camera at the control center, as long as the unit team is notified, based on the information available at the time
Staff to house two inmates in the room at the same time
Staff to maintain adequate control of the inmate without compromising the ability to observe and protect the inmate
questions.rationale:
Each institution must have one or more rooms specifically for suicide watch, and the room must allow staff to maintain adequate control of the inmate without compromising the ability to observe and protect the inmate.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.42: “(a) Housing. Each institution must have one or more rooms designated specifically for housing an inmate on suicide watch. The designated room must allow staff to maintain adequate control of the inmate without compromising the ability to observe and protect the inmate.”

questions.stem:
A search team asks which method to start with when an inmate is suspected of carrying a small item.

What principle does the regulation set?
options: Staff shall select the method that takes the least time for the officers
Staff shall employ the least intrusive method of search practicable, as indicated by the type of contraband and the method of suspected introduction
Staff shall begin with the most thorough method available to avoid missing contraband
Staff shall use a visual search for every suspected item
questions.rationale:
Staff shall employ the least intrusive method of search practicable, as indicated by the type of contraband and the method of suspected introduction.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.10: “In order to further the safe, secure, and orderly running of its institutions, the Bureau of Prisons conducts searches of inmates and of inmate housing and work areas to locate contraband and to deter its introduction and movement. Staff shall employ the least intrusive method of search practicable, as indicated by the type of contraband and the method of suspected introduction.”

questions.stem:
An inmate has a hobby project, a large painting, that does not fit in his locker. The officer wants to treat it as contraband.

What does the regulation say?
options: Staff must destroy any item that does not fit in a locker
Staff may make an exception only if the painting is a religious item, in accordance with the posted schedule, unless an emergency requires otherwise, for the duration of the incident
Staff may make an exception for an item whose size prohibits placing it in a locker, with the understanding that the placement is at the inmate's own risk
Staff must store the painting in the Warden's office
questions.rationale:
Staff shall limit hobby projects to those that can be stored in designated containers, but may make an exception for an item (such as a painting) where size prohibits it, at the inmate's own risk.

Source — 28 CFR § 553.11: “(e) Hobbycraft materials. Staff shall limit an inmate's hobby shop projects within the cell or living area to those projects which the inmate may store in designated personal property containers. Staff may make an exception for an item (for example, a painting) where size would prohibit placing the item in a locker. This exception is made with the understanding that the placement of the item is at the inmate's own risk. Staff shall require that hobby shop items be removed from the living area when completed, and be disposed of in accordance with the provisions of part 544, subpart D, of this chapter.”

questions.stem:
An inmate with a radio is transferred to another institution that does not allow that model.

What does the regulation say?
options: He must destroy the radio at his own expense
He must give the radio to the receiving institution's chaplain
He must leave the radio at the old institution until his release, during normal operating hours, based on the information available at the time
He shall be permitted to mail the radio, at the receiving institution's expense, to a destination of his choice
questions.rationale:
If the inmate is not allowed to use the radio or watch at the new institution, he shall be permitted to mail it, at the receiving institution's expense, to a destination of his choice.

Source — 28 CFR § 553.11: “(f) Radios and Watches. An inmate may possess only one approved radio and one approved watch at a time. The inmate must be able to demonstrate proof of ownership. An inmate who purchases a radio or watch through a Bureau of Prisons commissary is ordinarily permitted the use of that radio or watch at any Bureau institution if the inmate is later transferred. If the inmate is not allowed to use the radio or watch at the new institution, the inmate shall be permitted to mail, at the receiving institution's expense, the radio or watch to a destination of the inmate's choice. Where the inmate refuses to provide a mailing address, the radio and/or watch may be disposed of through approved methods, including destruction of the property.”

questions.stem:
A facility has no written plan on how first responders, medical staff, investigators, and leadership will work together after a sexual abuse incident.

What does the standard require?
options: A plan limited to the actions of the medical staff
A written institutional plan to coordinate actions among staff first responders, medical and mental health practitioners, investigators, and facility leadership
A verbal agreement among supervisors on duty
A plan written only by the PREA coordinator and not shared with staff
questions.rationale:
The facility shall develop a written institutional plan to coordinate actions taken in response to an incident of sexual abuse, among staff first responders, medical and mental health practitioners, investigators, and facility leadership.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.65: “The facility shall develop a written institutional plan to coordinate actions taken in response to an incident of sexual abuse, among staff first responders, medical and mental health practitioners, investigators, and facility leadership.”

questions.stem:
Sergeant Imani wants to place an inmate who is calm in an administrative detention cell in restraints "just to be safe" while she completes paperwork. There is no immediate need for restraints.

What does policy require before she may do this?
options: Approval of the unit team at its next meeting
Approval of the Warden or designee
Written consent from the inmate
Approval of the Captain by radio
questions.rationale:
Restraints may be applied in administrative detention or disciplinary segregation without immediate need only with the Warden's or designee's approval.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.22: “(g) Except when the immediate use of restraints is required for control of the inmate, staff may apply restraints to, or continue the use of progressive restraints on, an inmate while in a cell in administrative detention or disciplinary segregation only with approval of the Warden or designee.”

questions.stem:
At 8 hours and 30 minutes, an inmate remains in four-point restraints and is still combative. The institution administrative duty officer is on site.

Which pair of actions does policy require at this point?
options: Qualified health personnel supervise the restraint, and the Regional Director or Duty Officer is notified by telephone
The inmate is released, and the incident report is filed with the unit team
The Lieutenant continues reviews every two hours, and the Warden signs the incident report
The restraint is converted to handcuffs, and the Captain notifies the inmate's family
questions.rationale:
Use beyond eight hours requires supervision by qualified health personnel, and restraint longer than eight hours requires telephone notice up the chain.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.24: “(f) When the inmate is placed in four-point restraints, qualified health personnel shall initially assess the inmate to ensure appropriate breathing and response (physical or verbal). Staff shall also ensure that the restraints have not restricted or impaired the inmate's circulation. When inmates are so restrained, qualified health personnel ordinarily are to visit the inmate at least twice during each eight hour shift. Use of four-point restraints beyond eight hours requires the supervision of qualified health personnel. Mental health and qualified health personnel may be asked for advice regarding the appropriate time for removal of the restraints.”
28 CFR § 552.24: “(g) When it is necessary to restrain an inmate for longer than eight hours, the Warden (or designee) or institution administrative duty officer shall notify the Regional Director or Regional Duty Officer by telephone.”

questions.stem:
A pregnant inmate becomes violent, and staff are considering four-point restraints.

What does policy say about how she may be restrained?
options: In handcuffs behind the back only, since four-point restraints are never allowed, when staff resources allow, subject to the Warden's discretion
In other than face down four-point restraints, with the deciding staff assuming responsibility for her care
In any position, provided the Warden approves it in writing afterward
In face down four-point restraints, to protect her from injury
questions.rationale:
