When mental health or health personnel find an inmate needs continuing care, and especially when she is pregnant, the deciding staff assume responsibility, including restraining her in other than face-down four-point restraints.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.26: “(a) In immediate use of force situations, staff shall seek the assistance of mental health or qualified health personnel upon gaining physical control of the inmate. When possible, staff shall seek such assistance at the onset of the violent behavior. In calculated use of force situations, the use of force team leader shall seek the guidance of qualified health personnel (based upon a review of the inmate's medical record) to identify physical or mental problems. When mental health staff or qualified health personnel determine that an inmate requires continuing care, and particularly when the inmate to be restrained is pregnant, the deciding staff shall assume responsibility for the inmate's care, to include possible admission to the institution hospital, or, in the case of a pregnant inmate, restraining her in other than face down four-point restraints.”

questions.stem:
An armed, barricaded inmate threatens staff. A sergeant on scene wants to use a chemical agent immediately, and the Warden is off site.

Who may authorize the use of a less-than-lethal weapon in this situation?
options: A supervisor to whom the Warden has delegated authority, on duty and physically present, not below Lieutenant
The sergeant on scene, because the threat is immediate and a delay could endanger staff, as long as the unit team is notified
Any officer trained in the weapon who is on duty and physically present at the scene
Any Lieutenant the Warden can reach by telephone, even if he is off duty at home
questions.rationale:
A sergeant is below the rank of Lieutenant, so the authority must come from the Warden or a delegated supervisor, on duty and physically present, at Lieutenant or above.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.25: “(b) The Warden may delegate the authority under this regulation to one or more supervisors on duty and physically present, but not below the position of Lieutenant.”

questions.stem:
Officer Okonkwo is assaulted by an inmate wielding a metal pipe. He hits the alarm and uses force to stop the attack because there was no time to ask for help.

Which type of use of force does this describe, and why?
options: A Use of Force Team Technique, because several staff responded
Calculated use of force, because the inmate was in an area that could be isolated, after a supervisor has reviewed the matter
An exception to policy, because no supervisor was present
Immediate use of force, because the behavior was an immediate, serious threat to staff and security
questions.rationale:
Staff may immediately use force and restraints when behavior constitutes an immediate, serious threat to the inmate, staff, others, property, or security.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.21: “(a) Immediate use of force. Staff may immediately use force and/or apply restraints when the behavior described in § 552.20 constitutes an immediate, serious threat to the inmate, staff, others, property, or to institution security and good order.”

questions.stem:
A female inmate has been placed in a special housing unit, and the only officer available for the search right now is male. A same-sex officer will be on duty in two hours. The inmate could conceal contraband before then.

What does the regulation allow?
options: A search by another inmate who is trained in searches
A visual search by the male officer if delay would likely mean loss of contraband, with the reasons documented in the central file
A visual search by the male officer, with no documentation required
No search until a female officer arrives, with no exceptions
questions.rationale:
Same-sex staff conduct visual searches, except where delay would mean the likely loss of contraband, in which case the reasons for the opposite-sex search must be documented in the central file.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.11: “(2) Staff of the same sex as the inmate shall make the search, except where circumstances are such that delay would mean the likely loss of contraband. Where staff of the opposite sex makes a visual search, staff shall document the reasons for the opposite sex search in the inmate's central file.”

questions.stem:
Officer Petrakis suspects an inmate has hidden contraband in a body cavity. He proposes to perform a digital search himself in the unit's bathroom.

What should the supervisor say?
options: Designated qualified health personnel may do this with the Lieutenant's approval, and it need not be documented
Qualified health personnel may do this, but only with the inmate's written consent, which must be documented
Only designated qualified health personnel may do this, with the approval of the Warden or Acting Warden, and it must be documented in the central file

Any trained officer may do this, with the approval of the Captain, and it must be documented in the central file, unless an emergency requires otherwise, based on the information available at the time
questions.rationale:
A digital or simple instrument search may be conducted only by designated qualified health personnel, upon approval of the Warden or Acting Warden, and must be documented.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.11: “(d) Digital or simple instrument search—inspection for contraband or any other foreign item in a body cavity of an inmate by use of fingers or simple instruments, such as an otoscope, tongue blade, short nasal speculum, and simple forceps. A digital or simple instrument search may be conducted only by designated qualified health personnel (for example, physicians, physician assistants, and nurses) upon approval of the Warden or Acting Warden and only if the Warden or Acting Warden has reasonable belief that an inmate is concealing contraband in or on his person. If located, the contraband or foreign item may be removed immediately by medical staff if such removal can easily be effected by use of fingers or the simple instruments referred to above. Staff shall document all digital and simple instrument searches and the reasons for the searches in the inmate's central file.”

questions.stem:
Officers believe an inmate swallowed a balloon of contraband. A pat search would not find it, and an invasive search would likely injure him. The Captain asks what authority is needed to hold the inmate under close observation.

Who may authorize the placement?
options: The Warden or designee
The Segregation Review Official
The unit team
Any supervising officer on the shift
questions.rationale:
Close observation is allowed where there is reasonable belief of ingested or concealed contraband and standard searches are inappropriate or risky; the Warden or designee authorizes it.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.12: “When there is reasonable belief that an inmate has ingested contraband or concealed contraband in a body cavity and the methods of search specified in § 552.11 are inappropriate or likely to result in physical injury to the inmate, the Warden or designee may authorize the placement of an inmate in a room or cell for the purpose of staff's closely observing that inmate until the inmate has voided the contraband or until sufficient time has elapsed to preclude the possibility that the inmate is concealing contraband.”

questions.stem:
An inmate is on close observation. A male staff member is assigned to watch a male inmate, but wants to turn off the cell light at night so the inmate can sleep and leave the cell door area for short periods.

Which requirement does this plan violate?
options: The inmate must be allowed to keep personal property in the cell
The light must be kept on at all times and the supervising staff member must maintain complete and constant visual supervision
The inmate must be fed only meals not served to the general population, subject to the Warden's discretion, where the circumstances reasonably call for it
The staff member must be a supervisor of Lieutenant rank or higher
questions.rationale:
Close observation requires constant visual supervision, and the light must remain on at all times so staff can see any attempt to move contraband.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.12: “(b) The supervising staff member shall be the same sex as the inmate and shall maintain complete and constant visual supervision of the inmate.”
28 CFR § 552.12: “(2) The light will be kept on at all times.”

questions.stem:
Staff seized a weapon from an inmate's cell. The case is not going to be prosecuted, and the weapon is destroyed. The supervisor asks how long the written documentation of the destruction must be kept.

What is the answer?
options: At least one year
At least two years
Until the next shift change
At least thirty days
questions.rationale:
Hard contraband may be destroyed when not needed for prosecution, and written documentation of the destruction must be maintained for at least two years.

Source — 28 CFR § 553.13: “(c) Staff shall retain items of hard contraband for disciplinary action or prosecution or both. The contraband items may be delivered to law enforcement personnel for official use. When it is determined that the item is not needed for criminal prosecution, the hard contraband shall be destroyed as provided in paragraph (b)(2)(v) of this section. Written documentation of the destruction shall be maintained for at least two years.”

questions.stem:
Officer Murray finds $300 in cash in an inmate's property. That is above the institution's limit. A disciplinary action is pending.

What must happen with the cash?
options: It is held in the officer's locker until the investigation ends, and then destroyed with written documentation
It is delivered to the cashier and credited to the U.S. Treasury at once, with the inmate allowed to prove ownership later
It is delivered to the cashier, final disposition waits until discipline and appeals end, and the inmate gets a reasonable time to prove ownership
It is returned to the inmate after a warning, and the disciplinary action proceeds on the incident report alone
questions.rationale:
Cash over the allowable limit goes to the cashier; where discipline is appropriate, final disposition waits until it and appeals end, and the inmate may prove ownership first.

Source — 28 CFR § 553.13: “(d) Staff may not allow an inmate to possess funds in excess of established institutional limits. Staff shall deliver to the cashier any cash or negotiable instruments found in an inmate's possession which exceed the institution's allowable limits. Funds determined to be contraband shall be confiscated for crediting to the U.S. Treasury. (1) Where disciplinary action against the inmate is appropriate, staff shall delay final disposition of the funds until such action (including appeals) is completed. (2) Prior to a decision on the disposition of funds, staff shall allow the inmate a reasonable amount of time to prove ownership.”

questions.stem:
Staff plan to remove a locked-in inmate who has refused to come out of his cell for two hours. He is quiet, appears non-threatening, and says he is afraid to leave. A mental health professional has been called.

Which factor should guide staff before they decide to use force?
options: Whether the situation can be resolved without resorting to force, since there is time for calculated action
Whether other inmates may learn of the refusal, since it could encourage similar behavior
Whether the shift is scheduled to end soon, since an incoming shift may be unfamiliar with the inmate
Whether the inmate has refused two direct orders, since a second refusal justifies the use of a force team
questions.rationale:
Where an inmate can be isolated and there is no immediate threat, staff must first determine if the situation can be resolved without force.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.21: “(b) Calculated use of force and/or application of restraints. This occurs in situations where an inmate is in an area that can be isolated (e.g., a locked cell, a range) and where there is no immediate, direct threat to the inmate or others. When there is time for the calculated use of force or application of restraints, staff must first determine if the situation can be resolved without resorting to force (see § 552.23).”

questions.stem:
A supervisor asks an officer how much force is acceptable once an inmate who attacked staff is under control and is no longer resisting.

Which statement is consistent with policy?
options: Staff may use force until a supervisor orders them to stop
Staff may use only the amount of force necessary to gain control of the inmate
Staff may use as much force as the other officers on the team agree upon, when staff resources allow
Staff may use enough force to make certain it will not happen again
questions.rationale:
Force is limited to the amount necessary to gain control; once control is achieved and the inmate is not resisting, continued force is not authorized.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.22: “(c) Staff shall use only that amount of force necessary to gain control of the inmate. Situations when an appropriate amount of force may be warranted include, but are not limited to:”

questions.stem:
Officer Zhou used a restraint that pressed on an inmate's neck to hold him down. The inmate began to have trouble breathing, and a coworker said it was normal.

What does policy say?
options: Neck restraint is allowed if the officer has completed defensive tactics training, unless local procedures say otherwise, as long as the unit team is notified
Neck restraint is allowed if a second officer watches the inmate's breathing
Restraint equipment may not be used about the neck or face or in a manner that restricts circulation or obstructs the airways
Neck restraint is allowed for up to two minutes if the inmate is violent
questions.rationale:
Restraint equipment may not be used about an inmate's neck or face, or in any manner which restricts blood circulation or obstructs the inmate's airways.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.22: “(2) About an inmate's neck or face, or in any manner which restricts blood circulation or obstructs the inmate's airways.”

questions.stem:
A supervisor wants to use a metal detector wand on every inmate entering the dining hall as a routine measure, without any specific suspicion.

Is this permitted?
options: No; electronic searches may be done only on inmates returning from visits
No; electronic searches require reasonable belief that contraband is concealed
Yes; staff may conduct electronic device searches on a routine or random basis to control contraband, and the inmate does not have to remove clothing
Yes; but inmates must remove their shoes and outer clothing
questions.rationale:
Inspection with electronic devices does not require the inmate to remove clothing and may be conducted on a routine or random basis to control contraband.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.11: “(a) Electronic devices. Inspection of an inmate's person using electronic devices (for example, metal detector, ion spectrometry device, or body imaging search device) does not require the inmate to remove clothing. The inspection may also include a search of the inmate's clothing and personal effects. Staff may conduct an electronic device search of an inmate on a routine or random basis to control contraband.”

questions.stem:
A search team plans a visual search of an inmate. They intend to do it in the open housing unit so "everyone sees it happens fairly."

What is wrong with this plan?
options: The visual search must be done only after the inmate's consent, where the circumstances reasonably call for it
The visual search must be done in the presence of a chaplain
The visual search must be done by a Lieutenant
The visual search must be made in a manner designed to assure as much privacy to the inmate as practicable
questions.rationale:
A visual search must be made in a manner designed to assure as much privacy to the inmate as practicable.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.11: “(1) Staff may conduct a visual search where there is reasonable belief that contraband may be concealed on the person, or a good opportunity for concealment has occured. For example, placement in a special housing unit (see 28 CFR part 541, subpart B), leaving the institution, or re-entry into an institution after contact with the public (after a community trip, court transfer, or after a “contact” visit in a visiting room) is sufficient to justify a visual search. The visual search shall be made in a manner designed to assure as much privacy to the inmate as practicable.”

questions.stem:
An inmate establishes that he owns an altered radio that is now classified as contraband (not hard contraband). He is unwilling to pay postage to mail it home and refuses to provide a mailing address.

What does the regulation permit staff to do?
options: Return the radio to the inmate's locker
Dispose of the property through approved methods, including destruction
Give the radio to another inmate
Hold the radio for the inmate until release
questions.rationale:
Where ownership is established but the inmate is financially able and unwilling to pay postage or refuses to provide a mailing address, the property is disposed of through approved methods, including destruction.

Source — 28 CFR § 553.13: “(iii) If the inmate establishes ownership, but the item is identified as contraband, staff shall mail such items (other than hard contraband), at the inmate's expense, to a destination of the inmate's choice. The Warden or designee may authorize the institution to pay the cost of such mailings when the item had not been altered and originally had been permitted for admission to the institution or had been purchased from the commissary, or where the inmate has insufficient funds and no likelihood of new funds being received. Where the inmate has established ownership of a contraband item, but is unwilling, although financially able to pay postage as required, or refuses to provide a mailing address for return of the property, the property is to be disposed of through approved methods, including destruction of the property.”

questions.stem:
A Unit Discipline Committee (UDC) is being formed to review an incident report. Lieutenant Greer, who investigated the incident, is available and offers to serve.

Why can he not serve?
options: UDC members will not be victims, witnesses, investigators, or otherwise significantly involved in the incident
UDC members must hold a rank below Lieutenant so that the investigator can supervise their review
UDC members must be approved by the inmate before the review of the incident report begins
UDC members must be assigned to a different institution from the one where the incident took place
questions.rationale:
UDC members must not be involved in the incident, and an investigator is excluded.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.7: “(b) UDC members. The UDC ordinarily consists of two or more staff. UDC members will not be victims, witnesses, investigators, or otherwise significantly involved in the incident.”

questions.stem:
The UDC finds that an inmate committed a Moderate severity act. A member proposes sanctions that include disciplinary segregation and forfeiture of good conduct time.

Which statement is correct?
options: The UDC may impose any sanction in Tables 1 and 2
The UDC may impose disciplinary segregation, but not loss of good conduct time, subject to the Warden's discretion, with the approval of a supervisor on duty
The UDC cannot impose loss of good conduct time credit, FSA Time Credits, disciplinary segregation, or monetary fines
The UDC may impose any sanction if the Warden approves it later
questions.rationale:
UDC sanctions exclude loss of good conduct time, FSA Time Credits, disciplinary segregation, and fines; those must come from the DHO.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.7: “(f) Sanctions. If you committed a prohibited act or prohibited acts, the UDC can impose any of the available sanctions in Tables 1 and 2 of § 541.3, except loss of good conduct time credit, FSA Time Credits, disciplinary segregation, or monetary fines.”

questions.stem:
An inmate who cannot read well asks for help preparing for his DHO hearing. The staff member he asked to represent him was a witness to the incident and cannot serve.

What will the Warden do?
options: Postpone the hearing indefinitely until the inmate can read the report and select another witness
Appoint another inmate to represent him, since the staff he requested was involved in the incident
Appoint a staff representative, because the requested one cannot serve and the inmate has difficulty understanding the charges
Allow the hearing to proceed without any representative, since the inmate waived his rights by asking, under the direction of the senior officer present
questions.rationale:
The Warden appoints a staff representative when a request cannot be fulfilled and the inmate still wants one, or when the inmate cannot adequately represent himself, such as being illiterate.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.8: “(1) How to get a staff representative. You may request the staff representative of your choice, so long as that person was not a victim, witness, investigator, or otherwise significantly involved in the incident. If your request(s) cannot be fulfilled, and you still want a staff representative, the Warden will appoint one. The Warden will also appoint a staff representative if it appears you are unable to adequately represent yourself before the DHO, for example, if you are illiterate or have difficulty understanding the charges against you.”

questions.stem:
At a DHO hearing, an inmate asks to question a witness directly. His staff representative also wants to ask a question.

How are their questions handled?
options: The staff representative may question the witness directly, but the inmate may not
Both may question the witness directly if the DHO agrees
The inmate may question the witness directly, but his representative may not
Only the DHO may question witnesses; the questions are submitted to the DHO, who presents them in his or her discretion
questions.rationale:
Only the DHO may directly question witnesses; questions from the inmate or his staff representative go through the DHO.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.8: “(5) Only the DHO may directly question witnesses at the DHO's hearing. Any questions by you or your staff representative must be submitted to the DHO, who will present the question to the witness in his/her discretion.”

questions.stem:
An inmate asks the DHO to reveal the identity of a confidential informant whose information was used against him.

What does the regulation say?
options: The DHO may consider reliable CI evidence; the CI's identity is withheld, but the inmate is told the testimony to the extent security allows
The DHO may not consider CI evidence unless the CI appears in person and the inmate may question him
The DHO may consider CI evidence, and the inmate is told the CI's identity before the hearing begins
The DHO may consider CI evidence only if the reporting officer confirms it and the CI's name is read aloud, pending review by the appropriate official
questions.rationale:
The DHO may consider evidence from a reliable CI and does not disclose the CI's identity, though the inmate is told of the testimony to the extent it will not jeopardize security.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.8: “(6) The DHO may consider evidence provided by a confidential informant (CI) that the DHO finds reliable. You will not be informed of the CI's identity. You will be informed of the CI's testimony to the extent it will not jeopardize institution security, at the DHO's discretion.”

questions.stem:
An inmate is charged with a High severity act. The reporting officer suggests resolving the matter informally to save time and removing the report from the record.

What is the answer?
options: Informal resolution is available only if the inmate has no prior reports
Informal resolution is available at any stage for any severity level
Informal resolution is available only after the DHO hearing
Informal resolution is not available for Greatest and High severity acts
questions.rationale:
An incident report may be informally resolved at any stage except for Greatest and High severity acts, or as otherwise required.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.5: “(3) Informally resolving the incident report. The incident report may be informally resolved at any stage of the disciplinary process, except for prohibited acts in the Greatest and High severity levels, or as otherwise required by law or these regulations. If the incident report is informally resolved, it will be removed from your records.”

questions.stem:
An inmate tells Officer Bauer that his cellmate sexually assaulted him a short time ago. Officer Bauer is the first security staff member to respond.

Which set of actions is required?
options: Tell the victim to wash up and change clothes before seeing the medical staff, in most circumstances, with the approval of a supervisor on duty
Move the victim to the Special Housing Unit and clean the cell
Separate the alleged victim and abuser, preserve the scene, and ask the victim (and ensure the abuser) not to destroy physical evidence
Interview both inmates together to get both sides, then write a report
questions.rationale:
The first security responder must separate the parties, preserve and protect the crime scene, and request or ensure that no evidence-destroying actions such as washing or changing clothes occur.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.64: “(a) Upon learning of an allegation that an inmate was sexually abused, the first security staff member to respond to the report shall be required to: (1) Separate the alleged victim and abuser; (2) Preserve and protect any crime scene until appropriate steps can be taken to collect any evidence; (3) If the abuse occurred within a time period that still allows for the collection of physical evidence, request that the alleged victim not take any actions that could destroy physical evidence, including, as appropriate, washing, brushing teeth, changing clothes, urinating, defecating, smoking, drinking, or eating; and (4) If the abuse occurred within a time period that still allows for the collection of physical evidence, ensure that the alleged abuser does not take any actions that could destroy physical evidence, including, as appropriate, washing, brushing teeth, changing clothes, urinating, defecating, smoking, drinking, or eating.”

questions.stem:
An inmate who reported staff abuse has been receiving unexpected disciplinary reports and a sudden housing change. The PREA compliance manager asks how long the agency must monitor for retaliation.

What is the answer?
options: At least 180 days, and longer only if the Warden orders an extension
At least one year, regardless of what the initial monitoring shows
At least 30 days, and longer only if a retaliation complaint is filed
At least 90 days, and longer if the initial monitoring indicates a continuing need
questions.rationale:
The agency monitors for at least 90 days following a report, looking at items such as disciplinary reports and housing changes, and continues if needed.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.67: “(c) For at least 90 days following a report of sexual abuse, the agency shall monitor the conduct and treatment of inmates or staff who reported the sexual abuse and of inmates who were reported to have suffered sexual abuse to see if there are changes that may suggest possible retaliation by inmates or staff, and shall act promptly to remedy any such retaliation. Items the agency should monitor include any inmate disciplinary reports, housing, or program changes, or negative performance reviews or reassignments of staff. The agency shall continue such monitoring beyond 90 days if the initial monitoring indicates a continuing need.”

questions.stem:
A facility places an inmate at high risk for sexual victimization into involuntary segregated housing without assessing alternatives, intending to keep him there for 90 days.

What is wrong with this decision?
options: Involuntary segregation requires an assessment of all available alternatives, and the assignment should not ordinarily exceed 30 days
Involuntary segregation needs the inmate's written consent
Involuntary segregation may not be used for more than 24 hours in any case, where the circumstances reasonably call for it, during normal operating hours
Involuntary segregation may be used only for abusers, never victims
questions.rationale:
Segregation requires an assessment of alternatives, and such assignments shall not ordinarily exceed 30 days, with a review every 30 days.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.43: “(a) Inmates at high risk for sexual victimization shall not be placed in involuntary segregated housing unless an assessment of all available alternatives has been made, and a determination has been made that there is no available alternative means of separation from likely abusers. If a facility cannot conduct such an assessment immediately, the facility may hold the inmate in involuntary segregated housing for less than 24 hours while completing the assessment.”
28 CFR § 115.43: “(c) The facility shall assign such inmates to involuntary segregated housing only until an alternative means of separation from likely abusers can be arranged, and such an assignment shall not ordinarily exceed a period of 30 days.”

questions.stem:
A supervisor makes a night shift unannounced round. Afterward, an officer jokes that he had texted the whole unit staff "heads up" as the supervisor walked in.

What does the standard say about this?
options: Staff may alert other staff whenever the supervisor making the rounds is of lower rank
Staff are required to alert the unit before rounds so that supervisors do not surprise officers on duty
Staff are prohibited from alerting other staff that supervisory rounds are occurring, unless related to legitimate operational functions
Staff may alert other staff on night shifts but not day shifts, since nights have fewer employees
questions.rationale:
Agencies must prohibit staff from alerting others about supervisory rounds, on both night and day shifts.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.13: “(d) Each agency operating a facility shall implement a policy and practice of having intermediate-level or higher-level supervisors conduct and document unannounced rounds to identify and deter staff sexual abuse and sexual harassment. Such policy and practice shall be implemented for night shifts as well as day shifts. Each agency shall have a policy to prohibit staff from alerting other staff members that these supervisory rounds are occurring, unless such announcement is related to the legitimate operational functions of the facility.”

questions.stem:
During PREA screening, an inmate declines to answer a question about whether he has previously experienced sexual victimization. The screening officer says he will write the inmate up for refusing.

What is the correct response?
options: The inmate may be disciplined only if he lies
The inmate may be disciplined for refusing any screening question
Inmates may not be disciplined for refusing to answer or not disclosing complete information on those questions
The inmate may be disciplined after a second refusal
questions.rationale:
Inmates cannot be disciplined for refusing to answer the specified sensitive questions, including prior victimization.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.41: “(h) Inmates may not be disciplined for refusing to answer, or for not disclosing complete information in response to, questions asked pursuant to paragraphs (d)(1), (d)(7), (d)(8), or (d)(9) of this section.”

questions.stem:
An inmate is a transgender woman. A supervisor wants to search her only to determine her genital status for housing records.

What does the standard say?
options: The facility may require a visual search to determine genital status when she is first housed
The facility may search her to determine genital status whenever a supervisor of the same gender approves it, during normal operating hours, with the approval of a supervisor on duty
The facility shall assume her status from her appearance and may not ask about it in any form
The facility shall not search or examine her for the sole purpose of determining genital status; it may be learned in conversation, from records, or in a private medical exam
questions.rationale:
The standard prohibits searching or examining transgender or intersex inmates solely to determine genital status.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.15: “(e) The facility shall not search or physically examine a transgender or intersex inmate for the sole purpose of determining the inmate's genital status. If the inmate's genital status is unknown, it may be determined during conversations with the inmate, by reviewing medical records, or, if necessary, by learning that information as part of a broader medical examination conducted in private by a medical practitioner.”

questions.stem:
An inmate who is deaf and has limited reading skills is scheduled for PREA education.

What does the standard require?
options: Education may be provided in standard written form, with other formats offered only if an inmate files a request
Education may be skipped for inmates who are deaf, since they will receive the written handbook
Education must be provided in formats accessible to all inmates, including those who are deaf or have limited reading skills
Education must be provided in formats accessible to inmates with disabilities, but not to those with limited English, in most circumstances
questions.rationale:
The agency must provide inmate education in formats accessible to all inmates, including deaf inmates and those with limited reading skills.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.33: “(d) The agency shall provide inmate education in formats accessible to all inmates, including those who are limited English proficient, deaf, visually impaired, or otherwise disabled, as well as to inmates who have limited reading skills.”

questions.stem:
A facility's incident review team meets after an investigation into an unsubstantiated sexual abuse allegation. A member says reviews are only for substantiated cases.

What does the standard say?
options: A review is conducted only when the Warden requests one or a criminal charge has been filed
A review is conducted only at the end of investigations in which the allegation was substantiated
A review is conducted at the end of every investigation, including those determined to be unfounded
A review is conducted at the end of every investigation, including unsubstantiated ones, unless the allegation was determined to be unfounded
questions.rationale:
Reviews occur after every sexual abuse investigation, including where the allegation has not been substantiated, unless it was determined to be unfounded.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.86: “(a) The facility shall conduct a sexual abuse incident review at the conclusion of every sexual abuse investigation, including where the allegation has not been substantiated, unless the allegation has been determined to be unfounded.”

questions.stem:
An alleged victim is 17 years old. A supervisor says reporting to outside agencies is unnecessary because the matter is being handled internally.

What does the standard require?
options: Keep the report within the agency until the alleged victim turns 18, then refer it to local services
Report the allegation only if the alleged victim's parents give their permission to do so
Report the allegation only if the alleged abuser is a staff member rather than another inmate
Report the allegation to the designated State or local services agency under applicable mandatory reporting laws
questions.rationale:
If the alleged victim is under 18 or a vulnerable adult, the agency must report to the designated State or local services agency.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.61: “(d) If the alleged victim is under the age of 18 or considered a vulnerable adult under a State or local vulnerable persons statute, the agency shall report the allegation to the designated State or local services agency under applicable mandatory reporting laws.”

questions.stem:
A union contract proposal would prevent the agency from removing an alleged staff abuser from contact with inmates while an investigation is pending.

What does the standard say about such an agreement?
options: The agency may not enter into or renew an agreement that limits its ability to remove alleged staff abusers from contact with inmates pending the outcome
The agency may sign if the alleged abuser requests it and the union provides a representative, based on the information available at the time, as long as no other inmate is affected
The agency may sign if the agreement limits such removal to a period of not more than 30 days
The agency may sign if the Warden approves it and the PREA coordinator is notified in writing
questions.rationale:
The agency may not enter or renew agreements that limit its ability to remove alleged staff sexual abusers from contact with inmates pending the outcome of the investigation or discipline decision.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.66: “(a) Neither the agency nor any other governmental entity responsible for collective bargaining on the agency's behalf shall enter into or renew any collective bargaining agreement or other agreement that limits the agency's ability to remove alleged staff sexual abusers from contact with any inmates pending the outcome of an investigation or of a determination of whether and to what extent discipline is warranted.”

questions.stem:
An inmate at a minimum security institution seals an outgoing letter addressed to another inmate in a different institution.

How may staff treat it?
options: Staff may open it because correspondence between inmates is an exception to the sealed-mail rule
Staff must hold it until the other inmate asks for it
Staff must send it unopened because it is sealed
Staff must reject it because inmates may not write to each other, pending review by the appropriate official
questions.rationale:
Staff may open an outgoing sentenced inmate's mail if it is between inmates (see 540.17), among other exceptions.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.14: “(iii) If the correspondence is between inmates (see § 540.17); or”

questions.stem:
A letter to an inmate contains a diagram showing how to cut through a perimeter fence and a plan for an escape on Saturday.

What should the Warden do?
options: Hold it in the inmate's property until release, because an escape plan is a matter for the Warden alone, subject to the Warden's discretion, as determined by the shift supervisor
Reject it and return it to the sender with a written notice of the reasons and the right to appeal
Reject it; escape plots are grounds for rejection, and because it discusses a crime it need not be returned but should be referred to law enforcement
Deliver it after removing the diagram, because the rest of the letter is general correspondence
questions.rationale:
Information of escape plots is grounds for rejection, and correspondence with plans for or evidence of a crime need not be returned or noticed; it should be referred to law enforcement.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.14: “(3) Information of escape plots, of plans to commit illegal activities, or to violate Bureau rules or institution guidelines;”
28 CFR § 540.13: “When correspondence is rejected, the Warden shall notify the sender in writing of the rejection and the reasons for the rejection. The Warden shall also give notice that the sender may appeal the rejection. The Warden shall also notify an inmate of the rejection of any letter addressed to that inmate, along with the reasons for the rejection and shall notify the inmate of the right to appeal the rejection. The Warden shall refer an appeal to an official other than the one who originally disapproved the correspondence. The Warden shall return rejected correspondence to the sender unless the correspondence includes plans for or discussion of commission of a crime or evidence of a crime, in which case there is no need to return the correspondence or give notice of the rejection, and the correspondence should be referred to appropriate law enforcement authorities. Also, contraband need not be returned to the sender.”

questions.stem:
A sentenced inmate wants to write his bank about refinancing his existing mortgage on a house he owned before he came to prison. He also wants to write to a customer about running his old insurance business from prison.

Which request is allowed?
options: Writing about the insurance business, but not the mortgage
Writing about refinancing the existing mortgage, but not directing the insurance business
Writing about neither, since business correspondence is prohibited, pending review by the appropriate official
Writing about both, as long as the mail is not sealed
questions.rationale:
An inmate may correspond to protect property and funds legitimately his at commitment (such as refinancing a mortgage), but may not direct a business while confined.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.14: “(4) Direction of an inmate's business (See § 541.13, Prohibited Act No. 408). An inmate, unless a pre-trial detainee, may not direct a business while confined.”
28 CFR § 540.14: “This does not, however, prohibit correspondence necessary to enable an inmate to protect property and funds that were legitimately the inmate's at the time of commitment. Thus, for example, an inmate may correspond about refinancing an existing mortgage or sign insurance papers, but may not operate a mortgage or insurance business while in the institution.”

questions.stem:
A 14-year-old arrives at the visiting room alone and asks to see his father.

What is the correct response?
options: Children under 16 may visit alone on weekends, though the Warden may require an adult in the room
Children under 16 may not visit unless accompanied by a responsible adult, though the Warden may approve an exception in unusual circumstances
Children under 16 may not visit at all, though a chaplain may approve an exception in unusual circumstances
Children under 16 may visit alone if a parent has given written permission, though the Warden may deny the visit, after a supervisor has reviewed the matter
questions.rationale:
Children under 16 may not visit without a responsible adult unless the Warden approves an exception in unusual circumstances.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.44: “(e) Children under sixteen. Children under the age of 16 may not visit unless accompanied by a responsible adult. Children shall be kept under supervision of a responsible adult or a children's program. Exceptions in unusual circumstances may be made by special approval of the Warden.”

questions.stem:
An inmate's proposed visitor has a prior conviction from nine years ago for a non-violent offense. An officer says anyone with a record is automatically barred.

What does the regulation say?
options: A conviction precludes visits unless the offense was non-violent, in which case staff must approve
A conviction precludes visits for ten years after release from custody, unless the Warden waives it, provided that the action is documented
A conviction alone does not preclude visits; staff weigh the nature, extent, and recentness against security considerations
A conviction does not matter, and staff may not consider it in deciding on a visit
questions.rationale:
The existence of a criminal conviction alone does not preclude visits. Staff consider nature, extent, and recentness, and the Warden may need to approve.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.44: “(d) Persons with prior criminal convictions. The existence of a criminal conviction alone does not preclude visits. Staff shall give consideration to the nature, extent and recentness of convictions, as weighed against the security considerations of the institution. Specific approval of the Warden may be required before such visits take place.”

questions.stem:
A consular representative of a foreign inmate's country arrives to discuss legitimate business. The inmate is currently serving a disciplinary sanction that restricts his regular visits.

What must the Warden do?
options: Deny the visit until the sanction ends
Permit the visit only if the Regional Director approves
Permit the visit only if the inmate had a pre-confinement relationship with the representative
Permit the visit, because the privilege may not be withheld even when the inmate is in disciplinary status
questions.rationale:
The Warden must permit the consular representative to visit on matters of legitimate business and may not withhold the privilege even in disciplinary status.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.45: “(b) Consular visitors. When it has been determined that an inmate is a citizen of a foreign country, the Warden must permit the consular representative of that country to visit on matters of legitimate business. The Warden may not withhold this privilege even though the inmate is in disciplinary status. The requirement for the existence of an established relationship prior to confinement does not apply to consular visitors.”

questions.stem:
An inmate places a call to his attorney. A supervisor asks to monitor it "for security."

What does the regulation say?
options: Staff may monitor all calls including attorney calls
Staff may not monitor an inmate's properly placed call to an attorney
Staff may monitor attorney calls only after an incident report
Staff may monitor attorney calls with a supervisor's approval
questions.rationale:
The Warden may monitor calls generally, but staff may not monitor a properly placed call to an attorney.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.102: “The Warden shall establish procedures that enable monitoring of telephone conversations on any telephone located within the institution, said monitoring to be done to preserve the security and orderly management of the institution and to protect the public. The Warden must provide notice to the inmate of the potential for monitoring. Staff may not monitor an inmate's properly placed call to an attorney. The Warden shall notify an inmate of the proper procedures to have an unmonitored telephone conversation with an attorney.”

questions.stem:
An inmate's proposed phone number belongs to a person who has threatened witnesses in a prior case. The Associate Warden denies placing it on his list.

What must the Associate Warden do?
options: Document the disapproval in writing to the inmate only, who may appeal through the Administrative Remedy Program, in most circumstances, under the direction of the senior officer present
Document the disapproval in writing to both, who may appeal by writing to the Regional Director within 15 days
Notify the proposed recipient verbally, who may appeal by writing to the Warden within 30 days
Document the disapproval in writing to both the inmate and the proposed recipient, who may appeal by writing to the Warden within 15 days
questions.rationale:
A denial must be documented in writing to both the inmate and the proposed recipient, and the recipient may appeal to the Warden within 15 days.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.101: “(3) The Associate Warden may deny placement of a telephone number on an inmate's telephone list if the Associate Warden determines that there is a threat to institution security or good order, or a threat to the public. Any disapproval must be documented in writing to both the inmate and the proposed recipient. As with concerns about any correctional issue, including any portion of these telephone regulations, an inmate may appeal the denial through the administrative remedy procedure (see 28 CFR part 542). The Associate Warden will notify the denied recipient that he or she may appeal the denial by writing to the Warden within 15 days of the receipt of the denial.”

questions.stem:
An inmate without money asks for a collect call. His account balance has been under $6.00 for more than thirty days.

What does the regulation say?
options: The Warden provides at least one collect call each week for an inmate without funds, defined as one without a $6.00 balance for the past 30 days
The Warden provides at least one collect call each month for an inmate without funds, defined as one without a $6.00 balance for the past 30 days
The Warden provides at least one collect call each month for an inmate without funds, defined as one without a $60.00 balance for the past 90 days
The Warden provides collect calls only in family emergencies for an inmate without funds
questions.rationale:
An inmate without funds is one who has not had a $6.00 balance for 30 days, and the Warden provides at least one collect call per month.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.105: “(b) The Warden shall provide at least one collect call each month for an inmate who is without funds. An inmate without funds is defined as an inmate who has not had a trust fund account balance of $6.00 for the past 30 days. The Warden may increase the number of collect calls based upon local institution conditions (e.g., institution population, staff resources, and usage demand). To prevent abuses of this provision (e.g., inmate shows a pattern of depleting his or her commissary funds prior to placing collect calls), the Warden may impose restrictions on the provisions of this paragraph (b).”

questions.stem:
An inmate is confined in disciplinary segregation and needs to prepare a court filing.

What must the Warden provide?
options: Legal materials delivered by the inmate's family, with no institution law library access
Access to the main law library at any time the inmate asks, regardless of staff availability
A means of access to legal materials and an opportunity to prepare legal documents, subject to the needs of other inmates and staff availability
An opportunity to prepare legal documents, but no access to legal materials while in segregation, in accordance with the posted schedule, pending review by the appropriate official
questions.rationale:
The Warden must provide an inmate in disciplinary segregation or administrative detention a means of access to legal materials and an opportunity to prepare documents, within limits.

Source — 28 CFR § 543.11: “(j) With consideration of the needs of other inmates and the availability of staff and other resources, the Warden shall provide an inmate confined in disciplinary segregation or administrative detention a means of access to legal materials, along with an opportunity to prepare legal documents. The Warden shall allow an inmate in segregation or detention a reasonable amount of personal legal materials. In no case shall the amount of personal legal materials be such as to pose a fire, sanitation, security, or housekeeping hazard.”

questions.stem:
An attorney asks to meet with an inmate and tells the officer the subject of the case. A supervisor tells the officer to ask for the details of the lawsuit before approving the visit.

What should the officer do?
options: Ask the attorney to state the subject matter, and then confirm it with the inmate
Ask the attorney for a written summary of the case before the visit is approved
Ask the attorney only about the place of licensure, and the subject of the case if time permits
Not ask the attorney to state the subject matter of the lawsuit or interview
questions.rationale:
The Warden may require the attorney to identify himself and where he is licensed, but may not ask the attorney to state the subject matter.

Source — 28 CFR § 543.13: “(d) The Warden may require an attorney to indicate where he is licensed as an attorney and how that fact may be verified. Prior to each appointment or visit, the Warden shall require each attorney to identify himself and to confirm that he wishes to visit an inmate who has requested his visit or whom he represents or whom he wishes to interview as a witness. The Warden may not ask the attorney to state the subject matter of the law suit or interview. If there is any question about the identity of the visitor or his qualification as an attorney in good standing, the Warden shall refer the matter to the Regional Counsel.”

questions.stem:
An attorney is visiting an inmate. An officer wants to stand close enough to hear the conversation "for safety."

What does the regulation say?
options: Staff shall not subject visits between an attorney and an inmate to auditory supervision
Staff shall supervise visits by sound, but the officer may not take notes of the conversation
Staff may supervise visits by sound if a Lieutenant approves it for security reasons
Staff may listen to visits if they suspect that the attorney may have brought in contraband
questions.rationale:
Attorney visits shall not be subject to auditory supervision.

Source — 28 CFR § 543.13: “(e) Staff shall not subject visits between an attorney and an inmate to auditory supervision. The Warden may permit tape recordings to be used by an attorney during the course of a visit only if the attorney states in writing in advance of the interview that the sole purpose of the recording is to facilitate the attorney-client or attorney-witness relationship.”

questions.stem:
An attorney is found passing contraband to an inmate. The Warden is considering banning the attorney from all future visits.

What does the regulation say about the response?
options: No action may be taken against an attorney, and the matter must be referred to the court
Unless the breach is extreme or repeated, limitation rather than denial of rights is proper, and the Warden shall consider referral to the state agency regulating the attorney
Limitation is proper only for the first breach, and denial is required for any later breach
Denial of all visitation and correspondence rights is proper for any breach involving contraband
questions.rationale:
Introducing contraband is a ground for limitation or denial; however, unless extreme or repeated, limitation is proper, and referral to the state regulator is considered.

Source — 28 CFR § 543.14: “(b) Unless the breach of regulations is extreme or repeated, limitation rather than a denial of visitation or correspondence rights is proper, especially where the inmate is represented by the attorney and is confronted with a court deadline. For example, the Warden may subject an attorney to a search of his person and belongings or may permit the attorney only non-privileged correspondence. The Warden shall also consider referral of the matter to the state agency regulating the attorney's professional conduct.”

questions.stem:
An inmate believes that he will be in danger if staff at his institution learn about his complaint against an officer.

What can he do?
options: Submit the Request to the Warden marked "Confidential" and ask that the unit team not be told
Mark the Request "Sensitive" and submit it directly to the Regional Director with a written explanation of why
Submit the Request to the unit officer and ask that it be sealed in an envelope
Mark the Request "Urgent" and submit it directly to the General Counsel with a written explanation
questions.rationale:
If an inmate reasonably believes the issue is sensitive and his safety would be endangered, he may mark it "Sensitive" and submit it to the Regional Director.

Source — 28 CFR § 542.14: “(d) Exceptions to initial filing at institution—(1) Sensitive issues. If the inmate reasonably believes the issue is sensitive and the inmate's safety or well-being would be placed in danger if the Request became known at the institution, the inmate may submit the Request directly to the appropriate Regional Director. The inmate shall clearly mark “Sensitive” upon the Request and explain, in writing, the reason for not submitting the Request at the institution. If the Regional Administrative Remedy Coordinator agrees that the Request is sensitive, the Request shall be accepted. Otherwise, the Request will not be accepted, and the inmate shall be advised in writing of that determination, without a return of the Request. The inmate may pursue the matter by submitting an Administrative Remedy Request locally to the Warden. The Warden shall allow a reasonable extension of time for such a resubmission.”

questions.stem:
An inmate lists three unrelated complaints on one BP-9: a food issue, a lost package, and a work assignment.

What will happen?
options: It will be accepted, but the Warden will answer only the first issue listed
It will be accepted, and the Warden will answer the issues in the order they appear
It will be rejected and returned without response, and he will be told to use a separate form for each unrelated issue
It will be accepted and forwarded to the Regional Director for a single combined response, once the shift lieutenant has been informed
questions.rationale:
Multiple unrelated issues on one form lead to rejection and return without a response.

Source — 28 CFR § 542.14: “(2) The inmate shall place a single complaint or a reasonable number of closely related issues on the form. If the inmate includes on a single form multiple unrelated issues, the submission shall be rejected and returned without response, and the inmate shall be advised to use a separate form for each unrelated issue. For DHO and UDC appeals, each separate incident report number must be appealed on a separate form.”

questions.stem:
An inmate files an emergency request claiming a threat to his immediate health. He asks how quickly the Warden must respond.

What is the requirement?
options: Not later than the third calendar day after filing
Within 24 hours
Within 20 calendar days
Within 30 calendar days
questions.rationale:
If the Request is determined to be an emergency threatening immediate health or welfare, the Warden responds not later than the third calendar day.

Source — 28 CFR § 542.18: “If accepted, a Request or Appeal is considered filed on the date it is logged into the Administrative Remedy Index as received. Once filed, response shall be made by the Warden or CCM within 20 calendar days; by the Regional Director within 30 calendar days; and by the General Counsel within 40 calendar days. If the Request is determined to be of an emergency nature which threatens the inmate's immediate health or welfare, the Warden shall respond not later than the third calendar day after filing. If the time period for response to a Request or Appeal is insufficient to make an appropriate decision, the time for response may be extended once by 20 days at the institution level, 30 days at the regional level, or 20 days at the Central Office level. Staff shall inform the inmate of this extension in writing. Staff shall respond in writing to all filed Requests or Appeals. If the inmate does not receive a response within the time allotted for reply, including extension, the inmate may consider the absence of a response to be a denial at that level.”

questions.stem:
An inmate submits an appeal to the General Counsel that raises a new issue he never raised at the institution level.

What does the regulation say?
options: New issues are accepted if a staff member agrees
An inmate may not raise in an appeal issues not raised in the lower level filings
New issues are accepted if a lawyer prepares them, after a supervisor has reviewed the matter
New issues are welcome
questions.rationale:
An inmate may not raise issues in an appeal that were not raised in lower level filings, nor combine separate appeals.

Source — 28 CFR § 542.15: “(2) An inmate may not raise in an Appeal issues not raised in the lower level filings. An inmate may not combine Appeals of separate lower level responses (different case numbers) into a single Appeal.”

questions.stem:
An inmate has been in administrative detention for five days. He asks when the Segregation Review Official (SRO) will formally review his status at a hearing he can attend.

Within what period will that hearing occur?
options: Within 60 days of placement
Within three work days of placement
Within seven continuous calendar days of placement
Within 30 days of placement
questions.rationale:
The seven day review is a formal hearing the inmate can attend. The three-day review is a records review, and the 30-day review is another formal hearing.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.26: “(b) Seven day reviews. Within seven continuous calendar days of your placement in either administrative detention or disciplinary segregation status, the SRO will formally review your status at a hearing you can attend. Subsequent reviews of your records will be performed in your absence by the SRO every seven continuous calendar days thereafter.”

questions.stem:
An inmate in disciplinary segregation asks whether the SRO will do a three-work-day review of his supporting records.

What is the answer?
options: No; the three-work-day review applies to disciplinary segregation and does not occur for administrative detention
Yes; the three-work-day review applies to both statuses, but only if the inmate requests it in writing
Yes; the three-work-day review applies to both statuses, with a formal hearing the inmate can attend
No; the three-work-day review applies to administrative detention and does not occur for disciplinary segregation
questions.rationale:
The three day review is for administrative detention; if the inmate is in disciplinary segregation, the review will not occur.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.26: “(a) Three day review. Within three work days of your placement in administrative detention status, not counting the day you were admitted, weekends, and holidays, the SRO will review the supporting records. If you are in disciplinary segregation status, this review will not occur.”

questions.stem:
An inmate refuses to enter the general population because of alleged pressures from unidentified inmates, and gives no other explanation.

What status may staff use?
options: Close observation
Administrative detention as a protection case
Release to the general population by force
Disciplinary segregation without a hearing
questions.rationale:
A refusal to enter general population because of alleged pressure from unidentified inmates, or for no expressed reason, is one of the protection case circumstances for administrative detention.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.27: “(c) Inmate refusal to enter general population. You refuse to enter the general population because of alleged pressures or threats from unidentified inmates, or for no expressed reason.”

questions.stem:
A disciplinary segregation inmate is told that the Warden cannot release him before his sanction ends under any circumstances.

What does the regulation say?
options: The SRO may release him earlier if it is determined he no longer requires disciplinary segregation status
He must serve the full sanction because only the DHO can shorten it
The DHO must approve any release before the sanction has been fully served
The Warden may release him only after he has served at least half of the sanction
questions.rationale:
He is released after satisfying the sanction, but the SRO may release him earlier if he no longer requires disciplinary segregation.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.33: “(b) Disciplinary segregation status. You will be released from disciplinary segregation status after satisfying the sanction imposed by the DHO. The SRO may release you earlier if it is determined you no longer require disciplinary segregation status.”

questions.stem:
An inmate in the SHU in disciplinary segregation status asks to keep all of his personal property. A staff member agrees.

What does the regulation say about property in disciplinary segregation?
options: Personal property will be limited to the amount he can store in a locker, with the rest mailed home, as determined by the shift supervisor
Personal property will be impounded, except for limited reading and writing materials and religious articles
Personal property will be allowed in a reasonable amount, with reasonable access to the commissary
Personal property will be impounded entirely, with no exceptions for reading or religious items
questions.rationale:
In disciplinary segregation, personal property is impounded with limited exceptions, while administrative detention allows a reasonable amount.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.31: “(2) In disciplinary segregation status your personal property will be impounded, with the exception of limited reading/writing materials, and religious articles. Also, your commissary privileges may be limited.”

questions.stem:
An SHU inmate asks how much exercise he must be given.

What is the minimum?
options: At least one hour per week outside his individual quarters, ordinarily on the same day each week
At least ten hours per week outside his individual quarters, ordinarily in two-hour periods
At least five hours per week outside his individual quarters, ordinarily in one-hour periods on different days
At least five hours per month outside his individual quarters, ordinarily in one-hour periods on different days
questions.rationale:
SHU inmates receive the opportunity to exercise at least five hours per week; the Warden may deny exercise periods for a week at a time if use threatens safety or security.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.31: “(g) Exercise. You will receive the opportunity to exercise outside your individual quarters at least five hours per week, ordinarily on different days in one-hour periods. You can be denied these exercise periods for a week at a time by order of the Warden if it is determined that your use of exercise privileges threatens safety, security, and orderly operation of a correctional facility, or public safety.”

questions.stem:
A job applicant for a position with inmate contact has a past civil adjudication finding he engaged in sexual activity by coercion in the community.

What does the standard require?
options: The agency may hire such a person if he has no contact with inmates in a housing unit
The agency shall not hire or promote anyone who has been civilly or administratively adjudicated to have engaged in such activity
The agency may hire such a person if he completes retraining and is assigned to a day shift, in most circumstances, pending review by the appropriate official
The agency may hire such a person after five years have passed since the adjudication
questions.rationale:
The agency may not hire or promote anyone who has been civilly or administratively adjudicated to have engaged in sexual activity facilitated by force, threat, or coercion.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.17: “(a) The agency shall not hire or promote anyone who may have contact with inmates, and shall not enlist the services of any contractor who may have contact with inmates, who— (3) Has been civilly or administratively adjudicated to have engaged in the activity described in paragraph (a)(2) of this section.”

questions.stem:
An HR officer asks how often the agency must run criminal background checks on current employees with inmate contact.

What is the requirement?
options: At least every year, or have a system in place for otherwise capturing such information
At least every ten years, or have a system in place for otherwise capturing such information
At least every five years, or have a system in place for otherwise capturing such information
Only at the time of hire, with a new check required only if the employee is promoted
questions.rationale:
The agency must conduct criminal background records checks at least every five years of current employees and contractors with inmate contact, or have a system in place for capturing such information.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.17: “(e) The agency shall either conduct criminal background records checks at least every five years of current employees and contractors who may have contact with inmates or have in place a system for otherwise capturing such information for current employees.”

questions.stem:
An applicant omits a prior dismissal for sexual misconduct from an application. It is discovered later.

What does the standard say?
options: Material omissions are overlooked if the applicant corrects the application within thirty days, when staff resources allow, in accordance with the posted schedule
Material omissions are grounds for a suspension, with termination only for a second omission
Material omissions are grounds for termination only if the applicant is promoted to supervisor
Material omissions regarding such misconduct, or the provision of materially false information, shall be grounds for termination
questions.rationale:
Material omissions or false information regarding such misconduct are grounds for termination.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.17: “(g) Material omissions regarding such misconduct, or the provision of materially false information, shall be grounds for termination.”

questions.stem:
A facility's policy places all gay and lesbian inmates in one dedicated wing "for convenience."

Is this allowed?
options: Yes; the agency may place LGBTI inmates in dedicated units for convenience if the inmates are informed
No; the agency shall not place LGBTI inmates in dedicated units solely on the basis of identification, unless under a consent decree, settlement, or judgment
No; the agency may place LGBTI inmates in dedicated units only for their first thirty days
Yes; the agency may place LGBTI inmates in dedicated units if the Warden approves it in writing
questions.rationale:
The agency may not place LGBTI inmates in dedicated facilities, units, or wings solely on the basis of such identification or status, unless required by a consent decree, legal settlement, or judgment protecting them.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.42: “(g) The agency shall not place lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, or intersex inmates in dedicated facilities, units, or wings solely on the basis of such identification or status, unless such placement is in a dedicated facility, unit, or wing established in connection with a consent decree, legal settlement, or legal judgment for the purpose of protecting such inmates.”

questions.stem:
A transgender inmate's housing assignment was reviewed eight months ago and has not been reviewed since.

What does the standard require?
options: They must be reassessed only when the inmate requests, during normal operating hours
They must be reassessed every five years
Placement and programming assignments must be reassessed at least twice each year
They must be reassessed once at intake
questions.rationale:
Placement and programming assignments for each transgender or intersex inmate are reassessed at least twice each year.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.42: “(d) Placement and programming assignments for each transgender or intersex inmate shall be reassessed at least twice each year to review any threats to safety experienced by the inmate.”

questions.stem:
An inmate files a grievance alleging sexual abuse on a date more than a year ago. The staff member says it is too late to file.

What does the standard say?
options: The agency may require a grievance regarding sexual abuse to be filed within 20 days of the incident
The agency may require a grievance regarding sexual abuse to be filed within one year of the incident, pending review by the appropriate official
The agency may require a grievance regarding sexual abuse to be filed within 90 days of the incident
The agency shall not impose a time limit on when an inmate may submit a grievance regarding an allegation of sexual abuse
questions.rationale:
There is no time limit on submitting a grievance alleging sexual abuse.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.52: “(b)(1) The agency shall not impose a time limit on when an inmate may submit a grievance regarding an allegation of sexual abuse.”

questions.stem:
An inmate wants to file a grievance alleging sexual abuse by an officer. The unit rules require him to hand grievances to the officer on duty, who is the subject of the complaint.

What does the standard require?
options: The inmate may submit a grievance without giving it to the staff member who is the subject of the complaint, and it must not be referred to that staff member
The inmate must give the grievance to the unit officer, who must not read it if he is the subject
The inmate must wait until the officer is reassigned before filing a grievance that names him
The inmate may submit a grievance only through his unit team, which may refer it to the subject for a response
questions.rationale:
The agency must ensure that the inmate can submit a grievance without going through the accused staff member and that it is not referred to that person.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.52: “(1) An inmate who alleges sexual abuse may submit a grievance without submitting it to a staff member who is the subject of the complaint, and (2) Such grievance is not referred to a staff member who is the subject of the complaint.”

questions.stem:
An inmate files a grievance alleging sexual abuse. The facility says it must first be resolved informally with staff.

What does the standard say?
options: The agency may require the inmate to try informal resolution with a supervisor for up to 20 days
The agency shall not require an inmate to use an informal grievance process or to attempt to resolve an alleged sexual abuse incident with staff
The agency may require the inmate to try informal resolution, except when the accused is a staff member, with the approval of a supervisor on duty, where the circumstances reasonably call for it
The agency may require the inmate to try informal resolution with the accused before a formal grievance
questions.rationale:
The inmate does not have to attempt informal resolution for allegations of sexual abuse.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.52: “(3) The agency shall not require an inmate to use any informal grievance process, or to otherwise attempt to resolve with staff, an alleged incident of sexual abuse.”

questions.stem:
An inmate files an emergency grievance alleging a substantial risk of imminent sexual abuse. The grievance coordinator says it will be answered in the normal 20 days.

What does the standard require?
options: Forward it to the Warden within a week, respond within 72 hours, and issue a final decision within 30 days
Immediately forward it to a level where corrective action may be taken, respond within 7 days, and issue a final decision within 90 days, as long as the unit team is notified
Immediately forward it to a level where corrective action may be taken, respond within 48 hours, and issue a final decision within 5 calendar days
Forward it to the unit team in the normal course, respond within 20 days, and issue a final decision within 40 days
questions.rationale:
Emergency grievances alleging a substantial risk of imminent sexual abuse receive an initial response within 48 hours and a final agency decision within 5 calendar days.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.52: “(2) After receiving an emergency grievance alleging an inmate is subject to a substantial risk of imminent sexual abuse, the agency shall immediately forward the grievance (or any portion thereof that alleges the substantial risk of imminent sexual abuse) to a level of review at which immediate corrective action may be taken, shall provide an initial response within 48 hours, and shall issue a final agency decision within 5 calendar days. The initial response and final agency decision shall document the agency's determination whether the inmate is in substantial risk of imminent sexual abuse and the action taken in response to the emergency grievance.”

questions.stem:
An inmate files a grievance about sexual abuse and gets no response after the 90-day period (including any properly noticed extension) has passed.

What may the inmate consider?
options: A request for more information
A referral to the court
A grant of the grievance
The absence of a response a denial at that level
questions.rationale:
If the inmate does not receive a response within the allotted time, including any properly noticed extension, he may consider the absence a denial at that level.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.52: “(4) At any level of the administrative process, including the final level, if the inmate does not receive a response within the time allotted for reply, including any properly noticed extension, the inmate may consider the absence of a response to be a denial at that level.”

questions.stem:
A family member wants to file a sexual abuse grievance on behalf of an inmate.

What does the standard say?
options: Third parties are permitted to assist inmates and file requests on their behalf, though the facility may require the alleged victim to agree
Third parties are permitted to assist inmates, but only the inmate himself may file the request
Third parties are not permitted to assist, but the inmate may ask a staff member to deliver his request, provided that the action is documented
Third parties may file requests on behalf of inmates only if they are attorneys or staff members
questions.rationale:
Third parties including family members, staff, attorneys, and advocates may assist or file on behalf of inmates; the facility may require the alleged victim's agreement.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.52: “(e)(1) Third parties, including fellow inmates, staff members, family members, attorneys, and outside advocates, shall be permitted to assist inmates in filing requests for administrative remedies relating to allegations of sexual abuse, and shall also be permitted to file such requests on behalf of inmates. (2) If a third party files such a request on behalf of an inmate, the facility may require as a condition of processing the request that the alleged victim agree to have the request filed on his or her behalf, and may also require the alleged victim to personally pursue any subsequent steps in the administrative remedy process.”

questions.stem:
An inmate who files a sexual abuse grievance in good faith cannot prove it. A supervisor wants to charge him with lying.

What does the standard say?
options: A report that an investigation finds unsubstantiated may be charged as false reporting if the inmate cannot name a witness, where the circumstances reasonably call for it
A report made in good faith upon a reasonable belief that the conduct occurred is not false reporting, even if the investigation does not substantiate it
A report made in good faith is protected only if the investigation finds the allegation substantiated
A report may be charged as lying if the investigation finds insufficient evidence after 90 days
questions.rationale:
A good-faith report based on a reasonable belief is not false reporting even if the investigation does not establish enough evidence.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.78: “(f) For the purpose of disciplinary action, a report of sexual abuse made in good faith based upon a reasonable belief that the alleged conduct occurred shall not constitute falsely reporting an incident or lying, even if an investigation does not establish evidence sufficient to substantiate the allegation.”

questions.stem:
A facility head receives an allegation that an inmate was sexually abused at another facility.

What must the head do?
options: Notify the inmate's family within 72 hours, and ask them to contact the other facility
Notify the head of the facility where the alleged abuse occurred within 30 days, and document it
Hold the report until the inmate has been transferred back to the facility where the abuse occurred
Notify the head of the facility or appropriate office where the alleged abuse occurred as soon as possible, but no later than 72 hours, and document it
questions.rationale:
The receiving facility head must notify the head of the other facility or office as soon as possible, no later than 72 hours, and document it.
