Source — 28 CFR § 115.63: “(a) Upon receiving an allegation that an inmate was sexually abused while confined at another facility, the head of the facility that received the allegation shall notify the head of the facility or appropriate office of the agency where the alleged abuse occurred. (b) Such notification shall be provided as soon as possible, but no later than 72 hours after receiving the allegation. (c) The agency shall document that it has provided such notification.”

questions.stem:
An investigator wants to require an inmate who alleges sexual abuse to take a polygraph test before the investigation proceeds.

What does the standard say?
options: No agency shall require an inmate who alleges sexual abuse to submit to a polygraph or other truth-telling device as a condition for proceeding
An agency may require a polygraph when the inmate has a prior disciplinary record for dishonesty
An agency shall require a polygraph of the alleged victim before an investigation begins
An agency may require an inmate who alleges sexual abuse to take a polygraph if the Warden approves, for the duration of the incident, pending review by the appropriate official
questions.rationale:
The credibility of a victim, suspect, or witness is assessed individually, not by status, and no polygraph can be required of an inmate alleging abuse.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.71: “(e) The credibility of an alleged victim, suspect, or witness shall be assessed on an individual basis and shall not be determined by the person's status as inmate or staff. No agency shall require an inmate who alleges sexual abuse to submit to a polygraph examination or other truth-telling device as a condition for proceeding with the investigation of such an allegation.”

questions.stem:
An alleged abuser transfers out of the facility during the investigation, and a supervisor says the investigation can be closed.

What does the standard say?
options: The investigation may be closed when the alleged abuser leaves the agency, since he is no longer under its control
The departure of the alleged abuser or victim from the employment or control of the facility or agency shall not provide a basis for terminating an investigation
The investigation continues only if a prosecutor asks the agency in writing to keep it open
The investigation may be closed when the alleged victim is transferred, since a statement cannot be taken
questions.rationale:
Departure of the alleged abuser or victim does not provide a basis for ending an investigation.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.71: “(j) The departure of the alleged abuser or victim from the employment or control of the facility or agency shall not provide a basis for terminating an investigation.”

questions.stem:
An administrative investigation into an allegation of sexual abuse is concluding. A supervisor asks how long written reports must be kept.

What does the standard say?
options: For ten years after the date the allegation was made, regardless of the abuser's status
For as long as the alleged abuser is incarcerated or employed by the agency, plus one year, as long as no other inmate is affected
For as long as the alleged abuser is incarcerated or employed by the agency, plus five years
Until the investigation is closed, and then destroyed to protect privacy
questions.rationale:
Written investigation reports must be retained for as long as the alleged abuser is incarcerated or employed, plus five years.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.71: “(i) The agency shall retain all written reports referenced in paragraphs (f) and (g) of this section for as long as the alleged abuser is incarcerated or employed by the agency, plus five years.”

questions.stem:
An inmate alleged that an officer abused him. The investigation concluded the allegation was substantiated, and the officer has been removed from the inmate's unit.

What must the agency do?
options: Inform the inmate's family of the outcome and any later developments, but not the inmate
Inform the inmate of the outcome only, since later developments are confidential personnel matters, subject to the Warden's discretion, after a supervisor has reviewed the matter
Inform the inmate of the outcome only if the allegation was substantiated, and not otherwise
Inform the inmate of the outcome and later inform him if the staff member leaves his unit or the facility or is indicted or convicted, and document it
questions.rationale:
The agency informs the inmate of the result and subsequent developments such as removal from the unit, employment status, indictment, or conviction, documenting all notifications.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.73: “(a) Following an investigation into an inmate's allegation that he or she suffered sexual abuse in an agency facility, the agency shall inform the inmate as to whether the allegation has been determined to be substantiated, unsubstantiated, or unfounded. (c) Following an inmate's allegation that a staff member has committed sexual abuse against the inmate, the agency shall subsequently inform the inmate (unless the agency has determined that the allegation is unfounded) whenever: (1) The staff member is no longer posted within the inmate's unit; (2) The staff member is no longer employed at the facility; (3) The agency learns that the staff member has been indicted on a charge related to sexual abuse within the facility; or (4) The agency learns that the staff member has been convicted on a charge related to sexual abuse within the facility. (e) All such notifications or attempted notifications shall be documented.”

questions.stem:
A staff member is found to have engaged in sexual abuse of an inmate. A manager proposes a written warning.

What does the standard say about the presumptive sanction?
options: Termination shall be the presumptive disciplinary sanction for staff who have engaged in sexual abuse
Reassignment to a post without inmate contact shall be the presumptive sanction
A written warning and retraining shall be the presumptive sanction for a first violation
A suspension without pay shall be the presumptive sanction for staff who have engaged in sexual abuse
questions.rationale:
Termination is the presumptive sanction for staff who have engaged in sexual abuse.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.76: “(b) Termination shall be the presumptive disciplinary sanction for staff who have engaged in sexual abuse.”

questions.stem:
A volunteer who engaged in sexual abuse of an inmate asks to continue volunteering.

What does the standard require?
options: The volunteer shall be prohibited from contact with the victim only, and may continue elsewhere in the facility
The volunteer shall be prohibited from contact with inmates and reported to law enforcement and licensing bodies, unless clearly not criminal
The volunteer may continue with supervision, and the incident is reported to law enforcement only if the inmate asks, in most circumstances, unless an emergency requires otherwise
The volunteer shall be reassigned to a program without contact with the victim, and no report is required
questions.rationale:
Any contractor or volunteer who engages in sexual abuse is prohibited from contact with inmates and reported to law enforcement and relevant licensing bodies unless clearly not criminal.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.77: “(a) Any contractor or volunteer who engages in sexual abuse shall be prohibited from contact with inmates and shall be reported to law enforcement agencies, unless the activity was clearly not criminal, and to relevant licensing bodies.”

questions.stem:
A disciplinary panel is deciding on a sanction for an inmate found to have committed inmate-on-inmate sexual abuse. The inmate has a documented mental illness.

What must the panel consider?
options: Whether the inmate's victim consented, because mental health is not relevant to the sanction
Whether the inmate agrees to attend counseling, because mental health is considered only for juveniles
Whether the inmate's mental disabilities or mental illness contributed to his behavior when determining the type of sanction, if any
Whether the inmate has been disciplined before, because mental health is considered only at the appeal stage, in accordance with the posted schedule
questions.rationale:
The disciplinary process shall consider whether mental disabilities or mental illness contributed to the behavior.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.78: “(c) The disciplinary process shall consider whether an inmate's mental disabilities or mental illness contributed to his or her behavior when determining what type of sanction, if any, should be imposed.”

questions.stem:
An intake screening shows a new inmate previously experienced sexual victimization in the community.

What must staff ensure?
options: The inmate is offered a follow-up meeting with a medical practitioner within 72 hours of the intake screening
The inmate is offered a follow-up meeting with a mental health practitioner only after he requests one in writing
The inmate is offered a follow-up meeting with a medical or mental health practitioner within 30 days of the intake screening
The inmate is offered a follow-up meeting with a medical or mental health practitioner within 14 days of the intake screening
questions.rationale:
Staff ensure the inmate is offered a follow-up meeting with a medical or mental health practitioner within 14 days of intake screening.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.81: “(a) If the screening pursuant to § 115.41 indicates that a prison inmate has experienced prior sexual victimization, whether it occurred in an institutional setting or in the community, staff shall ensure that the inmate is offered a follow-up meeting with a medical or mental health practitioner within 14 days of the intake screening.”

questions.stem:
A victim of sexually abusive vaginal penetration while incarcerated asks about medical follow-up.

What must be offered?
options: Pregnancy tests, and tests for sexually transmitted infections as medically appropriate
Tests for sexually transmitted infections only, since pregnancy tests are offered only on request
Counseling only, with medical tests offered if the victim agrees to name the abuser
Pregnancy tests only, and a transfer to another facility as soon as one can be arranged
questions.rationale:
Victims of sexually abusive vaginal penetration are offered pregnancy tests, and victims of sexual abuse are offered STI tests as medically appropriate.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.83: “(d) Inmate victims of sexually abusive vaginal penetration while incarcerated shall be offered pregnancy tests.”
28 CFR § 115.83: “(f) Inmate victims of sexual abuse while incarcerated shall be offered tests for sexually transmitted infections as medically appropriate.”

questions.stem:
Medical staff learn an inmate is a known inmate-on-inmate abuser.

What does the standard say about mental health evaluation?
options: Within 30 days of learning of the abuse history, with treatment offered only at the inmate's request, after a supervisor has reviewed the matter
Within 60 days of learning of the abuse history, with treatment offered when mental health practitioners deem it appropriate
Within 6 months of learning of the abuse history, with treatment offered only after release
Within 14 days of learning of the abuse history, with treatment required in every case
questions.rationale:
Prisons attempt a mental health evaluation of known inmate-on-inmate abusers within 60 days of learning of the history, and offer treatment when appropriate.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.83: “(h) All prisons shall attempt to conduct a mental health evaluation of all known inmate-on-inmate abusers within 60 days of learning of such abuse history and offer treatment when deemed appropriate by mental health practitioners.”

questions.stem:
A new facility is planning a staffing plan. A planner asks which factors must be considered when determining adequate staffing and video monitoring.

Which of these is a required consideration?
options: The number of visits that the facility's inmates receive each month
The number of inmates who earn performance pay at the facility
The prevalence of substantiated and unsubstantiated incidents of sexual abuse
The average length of sentence of the inmates housed at the facility
questions.rationale:
The listed considerations include the prevalence of substantiated and unsubstantiated incidents of sexual abuse, physical plant blind-spots, and the composition of the inmate population.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.13: “(10) The prevalence of substantiated and unsubstantiated incidents of sexual abuse; and”

questions.stem:
A volunteer teaches classes for inmates but has not been trained on the agency's sexual abuse policies. The supervisor says only employees need training.

What is the correct response?
options: Volunteers who have contact with inmates must be trained, but contractors who are supervised by employees need not be
Volunteers and contractors who have contact with inmates must also be trained on the agency's zero-tolerance policy and how to report
Volunteers and contractors must be trained, but only after they have worked with inmates for one year
Only employees must be trained, and volunteers and contractors must be escorted at all times
questions.rationale:
The standard on volunteer and contractor training requires them to be trained on the zero-tolerance policy and reporting responsibilities.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.32: “(a) The agency shall ensure that all volunteers and contractors who have contact with inmates have been trained on their responsibilities under the agency's sexual abuse and sexual harassment prevention, detection, and response policies and procedures.”

questions.stem:
A supervisor suggests conducting an incident review of an unfounded sexual abuse allegation.

What does the standard say?
options: Reviews are conducted only at the conclusion of substantiated investigations, not unsubstantiated ones, as long as the unit team is notified, with the approval of a supervisor on duty
Reviews are conducted at the conclusion of every investigation, including unfounded ones
Reviews are conducted at the conclusion of every investigation, including unsubstantiated ones, unless the allegation was determined to be unfounded
Reviews are conducted only when the Warden requests one or when a criminal charge is filed
questions.rationale:
A review is conducted after every sexual abuse investigation unless the allegation has been determined to be unfounded.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.86: “(a) The facility shall conduct a sexual abuse incident review at the conclusion of every sexual abuse investigation, including where the allegation has not been substantiated, unless the allegation has been determined to be unfounded.”

questions.stem:
The facility's incident review team recommends adding cameras to a blind spot. The Warden decides not to act and tells no one.

What does the standard require?
options: The facility may decline the recommendations without documentation if the Warden disagrees
The facility shall implement only the recommendations that do not require new spending
The facility shall send the recommendations to the PREA coordinator and take no further action
The facility shall implement the recommendations or document its reasons for not doing so
questions.rationale:
The facility implements recommendations for improvement or documents its reasons for not doing so.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.86: “(e) The facility shall implement the recommendations for improvement, or shall document its reasons for not doing so.”

questions.stem:
An inmate who was approved for a religious diet withdraws from the program on Monday, then asks to rejoin on Wednesday.

What does the regulation say?
options: He may rejoin the next business day if the chaplain signs a new written statement of religious motivation
He may not rejoin for the remainder of his sentence, since withdrawal ends eligibility permanently
Inmates who withdraw or are removed may not be immediately reestablished; reapproval ordinarily may take up to thirty days
He may rejoin after sixty days, and only if the Warden approves the written request
questions.rationale:
To preserve integrity and prevent fraud, inmates who withdraw or are removed may not be immediately reestablished; reapproval ordinarily may take up to thirty days.

Source — 28 CFR § 548.20: “(b) An inmate who has been approved for a religious diet menu must notify the chaplain in writing if the inmate wishes to withdraw from the religious diet. Approval for an inmate's religious diet may be withdrawn by the chaplain if the inmate is documented as being in violation of the terms of the religious diet program to which the inmate has agreed in writing. In order to preserve the integrity and orderly operation of the religious diet program and to prevent fraud, inmates who withdraw (or are removed) may not be immediately reestablished back into the program. The process of reapproving a religious diet for an inmate who voluntarily withdraws or who is removed ordinarily may extend up to thirty days. Repeated withdrawals (voluntary or otherwise), however, may result in inmates being subjected to a waiting period of up to one year.”

questions.stem:
An inmate calls in sick and also leaves work for a visit during the month. He asks whether his performance pay will be affected.

What does the regulation say?
options: Absences for visits and phone calls are deducted, but absences for sick call and interviews are paid as worked time, according to the institution's local guidelines
Absences are deducted only when an inmate misses a full day of work, and not for shorter periods
Absences for call-outs, visits, sick call, interviews, or phone calls are deducted from the monthly hours worked and reduce the pay received
Absences for sick call are deducted, but absences for visits and phone calls are not deducted from the hours worked
questions.rationale:
Performance pay applies only to hours actually worked, and absences for such reasons are deducted.

Source — 28 CFR § 545.26: “(d) An inmate is eligible to receive performance pay only for those hours during which the inmate is actually performing satisfactory work or actively participating in an education or vocational training program. Absences from an inmate's scheduled assignment for such reasons as call-outs, visits, sick call, interviews, or making telephone calls shall be deducted from the monthly number of hours worked and will accordingly reduce the amount of pay received by the inmate. Any exception to such reduction in pay must be approved by the Assistant Director, Correctional Programs Division, Central Office.”

questions.stem:
A work supervisor wants to recommend a bonus for an inmate who worked beyond the scheduled work day and did exceptional work.

What is required?
options: The supervisor may award a bonus directly, and a written note is filed in the inmate's central file afterward
The Warden must approve a bonus, and the written justification is forwarded to the Regional Director for review
The supervisor may recommend a bonus only for work during the scheduled day, and not for extra hours worked
The supervisor may recommend a bonus, and written justification must be forwarded to the Department Head for approval
questions.rationale:
The supervisor may recommend a bonus for exceptional accomplishments, such as working in excess of the scheduled day, with written justification forwarded to the Department Head for approval.

Source — 28 CFR § 545.26: “(f) Bonus pay. When the supervisor of an inmate worker or program participant believes the inmate has made exceptional accomplishments or appreciably contributed to the work assignment, the supervisor may recommend that the inmate receive a bonus. For example, an inmate who works in excess of the scheduled work day can qualify for bonus pay. Written justification for the bonus request must be forwarded to the Department Head for approval.”

questions.stem:
An inmate working an institution job is found responsible for a drug-related prohibited act in the 100 series. He asks whether he will keep his current pay level.

What will happen?
options: His performance pay is eliminated for the rest of the month, and he is reassigned to the commissary
His performance pay is automatically reduced to maintenance pay level, and he is removed from outside work details, ordinarily for one year
His performance pay is unchanged, but he is removed from outside work details until the Warden reviews the case
His performance pay is reduced to maintenance level for thirty days, and he remains on his current outside work detail, based on the information available at the time
questions.rationale:
Inmates found to have committed a level 100 or 200 series drug- or alcohol-related act have pay reduced to maintenance level and are removed from outside details, ordinarily for one year.

Source — 28 CFR § 545.25: “(e) Inmates receiving performance pay who are found through the disciplinary process (part 541 of this subchapter) to have committed a level 100 or 200 series drug- or alcohol-related prohibited act will automatically have their performance pay reduced to maintenance pay level and will be removed from any assigned work detail outside the secure perimeter of the institution. This reduction to maintenance pay level, and removal from assigned work detail outside the secure perimeter of the institution, will ordinarily remain in effect for one year, unless otherwise authorized by the Warden.”

questions.stem:
An inmate has tested positive for an infectious disease and has not engaged in any behavior that could transmit it. A supervisor wants to charge him with a prohibited act and move him to a special unit for such inmates.

What does the regulation say?
options: The test alone is not grounds for discipline, and no special or separate housing units may be established for HIV-positive inmates
The test alone is not grounds for discipline, but a separate housing unit is required for HIV-positive inmates
The test alone is grounds for discipline, and a separate housing unit is required for HIV-positive inmates
The test alone is grounds for discipline, but no special or separate housing units may be established for HIV-positive inmates, subject to the Warden's discretion
questions.rationale:
A positive test alone does not constitute sole grounds for discipline, and no special or separate housing units may be established for HIV-positive inmates except as provided in the disciplinary policy.

Source — 28 CFR § 549.13: “(c) If an inmate tests positive for an infectious disease, that test alone does not constitute sole grounds for disciplinary action. Disciplinary action may be considered when coupled with a secondary action that could lead to transmission of an infectious agent. Inmates testing positive for infectious disease are subject to the same disciplinary policy that applies to all inmates (see 28 CFR part 541, subpart B). Except as provided for in our disciplinary policy, no special or separate housing units may be established for HIV-positive inmates.”

questions.stem:
A nurse refuses to release an inmate's HIV test result to a requesting officer who has no role in the inmate's care. The officer says all staff are entitled to know.

What law does the regulation cite for how results are disclosed?
options: The Health Insurance Portability Act of 1996 and the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990
The Privacy Act of 1974 and the Correction Officers Health and Safety Act of 1998
The Violent Crime Control and Law Enforcement Act of 1994 and the Civil Rights Act of 1964
The Freedom of Information Act of 1966 and the Prison Litigation Reform Act of 1995
questions.rationale:
Disclosure of test results or medical information follows the Privacy Act of 1974 and the Correction Officers Health and Safety Act of 1998.

Source — 28 CFR § 549.14: “(a) The Privacy Act of 1974, under which the Bureau publishes routine uses of such information in the Department of Justice Privacy Act System of Records Notice entitled “Inmate Physical and Mental Health Record System, JUSTICE/BOP-007”; and (b) The Correction Officers Health and Safety Act of 1998 (codified at 18 U.S.C. 4014), which provides that test results must be communicated to a person requesting the test, the person tested, and, if the results of the test indicate the presence of HIV, to correctional facility personnel consistent with Bureau policy.”

questions.stem:
An inmate is refusing food and fluids and a physician determines his life will be threatened unless treatment begins immediately.

What must staff do before treatment is administered against his will?
options: Wait seventy-two hours for him to change his mind, and document the delay in the medical record
Ask another inmate to persuade him, and document the conversation in the housing unit log instead of the medical record, based on the information available at the time
Make reasonable efforts to convince him to accept treatment, explain the medical risks, and document the efforts in the medical record
Order the treatment at once without explaining the risks, and document the order in the medical record afterward
questions.rationale:
Before treatment against an inmate's will, staff make reasonable efforts to convince him and explain risks, documenting their efforts; in an emergency preventing such efforts, the physician may order treatment.

Source — 28 CFR § 549.65: “(b) Prior to medical treatment being administered against the inmate's will, staff shall make reasonable efforts to convince the inmate to voluntarily accept treatment. Medical risks faced by the inmate if treatment is not accepted shall also be explained to the inmate. Staff shall document their treatment efforts in the medical record of the inmate.”

questions.stem:
An officer notices an inmate has accumulated stacks of commissary items and old newspapers that make his locker overflow and are a fire hazard.

What does the regulation say staff may not allow?
options: Staff may allow accumulation of commissary items without limit, but not accumulation of newspapers or magazines
Staff may allow accumulation of materials until the number of items exceeds the numerical limit set for the institution, after a supervisor has reviewed the matter
Staff may allow accumulation of any materials, as long as they are stored in the inmate's own locker
Staff may not allow an inmate to accumulate materials to the point where they become a fire, sanitation, security, or housekeeping hazard
questions.rationale:
Staff may not allow an inmate to accumulate materials to the point where they become a fire, sanitation, security, or housekeeping hazard.

Source — 28 CFR § 553.11: “(b) Storage space. Staff shall set aside space within each housing area for use by an inmate. The designated area shall include a locker or other securable area in which the inmate is to store authorized personal property. The inmate shall be allowed to purchase an approved locking device for personal property storage in regular living units. Staff may not allow an inmate to accumulate materials to the point where the materials become a fire, sanitation, security, or housekeeping hazard.”

questions.stem:
An inmate wants to marry. He gives a written request directly to the Warden's secretary.

What is the correct process?
options: He submits the request to his unit team, which evaluates it and forwards it to the Regional Director for a final decision
He submits the request to the Warden, who forwards it to the unit team for a written report and final decision
He submits the request to his unit team, which evaluates it and forwards a written report and recommendation to the Warden for a final decision
He submits the request to the chaplain, who evaluates it and makes a final decision after consulting the Warden
questions.rationale:
A request to marry is submitted to the unit team, evaluated, and forwarded with a recommendation to the Warden for a final decision.

Source — 28 CFR § 551.13: “(a) A federal inmate confined in a Bureau institution who wants to get married shall submit a request to marry to the inmate's unit team. The unit team shall evaluate the request based on the criteria identified in § 551.12. A written report of the unit team's findings, and its recommendation, shall be forwarded to the Warden for a final decision.”

questions.stem:
A group of inmates start a book club and begin meeting in the dayroom without telling staff.

What does the regulation require?
options: An inmate must submit a request for recognition to the Warden, and the organization may not become active without the Warden's approval
An inmate must notify the unit officer, and the organization may become active once five members have signed up, in accordance with the posted schedule
An inmate must submit a request to the unit team, and the organization may become active after one meeting
An inmate must notify the chaplain, and the organization may become active thirty days after the notice
questions.rationale:
An inmate organization may not become active without the Warden's approval.

Source — 28 CFR § 551.31: “(a) An inmate must submit a request for recognition of a proposed inmate organization to the Warden. The organization may not become active without the Warden's approval.”

questions.stem:
An approved inmate organization proposes a bake sale to raise funds for new equipment.

What does the regulation say?
options: Fund-raising is permitted on weekends
Activities may not include fund-raising projects
Fund-raising is permitted if staff approve
Fund-raising is permitted
questions.rationale:
Activities include meetings, speakers, competitions, banquets, or community programs, but may not include fund-raising projects.

Source — 28 CFR § 551.34: “(a) An officer of the inmate organization must submit a written request for approval of an activity to the Warden or designee. Activities include, but are not limited to, meetings, guest speakers, sports competitions, banquets, or community programs. Activities may not include fund-raising projects. The request must specifically include:”

questions.stem:
An inmate organization continues to violate Bureau policy.

What may the Warden do?
options: The Warden may suspend its activities immediately without notice, and may withdraw approval only after one year

The Warden may fine its members after written notice and a chance to respond, and may transfer them for continued noncompliance, as long as no other inmate is affected, once the shift lieutenant has been informed
The Warden may temporarily suspend its activities after written notice and a chance to respond, and may increase the sanction for continued noncompliance, up to withdrawing approval
The Warden may disband the organization after one violation, without written notice or a chance to respond
questions.rationale:
Activities may be suspended temporarily for noncompliance after written notice and an opportunity to respond, and continued noncompliance increases the severity and may include withdrawal of approval.

Source — 28 CFR § 551.34: “(e) The activities of an inmate organization may be suspended temporarily due to noncompliance with Bureau policy. The IOM is responsible for recommending the specific suspension sanction for the Warden's approval. The inmate organization is to receive written notice of the proposed suspension sanction and shall have the opportunity to respond to the Warden. Continued noncompliance with Bureau policy shall result in an increase in the severity of the suspension sanction, and may include withdrawal of approval of the organization.”

questions.stem:
A pretrial inmate in a general housing unit has not gone outdoors for several days. Staff are short-staffed but there are no security concerns.

What recreation must staff provide at a minimum?
options: Thirty minutes daily of outside recreation, weather permitting, or one hour daily of indoor recreation
Two hours daily of outside recreation, weather permitting, or four hours daily of indoor recreation
One hour daily of outside recreation, weather permitting, or two hours daily of indoor recreation
One hour weekly of outside recreation, weather permitting, or two hours weekly of indoor recreation
questions.rationale:
Unless compelling security or safety reasons dictate otherwise (and are documented), staff provide at least one hour daily of outside recreation or two hours daily of indoor recreation.

Source — 28 CFR § 551.115: “(b) At a minimum, and except as noted in paragraph (d) of this section, staff shall provide the pretrial inmate with the following recreational opportunities: (1) One hour daily of outside recreation, weather permitting; or (2) Two hours daily of indoor recreation. (e) Provisions of paragraphs (b) and (c) of this section must be carried out unless compelling security or safety reasons dictate otherwise. Institution staff shall document these reasons.”

questions.stem:
A pretrial inmate repeatedly causes serious disruptions. A staff member asks who must be informed.

What does the regulation require?
options: Staff shall advise the court, through the inmate's attorney, of repeated or serious disruptive behavior
Staff shall advise the inmate's family, through the unit team, of repeated or serious disruptive behavior
Staff shall advise the Regional Director, through the Warden, of repeated or serious disruptive behavior
Staff shall advise the court, through the U.S. Marshal, of repeated or serious disruptive behavior
questions.rationale:
Staff advise the court, through the U.S. Marshal, of repeated or serious disruptive behavior by a pretrial inmate.

Source — 28 CFR § 551.116: “(b) Staff shall advise the court, through the U.S. Marshal, of repeated or serious disruptive behavior by a pretrial inmate.”

questions.stem:
A reporter wants to photograph an inmate in a program. The inmate does not want to be photographed.

What does the regulation say?
options: An inmate may be photographed if the program is open to the public, even if the inmate objects
An inmate has the right not to be photographed or recorded by the media, and the reporter must obtain the inmate's written permission
An inmate may be photographed during an authorized program if the Warden gives written permission for the reporter, under the direction of the senior officer present
An inmate may be photographed if his face is hidden, and the reporter has the unit officer's verbal permission
questions.rationale:
An inmate has the right not to be photographed or voice-recorded by the media, and the representative must obtain written permission from the inmate.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.62: “(b) When media representatives visit the institutions, photographs of programs and activities may be taken, and media representatives may meet with groups of inmates engaged in authorized programs and activities. An inmate has the right not to be photographed and not to have his or her voice recorded by the media. A visiting representative of the media is required to obtain written permission from an inmate before photographing or recording the voice of an inmate participating in authorized programs and activities.”

questions.stem:
A magazine arrives that routinely features sexually explicit pictorial depictions. The mailroom wants to know how to dispose of it.

What does the regulation say about publications restricted by statute?
options: The Warden or designee shall give the material to staff and advise the inmate that an appeal may be filed
The Warden or designee shall keep the material in the mailroom and notify the inmate that it has been rejected
The Warden or designee shall destroy the material and advise the publisher that an independent review may be requested, pending review by the appropriate official
The Warden or designee shall return the material to the publisher or sender and advise that an independent review of the decision may be requested
questions.rationale:
When material cannot be distributed due to statutory restrictions, the Warden or designee returns it to the publisher or sender and advises of independent review.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.72: “(a) When commercially published information or material may not be distributed by staff or made available to inmates due to statutory restrictions (for example, a prohibition on the use of appropriated funds to distribute or make available to inmates information or material which is sexually explicit or features nudity), the Warden or designee shall return the information or material to the publisher or sender. The Warden or designee shall advise the publisher or sender that an independent review of the decision may be obtained by writing to the Regional Director within 20 days of receipt of the notification letter. Staff shall provide the inmate with written notice of the action.”

questions.stem:
An inmate wants to volunteer for a community service project recommended by the Warden. He asks how to apply.

What does the regulation require?
options: He submits a verbal request to the unit officer, and the Warden's decision is documented in the log
He submits a written request for the Warden's approval, and the Warden's decision is documented in writing
He submits a written request to the sponsoring organization, and the sponsor's decision is documented in writing
He submits a written request to the Regional Director, and the Regional Director's decision is documented in writing
questions.rationale:
An inmate may volunteer by submitting a written request for the Warden's approval, and the decision is documented in writing.

Source — 28 CFR § 551.60: “(b) An inmate may volunteer to participate in a community service project by submitting a written request for the Warden's approval. The inmate must have custody classification appropriate for the project and be otherwise eligible for the conditions of the project. The decision of the Warden to approve or disapprove an inmate's request shall be documented in writing.”

questions.stem:
A rejected remedy request used abusive language. The inmate asks whether the rejection can be appealed and corrected.

What does the regulation say about rejections?
options: The Coordinator may not reject a request for any reason, but may ask the inmate to rewrite it
The Coordinator may reject a request, and the rejection is final with no notice or chance to correct
The Coordinator may reject a request only after a hearing at which the inmate may speak
The Coordinator may reject an obscene or abusive request, and the notice of rejection gives the reason and time to correct if the defect is correctable
questions.rationale:
A Coordinator may reject an obscene or abusive request, must give written notice of the reason, and if correctable must allow a reasonable time to correct and resubmit.

Source — 28 CFR § 542.17: “(a) Rejections. The Coordinator at any level (CCM, institution, region, Central Office) may reject and return to the inmate without response a Request or an Appeal that is written by an inmate in a manner that is obscene or abusive, or does not meet any other requirement of this part.”
28 CFR § 542.17: “(b) Notice. When a submission is rejected, the inmate shall be provided a written notice, signed by the Administrative Remedy Coordinator, explaining the reason for rejection. If the defect on which the rejection is based is correctable, the notice shall inform the inmate of a reasonable time extension within which to correct the defect and resubmit the Request or Appeal.”

questions.stem:
An inmate is late filing a Request because he was in transit for a month and separated from his documents.

What does the regulation say?
options: A valid reason for delay, including an extended period in transit separated from documents, can lead to an extension
A valid reason for delay allows an extension, but only for a period of up to five days
No reason is accepted as valid, and a late filing is rejected without exception
A reason for delay is valid only if the inmate was in disciplinary segregation during the filing period
questions.rationale:
Valid reasons for delay include an extended period in transit during which the inmate was separated from documents needed to prepare the Request.

Source — 28 CFR § 542.14: “(b) Extension. Where the inmate demonstrates a valid reason for delay, an extension in filing time may be allowed. In general, valid reason for delay means a situation which prevented the inmate from submitting the request within the established time frame. Valid reasons for delay include the following: an extended period in-transit during which the inmate was separated from documents needed to prepare the Request or Appeal; an extended period of time during which the inmate was physically incapable of preparing a Request or Appeal; an unusually long period taken for informal resolution attempts; indication by an inmate, verified by staff, that a response to the inmate's request for copies of dispositions requested under § 542.19 of this part was delayed.”

questions.stem:
A newly admitted inmate has not been screened for suicide risk. Two days have passed.

What does the regulation say about the screening timeline?
options: Housing unit staff are to screen a newly admitted inmate for suicide risk, ordinarily within twenty-four hours
Medical staff are to screen a newly admitted inmate for suicide risk, ordinarily within thirty days of admission
Medical staff are to screen a newly admitted inmate for suicide risk, ordinarily within twenty-four hours of admission
Medical staff are to screen a newly admitted inmate for suicide risk, ordinarily within seventy-two hours of admission
questions.rationale:
Medical staff screen newly admitted inmates for suicide risk, ordinarily within twenty-four hours.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.41: “(c) Identification of at risk inmates. (1) Medical staff are to screen a newly admitted inmate for signs that the inmate is at risk for suicide. Ordinarily, this screening is to take place within twenty-four hours of the inmate's admission to the institution.”

questions.stem:
After a suicide watch assessment, the inmate is no longer at imminent risk.

What happens next?
options: Based on the Warden's judgment, the Warden removes the inmate from watch or orders disciplinary segregation
Based on the inmate's request, the inmate may leave the watch once he has signed a statement that he is safe
Based on the Captain's judgment, the Captain removes the inmate from watch or arranges transfer to a different housing unit
Based on clinical findings, the Program Coordinator or designee removes the inmate from watch or arranges transfer to a medical referral center or health care facility
questions.rationale:
Based upon clinical findings, the Program Coordinator or designee removes the inmate from watch when no longer at imminent risk, or arranges transfer.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.42: “(d) Termination. Based upon clinical findings, the Program Coordinator or designee will: (1) Remove the inmate from suicide watch when the inmate is no longer at imminent risk for suicide, or (2) Arrange for the inmate's transfer to a medical referral center or health care facility.”

questions.stem:
A visitor leaves a package of clothing at the front desk for his brother, an inmate. The package has not been approved in advance.

What does the regulation say about accepting articles or gifts in the visiting room?
options: The visiting room officer may accept any article that is inspected for contraband
The visiting room officer may accept articles that are under a certain dollar value, subject to the Warden's discretion, unless an emergency requires otherwise, as long as the unit team is notified
The visiting room officer may accept articles if the inmate's counselor is told
The visiting room officer may not accept articles or gifts for an inmate, except packages that have had prior approval by the Warden or a designated staff member
questions.rationale:
The visiting room officer may not accept articles or gifts of any kind for an inmate, except packages which have had prior approval.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.51: “(3) The visiting room officer may not accept articles or gifts of any kind for an inmate, except packages which have had prior approval by the Warden or a designated staff member.”

questions.stem:
Officer Wright sees a visitor slip something small into an inmate's hand during an embrace at the end of a contact visit.

What is the officer permitted to do?
options: Examine the item, since there is a reasonable basis to believe an item is being passed that is contraband or violates law or regulations
Ignore the exchange until the visit is over and the visitor has left, in most circumstances, once the shift lieutenant has been informed, for the duration of the incident
Ask the visitor to retrieve the item and give it to the front desk
Stop the visit and charge the visitor with a prohibited act
questions.rationale:
The visiting room officer shall be aware of articles passed, and if there is any reasonable basis to believe an item constitutes contraband or violates the law or regulations, may examine the item.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.51: “(4) The visiting room officer shall be aware of any articles passed between the inmate and the visitor. If there is any reasonable basis to believe that any item is being passed which constitutes contraband or is otherwise in violation of the law or Bureau regulations, the visiting room officer may examine the item.”

questions.stem:
A visitor and an inmate are talking loudly and laughing in the visiting room, and other families are starting to complain.

What authority does the visiting room officer have?
options: The officer may only issue a verbal warning and may not end a visit
The officer may end the visit only after getting the Warden's approval
The officer may terminate visits that are not conducted in a quiet, orderly, and dignified manner
The officer may end the visit only if the inmate has been disciplined for prior visit violations, after a supervisor has reviewed the matter
questions.rationale:
The visiting room officer shall ensure all visits are quiet, orderly, and dignified, and may terminate visits that are not.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.51: “(1) The visiting room officer shall ensure that all visits are conducted in a quiet, orderly, and dignified manner. The visiting room officer may terminate visits that are not conducted in the appropriate manner. See 28 CFR 541.12, item 5, for description of an inmate's responsibility during visits.”

questions.stem:
A visitor is surprised to learn that a camera records the visiting room and asks whether she should have been told.

What does the regulation say about monitoring the visiting area?
options: The Warden must provide notice to inmates only, since visitors are not covered by the rule
The Warden may monitor the visiting area without giving notice to visitors or inmates
The Warden may monitor the visiting area only with a court order
The Warden may establish monitoring procedures, but must provide notice to both visitors and inmates of the potential for monitoring
questions.rationale:
The Warden may establish procedures to monitor the visiting area but must provide notice to both visitors and inmates of the potential for monitoring.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.51: “(h) Supervision of visits. Staff shall supervise each inmate visit to prevent the passage of contraband and to ensure the security and good order of the institution. The Warden may establish procedures to enable monitoring of the visiting area, including restrooms located within the visiting area. The Warden must provide notice to both visitors and inmates of the potential for monitoring the visiting area. The Warden may monitor a visitor restroom within the visiting area when there is reasonable suspicion that a visitor and/or an inmate is engaged, or attempting or about to engage, in criminal behavior or other prohibited behavior.”

questions.stem:
Staff want to run a background check on a proposed visitor who is a friend (not immediate family). The inmate asks who sends the release authorization form to the visitor.

What does the regulation say?
options: The inmate is responsible for mailing the release authorization form to the proposed visitor, who must sign and return it to staff
The inmate's family is responsible for mailing the form and for returning it to the unit team, with the approval of a supervisor on duty
The Warden is responsible for mailing the form, and the visitor returns it within five days
Staff are responsible for mailing the form, and the visitor returns it to the inmate
questions.rationale:
If a background investigation is necessary, the inmate is held responsible for mailing a release authorization form to the proposed visitor, who must sign and return it before further action.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.51: “(3) If a background investigation is necessary before approving a visitor, the inmate shall be held responsible for mailing a release authorization form to the proposed visitor. That form must be signed and returned to staff by the proposed visitor prior to any further action regarding visiting. Upon receipt of the authorization form, staff may then forward a questionnaire, along with the release authorization, to the appropriate law enforcement or crime information agency.”

questions.stem:
An inmate in segregation status asks whether he will lose all visiting privileges simply because he is in segregation.

What does the regulation say?
options: He retains visiting privileges, which may be restricted only by the Regional Director
He loses all visiting privileges for as long as he is in segregation

He retains visiting privileges, but only with immediate family members and only by video, provided that the action is documented, subject to the Warden's discretion, as long as no other inmate is affected

Ordinarily he retains visiting privileges, which may be restricted or disallowed if he is charged with or found to have committed a visiting-related prohibited act or poses a threat to the visiting room
questions.rationale:
Ordinarily an inmate retains visiting privileges while in detention or segregation status; visiting may be restricted or disallowed for a visiting-related prohibited act or other conduct indicating a threat to the visiting room.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.50: “(c) Detention or segregation status. Ordinarily, an inmate retains visiting privileges while in detention or segregation status. Visiting may be restricted or disallowed, however, when an inmate, while in detention or segregation status, is charged with, or has been found to have committed, a prohibited act having to do with visiting guidelines or has otherwise acted in a way that would reasonably indicate that he or she would be a threat to the orderliness or security of the visiting room. Loss of an inmate's visiting privileges for other reasons may not occur unless the inmate is provided a hearing before the Discipline Hearing Officer (DHO) in accordance with the provisions of § 541.17 of this chapter, following those provisions which are appropriate to the circumstances, which results in a finding by the DHO that the inmate committed a prohibited act and that there is a lack of other appropriate sanctions or that imposition of an appropriate sanction previously has been ineffective. The Unit Discipline Committee (UDC) may not impose a loss of visiting privileges for inmates in detention or segregation status. The provisions of this paragraph (c) do not interrupt or delay a loss of visiting sanction imposed by the UDC or DHO prior to the inmate's placement in detention or segregation status.”

questions.stem:
A family asks to visit an inmate who is hospitalized inside the institution.

Who determines whether the visit may occur?
options: The Chief Medical Officer (or the Health Services Administrator in his absence), in consultation with the Captain
The Warden, in consultation with the inmate's case manager
The Captain alone, in consultation with the chaplain
The visiting room officer, in consultation with the unit manager
questions.rationale:
When visitors request to see an inmate who is hospitalized in the institution, the Chief Medical Officer (or the Health Services Administrator), in consultation with the Captain, determines whether a visit may occur and whether it may be held in the hospital.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.50: “(b) Hospital patients. (1) When visitors request to see an inmate who is hospitalized in the institution, the Chief Medical Officer (or, in his absence, the Health Services Administrator), in consultation with the Captain, shall determine whether a visit may occur, and if so, whether it may be held in the hospital.”

questions.stem:
There is no incident report, but the Warden decides to place an inmate on restricted general correspondence as a matter of classification.

What must the Warden do first?
options: Notify the inmate's family in writing of the reasons, and give the family the opportunity to respond, under the direction of the senior officer present, based on the information available at the time
Advise the inmate orally of the reasons, and give him seven days to find another correspondent
Advise the inmate in writing of the reasons, give him the opportunity to respond orally or in writing, and notify him of the decision and the right to appeal
Obtain the approval of the Regional Director, and then notify the inmate of the decision
questions.rationale:
Where there is no incident report, the Warden must advise the inmate in writing of the reasons, give him an opportunity to respond orally or in writing, and notify him of the decision, reasons, and right to appeal through the Administrative Remedy Procedure.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.15: “(2) Where there is no incident report, the Warden: (i) Shall advise the inmate in writing of the reasons the inmate is to be placed on restricted general correspondence; (ii) Shall give the inmate the opportunity to respond to the classification or change in classification; the inmate has the option to respond orally or to submit written information or both; and (iii) Shall notify the inmate of the decision and the reasons, and shall advise the inmate that the inmate may appeal the decision under the Administrative Remedy Procedure.”

questions.stem:
An inmate on restricted general correspondence wants to write to his mother and his sister.

What does the regulation say?
options: He may not correspond with anyone outside the institution while on restriction
He may correspond with family only if the Warden reads each letter before it is sent
He may correspond only with his spouse, and other family members must be added to the list
He may correspond with his spouse, mother, father, children, and siblings, unless the correspondent is involved in a violation or poses a threat
questions.rationale:
An inmate on restricted correspondence may correspond with his spouse, mother, father, children, and siblings unless the correspondent is involved in a violation of correspondence regulations or would be a threat.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.15: “(d) When an inmate is placed on restricted general correspondence, the inmate may, except as provided in §§ 540.16 and 540.17: (1) Correspond with the inmate's spouse, mother, father, children, and siblings, unless the correspondent is involved in any violation of correspondence regulations, or would be a threat to the security or good order of the institution;”

questions.stem:
Two inmates in different federal institutions are brothers and want to write to each other.

Who must approve the correspondence?
options: The Wardens of both institutions, and the letters may be sealed and sent unopened
The appropriate unit manager at each institution, and the letters may be inspected and read by staff and may not be sealed
No approval is needed for immediate family, and the letters may be sealed
The Regional Director, and the letters may be sealed but staff may inspect the envelopes
questions.rationale:
If both inmates are in federal institutions and are members of the same immediate family, the appropriate unit manager at each institution must approve; such correspondence may always be inspected and read and may not be sealed.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.17: “(a) Such correspondence at institutions of all security levels may always be inspected and read by staff at the sending and receiving institutions (it may not be sealed by the inmate); and (b)(1) The appropriate unit manager at each institution must approve of the correspondence if both inmates are housed in Federal institutions and both inmates are members of the same immediate family or are a party or witness in a legal action in which both inmates are involved.”

questions.stem:
A federal inmate wants to write to an inmate at a state prison who is a witness in a case in which both are involved.

Who must approve this correspondence?
options: The Regional Director, because the correspondence crosses jurisdictions
The unit managers of both institutions, because both inmates are parties or witnesses
The Wardens of both institutions, because one of the inmates is housed at a non-Federal institution
The Warden of the federal institution only, because the state prison has its own rules, when staff resources allow
questions.rationale:
The Wardens of both institutions must approve if one of the inmates is housed at a non-Federal institution or if approval is granted on the basis of exceptional circumstances.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.17: “(2) The Wardens of both institutions must approve of the correspondence if one of the inmates is housed at a non-Federal institution or if approval is being granted on the basis of exceptional circumstances.”

questions.stem:
A reporter calls the institution and asks to interview an inmate tomorrow morning. The inmate has not been told.

What must staff do before the interview can take place?
options: Obtain the Warden's written consent and notify the inmate after the interview is scheduled
Obtain the consent of the inmate's family and place a copy in his visiting file
Obtain the inmate's verbal consent and notify the reporter by telephone
Notify the inmate of the request and obtain his written consent before the interview, and place the consent or denial in his central file
questions.rationale:
Staff shall notify an inmate of each interview request and, as a prerequisite, obtain written consent from the inmate before the interview; the consent or denial becomes part of the central file.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.63: “(d) Staff shall notify an inmate of each interview request, and shall, as a prerequisite, obtain from the inmate written consent for the interview prior to the interview taking place. The written consent or denial becomes part of the inmate's central file.”

questions.stem:
The Warden receives a media interview request on Monday morning.

When should the Warden normally decide on the request?
options: Within 24 to 48 hours of the request
On the same day, before the end of the shift
Within 30 days of the request
Within 5 work days of the request
questions.rationale:
The Warden shall normally approve or disapprove an interview request within 24 to 48 hours of the request.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.63: “(f) The Warden shall normally approve or disapprove an interview request within 24 to 48 hours of the request.”

questions.stem:
A reporter asks to interview a 16-year-old inmate who has written to her. The inmate's parents have not given consent.

What does the regulation say may be a reason for denial?
options: The inmate is under age 25 and has not completed a high school program
The inmate is a juvenile and written consent has not been obtained from his parent or guardian
The inmate is a juvenile, and the interview would be held in the visiting room
The inmate has not received a visit from the news media within the past year
questions.rationale:
A request may be denied if the inmate is a juvenile (under 18) and written consent has not been obtained from the parent or guardian.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.63: “(3) The inmate is a juvenile (under age 18) and written consent has not been obtained from the inmate's parent or guardian. If the juvenile inmate's parents or guardians are not known or their addresses are not known, the Warden of the institution shall notify the representative of the news media of the inmate's status as a juvenile, and shall then consider the request.”

questions.stem:
A reporter wants to interview an inmate who is in protective custody because other inmates are threatening him.

What may the Warden do?
options: Approve the request only if the reporter agrees not to publish the inmate's name, pending review by the appropriate official
Approve the request only if the inmate's attorney attends the interview
Deny the request, since the inmate is a protection case and revealing his whereabouts would endanger his safety
Approve the request, since all inmates may be interviewed on request
questions.rationale:
A request may be denied if the inmate is a protection case and revelation of his whereabouts would endanger his safety, with the denial documented.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.63: “(7) The inmate is a “protection” case and revelation of his or her whereabouts would endanger the inmate's safety.”

questions.stem:
A reporter is interviewing an inmate in the visiting room. A staff member stands nearby to listen to the conversation "for security."

What does the regulation say about supervision of interviews?
options: Interviews are subject to auditory supervision by the Public Information Officer
Interviews are subject to auditory supervision whenever the Warden approves
Interviews are subject to auditory supervision when the inmate is in segregation
Interviews are not subject to auditory supervision
questions.rationale:
Paragraph (j) is direct: interviews are not subject to auditory supervision.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.63: “(j) Interviews are not subject to auditory supervision.”

questions.stem:
A reporter offers an inmate $200 for an interview.

What does the regulation say about compensation?
options: An inmate may not receive compensation or anything of value for interviews with the news media
An inmate may accept compensation if the interview concerns his own case
An inmate may accept compensation if the Warden approves it in writing
An inmate may accept compensation if it is deposited in his commissary account
questions.rationale:
An inmate may not receive compensation or anything of value for interviews with the news media.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.63: “(a) An inmate may not receive compensation or anything of value for interviews with the news media.”

questions.stem:
A reporter has obtained personal details about one inmate from another inmate who refused to be interviewed himself.

What does the regulation say?
options: A news representative may use such information if it is already a matter of public record
A news representative may use such information if the first inmate gives written permission
A news representative shall collect information only from the primary source and may not obtain and use personal information from one inmate about another who refuses to be interviewed
A news representative may use information from any inmate who is willing to talk
questions.rationale:
A representative of the news media shall collect information only from the primary source and may not obtain and use personal information from one inmate about another inmate who refuses to be interviewed.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.61: “(d) A representative of the news media shall collect information only from the primary source. A representative of the news media may not obtain and use personal information from one inmate about another inmate who refuses to be interviewed.”

questions.stem:
Three issues of a monthly magazine have been rejected for describing how to build weapons. The mailroom wants to cancel the whole subscription.

What does the regulation say?
options: The subscription may be rejected in its entirety if the Regional Director approves, as long as no other inmate is affected, after a supervisor has reviewed the matter
Rejection of several issues of a subscription publication is not sufficient reason to reject the subscription publication in its entirety
The subscription may be rejected in its entirety after two issues are rejected
The subscription may be rejected in its entirety if the inmate agrees
questions.rationale:
The Warden must review the individual publication before rejection, and rejection of several issues of a subscription is not sufficient reason to reject the subscription in its entirety.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.71: “(c) The Warden may not establish an excluded list of publications. This means the Warden shall review the individual publication prior to the rejection of that publication. Rejection of several issues of a subscription publication is not sufficient reason to reject the subscription publication in its entirety.”

questions.stem:
A Warden rejects a book for an inmate. The notice says only, "It is unacceptable."

What is wrong with the notice?
options: The notice must be approved by the Regional Director before it is sent
The notice must be sent to the inmate's family, not the inmate
The notice must give the reasons and refer to the specific article(s) or material(s) considered objectionable
The notice must be sent within 30 days, and may not list the objectionable material
questions.rationale:
The Warden shall promptly advise the inmate in writing of the decision and the reasons, with reference to the specific article(s) or material(s) considered objectionable.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.71: “(d) Where a publication is found unacceptable, the Warden shall promptly advise the inmate in writing of the decision and the reasons for it. The notice must contain reference to the specific article(s) or material(s) considered objectionable. The Warden shall permit the inmate an opportunity to review this material for purposes of filing an appeal under the Administrative Remedy Program unless such review may provide the inmate with information of a nature which is deemed to pose a threat or detriment to the security, good order or discipline of the institution or to encourage or instruct in criminal activity.”

questions.stem:
The victim of a violent crime calls an institution directly and asks to be notified when the inmate is released.

How should staff handle the request?
options: Refer the request to the U.S. Attorney in the district where the prosecution occurred for approval
Tell the victim to write to the Warden and to renew the request each year
Approve the request at once and enter the victim's name on the institution's release roster, with the approval of a supervisor on duty
Refer the victim to the local court clerk, who keeps the records of release notices
questions.rationale:
A victim or witness of a serious crime who wants release notification must make the request to the U.S. Attorney in the district of prosecution; requests received directly by the Bureau are referred there.

Source — 28 CFR § 551.152: “(a) A victim and/or witness of a serious crime who wants to be notified of a specific inmate's release must make this request to the United States Attorney in the district where the prosecution occurred. Requests for notification received by the Bureau of Prisons directly from a victim and/or witness will be referred to the U.S. Attorney in the district of prosecution for approval.”

questions.stem:
A Warden wants to recommend an inmate for a control unit because of the serious nature of his offense alone. The inmate has no incidents of violence or disruption in custody.

What does the regulation say?
options: The nature of the offense may never be considered under any circumstances
An inmate may not be considered solely on the nature of the crime, though it may be considered with other factors
The nature of the offense is enough if the inmate is a protection case
The nature of the offense alone is enough for a referral
questions.rationale:
An inmate may not be considered solely on the nature of the crime that resulted in his incarceration; it may be considered in combination with other factors.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.41: “(7) The nature of the offense for which committed. An inmate may not be considered solely on the nature of the crime which resulted in that inmate's incarceration; however, the nature of the crime may be considered in combination with other factor(s) as described in paragraph (b) of this section.”

questions.stem:
An inmate who has a documented major physical disability and has been involved in a disturbance is being considered for a control unit.

What does the regulation say?
options: The Warden may refer the inmate if the disturbance was serious enough
The Warden may refer the inmate if the physical disability is temporary, based on the information available at the time, when staff resources allow, according to the institution's local guidelines
The Warden may not refer an inmate who shows evidence of significant mental disorder or major physical disabilities documented in an evaluation or examination
The Warden may refer the inmate if the Regional Director approves
questions.rationale:
The Warden may not refer an inmate who shows evidence of significant mental disorder or major physical disabilities as documented in a mental health evaluation or physical examination.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.41: “(c) The Warden may not refer an inmate for placement in a control unit: (1) If the inmate shows evidence of significant mental disorder or major physical disabilities as documented in a mental health evaluation or a physical examination;”

questions.stem:
The control unit inmate asks if group religious services are allowed in the unit.

What does the regulation say?
options: Individual prayer or worship is allowed, but religious assemblies or group meetings are not allowed
No form of worship is allowed in a control unit
Group worship is allowed only if the chaplain leads it
Group worship is allowed on weekends in the unit dayroom, in most circumstances, once the shift lieutenant has been informed
questions.rationale:
Individual prayer and worship are allowed in a control unit, but religious assemblies or group meetings are not.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.46: “(j) Religion. Staff shall issue religious materials upon request, limited by security consideration and housekeeping rules in the unit. This material may come from an inmate's personal property or from the chaplain's office. The institutional chaplains shall make at least weekly visits to the control unit. While individual prayer and/or worship is allowed in a control unit, religious assemblies or group meetings are not allowed.”

questions.stem:
Officer Mbeki must restrain an inmate who is trying to harm himself by striking his head against a wall. The inmate has not threatened anyone else.

Does policy authorize applying restraints in this situation?
options: No; restraints may be used only after the Warden has given verbal approval
No; restraints may be used only to control an inmate who assaults another individual, provided that the action is documented, unless an emergency requires otherwise
Yes; staff are authorized to apply restraints to control an inmate who appears dangerous because he inflicts injury upon himself
Yes; but only if the inmate has first been placed on suicide watch
questions.rationale:
Staff may apply physical restraints to gain control of an inmate who appears dangerous because he assaults another, destroys government property, attempts suicide, inflicts injury on himself, or becomes violent or shows signs of imminent violence.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.20: “The Bureau of Prisons authorizes staff to use force only as a last alternative after all other reasonable efforts to resolve a situation have failed. When authorized, staff must use only that amount of force necessary to gain control of the inmate, to protect and ensure the safety of inmates, staff, and others, to prevent serious property damage and to ensure institution security and good order. Staff are authorized to apply physical restraints necessary to gain control of an inmate who appears to be dangerous because the inmate: (d) Inflicts injury upon self; or”

questions.stem:
An inmate is being escorted from his cell to the Special Housing Unit pending an investigation. He has been calm and cooperative, but the escorting officer wants to use handcuffs for the walk.

What does policy say about this precaution?
options: It is not allowed; handcuffs may be used only on inmates who have committed an assault, under the direction of the senior officer present, as long as the unit team is notified
It is not allowed; handcuffs may be used only after the inmate refuses a direct order
It is allowed only if the Warden has approved the use of handcuffs in writing
It is allowed; the rule does not restrict precautionary restraints, such as handcuffs when moving inmates to and from a cell or escorting an inmate to the SHU
questions.rationale:
The rule on application of restraints "does not restrict the use of restraints in situations requiring precautionary restraints, particularly in the movement or transfer of inmates (e.g., ... escorting an inmate to a Special Housing Unit pending investigation)."

Source — 28 CFR § 552.20: “This rule on application of restraints does not restrict the use of restraints in situations requiring precautionary restraints, particularly in the movement or transfer of inmates (e.g., the use of handcuffs in moving inmates to and from a cell in detention, escorting an inmate to a Special Housing Unit pending investigation, etc.).”

questions.stem:
Two officers are arguing over whether a cell extraction was necessary. One says it was routine because the inmate refused to hand over a razor.

Which statement matches the policy on exceptions to the force rules?
options: Exceptions are permitted whenever an inmate refuses a direct order from an officer
Exceptions are prohibited unless a sound correctional judgment would reasonably believe other action is a last resort to prevent serious injury or immediately endangering property damage
Exceptions are permitted whenever a supervisor on the scene approves
Exceptions are prohibited in every case, even to prevent serious injury
questions.rationale:
Any exception is prohibited except where the facts known to the staff member would warrant a person using sound correctional judgment to reasonably believe other action is necessary, as a last resort, to prevent serious physical injury or serious property damage that would immediately endanger safety.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.21: “(d) Exceptions. Any exception to this rule is prohibited, except where the facts and circumstances known to the staff member would warrant a person using sound correctional judgment to reasonably believe other action is necessary (as a last resort) to prevent serious physical injury, or serious property damage which would immediately endanger the safety of staff, inmates, or others.”

questions.stem:
An inmate in four-point restraints is dressed in a thin gown, and the room is cold. Staff say they will fix it "when someone has time." It is 40 minutes into the placement.

Which required element is missing?
options: A written consent signed by the inmate
A radio check by the Warden every hour
Clothing appropriate to the temperature
A Lieutenant's review every fifteen minutes
questions.rationale:
Under the four-point restraint procedures, inmates will be dressed in clothing appropriate to the temperature.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.24: “(b) Inmates will be dressed in clothing appropriate to the temperature.”

questions.stem:
A Lieutenant reviews an inmate in four-point restraints at the two-hour mark. The inmate is calm and requests release from the restraints.

What is the purpose of the review?
options: To decide whether the inmate should be disciplined for the behavior that led to the restraints, pending review by the appropriate official, provided that the action is documented
To decide whether the inmate should remain restrained until the end of the Warden's shift
To confirm that the restraint log has been signed by the inmate's case manager
To determine whether the restraints have had the required calming effect so the inmate may be released, completely or to lesser restraints, as soon as possible
questions.rationale:
A Lieutenant reviews every two hours to determine if the use of restraints has had the required calming effect "so that the inmate may be released from these restraints (completely or to lesser restraints) as soon as possible."

Source — 28 CFR § 552.24: “(e) A review of the inmate's placement in four-point restraints shall be made by a Lieutenant every two hours to determine if the use of restraints has had the required calming effect and so that the inmate may be released from these restraints (completely or to lesser restraints) as soon as possible. At every two-hour review, the inmate will be afforded the opportunity to use the toilet, unless the inmate is continuing to actively resist or becomes violent while being released from the restraints for this purpose.”

questions.stem:
Staff placed an inmate in four-point restraints on a bed. A nurse examined the inmate at the start and says she will not be back until the next day.

What does policy ordinarily require of qualified health personnel?
options: Visit the inmate at least twice during each eight-hour shift, after an initial assessment of breathing and circulation
Visit the inmate once every two hours, along with the Lieutenant's review
Visit the inmate only if the inmate asks for medical attention
Visit the inmate once at the start and once at the end of the placement
questions.rationale:
Health personnel initially assess breathing and response and circulation, and "ordinarily are to visit the inmate at least twice during each eight hour shift."

Source — 28 CFR § 552.24: “(f) When the inmate is placed in four-point restraints, qualified health personnel shall initially assess the inmate to ensure appropriate breathing and response (physical or verbal). Staff shall also ensure that the restraints have not restricted or impaired the inmate's circulation. When inmates are so restrained, qualified health personnel ordinarily are to visit the inmate at least twice during each eight hour shift. Use of four-point restraints beyond eight hours requires the supervision of qualified health personnel. Mental health and qualified health personnel may be asked for advice regarding the appropriate time for removal of the restraints.”

questions.stem:
An inmate is under close observation for suspected ingestion of contraband. He asks to keep his personal belongings and go to the recreation yard.

What does the regulation say?
options: He may keep all of his personal property but may not leave the cell for recreation, once the shift lieutenant has been informed, where the circumstances reasonably call for it, as long as the unit team is notified
He may keep his property and have yard recreation if the Captain is present
He ordinarily may not have personal property except legal and personal mail and a reasonable amount of legal materials, and ordinarily may not have recreation outside the cell
He may have recreation in the yard but may not keep any personal property
questions.rationale:
Under close observation the inmate ordinarily may not be allowed personal property except legal and personal mail and a reasonable amount of legal materials, and ordinarily may not be permitted recreation outside of the cell.
