Source — 28 CFR § 552.12: “(4) The inmate ordinarily may not be allowed personal property while under close observation status, except legal and personal mail and a reasonable amount of legal materials when requested. Personal hygiene items will be controlled by staff. (6) Due to security concerns, the inmate ordinarily may not be permitted recreation outside of the cell.”

questions.stem:
An inmate on close observation is lying under a blanket on his bed. His hands are out of sight beneath the blanket.

What does the regulation require?
options: He may cover his body as long as his hands are on his chest
He may cover his whole body if the room temperature is low and the light is dim, provided that the action is documented, for the duration of the incident
He may cover his body if he asks for permission from the officer every hour
When the inmate is lying on a bed he must lie on top of the mattress in full view, and if he uses cover, his hands must remain visible at all times
questions.rationale:
The inmate is required to lie on top of the mattress in full view, weather and room temperature permitting, and when it is necessary to use cover, hands must remain visible at all times.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.12: “(5) When the inmate is lying on a bed, the inmate shall be required to lie on top of the mattress in full view, weather and room temperature permitting. When necessary for the inmate to use cover, hands must remain visible at all times so that staff can observe any attempt to move contraband.”

questions.stem:
An inmate on close observation has been held for three days. The Segregation Review Official has not yet reviewed his status.

What does the regulation require?
options: The unit team must hold an informal meeting in the cell with the inmate
An inmate under close observation for as long as three days must be reviewed by the Segregation Review Official, and the initial review within three work days is a formal hearing
The Warden must review the case after seven days, with no earlier review required

The Captain must decide whether to continue the watch, with no formal hearing required, provided that the action is documented, with the approval of a supervisor on duty, unless an emergency requires otherwise
questions.rationale:
The status of an inmate under close observation for as long as three days must be reviewed by the Segregation Review Official, and the initial SRO review within three work days shall be a formal hearing.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.12: “(a) The length of close observation status will be determined on an individual basis. Ordinarily, the Captain, in consultation with qualified health personnel, shall determine when termination is appropriate. The status of an inmate under close observation for as long as three days must be reviewed by the Segregation Review Official according to the provisions in § 541.22(c) of this chapter, and the initial SRO review conducted within three work days shall be a formal hearing. Maintaining an inmate under close observation beyond seven days requires approval of the Warden, who makes this decision in consultation with the Captain and qualified health personnel.”

questions.stem:
A health services staff member is told to perform a digital search. The Warden is on vacation, and the Acting Warden has not been informed.

What is required for the digital or simple instrument search?
options: Approval of the Regional Director, and a reasonable belief on the part of the Segregation Review Official
Approval of the inmate's written consent, and a reasonable belief on the part of the officer
Approval of the Captain, and a reasonable belief on the part of the health services staff member
Approval of the Warden or Acting Warden, and a reasonable belief on the part of the Warden or Acting Warden that the inmate is concealing contraband
questions.rationale:
A digital or simple instrument search may be conducted only by designated qualified health personnel upon approval of the Warden or Acting Warden and only if the Warden or Acting Warden has reasonable belief that the inmate is concealing contraband.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.11: “(d) Digital or simple instrument search—inspection for contraband or any other foreign item in a body cavity of an inmate by use of fingers or simple instruments, such as an otoscope, tongue blade, short nasal speculum, and simple forceps. A digital or simple instrument search may be conducted only by designated qualified health personnel (for example, physicians, physician assistants, and nurses) upon approval of the Warden or Acting Warden and only if the Warden or Acting Warden has reasonable belief that an inmate is concealing contraband in or on his person. If located, the contraband or foreign item may be removed immediately by medical staff if such removal can easily be effected by use of fingers or the simple instruments referred to above. Staff shall document all digital and simple instrument searches and the reasons for the searches in the inmate's central file.”

questions.stem:
A nurse is about to perform a simple instrument search when she realizes the inmate has a condition making the search likely to cause injury.

What does the regulation say?
options: Staff may not conduct the search if it is likely to result in physical injury to the inmate
Staff may proceed if the inmate signs a written consent
Staff may proceed if the inmate is told of the risk beforehand
Staff may proceed if the Warden approves it again
questions.rationale:
Staff may not conduct a digital or simple instrument search if it is likely to result in physical injury to the inmate.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.11: “(2) Staff may not conduct a digital or simple instrument search if it is likely to result in physical injury to the inmate.”

questions.stem:
An officer seizes a government-issued tool that an inmate had taken from the maintenance shop. The tool may be needed as evidence in a criminal prosecution.

What does the regulation allow?
options: Staff must hold the tool in the inmate's property until his release
Staff must destroy the tool and document the destruction
Staff may retain the seized property as evidence instead of returning it to the issuing authority
Staff must return the tool to the shop immediately, without exception, in accordance with the posted schedule
questions.rationale:
Staff return government property to the issuing authority, "except where the item is needed as evidence for disciplinary action or criminal prosecution," in which case staff may retain it as evidence.

Source — 28 CFR § 553.13: “(1) Staff shall return to the institution's issuing authority any item of government property seized as contraband, except where the item is needed as evidence for disciplinary action or criminal prosecution. In such cases, staff may retain the seized property as evidence.”

questions.stem:
An inmate cannot show ownership of an item taken as contraband. A staff member wants to destroy it the same day to save storage space.

What must staff do first?
options: Destroy it at once, since the inmate could not show ownership
Mail it to the Warden's office for storage
Give it to the inmate's cellmate, who may claim it
Make reasonable efforts to identify the owner of the property before any decision to destroy it is made
questions.rationale:
If the inmate is unable to establish ownership, staff shall make reasonable efforts to identify the owner before any decision to destroy the property is made.

Source — 28 CFR § 553.13: “(iv) If the inmate is unable to establish ownership, staff shall make reasonable efforts to identify the owner of the property before any decision to destroy the property is made.”

questions.stem:
Staff seized contraband from an inmate, and disciplinary action against him is pending. A property officer asks when the contraband may be disposed of.

What does the regulation say?
options: Where disciplinary action is appropriate, staff shall delay disposition of the property until the action, including appeals, is complete
Staff may dispose of the property as soon as the incident report is written
Staff may dispose of the property after the UDC reviews the incident report
Staff may dispose of the property after thirty days regardless of the discipline, in accordance with the posted schedule, with the approval of a supervisor on duty
questions.rationale:
Where disciplinary action is appropriate, staff shall delay disposition of property until completion of such action (including appeals).

Source — 28 CFR § 553.13: “(vi) Where disciplinary action is appropriate, staff shall delay disposition of property until completion of such action (including appeals).”

questions.stem:
The UDC has found that an inmate committed the act charged. The inmate asks what he receives afterward.

What does the regulation say?
options: He receives a written copy only if he files a request within seven days, under the direction of the senior officer present
He receives only a verbal summary and may appeal to the UDC
He receives a copy of the DHO's decision and may appeal to the Warden
He receives a written copy of the UDC's decision and may appeal through the Administrative Remedy Program
questions.rationale:
The inmate receives a written copy of the UDC's decision and may appeal through the Administrative Remedy Program.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.7: “(h) Written report. You will receive a written copy of the UDC's decision following its review of the incident report. (i) Appeals. You may appeal the UDC's action(s) through the Administrative Remedy Program, 28 CFR part 542, subpart B.”

questions.stem:
An inmate escapes from custody while an incident report against him is pending. The UDC wants to know if the review can proceed.

What does the regulation say?
options: If the inmate escapes or is otherwise absent from custody, the UDC will conduct a review in his absence at the institution where he was last confined
The review is dismissed, since the inmate cannot respond
The review must be postponed until he is returned to custody
The review is conducted by the DHO at a location chosen by the Regional Director
questions.rationale:
If an inmate escapes or is otherwise absent from custody, the UDC will conduct a review in his absence at the institution where he was last confined.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.7: “(3) If you escape or are otherwise absent from custody, the UDC will conduct a review in your absence at the institution where you were last confined.”

questions.stem:
A DHO hearing is set, and the inmate's staff representative is out sick that day. The inmate wants to know his options.

What may the inmate do?
options: Require the DHO to appoint a fellow inmate as a representative
Select another staff representative, request that the hearing be postponed for a reasonable time, or proceed without a representative
Require the Warden to cancel the hearing and start the process over
Require the DHO to dismiss the charges until the representative returns
questions.rationale:
If the staff representative is not available, the inmate may select another, request a reasonable postponement, or proceed without one.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.8: “(3) How the staff representative may appear. Your staff representative may appear either in person or electronically (for example, by video or telephone conferencing) at the DHO's discretion. If your staff representative is not available for the scheduled hearing, you may either select another staff representative, request the hearing be postponed for a reasonable amount of time until your staff representative can appear, or proceed without a staff representative.”

questions.stem:
An inmate asks the DHO to call a witness who would repeat what two other witnesses have already said.

What may the DHO do?
options: Call the witness in every case, because a requested witness must always be heard, in most circumstances, once the shift lieutenant has been informed
Call the witness only if the inmate's staff representative agrees
Decline to call the witness, because requested witnesses may not appear if they would present repetitive evidence
Call the witness only if the Warden approves it in advance
questions.rationale:
Requested witnesses may not appear if, in the DHO's discretion, they are not reasonably available, their presence would jeopardize security, or they would present repetitive evidence.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.8: “(3) You or your staff representative may request witnesses appear at the hearing to testify on your behalf. Your requested witnesses may not appear if, in the DHO's discretion, they are not reasonably available, their presence at the hearing would jeopardize institution security, or they would present repetitive evidence.”

questions.stem:
An inmate in the SHU asks about showers and shaving.

What does the regulation say about personal hygiene?
options: He will ordinarily have the opportunity to shower and shave at least three times per week
He will ordinarily have the opportunity to shower daily but not to shave
He will ordinarily have the opportunity to shower and shave once per week
He will ordinarily have the opportunity to shower and shave only on request
questions.rationale:
SHU inmates have access to a wash basin and toilet and will ordinarily have an opportunity to shower and shave at least three times per week.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.31: “(f) Personal hygiene. You will have access to a wash basin and toilet. You will receive personal items necessary to maintain an acceptable level of personal hygiene, for example, toilet tissue, soap, toothbrush and cleanser, shaving utensils, etc. You will ordinarily have an opportunity to shower and shave at least three times per week. You will have access to hair care services as necessary.”

questions.stem:
An inmate in the SHU is told that exercise periods can never be reduced. The Warden wants to deny exercise to an inmate whose use of exercise is a threat to safety.

What does the regulation allow?
options: The Warden may deny exercise periods for a month at a time for any reason
The Warden may deny exercise periods for a week at a time if the inmate's use of exercise threatens safety, security, and orderly operation
The Warden may never deny exercise periods under any circumstances
The Warden may deny exercise periods only if the DHO orders it as a sanction, under the direction of the senior officer present, as long as no other inmate is affected
questions.rationale:
An inmate can be denied exercise periods for a week at a time by order of the Warden if it is determined that use of exercise privileges threatens safety, security, and orderly operation, or public safety.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.31: “(g) Exercise. You will receive the opportunity to exercise outside your individual quarters at least five hours per week, ordinarily on different days in one-hour periods. You can be denied these exercise periods for a week at a time by order of the Warden if it is determined that your use of exercise privileges threatens safety, security, and orderly operation of a correctional facility, or public safety.”

questions.stem:
A cell in the SHU is designed for one occupant, and the Warden wants to house two inmates there because of overcrowding.

What does the regulation say about cell occupancy?
options: Quarters may never house more than one occupant under any circumstances, in most circumstances, as long as the unit team is notified, based on the information available at the time
Quarters may house any number of occupants if the DHO approves
Quarters ordinarily house only the number of occupants for which they are designed, but the Warden may authorize more as long as adequate standards can be maintained
Quarters may house more occupants only if the inmates agree in writing
questions.rationale:
Living quarters will ordinarily house only the amount of occupants for which they are designed; the Warden may authorize more so long as adequate standards can be maintained.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.31: “(b) Cell Occupancy. Your living quarters will ordinarily house only the amount of occupants for which it is designed. The Warden, however, may authorize more occupants so long as adequate standards can be maintained.”

questions.stem:
A facility post notice says that "inmate-on-inmate sexual activity is permitted if no one complains." The PREA compliance manager is asked to review it.

What does the standard say about inmate sexual activity?
options: An agency may prohibit all sexual activity between inmates and discipline them, but may not deem non-coerced activity to be sexual abuse
An agency must permit sexual activity between inmates if both consent
An agency must deem all sexual activity between inmates to be sexual abuse, unless an emergency requires otherwise, unless local procedures say otherwise
An agency may not prohibit any sexual activity between inmates
questions.rationale:
An agency may, in its discretion, prohibit all sexual activity between inmates and discipline them for it, but may not deem such activity sexual abuse if it determines that the activity is not coerced.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.78: “(g) An agency may, in its discretion, prohibit all sexual activity between inmates and may discipline inmates for such activity. An agency may not, however, deem such activity to constitute sexual abuse if it determines that the activity is not coerced.”

questions.stem:
An inmate has a physical relationship with a staff member and says it was consensual. A supervisor wants to discipline the inmate.

What does the standard say about disciplining the inmate?
options: The agency may always discipline the inmate for sexual contact with staff
The agency may discipline an inmate for sexual contact with staff only upon a finding that the staff member did not consent to such contact
The agency may discipline the inmate only if the staff member reports it within 24 hours
The agency may never discipline the inmate for sexual contact with staff
questions.rationale:
The agency may discipline an inmate for sexual contact with staff only upon a finding that the staff member did not consent to such contact.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.78: “(e) The agency may discipline an inmate for sexual contact with staff only upon a finding that the staff member did not consent to such contact.”

questions.stem:
A transgender inmate has been placed in housing without any review in the past year. She tells staff she feels unsafe.

What does the standard say about her views?
options: The inmate's views are considered only if a medical practitioner agrees with them
The inmate's views are not considered, since housing is decided by classification alone
A transgender or intersex inmate's own views with respect to his or her safety shall be given serious consideration
The inmate's views are considered only at the annual review
questions.rationale:
A transgender or intersex inmate's own views with respect to his or her own safety shall be given serious consideration.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.42: “(e) A transgender or intersex inmate's own views with respect to his or her own safety shall be given serious consideration.”

questions.stem:
A male officer must supervise a female inmate who is showering. The unit has no privacy panels.

What do the policies and procedures have to enable?
options: Inmates must be able to shower only when staff of the same gender are on duty

Inmates must be able to shower only if they cover their bodies with a robe provided by staff, as long as the unit team is notified, where the circumstances reasonably call for it, in most circumstances
Inmates must be able to shower without any staff present, even in an emergency

Inmates must be able to shower, perform bodily functions, and change clothing without nonmedical staff of the opposite gender viewing their breasts, buttocks, or genitalia, except in exigent circumstances or when viewing is incidental to routine cell checks
questions.rationale:
Facilities must implement policies that enable inmates to shower, perform bodily functions, and change clothing without nonmedical staff of the opposite gender viewing their breasts, buttocks, or genitalia, except in exigent circumstances or when incidental to routine cell checks.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.15: “(d) The facility shall implement policies and procedures that enable inmates to shower, perform bodily functions, and change clothing without nonmedical staff of the opposite gender viewing their breasts, buttocks, or genitalia, except in exigent circumstances or when such viewing is incidental to routine cell checks. Such policies and procedures shall require staff of the opposite gender to announce their presence when entering an inmate housing unit.”

questions.stem:
A PREA coordinator asks how the agency should record the dispositions of its investigations when reporting to inmates.

Which classification applies when an investigation finds insufficient evidence to determine whether the event occurred?
options: Unsubstantiated
Substantiated
Unfounded
Exigent
questions.rationale:
An unsubstantiated allegation is one that was investigated and produced insufficient evidence to make a final determination whether or not the event occurred.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.5: “Unsubstantiated allegation means an allegation that was investigated and the investigation produced insufficient evidence to make a final determination as to whether or not the event occurred.”

questions.stem:
Following an inmate's allegation of sexual abuse by another inmate, the alleged abuser is later convicted of a related charge. The agency asks whether it must tell the victim.

What does the standard say?
options: The agency shall inform the alleged victim only of an indictment, not of a conviction
The agency shall inform the alleged victim whenever the alleged abuser has been indicted or convicted on a charge related to sexual abuse within the facility
The agency shall not inform the alleged victim of any court proceedings
The agency shall inform the alleged victim only if the victim asks in writing each month
questions.rationale:
Following an allegation of sexual abuse by another inmate, the agency shall inform the alleged victim whenever it learns the alleged abuser has been indicted or convicted on a related charge within the facility, and all notifications must be documented.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.73: “(d) Following an inmate's allegation that he or she has been sexually abused by another inmate, the agency shall subsequently inform the alleged victim whenever: (1) The agency learns that the alleged abuser has been indicted on a charge related to sexual abuse within the facility; or (2) The agency learns that the alleged abuser has been convicted on a charge related to sexual abuse within the facility.”

questions.stem:
Medical staff learn that an inmate disclosed prior sexual victimization from a time before he was incarcerated. A supervisor wants the practitioner to report the information to the facility's investigators immediately.

What does the standard say about such reports?
options: Practitioners may never report prior victimization, even if the inmate is a minor
Practitioners must report all prior victimization to investigators without the inmate's consent, unless an emergency requires otherwise, pending review by the appropriate official
Practitioners must obtain informed consent before reporting prior victimization that did not occur in an institutional setting, unless the inmate is under 18
Practitioners may report only if the inmate names the person who abused him
questions.rationale:
Medical and mental health practitioners shall obtain informed consent from inmates before reporting information about prior sexual victimization that did not occur in an institutional setting, unless the inmate is under the age of 18.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.81: “(e) Medical and mental health practitioners shall obtain informed consent from inmates before reporting information about prior sexual victimization that did not occur in an institutional setting, unless the inmate is under the age of 18.”

questions.stem:
A prison is using a screening tool that asks only about the inmate's age and builds. A reviewer says the tool must include more.

Which of the following must intake screening consider at a minimum?
options: Whether the inmate has family nearby, and whether he has any children, as long as the unit team is notified, subject to the Warden's discretion
Whether the inmate is employed, and whether he has a driver's license
Whether the inmate has a high school diploma, and whether he can read
Whether the inmate has a mental, physical, or developmental disability, and whether he has previously been incarcerated
questions.rationale:
The minimum criteria include disability, age, physical build, prior incarceration, whether the criminal history is exclusively nonviolent, prior sex offense convictions, perceived LGBTI identity, prior victimization, the inmate's own perception of vulnerability, and civil immigration detention.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.41: “(1) Whether the inmate has a mental, physical, or developmental disability; (4) Whether the inmate has previously been incarcerated;”

questions.stem:
An inmate detained solely for civil immigration purposes asks how to report abuse to someone outside the agency.

What does the standard require the agency to provide?
options: Information on how to contact relevant consular officials and relevant officials at the Department of Homeland Security
Information on how to contact the Warden and the PREA coordinator only
Information on how to contact the inmate's former employer and the local police
Information on how to contact the sentencing judge and the U.S. Attorney
questions.rationale:
Inmates detained solely for civil immigration purposes shall be provided information on how to contact relevant consular officials and relevant officials at the Department of Homeland Security.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.51: “(b) The agency shall also provide at least one way for inmates to report abuse or harassment to a public or private entity or office that is not part of the agency, and that is able to receive and immediately forward inmate reports of sexual abuse and sexual harassment to agency officials, allowing the inmate to remain anonymous upon request. Inmates detained solely for civil immigration purposes shall be provided information on how to contact relevant consular officials and relevant officials at the Department of Homeland Security.”

questions.stem:
A staff member wants to report abuse of an inmate but fears coworkers will learn who made the report.

What does the standard require?
options: The agency shall require staff to report in person to the Warden
The agency shall provide a method for staff to privately report sexual abuse and sexual harassment of inmates
The agency shall keep staff reports secret even from the investigators, with the approval of a supervisor on duty
The agency shall not allow staff to report privately
questions.rationale:
The agency shall provide a method for staff to privately report sexual abuse and sexual harassment of inmates.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.51: “(d) The agency shall provide a method for staff to privately report sexual abuse and sexual harassment of inmates.”

questions.stem:
A facility takes weeks to extend a deadline in a grievance alleging sexual abuse and does not tell the inmate. The agency asks what extension the standard allows.

What does the standard permit?
options: An extension of up to 90 days, with notice only to the inmate's attorney
An extension of up to 20 days, with verbal notice to the inmate
An extension of up to 70 days if the normal period is insufficient, with written notice to the inmate and a date by which a decision will be made
An extension of any length, with notice only to the PREA coordinator
questions.rationale:
The agency may claim an extension of time to respond, of up to 70 days, if the normal period is insufficient, and shall notify the inmate in writing and provide a date by which a decision will be made.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.52: “(3) The agency may claim an extension of time to respond, of up to 70 days, if the normal time period for response is insufficient to make an appropriate decision. The agency shall notify the inmate in writing of any such extension and provide a date by which a decision will be made.”

questions.stem:
A facility must decide whether to include protective custody in involuntary segregated housing for an inmate at high risk of being victimized. The inmate asks whether he will lose access to his work assignment.

What does the standard say?
options: Inmates in such housing keep work but lose education, with no need for documentation
Inmates in such housing lose all programs, privileges, education, and work opportunities
Inmates in such housing keep access only if the Warden approves each program in advance
Inmates in such housing shall have access to programs, privileges, education, and work opportunities to the extent possible, and any limits must be documented with the reasons
questions.rationale:
Inmates in segregated housing for this purpose shall have access to programs, privileges, education, and work opportunities to the extent possible; if restricted, the facility documents the opportunities limited, the duration, and the reasons.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.43: “(b) Inmates placed in segregated housing for this purpose shall have access to programs, privileges, education, and work opportunities to the extent possible. If the facility restricts access to programs, privileges, education, or work opportunities, the facility shall document: (1) The opportunities that have been limited; (2) The duration of the limitation; and (3) The reasons for such limitations.”

questions.stem:
The agency is drafting its staffing plan and a manager suggests skipping an annual review because the facility is meeting its goals.

What does the standard require?
options: Whenever necessary, but no less frequently than once each year, the agency assesses and documents whether adjustments are needed to the staffing plan, video monitoring, and resources
The agency assesses the staffing plan only when the Warden requests a review
The agency assesses the staffing plan once every five years with the PREA coordinator

The agency assesses the staffing plan only when an incident of sexual abuse is substantiated, subject to the Warden's discretion, in accordance with the posted schedule, as long as the unit team is notified
questions.rationale:
The agency shall assess, determine, and document whether adjustments are needed to the staffing plan, the deployment of video monitoring, and the resources available, whenever necessary but no less frequently than once each year.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.13: “(c) Whenever necessary, but no less frequently than once each year, for each facility the agency operates, in consultation with the PREA coordinator required by § 115.11, the agency shall assess, determine, and document whether adjustments are needed to:”

questions.stem:
A pretrial inmate is taking a medication that makes him drowsy. His trial begins next week.

What must staff do?
options: Stop the medication until the trial is over, to protect the inmate's rights
Keep the information in the medical file and give it to the court only on request, unless an emergency requires otherwise, subject to the Warden's discretion
Tell the inmate's attorney only, and leave the court uninformed
Advise the court, through the U.S. Marshal, of medication the pretrial inmate receives which may alter his courtroom behavior
questions.rationale:
Staff shall advise the court, through the U.S. Marshal, of medication the pretrial inmate receives which may alter the inmate's courtroom behavior.

Source — 28 CFR § 551.114: “(b) Staff shall advise the court, through the U.S. Marshal, of medication the pretrial inmate receives which may alter the inmate's courtroom behavior.”

questions.stem:
A pretrial inmate dies unexpectedly in the infirmary. A supervisor asks who must be notified.

Which group does the regulation list?
options: The committing court, the U.S. Marshal, the U.S. Attorney's Office, the inmate's attorney of record, and the designated family member or next of kin
The Regional Director, the inmate's cellmates, and the media
The Bureau's Public Information Officer and the inmate's former employer, after a supervisor has reviewed the matter, during normal operating hours, for the duration of the incident
The sentencing judge, the Warden's staff, and the local coroner
questions.rationale:
In the event of serious illness or death of a pretrial inmate, staff notify the committing court, U.S. Marshal, U.S. Attorney's Office, the inmate's attorney of record, and the designated family member or next of kin.

Source — 28 CFR § 551.114: “(c) In event of serious illness or death of a pretrial inmate, staff shall notify the committing court, U.S. Marshal, U.S. Attorney's Office, the inmate's attorney of record, and the designated family member or next of kin.”

questions.stem:
An inmate is transferred to another institution as a reward for good adjustment and had accumulated vacation credit. He asks whether it is lost.

What may the Warden or designee do?
options: Authorize him to accumulate vacation credit when he is transferred for the benefit of the government or because of favorable adjustment
Cancel all accumulated vacation credit upon any transfer
Pay out the credit in cash on the day of the transfer
Require him to restart vacation credit at zero in all circumstances, subject to the Warden's discretion, as long as the unit team is notified
questions.rationale:
The Warden or designee may authorize an inmate to accumulate vacation credit when he is transferred for the benefit of the government or because of favorable adjustment (custody reduction).

Source — 28 CFR § 545.27: “(c) The Warden or designee may authorize an inmate to accumulate vacation credit when: (1) The inmate is transferred to another institution for the benefit of the government or because of the inmate's favorable adjustment (custody reduction); or”

questions.stem:
A psychiatrist proposes to hospitalize an inmate involuntarily for psychiatric treatment under Bureau authority (not under a court commitment). The inmate asks what protections he has.

Which protection does the regulation provide?
options: Seven days' written notice and the right to select the psychiatrist who conducts the hearing, under the direction of the senior officer present, based on the information available at the time
No hearing, since the examiner's finding is final in all cases
24-hours advance written notice of the hearing, the right to appear, to present evidence, to have a staff representative, and to request witnesses
Verbal notice at the start of the hearing and no right to a staff representative
questions.rationale:
The inmate must be provided 24-hours advance written notice of the hearing and informed of the right to appear, present evidence, have a staff representative, request witnesses, and request that witnesses be questioned.

Source — 28 CFR § 549.45: “(2) The inmate must be provided 24-hours advance written notice of the date, time, place, and purpose, of the hearing, including an explanation of the reasons for the proposal to hospitalize the inmate for psychiatric care or treatment. (3) The inmate must be informed of the right to appear at the hearing, to present evidence, to have a staff representative, to request witnesses, and to request that witnesses be questioned by the staff representative or by the person conducting the hearing. If the inmate does not request a staff representative, or requests a staff representative with insufficient experience or education, or one who is not reasonably available, the institution mental health division administrator must appoint a qualified staff representative.”

questions.stem:
A psychiatrist who has been treating an inmate is asked to also preside over the hearing on involuntary hospitalization.

What does the regulation say?
options: The hearing may be conducted by the attending psychiatrist if the inmate agrees, pending review by the appropriate official, where the circumstances reasonably call for it
The hearing may be conducted by any physician in the institution
The hearing may be conducted by the Warden as the final decision maker
The hearing is to be conducted by a psychiatrist other than the attending psychiatrist, who is not currently involved in the diagnosis or treatment of the inmate
questions.rationale:
The hearing is to be conducted by a psychiatrist other than the attending psychiatrist, and who is not currently involved in the diagnosis or treatment of the inmate.

Source — 28 CFR § 549.45: “(4) The hearing is to be conducted by a psychiatrist other than the attending psychiatrist, and who is not currently involved in the diagnosis or treatment of the inmate.”

questions.stem:
After a hearing on involuntary hospitalization, an inmate wants to appeal. He asks how long he has.

What does the regulation require?
options: The inmate's appeal, which may be handwritten, must be submitted within 24 hours after receipt of the hearing officer's report, and hospitalization must not occur before the administrator decides
The inmate may not appeal, but may ask for a second hearing before the same psychiatrist
The inmate's appeal must be submitted within 30 days, and hospitalization may proceed during the appeal
The inmate's appeal must be typed and submitted within 7 days, and hospitalization may occur at once
questions.rationale:
The inmate's appeal, which may be handwritten, must be submitted within 24 hours after receipt of the report, and if he appeals, hospitalization must not occur before the administrator issues a decision.

Source — 28 CFR § 549.45: “(8) The psychiatrist must prepare a written report regarding the initial decision. The inmate must be promptly provided a copy of the initial decision report, and informed that he/she may appeal it to the institution's mental health division administrator. The inmate's appeal, which may be handwritten, must be submitted within 24 hours after receipt of the hearing officer's report. Upon request of the inmate, the staff representative will assist the inmate in preparing and submitting the appeal. (9) If the inmate appeals the initial decision, hospitalization must not occur before the administrator issues a decision on the appeal. The inmate's appeal will ordinarily be reviewed by the administrator or his designee within 24 hours of its submission. The administrator will review the initial decision and ensure that the inmate received all necessary procedural protections, and that the justification for hospitalization is appropriate.”

questions.stem:
An inmate's friend persuades him to help hide a weapon in the yard but is caught before the weapon is hidden. The inmate says he should not be charged because the act was never completed.

How does the regulation treat aiding, attempting, abetting, or planning a prohibited act?
options: It is treated as a separate violation in the Low severity category
It is treated as a lesser violation than committing the act
It is not a prohibited act unless the act is completed
It is treated the same as committing the act itself
questions.rationale:
Aiding, attempting, abetting, or making plans to commit any of the prohibited acts is treated the same as committing the act itself.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.3: “(a) Prohibited acts. The list of prohibited acts are divided into four separate categories based on severity: Greatest; High; Moderate; and Low. We describe the prohibited acts in Table 1—Prohibited Acts and Available Sanctions. Aiding, attempting, abetting, or making plans to commit any of the prohibited acts is treated the same as committing the act itself.”

questions.stem:
During the investigation of an incident report, the investigator learns the matter may be referred for criminal prosecution.

What does the regulation say about the staff investigation?
options: The staff investigation of the incident report may be suspended before requesting the inmate's statement if it is being investigated for possible criminal prosecution
The staff investigation must continue without any change
The staff investigation must be completed within 24 hours
The staff investigation is cancelled and the incident report is removed from the file, pending review by the appropriate official, provided that the action is documented
questions.rationale:
The staff investigation of the incident report may be suspended before requesting the inmate's statement if it is being investigated for possible criminal prosecution.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.5: “(2) Statement: When the investigator asks for your statement, you may give an explanation of the incident, request any witnesses be interviewed, or request that other evidence be obtained and reviewed. However, the staff investigation of the incident report may be suspended before requesting your statement if it is being investigated for possible criminal prosecution.”

questions.stem:
A UDC review is delayed because the matter has been referred for a possible criminal prosecution. The inmate complains about the delay.

What does the regulation allow?
options: UDC review must be handled by the DHO instead of the UDC
UDC review of the incident report may be suspended if it is being investigated for possible criminal prosecution
UDC review must be completed within five work days in every case, unless local procedures say otherwise, subject to the Warden's discretion
UDC review is cancelled when a criminal referral is made
questions.rationale:
The UDC will ordinarily review within five work days, but review may also be suspended if the matter is being investigated for possible criminal prosecution.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.7: “(c) Timing. The UDC will ordinarily review the incident report within five work days after it is issued, not counting the day it was issued, weekends, and holidays. UDC review of the incident report may also be suspended if it is being investigated for possible criminal prosecution.”

questions.stem:
An inmate asks to appear before the UDC by video from a different building instead of in person.

What does the regulation say?
options: An inmate may appear only in person
An inmate may appear electronically only if he is in a Special Housing Unit
An inmate may appear either in person or electronically (for example, by video or telephone conferencing) at the UDC's discretion
An inmate may appear electronically only if the Warden is also present
questions.rationale:
The inmate may appear either in person or electronically (for example, by video or telephone conferencing) at the UDC's discretion, except during deliberations or when his presence would jeopardize security.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.7: “(d) Inmate appearance. You are permitted to appear before the UDC during its review of the incident report, except during UDC deliberations or when your presence would jeopardize institution security, at the UDC's discretion. Also: (1) You may appear either in person or electronically (for example, by video or telephone conferencing) at the UDC's discretion.”

questions.stem:
An inmate wants to attend the DHO's deliberations after the evidence has been presented.

What does the regulation say?
options: The inmate has the right to be present for all deliberations
The inmate may attend deliberations only if his staff representative asks, unless an emergency requires otherwise, once the shift lieutenant has been informed
The inmate may attend deliberations if the Warden is also present
The inmate's appearance may be prohibited during DHO deliberations or when his presence would jeopardize institution security, at the DHO's discretion
questions.rationale:
The inmate's appearance may be prohibited during DHO deliberations or when his presence would jeopardize institution security, at the DHO's discretion.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.8: “(2) Your appearance may be prohibited during DHO deliberations or when your presence would jeopardize institution security, at the DHO's discretion.”

questions.stem:
An inmate asks the DHO to require every adverse witness to testify in person, even though their statements are already summarized in the incident report.

What does the regulation say?
options: The DHO need not call witnesses adverse to the inmate if their testimony is adequately summarized in the incident report or other investigation materials
The DHO must call every adverse witness on request
The DHO must call adverse witnesses only if the inmate pays for their travel, for the duration of the incident, in accordance with the posted schedule, pending review by the appropriate official
The DHO must call adverse witnesses only if the Warden approves
questions.rationale:
The DHO will call witnesses with directly relevant information who are reasonably available, but need not call adverse witnesses whose testimony is adequately summarized in the incident report or other materials.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.8: “(2) The DHO will call witnesses who have information directly relevant to the charge(s) and who are reasonably available. However, the DHO need not call witnesses adverse to you if their testimony is adequately summarized in the incident report or other investigation materials.”

questions.stem:
An inmate's requested witness cannot attend the DHO hearing because he has been transferred to another institution.

What can be done?
options: The hearing must proceed, and the witness's account is ignored
Written statements can be requested by either the DHO or the staff representative and considered during the hearing
The hearing must be cancelled until the witness returns
The inmate must pay for the witness to travel to the hearing
questions.rationale:
If requested witnesses are unavailable to appear, written statements can be requested by either the DHO or the staff representative and considered during the hearing.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.8: “(4) If your requested witnesses are unavailable to appear, written statements can be requested by either the DHO or staff representative. The written statements can then be considered during the DHO's hearing.”

questions.stem:
The DHO finds that an inmate committed a prohibited act. The inmate asks what sanctions the DHO can impose.

What does the regulation say?
options: The DHO can impose sanctions only with the Warden's written approval, unless local procedures say otherwise
The DHO can impose only the sanctions the UDC could impose
The DHO can impose any of the available sanctions listed in Tables 1 and 2
The DHO can impose only loss of good conduct time
questions.rationale:
If the inmate committed a prohibited act, the DHO can impose any of the available sanctions listed in Tables 1 and 2, including those the UDC cannot impose.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.8: “(g) Sanctions. If you committed a prohibited act(s), the DHO can impose any of the available sanctions listed in Tables 1 and 2.”

questions.stem:
An inmate asks to be placed in administrative detention because other inmates have threatened to harm him unless he engages in sexual activity.

Which protection-case circumstance fits?
options: Staff concern that the inmate has not been classified
Victim of inmate assault or threats, including threats of harm unless the inmate engages in sexual activity
Pending transfer to a state institution
Inmate refusal to enter general population for no stated reason, for the duration of the incident, in most circumstances
questions.rationale:
A protection case includes an inmate who was the victim of an assault or is being threatened by other inmates, including threats of harm unless he engages in sexual activity.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.27: “(a) Victim of inmate assault or threats. You were the victim of an inmate assault, or are being threatened by other inmates, including threats of harm if you do not act in a certain way, for example, threats of harm unless you engage in sexual activity.”

questions.stem:
A Special Housing Unit officer wants to give an inmate only a thin sheet and no pillow to discourage him from staying in the SHU long.

What does the regulation require?
options: The inmate will receive a mattress only, and bedding after seven days
The inmate will receive bedding only in cold weather and only upon request
The inmate will receive linens only if he is in administrative detention
The inmate will receive a mattress, blankets, a pillow, and linens for sleeping, with necessary opportunities to exchange linens
questions.rationale:
Living conditions in the SHU must meet or exceed standards for healthy and humane treatment, and inmates receive a mattress, blankets, a pillow, and linens, with necessary opportunities to exchange linens.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.31: “(d) Bedding. You will receive a mattress, blankets, a pillow, and linens for sleeping. You will receive necessary opportunities to exchange linens.”

questions.stem:
A supervisor asks whether SHU staff must monitor inmates, and who counts as monitoring staff.

What does the regulation say?
options: Inmates will be monitored by staff assigned to the SHU, including program and unit team staff
Inmates will be monitored only by the Captain's office
Inmates will be monitored only by cameras, with no staff presence, with the approval of a supervisor on duty
Inmates will be monitored by other inmates assigned to the SHU
questions.rationale:
In the SHU, inmates are monitored by staff assigned to the SHU, including program and unit team staff.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.31: “(m) Staff monitoring. You will be monitored by staff assigned to the SHU, including program and unit team staff.”

questions.stem:
A volunteer teaching art classes is asked how detailed the PREA training must be.

What does the standard say about the level and type of training?
options: It is optional for volunteers who work fewer than ten hours a week
It is based on the services provided and the level of contact with inmates, but all volunteers and contractors with contact must be notified of the zero-tolerance policy and informed how to report

It is the same for every volunteer and contractor, regardless of contact, after a supervisor has reviewed the matter, under the direction of the senior officer present, for the duration of the incident
It is required only for contractors, not for volunteers
questions.rationale:
The level and type of training depends on services provided and contact with inmates, but all volunteers and contractors who have contact with inmates shall be notified of the zero-tolerance policy and informed how to report incidents.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.32: “(b) The level and type of training provided to volunteers and contractors shall be based on the services they provide and level of contact they have with inmates, but all volunteers and contractors who have contact with inmates shall be notified of the agency's zero-tolerance policy regarding sexual abuse and sexual harassment and informed how to report such incidents.”

questions.stem:
An administrative investigation concludes that an inmate was abused. The report mentions only the testimony of the alleged victim and does not discuss staff actions.

What must administrative investigations include?
options: A summary of the inmate's disciplinary history only
A recommendation for the inmate's transfer to another institution, as determined by the shift supervisor, pending review by the appropriate official, for the duration of the incident
A decision on the staff member's pay and benefits
An effort to determine whether staff actions or failures to act contributed to the abuse, documented in a written report describing the evidence, credibility assessments, and findings
questions.rationale:
Administrative investigations shall include an effort to determine whether staff actions or failures to act contributed to the abuse and be documented in written reports describing the physical and testimonial evidence, credibility reasoning, and investigative facts and findings.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.71: “(f) Administrative investigations: (1) Shall include an effort to determine whether staff actions or failures to act contributed to the abuse; and (2) Shall be documented in written reports that include a description of the physical and testimonial evidence, the reasoning behind credibility assessments, and investigative facts and findings.”

questions.stem:
An investigator wants to compel an interview of a suspect before talking to the prosecutor, even though the evidence appears to support a criminal case.

What should the investigator do first?
options: Consult with prosecutors as to whether compelled interviews may be an obstacle to subsequent criminal prosecution
Ask the Warden to decide whether to compel the interview
Conduct the compelled interview, and then consult with prosecutors, where the circumstances reasonably call for it, according to the institution's local guidelines
Skip the interview and close the investigation
questions.rationale:
When the quality of evidence appears to support criminal prosecution, the agency shall conduct compelled interviews only after consulting with prosecutors as to whether compelled interviews may be an obstacle.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.71: “(d) When the quality of evidence appears to support criminal prosecution, the agency shall conduct compelled interviews only after consulting with prosecutors as to whether compelled interviews may be an obstacle for subsequent criminal prosecution.”

questions.stem:
An investigation substantiates conduct that appears to be criminal.

What does the standard require?
options: Such allegations are handled only through administrative discipline
Substantiated allegations of conduct that appears to be criminal shall be referred for prosecution
Such allegations are referred for prosecution only if the victim asks
Such allegations are held until the abuser's sentence ends
questions.rationale:
Substantiated allegations of conduct that appears to be criminal shall be referred for prosecution.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.71: “(h) Substantiated allegations of conduct that appears to be criminal shall be referred for prosecution.”

questions.stem:
An outside agency is investigating a sexual abuse allegation inside the facility. The Warden tells staff not to share anything with the outside investigators.

What does the standard require?
options: The facility shall cooperate but shall not seek updates on the progress
The facility shall refuse to cooperate with outside investigators
The facility shall cooperate with outside investigators and endeavor to remain informed about the progress of the investigation
The facility shall cooperate only if the investigators obtain the Warden's approval, after a supervisor has reviewed the matter, as long as the unit team is notified
questions.rationale:
When outside agencies investigate sexual abuse, the facility shall cooperate with outside investigators and shall endeavor to remain informed about the progress of the investigation.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.71: “(l) When outside agencies investigate sexual abuse, the facility shall cooperate with outside investigators and shall endeavor to remain informed about the progress of the investigation.”

questions.stem:
A staff member is terminated for violating the agency's sexual abuse policies, and the incident appears criminal.

To whom must the termination be reported?
options: The staff member's former employers only
The inmate's family and the local newspaper
No one outside the agency, since it is a personnel matter
Law enforcement agencies, unless the activity was clearly not criminal, and any relevant licensing bodies
questions.rationale:
All terminations for violations of agency sexual abuse or sexual harassment policies, or resignations by staff who would have been terminated, shall be reported to law enforcement agencies, unless the activity was clearly not criminal, and to any relevant licensing bodies.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.76: “(d) All terminations for violations of agency sexual abuse or sexual harassment policies, or resignations by staff who would have been terminated if not for their resignation, shall be reported to law enforcement agencies, unless the activity was clearly not criminal, and to any relevant licensing bodies.”

questions.stem:
The agency considers disciplining a staff member for repeated unwelcome comments of a sexual nature to an inmate. A manager says the sanction should always be the same for every employee.

What does the standard say about these sanctions?
options: They shall be commensurate with the nature and circumstances of the acts, the staff member's disciplinary history, and sanctions imposed for comparable offenses by other staff with similar histories
They shall be the same for every staff member, whatever the circumstances, as determined by the shift supervisor, during normal operating hours, for the duration of the incident
They shall be limited to a written warning for a first offense
They shall be decided by the inmate who was harassed
questions.rationale:
Disciplinary sanctions for violations other than actually engaging in sexual abuse shall be commensurate with the nature and circumstances of the acts, the staff member's disciplinary history, and sanctions imposed for comparable offenses by other staff with similar histories.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.76: “(c) Disciplinary sanctions for violations of agency policies relating to sexual abuse or sexual harassment (other than actually engaging in sexual abuse) shall be commensurate with the nature and circumstances of the acts committed, the staff member's disciplinary history, and the sanctions imposed for comparable offenses by other staff with similar histories.”

questions.stem:
An inmate who committed inmate-on-inmate sexual abuse is being sanctioned. The facility offers counseling designed to address the reasons for the abuse.

What does the standard say about the counseling?
options: The facility shall offer counseling only after the inmate's release
The facility shall consider whether to require the offending inmate to participate in such interventions as a condition of access to programming or other benefits

The facility shall not offer counseling to an inmate who has been sanctioned, as long as no other inmate is affected, in accordance with the posted schedule, according to the institution's local guidelines
The facility shall require counseling for every inmate in all cases
questions.rationale:
If the facility offers therapy, counseling, or other interventions, it shall consider whether to require the offending inmate to participate as a condition of access to programming or other benefits.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.78: “(d) If the facility offers therapy, counseling, or other interventions designed to address and correct underlying reasons or motivations for the abuse, the facility shall consider whether to require the offending inmate to participate in such interventions as a condition of access to programming or other benefits.”

questions.stem:
Staff find that an inmate-on-inmate sexual abuse allegation is substantiated by an administrative finding.

What does the standard require?
options: Inmates are not subject to sanctions, since the facility is responsible, according to the institution's local guidelines, unless an emergency requires otherwise
Inmates are subject to sanctions without any formal process
Inmates are subject to disciplinary sanctions pursuant to a formal disciplinary process following an administrative finding or a criminal finding of guilt
Inmates are subject to sanctions only after a criminal conviction
questions.rationale:
Inmates shall be subject to disciplinary sanctions pursuant to a formal disciplinary process following an administrative finding that the inmate engaged in inmate-on-inmate sexual abuse or a criminal finding of guilt.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.78: “(a) Inmates shall be subject to disciplinary sanctions pursuant to a formal disciplinary process following an administrative finding that the inmate engaged in inmate-on-inmate sexual abuse or following a criminal finding of guilt for inmate-on-inmate sexual abuse.”

questions.stem:
A new facility opens, and the agency asks whether it must designate someone to coordinate PREA efforts at each facility.

What does the standard require?
options: The agency shall designate a single compliance manager for all facilities
Each facility shall designate a compliance manager only if it has more than 500 inmates
Each facility shall rely on the Warden to coordinate efforts, with no designation
Each facility shall designate a PREA compliance manager with sufficient time and authority to coordinate the facility's efforts
questions.rationale:
Where an agency operates more than one facility, each facility shall designate a PREA compliance manager with sufficient time and authority to coordinate the facility's efforts to comply.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.11: “(c) Where an agency operates more than one facility, each facility shall designate a PREA compliance manager with sufficient time and authority to coordinate the facility's efforts to comply with the PREA standards.”

questions.stem:
A facility plans to install new cameras in housing units and asks what factor must be considered.

What does the standard require the agency to consider when installing or updating monitoring technology?
options: How such technology may lower the cost of building maintenance
How such technology may enhance the agency's ability to protect inmates from sexual abuse
How such technology may increase visibility of inmates to the public
How such technology may reduce the number of staff needed on each shift, in accordance with the posted schedule
questions.rationale:
When installing or updating a video monitoring system, electronic surveillance system, or other monitoring technology, the agency shall consider how such technology may enhance the agency's ability to protect inmates from sexual abuse.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.18: “(b) When installing or updating a video monitoring system, electronic surveillance system, or other monitoring technology, the agency shall consider how such technology may enhance the agency's ability to protect inmates from sexual abuse.”

questions.stem:
A facility is designing the intake screening process. The PREA coordinator wants to use a simple verbal impression instead of a formal tool.

What does the standard require?
options: Assessments shall be conducted using the inmate's disciplinary record only
Assessments shall be conducted using the officer's judgment based on the inmate's appearance
Assessments shall be conducted using an objective screening instrument
Assessments shall be conducted using a form completed by the inmate's family
questions.rationale:
Such assessments shall be conducted using an objective screening instrument.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.41: “(c) Such assessments shall be conducted using an objective screening instrument.”

questions.stem:
A screening officer shares an inmate's sensitive screening responses with all staff in the housing unit, and other inmates overhear.

What does the standard require?
options: The agency shall share the responses with other inmates to prevent victimization
The agency shall destroy the responses immediately after screening

The agency shall publish the responses to all staff so they can protect the inmate, according to the institution's local guidelines, subject to the Warden's discretion, for the duration of the incident
The agency shall implement appropriate controls on the dissemination within the facility of responses to ensure that sensitive information is not exploited to the inmate's detriment
questions.rationale:
The agency shall implement appropriate controls on the dissemination within the facility of responses to questions asked pursuant to the standard, to ensure sensitive information is not exploited to the inmate's detriment by staff or other inmates.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.41: “(i) The agency shall implement appropriate controls on the dissemination within the facility of responses to questions asked pursuant to this standard in order to ensure that sensitive information is not exploited to the inmate's detriment by staff or other inmates.”

questions.stem:
A mailroom officer is unsure whether to treat a letter from a county prosecutor to an inmate as special mail.

Which of these is listed as special mail?
options: Correspondence from a bail bond company
Correspondence from a private investigator hired by the family, when staff resources allow, with the approval of a supervisor on duty
Correspondence from the inmate's former employer
Correspondence from Prosecuting Attorneys, if the sender is adequately identified and the envelope is properly marked
questions.rationale:
Special mail includes correspondence from attorneys, Members of Congress, embassies and consulates, the U.S. Department of Justice, State Attorneys General, Prosecuting Attorneys, Governors, and U.S. and State courts, if properly identified and marked.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.12: “The staff of each institution of the Bureau of Prisons has the authority to open all mail addressed to you before it is delivered to you. “Special Mail” (mail from the President and Vice President of the U.S., attorneys, Members of the U.S. Congress, Embassies and Consulates, the U.S. Department of Justice (excluding the Bureau of Prisons but including U.S. Attorneys), other Federal law enforcement officers, State Attorneys General, Prosecuting Attorneys, Governors, U.S. Courts (including U.S. Probation Officers), and State Courts) may be opened only in your presence to be checked for contraband. This procedure occurs only if the sender is adequately identified on the envelope and the front of the envelope is marked “Special Mail—Open only in the presence of the inmate.” Other mail may be opened and read by the staff. If you do not want your general correspondence opened and read, the Bureau will return it to the Postal Service. This means that you will not receive such mail. You may choose whether you want your general correspondence delivered to you subject to the above conditions, or returned to the Postal Service. Whatever your choice, special mail will be delivered to you, after it is opened in your presence and checked for contraband. You can make your choice by signing part I or part II. Part I—General Correspondence to be Returned to the Postal Service I have read or had read to me the foregoing notice regarding mail. I do not want my general correspondence opened and read. I REQUEST THAT THE BUREAU OF PRISONS RETURN MY GENERAL CORRESPONDENCE TO THE POSTAL SERVICE. I understand that special mail will be delivered to me, after it is opened in my presence and checked for contraband. (Name) (Reg. No.) (Date) Part II—General Correspondence to be Opened, Read, and Delivered I have read or had read to me the foregoing notice regarding mail, I WISH TO RECEIVE MY GENERAL CORRESPONDENCE. I understand that the Bureau of Prisons may open and read my general correspondence if I choose to receive same. I also understand that special mail will be delivered to me, after it is opened in my presence and checked for contraband. (Name) (Reg. No.) (Date) Inmate (Name), (Reg. No.), refused to sign this form. He (she) was advised by me that the Bureau of Prisons retains the authority to open and read all general correspondence. The inmate was also advised that his (her) refusal to sign this form will be interpreted as an indication that he (she) wishes to receive general correspondence subject to the conditions in part II above. Staff Member's Signature Date”

questions.stem:
An inmate with sufficient funds is cut off after exactly three minutes. He says the staff violated the rules. The institution is crowded, and many inmates are waiting for the phone.

What does the regulation allow?
options: The inmate may be cut off after one minute if another inmate is waiting
Ordinarily an inmate with funds is allowed at least three minutes, and the Warden may limit maximum call length based on population or usage demand
The inmate must be allowed fifteen minutes per call regardless of demand
The inmate may not be limited in any way if he has money in his account
questions.rationale:
Ordinarily an inmate with sufficient funds is allowed at least three minutes for a call, and the Warden may limit the maximum length based on the situation at the institution, such as population or usage demand.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.101: “(d) Placement and duration of telephone call. The placement and duration of any telephone call is subject to availability of inmate funds. Ordinarily, an inmate who has sufficient funds is allowed at least three minutes for a telephone call. The Warden may limit the maximum length of telephone calling based on the situation at that institution (e.g., institution population or usage demand).”

questions.stem:
An inmate wants his attorney's paralegal to write to him. The paralegal's envelope shows only her own name with no reference to the attorney.

What does the regulation require for mail from an attorney's assistant to be treated as special mail?
options: The envelope must be sent through the institution's legal office, which forwards it to the inmate
The envelope must be marked with the paralegal's name only, and the Warden must approve each letter, once the shift lieutenant has been informed
The envelope must be marked with the inmate's register number and the date it was mailed
The envelope must be properly identified as required and marked on the front as mail from the attorney or the legal aid supervisor
questions.rationale:
Mail from an attorney's assistant or legal aid student must be properly identified on the envelope and marked on the front as being mail from the attorney or the legal aid supervisor to be treated as special mail.

Source — 28 CFR § 540.19: “(e) Mail to an inmate from an attorney's assistant or legal aid student or assistant, in order to be identified and treated by staff as special mail, must be properly identified on the envelope as required in paragraph (b) of this section, and must be marked on the front of the envelope as being mail from the attorney or from the legal aid supervisor.”

questions.stem:
An inmate is accumulating a very large amount of legal paperwork in his cell, and it is becoming a fire hazard.

What does the regulation allow the Warden to do?
options: Confiscate all legal materials until the inmate's case is finished
Limit the amount of legal materials an inmate may accumulate for security or housekeeping reasons
Prohibit the inmate from keeping any legal materials in his cell
Require the inmate to mail all legal materials to his attorney
questions.rationale:
The Warden may limit the amount of legal materials an inmate may accumulate for security or housekeeping reasons.

Source — 28 CFR § 543.11: “(2) Staff may allow an inmate to possess those legal materials which are necessary for the inmate's own legal actions. Staff may also allow an inmate to possess the legal materials of another inmate subject to the limitations of paragraph (f)(2) of this section. The Warden may limit the amount of legal materials an inmate may accumulate for security or housekeeping reasons.”

questions.stem:
After a possible tuberculosis exposure in a dormitory, the health services staff want to know who gets tested.

What does the regulation say?
options: The Bureau tests only the inmate who was first diagnosed with TB
The Bureau waits for inmates to report symptoms before testing anyone, for the duration of the incident, in most circumstances, as long as no other inmate is affected
The Bureau tests only staff members who work in the dormitory
The Bureau conducts TB contact investigations following any incident in which inmates or staff may have been exposed, and inmates are tested under the TB screening procedures
questions.rationale:
The Bureau conducts TB contact investigations following any incident in which inmates or staff may have been exposed to tuberculosis, and inmates are tested according to the screening paragraph.

Source — 28 CFR § 549.12: “(5) The Bureau conducts TB contact investigations following any incident in which inmates or staff may have been exposed to tuberculosis. Inmates will be tested according to paragraph (b)(4) of this section.”

questions.stem:
An inmate has a newly diagnosed infectious disease transmitted by casual contact and is working in the kitchen.

What does the regulation say?
options: Inmates with infectious diseases transmitted through casual contact will be prohibited from work assignments in any area until fully evaluated by a health care provider
The inmate is permanently barred from every work assignment

The inmate may continue working in the kitchen if he wears gloves, with the approval of a supervisor on duty, after a supervisor has reviewed the matter, where the circumstances reasonably call for it
The inmate may continue working if the work supervisor agrees
questions.rationale:
The Clinical Director assesses an inmate with an infectious disease for programming, duty, and housing, and inmates with diseases transmitted through casual contact are prohibited from work assignments in any area until fully evaluated by a health care provider.

Source — 28 CFR § 549.13: “(a) The CD will assess any inmate with an infectious disease for appropriateness for programming, duty, and housing. Inmates with infectious diseases that are transmitted through casual contact will be prohibited from work assignments in any area, until fully evaluated by a health care provider.”

questions.stem:
An inmate has been in the SHU for 30 continuous calendar days. He asks whether he will get another hearing he can attend.

What does the regulation say?
options: After every 30 calendar days of continuous placement, the SRO will formally review his status at a hearing he can attend
After every 30 days, the Warden will review his status with the unit team only
After 30 days, no further review occurs until he requests one
After every 30 days, the SRO will review his status in his absence
questions.rationale:
After every 30 calendar days of continuous placement in administrative detention or disciplinary segregation, the SRO will formally review the inmate's status at a hearing he can attend.

Source — 28 CFR § 541.26: “(c) Thirty day reviews. After every 30 calendar days of continuous placement in either administrative detention or disciplinary segregation status, the SRO will formally review your status at a hearing you can attend.”

questions.stem:
During a hostage incident, a staff member asks who ordinarily conducts the negotiations.

What does the regulation say?
options: The shift Lieutenant ordinarily conducts negotiations
The Warden is not ordinarily involved directly; the responsibility is ordinarily assigned to a team trained in hostage negotiation techniques
The hostage takers choose the negotiator
The Warden ordinarily conducts negotiations personally
questions.rationale:
The Warden is not ordinarily involved directly in the negotiation process; it is ordinarily assigned to a team of individuals specifically trained in hostage negotiation techniques.

questions.stem:
Staff are planning a search of an inmate who is returning to the institution after a court transfer and need to decide which type is justified.

Which search does the regulation say may be justified by re-entry after a court transfer?
options: A visual search, since leaving the institution and re-entry after contact with the public is sufficient to justify one
No search, since inmates in court custody are exempt
A search by electronic device only, since a visual search requires a supervisor's approval
A digital search, since a court transfer always creates reasonable belief of concealed contraband
questions.rationale:
Staff may conduct a visual search where there is reasonable belief that contraband may be concealed or a good opportunity for concealment has occurred; leaving the institution or re-entry after contact with the public (after a community trip, court transfer, or contact visit) is sufficient.

Source — 28 CFR § 552.11: “(1) Staff may conduct a visual search where there is reasonable belief that contraband may be concealed on the person, or a good opportunity for concealment has occured. For example, placement in a special housing unit (see 28 CFR part 541, subpart B), leaving the institution, or re-entry into an institution after contact with the public (after a community trip, court transfer, or after a “contact” visit in a visiting room) is sufficient to justify a visual search. The visual search shall be made in a manner designed to assure as much privacy to the inmate as practicable.”

questions.stem:

Procedures for correspondence, with limits on forwarding mail
Procedures for searching visitors, with limits on the property they may bring, when staff resources allow, where the circumstances reasonably call for it
questions.rationale:
Section 553.14 governs inmate transfer between institutions and inmate release, including how property is handled at departure.

Source — 28 CFR § 553.14: “(a) Except as provided for in paragraphs (a)(1) through (3) of this section, authorized personal property shall be shipped by staff to the receiving institution.”

questions.stem:
A mental health practitioner at a facility wants to know whether she can keep knowledge of an inmate's abuse history secret from the staff who make housing decisions.

What does the standard say about information on sexual victimization or abusiveness that occurred in an institutional setting?
options: It is never shared with anyone, including housing staff
It is strictly limited to medical and mental health practitioners and other staff as necessary to inform treatment plans and security and management decisions
It is shared with all staff so they can protect the inmate
It is shared with other inmates to warn them
questions.rationale:
Any information related to sexual victimization or abusiveness that occurred in an institutional setting shall be strictly limited to medical and mental health practitioners and other staff, as necessary, to inform treatment plans and security and management decisions.

Source — 28 CFR § 115.81: “(d) Any information related to sexual victimization or abusiveness that occurred in an institutional setting shall be strictly limited to medical and mental health practitioners and other staff, as necessary, to inform treatment plans and security and management decisions, including housing, bed, work, education, and program assignments, or as otherwise required by Federal, State, or local law.”

questions.stem:
