Facility Rule 11.2 requires a written movement pass for all inmate movement outside assigned areas; Rule 11.6 requires staff to document any authorization they grant.'"

Based strictly on the report, which conclusion is best supported?
options: Only inmate Locke violated a rule, and no staff rule is implicated
Neither Locke nor any staff violated a rule because a verbal authorization existed
Locke lacked the required written pass (Rule 11.2), and the staff documentation requirement (Rule 11.6) was also not met
Only Officer Prine violated a rule; Locke is fully cleared
questions.rationale: Locke had no written movement pass, which Rule 11.2 requires, and Prine confirmed she granted authorization without documenting it, which Rule 11.6 requires, so both requirements were unmet. A verbal authorization does not satisfy the written-pass rule, so the 'neither violated' option is wrong. Because both a movement rule and a documentation rule are implicated, the options limiting the issue to only one party are incomplete.

questions.stem:
Manual excerpt (Inmate Injury Reporting, Section 6):
"When an inmate sustains an injury, the officer shall: (1) summon medical immediately, (2) not move the inmate if a serious head, neck, or back injury is suspected, (3) notify the shift supervisor, and (4) complete an injury report before end of shift. If the injury appears life-threatening, medical must be summoned before any other step."

Inmate Ruiz falls and is unconscious with a suspected neck injury; the situation appears life-threatening. According to the manual, what should the officer do FIRST?
options: Complete the injury report before the shift ends
Summon medical immediately, before any other step
Notify the shift supervisor before summoning medical
Move Ruiz to a safer location before doing anything else
questions.rationale: Because the injury appears life-threatening, the manual states medical must be summoned before any other step, so that is the first action. Moving an inmate with a suspected neck injury is prohibited, completing the report is a later step, and notifying the supervisor comes after summoning medical in a life-threatening situation.
questions.source: determine correct procedure from a manual excerpt

questions.stem:
Reconstructed Timeline (Multi-source, Weller Detention Center):
Control log: 'Alarm activated in C-Pod at 2202.'
Officer Adair report: 'I heard the alarm and arrived at C-Pod approximately three minutes after it sounded.'
Nurse log: 'Called to C-Pod at 2210; treated inmate for a laceration.'
Sergeant note: 'Notified by Officer Adair two minutes after his arrival.'

Based on these sources, at what time was the sergeant most likely notified?
questions.rationale: The alarm sounded at 2202, Adair arrived about three minutes later at roughly 2205, and he notified the sergeant two minutes after arrival, placing notification near 2207. 2202 is the alarm time, 2205 is Adair's arrival, and 2210 is when the nurse was called, none of which match the two-minutes-after-arrival notification.

questions.stem:
Incident Report excerpt with narrative and log (Brackenridge Facility):
Narrative: 'Officer Sable states that at 1500 he confiscated a state-issued blanket that inmate Voss had cut into strips.'
Property log for Voss: 'One state blanket issued 06/02; no replacement authorized.'
Rule reference sheet: 'Rule 3.4 - altering facility-issued items. Rule 8.5 - destruction of state property.'

Which rule violation(s) are supported by the combined narrative and log?
options: Only Rule 3.4, because cutting is merely altering
Only Rule 8.5, because the blanket is state property
Both Rule 3.4 (altering the item) and Rule 8.5 (destruction of state property)
Neither, because the blanket was properly issued to Voss
questions.rationale: Cutting a state-issued blanket into strips both alters a facility-issued item (Rule 3.4) and destroys state property (Rule 8.5), so both violations are supported. The blanket being properly issued to Voss does not permit destroying it, and each single-rule option ignores the other rule that the conduct clearly implicates.

questions.stem:
Manual excerpt (Chemical Agent Deployment, Section 8):
"A chemical agent may be deployed only after (1) a verbal warning is given, (2) the inmate is allowed a reasonable opportunity to comply, and (3) supervisor approval is obtained, except that steps 1 and 3 may be skipped when there is an immediate threat of serious bodily harm. After any deployment, medical shall evaluate the inmate and decontamination shall be offered."

An inmate is refusing to leave a dayroom but is calm and poses no immediate threat of serious harm. According to the manual, which action would be a procedure violation?
options: Deploying the chemical agent without a warning or supervisor approval
Offering decontamination after any deployment
Obtaining supervisor approval before deployment
Giving a verbal warning before considering deployment
questions.rationale: The exception allowing steps 1 and 3 to be skipped applies only to an immediate threat of serious bodily harm, which is absent here, so deploying without a warning or supervisor approval would violate the procedure. Giving a warning, obtaining approval, and offering decontamination are all consistent with the manual's requirements.
questions.source: determine correct procedure from a manual excerpt

questions.stem:
Incident Report Accuracy Review (Cranfield Jail):
Narrative: 'At 1250 I responded to a disturbance in B-Wing. I secured inmate Hale and inmate Pryor and called for backup at 1255.'
Unit log for the same event: 'Disturbance reported 1240. Backup requested 1255. Two inmates secured 1258.'

Comparing the narrative to the unit log, which statement is the best assessment of the report's accuracy?
options: The narrative is accurate about the backup time but inconsistent about when the inmates were secured relative to the backup call
The narrative and log fully agree on every time
The log is incomplete because it omits the backup request
The narrative is more reliable than the log for every detail
questions.rationale: Both sources agree backup was requested at 1255, but the narrative implies the inmates were secured before the 1255 backup call, while the log shows them secured at 1258, after the call, revealing an inconsistency in sequence. The sources do not fully agree, the narrative is not uniformly more reliable, and the log does include the backup request at 1255.

questions.stem:
Manual excerpt (Segregation Placement Review, Rule 20):
"An inmate placed in administrative segregation shall receive a written notice of the reason within 24 hours. A review hearing shall be held within 72 hours of placement. If the 72-hour hearing cannot be held due to a documented emergency, it shall be held within 24 hours after the emergency ends."

Inmate Frick is placed in segregation on Monday at 0800. A documented facility emergency lasts from Wednesday 0600 until Thursday 0600. According to the manual, by when must the review hearing be held?
options: By Friday at 0600, which is 24 hours after the emergency ends
No hearing is required once an emergency occurs
By Monday at 0800, the same time as placement
By Thursday at 0800
questions.rationale: The normal 72-hour deadline (Thursday 0800) is disrupted by the documented emergency, so the rule requires the hearing within 24 hours after the emergency ends; the emergency ends Thursday 0600, making the deadline Friday 0600. The same-time-as-placement option ignores the review window, Thursday 0800 ignores the emergency extension, and a hearing is still required, so the last option is wrong.
questions.source: determine correct procedure from a manual excerpt

questions.stem:
Reconstructed Chronology (Kingsley Correctional):
A report contains these statements out of order:
- 'After medical cleared the inmate, I escorted him back to his cell.'
- 'The fight ended when I gave a second verbal order.'
- 'I first noticed two inmates arguing near the phones.'
- 'Once the argument turned physical, I radioed for assistance.'

Placing the events in the correct chronological order, which event occurred SECOND?
options: The officer radioed for assistance when it turned physical
The officer noticed two inmates arguing
The fight ended after a second verbal order
Medical cleared the inmate and he was escorted back
questions.rationale: The logical order is: noticing the argument, then radioing for assistance when it turned physical, then the fight ending after the second order, then medical clearance and escort. Therefore the second event is radioing for assistance. Noticing the argument is first, the fight ending is third, and the medical clearance and escort are last.

questions.stem:
Incident Report and Policy (Larkspur Facility):
Narrative: 'Officer Tave reports that inmate Gale entered the kitchen at 0500 without authorization, took a knife from the secured rack, and returned it before staff arrived.'
Policy sheet: 'Rule 5.2 - being in an unassigned area. Rule 3.1 - possession of a weapon. Rule 12.0 - tampering with secured equipment. Rule 10.1 - fighting.'

Based strictly on the narrative, which rule violations are supported? (Select all that apply.)
options: Rule 5.2 - being in an unassigned area (the kitchen without authorization)
Rule 12.0 - tampering with secured equipment (the secured knife rack)
Rule 10.1 - fighting
Rule 3.1 - possession of a weapon (taking the knife)
questions.rationale: The narrative supports Gale being in an unassigned area (Rule 5.2), possessing a knife (Rule 3.1), and accessing a secured rack (Rule 12.0), so all three are supported. The narrative describes no fighting, so Rule 10.1 is not supported by the facts stated.

questions.stem:
Manual excerpt and log (Restraint Check Policy, Hartwell Jail):
Policy: 'An inmate in four-point restraints shall have circulation checked every 15 minutes and shall be offered range-of-motion and toileting every 2 hours. Each check shall be logged with the officer's initials and exact time. A supervisor must review the restraint status every 4 hours.'
Log: '1300 circ check (JD); 1315 circ check (JD); 1330 circ check (JD); 1400 circ check (JD); 1415 circ check (JD).'

Based on the policy and log, which deficiency is present?
options: A circulation check is missing between 1330 and 1400, exceeding the 15-minute interval
The officer failed to initial the entries
No deficiency; all required entries are present
A supervisor review was due at 1315 and is missing
questions.rationale: The policy requires circulation checks every 15 minutes, but the log jumps from 1330 to 1400, a 30-minute gap with a missing 1345 check, so that interval deficiency is present. The entries are all initialed (JD), so that option is wrong, and the supervisor review is not due until four hours from the start (about 1700), not 1315.

questions.stem:
Incident Report Excerpt:
"On 08/01 at 1210 hours, during lunch, Officer Prabhu observed Inmate T. Voll pocket an apple and a plastic fork from the serving line. When questioned, Voll surrendered the apple and the fork. The two confiscated items were logged and, because the plastic fork was intact and reusable, only the apple was discarded. The dining supervisor was notified at 1215 hours. Later in the same report, Officer Prabhu wrote that the missing fork was never located."

A supervisor reviewing this report for accuracy notes one internal inconsistency. What is it?
options: The report says the apple was discarded but also says it was returned to the serving line
The report gives two different times for when the theft occurred
The report first says Voll surrendered the fork, but later says the fork was never located
The report never identifies which officer observed the incident
questions.rationale: Early in the report Voll 'surrendered the apple and the fork' and the fork was logged, but later the report states the fork 'was never located,' which is a direct contradiction. Only one time (1210) is given for the theft, Officer Prabhu is clearly named as the observer, and the report consistently says the apple was discarded, so those are not the inconsistency.

questions.stem:
Incident Report Excerpt:
"On 11/07, Officer Salcedo was posted in the visitation room. At 1440 hours he observed Visitor P. Nunley pass a small folded paper to Inmate R. Cade during an embrace. Officer Salcedo ended the visit at 1441 hours, secured the paper, and escorted Inmate Cade to a holding room at 1445 hours. The paper was found to contain a phone number and was logged as evidence at 1500 hours."

Place these events in the correct order: (1) paper logged as evidence, (2) visit ended, (3) paper passed, (4) inmate escorted to holding room.
questions.rationale: The paper was passed at 1440 (3), the visit ended at 1441 (2), the inmate was escorted at 1445 (4), and the paper was logged at 1500 (1), giving the order 3, 2, 4, 1. The other sequences misplace at least one event relative to the timestamps.

questions.stem:
Incident Report Excerpt:
"On 06/25 at 1408 hours, Officer Bhandari responded to Cell C-11 after Inmate S. Odell reported his personal radio missing. Odell stated he last saw it at 1300 hours before going to the dayroom. Between 1300 and 1408 hours, the cell had been accessible to Odell's cellmate, Inmate P. Voss, who returned from work detail at 1345 hours. A search at 1420 hours located the radio inside Voss's pillowcase. Voss claimed he found it in the dayroom."

A supervisor reviewing this report for accuracy notes a timeline problem with Voss's claim. Which observation correctly identifies it?
options: The search occurred before the radio went missing
Voss could not have taken the radio because he returned at 1345 hours
Voss could not have found the radio in the dayroom because he was at work detail until 1345 and Odell left the radio in the cell, not the dayroom
Odell's report is invalid because he did not witness the theft
questions.rationale: Odell reported last seeing the radio in the cell at 1300, not the dayroom, and Voss was on work detail until 1345, so Voss's claim that he found it in the dayroom conflicts with where the radio was and his whereabouts. Returning at 1345 does not exonerate Voss since he had cell access afterward; a report can be valid without a direct witness; and the 1420 search occurred after the 1300 disappearance, not before.

questions.stem:
Written Policy Excerpt:
"Policy 11.3 — Segregation Reviews: An inmate placed in administrative segregation must receive an initial review by the Classification Committee within 72 hours of placement (excluding weekends and holidays). Subsequent reviews occur every 7 calendar days thereafter."

Inmate D. Maren is placed in administrative segregation at 1000 hours on Friday, July 3. Saturday July 4 is observed as a holiday, and the facility counts Saturdays and Sundays as weekend days. By what deadline must the initial review occur under Policy 11.3?
options: By 1000 hours on Wednesday, July 8
By 1000 hours on Monday, July 6
By 1000 hours on Thursday, July 9
By 1000 hours on Saturday, July 4
questions.rationale: The 72-hour clock excludes weekends and holidays. From Friday 1000, Saturday (weekend and holiday) and Sunday (weekend) do not count, so counting resumes Monday: 24 hours by Tuesday 1000, 48 by Wednesday 1000, and 72 by Thursday, July 9 at 1000. The other options fail to exclude the holiday and weekend days properly.
questions.source: apply a written policy to a case

questions.stem:
Incident Report Excerpt:
"On 04/30, a fight occurred in Unit 7. Officer Ledford wrote: 'At 1912 hours I observed Inmate Anwar strike Inmate Bello. I ordered them to stop at 1913 hours. Inmate Bello was escorted to medical at 1916 hours with a bloody nose. Inmate Anwar was placed in a holding cell at 1918 hours.' Officer Ledford's partner, Officer Sim, wrote: 'At 1912 hours I saw Inmate Bello strike first, and Inmate Anwar struck back. I helped separate them at 1913 hours.'"

Which statement accurately describes the discrepancy between the two reports?
options: The two officers disagree about which inmate was injured
The two officers disagree about the time the fight started
The two officers disagree about who was placed in the holding cell
The two officers disagree about who struck first
questions.rationale: Ledford reports observing Anwar strike Bello, while Sim reports Bello struck first and Anwar struck back, a disagreement over who initiated the fight. Both agree the fight started at 1912, neither Sim's account contradicts that Bello was injured, and only Ledford addresses the holding cell, so those are not the discrepancy.

questions.stem:
Written Policy Excerpt:
"Policy 14.2 — Special Meal Accommodations: Inmates may receive a medical diet with written approval from a physician, or a religious diet with written approval from the Chaplain. Approvals are valid for 6 months and must be renewed. An inmate may hold only one special diet approval at a time; if both a medical and religious need exist, the medical diet takes precedence."

Inmate F. Osei has a physician-approved low-sodium medical diet approved on January 10 (valid 6 months). On May 1 he submits a Chaplain-approved request for a religious diet. Under Policy 14.2, what is the correct outcome as of May 1?
options: Osei switches to the religious diet, canceling the medical diet
Osei receives both the medical and religious diets simultaneously
Osei remains on the medical diet, which takes precedence over the religious diet
Osei's medical diet expires immediately upon the religious request
questions.rationale: The policy allows only one special diet at a time and states the medical diet takes precedence when both needs exist, so Osei stays on the still-valid medical diet. He cannot switch away from the precedence rule, cannot hold both at once, and his January 10 medical approval does not expire until mid-July.
questions.source: apply a written policy to a case

questions.stem:
Movement Log — Inmate T. Quill (all same day):
| Time | Location | Escorting Officer |
|------|----------|-------------------|
| 0730 | Housing Unit 2 | -- |
| 0800 | Medical | Officer Ruhl |
| 0845 | Housing Unit 2 | Officer Ruhl |
| 1300 | Law Library | Officer Tann |
| 1345 | Law Library | Officer Tann |
| 1400 | Housing Unit 2 | Officer Tann |

A sergeant auditing the log identifies an inconsistency. Which entry is problematic?
options: The 0730 entry, because it lists no escorting officer
The 0800 Medical entry, because no inmate can visit medical before 0900
The two consecutive Law Library entries at 1300 and 1345 with no movement between them
The 1400 return to Housing Unit 2 by a different officer than took him out
questions.rationale: Two consecutive Law Library entries at 1300 and 1345 with the same location suggest a logging error, since a movement log should record location changes, not the same location twice with no transit. The 0800 medical time is plausible, the 0730 entry sensibly lacks an escort because he was in his unit, and Officer Tann escorted him both to and from the library, so those are not inconsistencies.

questions.stem:
Written Manual Excerpt:
"Manual Section 9 — Suicide Watch Levels: Level 1 (Constant Watch) requires continuous, uninterrupted observation of the inmate at all times. Level 2 (Close Watch) requires staggered observations at intervals not to exceed 15 minutes. Any inmate who verbalizes a specific plan and has the means to carry it out shall be placed on Level 1. Downgrading from Level 1 to Level 2 requires mental health authorization."

Inmate R. Cho tells staff he plans to hang himself and has hidden a torn sheet for that purpose. Which watch level applies, and what is required to reduce it?
options: Level 1, and it may be downgraded at the next shift automatically
Level 2, and downgrading requires only supervisor approval
Level 2, and no authorization is needed to change levels
Level 1, and downgrading to Level 2 requires mental health authorization
questions.rationale: Cho verbalized a specific plan (hanging) and has the means (a hidden torn sheet), so the manual mandates Level 1, and downgrading to Level 2 requires mental health authorization. Level 2 does not apply given the specific plan and means, no supervisor-only or automatic downgrade is permitted, and constant observation cannot lapse without authorization.
questions.source: determine correct procedure from a manual excerpt

questions.stem:
Incident Report Excerpt:
"On 07/22, Officer Isley reported: 'At 2247 hours I heard glass breaking in the dayroom. I arrived at 2248 hours and found a shattered window and Inmate D. Pruett standing nearby with a cut on his right hand. Pruett said he punched the window. At 2250 hours I noticed a second inmate, M. Larkin, exiting the dayroom's rear door. No one else was present when I arrived.'"

A supervisor flags an internal contradiction in the report. What is it?
options: The report says the window shattered but also says it was intact
The report fails to identify the injured inmate
The report says no one else was present when the officer arrived, yet also describes a second inmate in the dayroom leaving at 2250 hours
The report gives two different times for when the glass broke
questions.rationale: The officer states 'No one else was present when I arrived' at 2248, but also reports Inmate Larkin exiting the dayroom's rear door at 2250, which contradicts the claim that only Pruett was present. The window is consistently described as shattered, only one time is given for the breakage, and the injured inmate (Pruett) is named, so those are not the contradiction.

questions.stem:
Written Policy Excerpt:
"Policy 2.9 — Use of Force Reporting: After any use of force, the involved officer must (1) complete a Use of Force Report before the end of the shift, (2) ensure the inmate receives a medical evaluation regardless of visible injury, (3) preserve any video footage of the incident, and (4) notify the Shift Commander within 30 minutes. Failure to complete any step is a reportable policy breach."

After deploying a takedown on a combative inmate at 1500 hours, Officer Navarro notifies the Shift Commander at 1515 hours and completes her Use of Force Report by end of shift, but she does not arrange a medical evaluation because the inmate has no visible injury and she does not preserve the body-camera footage. Under Policy 2.9, which steps did Officer Navarro FAIL to complete? (Select all that apply.)
options: Completing a Use of Force Report before end of shift
Preserving the video footage of the incident
Notifying the Shift Commander within 30 minutes
Ensuring the inmate received a medical evaluation
Deploying the takedown itself
questions.rationale: Navarro failed to ensure a medical evaluation (required regardless of visible injury) and failed to preserve the video footage, so those two steps were breached. She did complete the report by end of shift and notified the commander at 1515 (within 30 minutes of 1500), and deploying the takedown is the use of force itself, not a reporting step.

questions.stem:
SALLYPORT LOG — Vehicle Gate, Ansgar Correctional

Time  Vehicle       Action  Inner Gate  Outer Gate
1002  Supply truck  Enter   Closed      Open
1003  Supply truck  Enter   Open        Closed
1010  Van 4         Exit    Open        Closed
1011  Van 4         Exit    Closed      Open

Security rule: In a sallyport, the inner and outer gates must never be open at the same time (interlock rule). Reviewing the log, is the interlock rule maintained at every entry?
options: Yes, at each logged step only one gate is open at a time
No, at 1002 both gates were open
No, at 1010 both gates were open
No, the log shows both gates closed at 1003
questions.rationale: At each logged step exactly one gate is open while the other is closed, so the interlock rule is maintained throughout. At 1002 only the outer gate is open, at 1010 only the inner gate is open, and at 1003 the inner gate is open (not both closed), so each 'No' option misreads the log.

questions.stem:
POLICY — Disciplinary Segregation, Kilmartin State Prison

"Policy 15: An inmate placed in disciplinary segregation must receive a hearing within 72 hours of placement, excluding weekends and holidays. If the deadline falls on a weekend or holiday, the hearing must occur by the end of the next business day."

Inmate Farrow is placed in segregation at 1500 on a Thursday. There are no holidays that week. Under Policy 15, by when must his hearing be held?
options: By 1500 the following Tuesday
By the end of Friday
By 1500 Sunday
By 1500 Monday
questions.rationale: Counting 72 hours excluding the weekend: from Thursday 1500, the three business-day periods run through Friday and skip Sat/Sun, landing at 1500 the following Tuesday. Sunday and Friday are far too early, and Monday miscounts by dropping one business day.
questions.source: apply a written policy to a case

questions.stem:
MANUAL EXCERPT — Force Continuum, Oberlin Facility

"Officers shall use only the level of force reasonably necessary. The continuum, in ascending order, is: (1) officer presence, (2) verbal commands, (3) soft-hand control, (4) hard-hand control, (5) intermediate weapons, (6) deadly force. An officer may escalate one level when the current level fails to gain compliance and may skip levels only if the threat is immediate and severe."

An inmate ignores verbal commands (level 2) and passively goes limp but poses no immediate severe threat. Per the manual, what is the appropriate next level?
options: Soft-hand control (level 3)
Intermediate weapons (level 5)
Officer presence (level 1)
Hard-hand control (level 4)
questions.rationale: Since verbal commands failed and there is no immediate severe threat, the officer escalates just one level to soft-hand control. Jumping to hard-hand control or intermediate weapons would skip levels without the required immediate severe threat, and retreating to officer presence is a de-escalation, not the appropriate response to noncompliance.
questions.source: determine correct procedure from a manual excerpt

questions.stem:
INCIDENT REPORT — Conflicting Statements, Thornbury Jail

"Officer Nash's narrative states the altercation began at 1340 when Inmate Cobb struck Inmate Dial. Officer Reilly's supplement states Nash arrived at the scene at 1342, two minutes after the first blow. The dayroom camera timestamp shows the first contact at 1338."

A reviewer must reconcile these. According to the sources, which time is most reliable for when the altercation actually began?
options: 1342, per Officer Reilly
The time cannot be determined from any source
1340, per Officer Nash
1338, the camera timestamp
questions.rationale: The camera timestamp of 1338 is an objective, automatically recorded record of first contact, making it the most reliable start time. Nash's 1340 and Reilly's 1342 are human recollections that conflict with the objective footage, and the sources do provide a determinable time, so the 'cannot be determined' option is wrong.

questions.stem:
CONTROLLED-MOVEMENT LOG — Central Corridor, Waverly Prison

Movement rule: Only one housing unit may move through the central corridor at a time, and a unit must be fully cleared (all inmates arrived at destination) before the next unit is released.

0900  Unit 1 released to chow (est. clear 0915)
0912  Unit 2 released to chow
0915  Unit 1 cleared at chow hall
0930  Unit 2 cleared at chow hall

According to the log and rule, was there a movement violation?
options: Yes, Unit 2 was released at 0912 before Unit 1 cleared at 0915
No, both units cleared successfully
Yes, Unit 1 took too long to clear
No, the units used different corridors
questions.rationale: Unit 2 was released at 0912, but Unit 1 did not clear until 0915, so two units overlapped in the corridor in violation of the one-unit-at-a-time rule. Successful clearing does not cure the overlap, Unit 1's clearing time was within estimate, and the log gives no indication of separate corridors.

questions.stem:
MANUAL EXCERPT — Suicide Watch Levels, Grafton Correctional

"Level I (constant watch): continuous, uninterrupted visual observation by a staff member. Level II (close watch): visual checks at staggered intervals not to exceed 15 minutes. An inmate may be stepped down from Level I to Level II only upon written clearance by a qualified mental-health professional."

Inmate Sears is on Level I. An officer, believing Sears seems calmer, begins conducting checks every 12 minutes instead of watching continuously, without any documented clearance. Per the manual, what has occurred?
options: An improper step-down; Level I requires continuous observation and clearance to reduce it
A permissible adjustment since 12 minutes is within the 15-minute Level II limit
A Level III observation, which is the least restrictive
Correct procedure, because the inmate appeared calmer
questions.rationale: Level I demands continuous observation and may only be reduced with written mental-health clearance, neither of which was met, so the officer improperly stepped Sears down. The 15-minute interval belongs to Level II, which the inmate was not cleared to; an officer's impression of calmness is not authorization; and no Level III is defined in the excerpt.
questions.source: determine correct procedure from a manual excerpt

questions.stem:
TRUST ACCOUNT LEDGER — Inmate Banking, Everton Jail

Date    Description        Debit    Credit   Balance
06/01   Opening balance                       $52.40
06/03   Commissary          $18.75            $33.65
06/07   Deposit (family)             $40.00   $73.65
06/09   Postage             $4.10             $69.55
06/12   Commissary          $22.30            ______

According to the ledger, what is the balance after the 06/12 commissary purchase?
questions.rationale: Subtracting the $22.30 debit from the $69.55 balance gives $47.25. '$91.85' incorrectly adds the debit, '$51.35' and '$45.15' reflect arithmetic errors that do not match the running balance.

questions.stem:
POLICY — Emergency Lockdown, Aramis State Prison

"Policy 20: During a facility lockdown, staff shall: (a) secure all inmates in their assigned cells, (b) suspend all non-emergency movement, (c) maintain essential medical passes with a two-officer escort, and (d) continue meal service delivered to cells. Recreation, visitation, and programs are canceled."

During a lockdown, which of the following actions are CONSISTENT with Policy 20? (Select all that apply.)
options: Delivering meals directly to inmate cells
Securing all inmates in their assigned cells
Allowing a scheduled family visitation to proceed
Holding the weekly education program as planned
Escorting an inmate to an emergency dialysis appointment with two officers
questions.rationale: Delivering meals to cells, providing a two-officer escort for an essential medical pass, and securing inmates in their cells all align with Policy 20. Visitation and programs are expressly canceled during lockdown, so allowing a family visit or holding the education program both violate the policy.
questions.source: apply a written policy to a case

questions.stem:
INCIDENT REPORT — Timeline Reconstruction, Belhaven Jail

"Log entries: 2201 alarm sounded in Unit F. 2159 Officer Yost reported smoke near Cell F-3. 2203 fire suppression activated. 2158 an inmate first pressed the cell intercom reporting heat. 2205 all Unit F inmates evacuated."

Arranged in the correct chronological order, which event happened FIRST?
options: Fire suppression activated (2203)
An inmate pressed the intercom reporting heat (2158)
Officer Yost reported smoke (2159)
The alarm sounded (2201)
questions.rationale: The earliest timestamp is 2158, when an inmate pressed the intercom reporting heat, so that event happened first. The smoke report (2159), the alarm (2201), and suppression (2203) all carry later times, so none of them precedes the intercom press.

questions.stem:
MANUAL EXCERPT — Report Correction Procedure, Cranfield Facility

"An error discovered in a completed incident report shall be corrected by drawing a single line through the incorrect entry so it remains legible, writing the correction nearby, and initialing and dating the change. Reports shall never be erased, whited out, or rewritten to conceal the original entry."

Officer Vail realizes she wrote the wrong cell number in a filed report. Per the manual, how must she correct it?
options: Use correction fluid over the wrong number and write the correct one
Erase the wrong number and pencil in the correct one
Rewrite the entire report so it is clean
Draw a single line through the wrong number so it stays legible, write the correct number, and initial and date it
questions.rationale: The manual requires a single legible strike-through, a nearby correction, and initials with a date, which is exactly the first option. Correction fluid, rewriting to a clean copy, and erasing all conceal or destroy the original entry, which the manual expressly forbids.
questions.source: determine correct procedure from a manual excerpt

questions.stem: Incident Report #7788 (times in 24-hour format): 'At 2255, Officer Blaskiewicz began final rounds. At 2302, he noticed inmate G. Montag was not in his assigned bunk in dorm 3. At 2304, he checked the dorm bathroom and found it empty. At 2307, he notified Control and a facility count was ordered. At 2311, Montag was found asleep in an unassigned bunk two beds over. At 2319, Montag was returned to his assigned bunk and a report was started.' If a supervisor wants to know the total elapsed time from the START of final rounds until Montag was RETURNED to his assigned bunk, what is that duration?
options: 12 minutes
24 minutes
9 minutes
16 minutes
questions.rationale: Final rounds began at 2255 and Montag was returned to his bunk at 2319, so the elapsed time is 2319 minus 2255, which equals 24 minutes. 16 minutes is only rounds-start to when he was found (2311), 9 minutes is the discovery-to-notification span, and 12 is a partial interval; only 24 minutes spans the full requested period.

questions.stem: Incident Report #4102: 'At 0815, Officer Ramaswamy escorted five inmates from the sally port to intake. At 0818, inmate #3 in the line (T. Okafor) complained of dizziness. At 0821, the escort halted and medical was called. At 0826, four inmates continued to intake while Okafor waited with Officer Ramaswamy. At 0833, a nurse arrived and cleared Okafor. At 0838, Okafor was escorted to intake by a second officer.' A supervisor asks how many inmates reached intake by 0827. Based strictly on the report, what is the correct count?
options: None; all inmates were held
Four inmates
Five inmates
One inmate
questions.rationale: At 0826, four inmates continued to intake while Okafor stayed behind, so by 0827 exactly four had reached intake. Okafor was not escorted to intake until 0838, so five is too many and 'none' is wrong. 'One' misreads the report; only four is correct.
questions.source: extract facts from an incident report

questions.stem: Two reports describe the same event. Officer Halvard's report: 'At 1345, inmate B. Yıldız struck the wall with his fist and was placed in his cell.' Officer Duconge's report: 'At 1345, inmate B. Yıldız struck another inmate and was placed in restraints.' A lieutenant reviewing both for accuracy must note the conflict. On which factual point do the two reports DISAGREE?
options: The location of the incident
What Yıldız struck and how he was secured afterward
The identity of the inmate involved
The time the event occurred
questions.rationale: Both reports agree on the time (1345) and inmate (Yıldız), but they disagree on what he struck (a wall vs. another inmate) and how he was secured (placed in his cell vs. placed in restraints). Location is not stated in either report, so it is not the point of conflict. Only the object struck and the method of securing differ.

questions.stem:
Disciplinary Tracking Table:
Inmate | Charge Date | Charge | Hearing Date | Outcome
P. Sørensen | 05/02 | fighting | 05/06 | 15 days seg
M. Achterberg | 05/03 | contraband | 05/09 | dismissed
K. Villanueva | 05/03 | fighting | 05/07 | 10 days seg
R. Delatorre | 05/04 | threatening staff | (blank) | (blank)
Facility rule requires a hearing within 5 days of the charge date. Which inmate's case appears to VIOLATE this timing rule based on the table?
options: K. Villanueva (charged 05/03, heard 05/07)
M. Achterberg (charged 05/03, heard 05/09)
P. Sørensen (charged 05/02, heard 05/06)
All hearings were held on time
questions.rationale: Achterberg was charged 05/03 and heard 05/09, a gap of six days, exceeding the five-day limit. Sørensen (05/02 to 05/06) is four days and Villanueva (05/03 to 05/07) is four days, both within the rule. Delatorre has no hearing date recorded, so a timing violation cannot yet be determined; only Achterberg clearly violates the rule.

questions.stem: Incident Report #6070: 'At 1725, Officer Pemberton smelled smoke near cell block E. At 1727, she confirmed light smoke coming from cell E-2. At 1728, she radioed a possible fire and evacuation of adjacent cells began. At 1731, the source was found to be a smoldering mattress. At 1733, a fire extinguisher was discharged and the smoldering stopped. At 1740, the housing unit was ventilated. At 1749, occupants of the adjacent cells were returned.' Facility Policy F-9 requires that any time a fire is radioed, a Fire Incident Form must be completed regardless of the eventual cause. Based on the report and policy, is a Fire Incident Form required?
options: Only if an inmate was injured
No, because the cause turned out to be only a smoldering mattress
No, because no flames were ever confirmed
Yes, because a possible fire was radioed at 1728
questions.rationale: Policy F-9 triggers the Fire Incident Form whenever a fire is radioed, and Pemberton radioed a possible fire at 1728, so the form is required. The eventual cause being a smoldering mattress and the absence of open flames do not matter because the policy applies 'regardless of the eventual cause.' No injury condition exists, so the requirement stands.
questions.source: apply a written policy to a case

questions.stem: Incident Report #2288 narrative (unedited): 'I was doing my round when I saw the inmate. He told the other one to move. Then he hit him and the officer came. After that they were separated and it was over.' A sergeant notes the narrative is unusable for a disciplinary hearing. What is the SINGLE most serious clarity problem in this narrative?
options: It uses too many exact timestamps
It contains excessive technical jargon
It names the wrong facility
It relies on unidentified pronouns so it is unclear who did what
questions.rationale: The narrative repeatedly uses 'he,' 'the inmate,' and 'the other one' without identifying who is who, making it impossible to tell which inmate struck which, or which officer responded. It contains no timestamps, no facility name, and no jargon, so those options are false. The core defect is the ambiguous, unidentified pronoun use.

questions.stem: Incident Report #9910: 'At 1200, headcount for unit 9 was reported as 52. At 1205, one inmate (D. Marchand) departed for a court transport. At 1210, two inmates returned from a medical appointment. At 1230, the next scheduled count was conducted. Assume no other movements occurred.' Based on the report, what SHOULD the 1230 count total be for unit 9?
options: 53 inmates
52 inmates
51 inmates
55 inmates
questions.rationale: Starting from 52, one inmate departed (52 - 1 = 51) and two returned (51 + 2 = 53), so the 1230 count should be 53. Staying at 52 ignores the net gain of one, 51 counts only the departure, and 55 wrongly adds without subtracting. Only 53 reflects all movements.

questions.stem: Incident Report #3506: 'At 0910, Officer Escamilla issued a direct order to inmate L. Broadhurst to remove an unauthorized item from his window. At 0913, Broadhurst refused. At 0916, Sergeant Ito reissued the order. At 0918, Broadhurst removed the item. At 0925, Escamilla began a disciplinary report for the initial refusal.' The disciplinary process requires that a report cite the FIRST refusal, including its time. Which time should the report cite as the first refusal?
options: 0916, when the sergeant reissued the order
0918, when the item was removed
0913, when Broadhurst first refused
0910, when the first order was issued
questions.rationale: The first refusal occurred at 0913 when Broadhurst refused Escamilla's initial order, so that is the time to cite. 0910 is when the order was issued (not refused), 0916 is the reissued order, and 0918 is compliance, none of which is the first refusal. Only 0913 is correct.

questions.stem: Incident Report #4820: 'At 1330, Officer Wrenfield responded to a report of a fight in workshop 2. At 1332, she found inmates C. Abramowicz and T. Nightingale on the floor. At 1333, she called for backup. At 1335, backup arrived and separated the inmates. At 1338, Abramowicz was found to have a cut lip and Nightingale a swollen hand. At 1345, both were escorted to medical. At 1400, a supervisor was briefed.' A reviewer checks the report for completeness against required elements: time, location, persons involved, injuries, and actions taken. Which TWO required elements are clearly present in this report? (Select two.)
options: The disciplinary charge codes are listed
The names of any inmate witnesses are recorded
Injuries to the inmates are documented
The location of the incident is stated
The reporting officer's badge number is recorded
questions.rationale: The report documents injuries (cut lip and swollen hand at 1338) and states the location (workshop 2), so both of those required elements are present. The narrative does not include a badge number, does not name any witnesses, and does not list charge codes, so those three are absent. Only the injuries and location elements are clearly present.

questions.stem: Incident Report #5744: 'At 1450, Officer Broussard began escorting inmate H. Trawick to the visitation room. At 1452, Trawick refused to be searched before entry. At 1455, Broussard denied entry to visitation per policy. At 1458, Trawick agreed to be searched. At 1500, the search was completed with no contraband found. At 1503, Trawick entered visitation.' Facility Policy V-4 states: 'No inmate may enter visitation without first completing a search; an inmate who initially refuses may still enter if he later consents and passes the search.' Based on the report and policy, was Trawick correctly allowed into visitation?
options: No; his initial refusal at 1452 permanently barred him from visitation that day
Yes, but only because no contraband was found, regardless of his consent
No; the search must occur before any refusal is recorded
Yes; he later consented at 1458 and passed the search at 1500 before entering
questions.rationale: Policy V-4 allows an inmate who initially refuses to still enter if he later consents and passes the search; Trawick consented at 1458 and passed the clean search at 1500, so his 1503 entry was proper. An initial refusal is not a permanent bar under this policy, the policy sets no rule about search timing relative to a refusal, and consent (not merely a clean result) is the operative condition. Only the second option correctly applies the policy.
questions.source: apply a written policy to a case

questions.stem: Transport Manual excerpt: "For any inmate classified Medium or High risk, two officers must be assigned and the inmate must be secured with handcuffs, waist chain, and leg irons. For Low risk inmates, one officer and handcuffs only are required." Transport roster shows Inmate Tillman is classified High risk and is scheduled for a court trip with one assigned officer and handcuffs only. What is the correct procedure?
options: Reclassify Tillman to Low risk to match the current escort
Add leg irons only; one officer is sufficient for court trips
Assign a second officer and add a waist chain and leg irons
The current assignment is correct for a High risk inmate
questions.rationale: A High risk inmate requires two officers and handcuffs, waist chain, and leg irons, so a second officer plus the waist chain and leg irons must be added. The current assignment is insufficient, reclassifying to change the escort is improper, and one officer with only leg irons still fails the two-officer and full-restraint requirements.
questions.source: determine correct procedure from a manual excerpt

questions.stem: Grievance policy: "An inmate grievance must be filed within 10 calendar days of the incident. Staff must issue a written response within 15 calendar days of receiving the grievance. If no response is issued within 15 days, the grievance is automatically escalated to the warden's office." Log: Incident occurred on March 3. Inmate Quinlan filed the grievance on March 11. Staff received it March 11 and issued a written response on March 29. Which statement is correct?
options: The grievance was filed late and should be dismissed
The grievance was timely filed, but the response exceeded 15 days and should have escalated to the warden
Both the filing and the response met all deadlines
The grievance should escalate because it was filed on the 8th day
questions.rationale: Filing on March 11 is 8 days after the March 3 incident, within the 10-day window, so the filing is timely. However, the response on March 29 is 18 days after the March 11 receipt, exceeding the 15-day limit, which should have triggered automatic escalation to the warden. Choices claiming late filing, full compliance, or escalation due to timely filing all misapply the deadlines.

questions.stem:
Incident report timeline for a fight in Unit F:

- 1902: Officer Mendez hears shouting near the showers.
- 1903: Mendez radios a Code 4 and moves toward the showers.
- 1904: Backup Officers Pell and Trumble arrive.
- 1906: Inmates Aiken and Sowards are separated and cuffed.
- 1909: Nurse Okafor arrives and examines both inmates.
- 1915: Both inmates escorted to medical.

Policy: "Medical staff must respond to a Code 4 involving injuries within 5 minutes of the code being called." Did medical staff meet the response-time requirement?
options: No, because backup officers arrived after the Code 4
Yes, because the nurse arrived before the inmates were escorted to medical
No, because the nurse arrived 6 minutes after the Code 4 was called
Yes, because the nurse arrived within 5 minutes of the inmates being cuffed
questions.rationale: The Code 4 was called at 1903 and the nurse arrived at 1909, which is 6 minutes later, exceeding the 5-minute requirement. The requirement is measured from the code being called, not from when inmates were cuffed or escorted, so the first and third choices use the wrong reference point; the fourth cites an irrelevant fact about backup officers.

questions.stem:
Overtime and staffing table for the night shift (housing units require a minimum of 2 officers each):

Unit | Officers scheduled | On approved leave | Called in sick
East | 3 | 0 | 1
West | 2 | 0 | 0
North | 3 | 1 | 1
South | 2 | 0 | 1

Policy: "If actual available staff falls below the 2-officer minimum for any unit, the shift supervisor must call in overtime for that unit." For which unit(s) must overtime be called?
options: North and South
North only
East only
South only
questions.rationale: Available staff equals scheduled minus leave and sick. North has 3 minus 1 leave minus 1 sick = 1 available, below the minimum. South has 2 minus 1 sick = 1 available, also below the minimum. East has 3 minus 1 sick = 2 (meets minimum) and West has 2 (meets minimum), so only North and South require overtime.

questions.stem: Disciplinary hearing policy excerpt: "Before a disciplinary hearing, the inmate must (1) receive written notice of the charges at least 24 hours in advance, (2) be offered a staff advisor if the charge is a major violation, and (3) be permitted to call witnesses unless doing so would jeopardize institutional safety. A hearing conducted without meeting these requirements is invalid." Hearing report for Inmate Escobar (major violation): "Written notice served June 4 at 0900; hearing held June 4 at 1500. Staff advisor offered and declined. Inmate's request to call one witness was granted." Which requirement was NOT met, making the hearing invalid?
options: The 24-hour advance written notice requirement
The requirement to offer a staff advisor for a major violation
All requirements were met and the hearing is valid
The requirement to permit the inmate to call witnesses
questions.rationale: Written notice was served June 4 at 0900 and the hearing was held the same day at 1500, only 6 hours later, which fails the 24-hour advance notice requirement and makes the hearing invalid. The staff advisor was offered (and declined) and the witness request was granted, so those two requirements were met, and because notice was violated the hearing is not valid.

questions.stem: At the Cedar Ridge Correctional Center, the main hallway runs east to west. Starting at the west end, the rooms along the north wall are, in order: the Property Room, the Laundry, and the Medical Unit. If an officer walks east down the hallway from the west end, which north-wall room does the officer reach FIRST?
options: The Property Room
The Medical Unit
The Visitation Room
The Laundry
questions.rationale: Walking east from the west end, the first north-wall room in the stated order is the Property Room. The Laundry is second and the Medical Unit is third, so both come later. The Visitation Room is not part of the listed north-wall rooms.
questions.source: identifying a location from a description

questions.stem: Officer Reyes stands at the front lobby of the Pinewood Detention Facility facing north. The Control Room is directly in front of her, the Booking Desk is to her right, and the Staff Break Room is to her left. In which cardinal direction is the Booking Desk located from Officer Reyes?
options: West
North
South
East
questions.rationale: When facing north, the direction to your right is east, so the Booking Desk (to her right) is east. North is straight ahead (Control Room) and the Staff Break Room to her left is west. South would be directly behind her.

questions.stem: In Unit B of the Maple Grove Jail, four cells sit side by side along a single wall. From left to right they are Cell 21, Cell 22, Cell 23, and Cell 24. Which cell is immediately to the RIGHT of Cell 22?
options: Cell 24
Cell 20
Cell 21
Cell 23
questions.rationale: Reading left to right, Cell 23 comes immediately after Cell 22, so it is directly to the right of Cell 22. Cell 21 is to the left of Cell 22, and Cell 24 is two cells to the right, not immediately adjacent. Cell 20 is not in the row.

questions.stem: A corridor at the Riverside Correctional Annex has doors on both sides. On the west side are the Gymnasium and the Chapel. Directly across the corridor from the Chapel is the Library. Which room is directly across the corridor from the Library?
options: The Chapel
The Library itself
The Kitchen
The Gymnasium
questions.rationale: If the Library is directly across from the Chapel, then by reversal the Chapel is directly across from the Library. The Gymnasium is a separate west-side room, not across from the Library, and a room cannot be across from itself. The Kitchen is not mentioned.

questions.stem: Officer Tran must deliver meal trays on the following patrol route in order: Cell Block 1, then the Dining Hall, then Cell Block 2, and finally the Infirmary. Which location does Officer Tran visit SECOND?
options: Cell Block 1
The Infirmary
The Dining Hall
Cell Block 2
questions.rationale: The stated order is Cell Block 1, Dining Hall, Cell Block 2, Infirmary, so the second stop is the Dining Hall. Cell Block 1 is first, Cell Block 2 is third, and the Infirmary is last.

questions.stem: The exercise yard at the Fort Hollow Facility is rectangular. The Sally Port is at the north end and the Recreation Shed is at the south end. Watchtower 1 sits at the northwest corner. If an officer walks straight from the Sally Port to the Recreation Shed, in which direction is she walking?
options: South
North
East
West
questions.rationale: Walking from the north end (Sally Port) to the south end (Recreation Shed) means moving southward. North would be the reverse direction. East and West are perpendicular to that straight north-south path.

questions.stem: At the Glenwood Holding Center, a visitor is told: 'Enter the front door, walk straight down the main hall, and turn right at the first intersection. The Interview Room is the first door on your left.' The main hall runs north and the visitor enters heading north. After turning right, which direction is the visitor now facing?
options: West
East
South
North
questions.rationale: Heading north and turning right rotates you to face east. Turning left instead would face west, continuing straight would remain north, and facing south would require a full turnaround.

questions.stem: In the administrative wing of the Bayfront Jail, the offices in a straight row from left to right are: Warden's Office, Records Office, Payroll Office, and Training Office. Which office is located BETWEEN the Records Office and the Training Office?
options: Warden's Office
Payroll Office
Training Office
Records Office
questions.rationale: Reading the row left to right, the Payroll Office sits directly between the Records Office and the Training Office. The Warden's Office is to the far left of Records, and Records and Training are the two endpoints of the described span, not the room between them.

questions.stem: Officer Diaz is told the Contraband Locker is 'north of the Control Booth and just west of the Armory.' The Control Booth is at the center of the floor, and the Armory is at the northeast corner. Which description matches the Contraband Locker's position?
options: South of the Control Booth
At the southwest corner
East of the Armory
North of the Control Booth and west of the Armory
questions.rationale: The stem directly states the Contraband Locker is north of the Control Booth and just west of the Armory, which is exactly the correct description. 'South of the Control Booth' and 'east of the Armory' contradict the given directions, and 'southwest corner' places it in the wrong part of the floor.
questions.source: identifying a location from a description

questions.stem: A patrol at the Stonebrook Facility must pass these checkpoints in order: the East Gate, the Kitchen, the Chapel, and then the West Gate. Which checkpoint comes immediately AFTER the Kitchen?
options: The Laundry
The Chapel
The West Gate
The East Gate
questions.rationale: In the stated order (East Gate, Kitchen, Chapel, West Gate), the Chapel immediately follows the Kitchen. The East Gate comes before the Kitchen, the West Gate is last, and the Laundry is not part of the route.

questions.stem: The dayroom at the Ashford Correctional Facility is square. There is one door on each wall: the North Door leads to the corridor, the South Door leads to the yard, the East Door leads to the showers, and the West Door leads to the cells. An officer standing in the center facing the corridor door then turns to face the yard door. Which way does the door she now faces lead?
options: To the yard
To the cells
To the showers
To the corridor
questions.rationale: The South Door leads to the yard, and she has turned to face the yard door, so the door she now faces leads to the yard. The showers (East) and cells (West) are on the side walls, and the corridor (North) is the door she was originally facing.

questions.stem: At the Harborview Detention Center, the Booking Area is described as being 'the room you reach first after entering through the main entrance, before the metal detector.' The metal detector is between the Booking Area and the Holding Cells. Which room is farthest from the main entrance?
options: The Holding Cells
The main entrance
The Booking Area
The metal detector
questions.rationale: The order from the entrance is main entrance, Booking Area, metal detector, then Holding Cells, so the Holding Cells are farthest away. The Booking Area is first inside, and the metal detector sits in the middle of that sequence.
questions.source: identifying a location from a description

questions.stem: In the intake corridor of the Redland Detention Center, four rooms sit in a single row from left to right in this order: the Property Room, the Fingerprint Room, the Holding Cell, and the Medical Screening Room. Which room is immediately to the right of the Fingerprint Room?
options: Holding Cell
Property Room
Medical Screening Room
Fingerprint Room
questions.rationale: Reading left to right, the Holding Cell comes immediately after the Fingerprint Room, so it is directly to its right. The Property Room is to the left of the Fingerprint Room, the Medical Screening Room is two positions to the right (not immediately), and a room cannot be to the right of itself.

questions.stem: A hallway at the Bishop Creek Jail has offices along both sides. On the north wall, from west to east, are the Sergeant's Office and the Records Office. Directly across the hall on the south wall, opposite the Sergeant's Office, is the Break Room. Which office is located directly across the hall from the Break Room?
options: Records Office
Sergeant's Office
The Break Room has no office across from it
Both offices
questions.rationale: The Break Room is stated to be opposite the Sergeant's Office, so 'across the hall' from the Break Room is the Sergeant's Office. The Records Office is opposite a different point on the south wall, the claim that nothing is across is contradicted by the setup, and only one office is directly opposite.

questions.stem: On a facility map, the main entrance faces north. Officer Delgado stands at the entrance and walks straight ahead into the building. In which cardinal direction is Officer Delgado walking?
options: West
East
North
South
questions.rationale: If the entrance faces north and the officer walks straight ahead through it, she is heading north. South would be walking back out the way she faced, and east or west would require turning to one side rather than going straight ahead.

questions.stem: The cellblock dayroom at Harmon Correctional has five tables in one straight row, numbered 1 through 5 from left to right. Which table is directly between Table 2 and Table 4?
options: Table 5
Table 1
Table 2
Table 3
questions.rationale: Between Table 2 and Table 4 in the numbered row is Table 3, the middle of those three positions. Table 1 sits to the left of Table 2, Table 5 sits to the right of Table 4, and Table 2 is one of the endpoints, not the item between them.

questions.stem: On a facility map oriented with north at the top, the Kitchen is drawn directly below the Cafeteria. Which cardinal direction is the Kitchen from the Cafeteria?
options: North
East
West
South
questions.rationale: With north at the top of the map, directly below means toward the bottom, which is south. North is the top, while east and west are to the right and left rather than straight down.

questions.stem: Officer Pruitt is standing at Post A and needs to reach Post B. On the map, Post A and Post B are connected by a straight hallway that runs east to west. Post B is on the west end and Post A is on the east end. To walk from Post A to Post B, which direction should Officer Pruitt travel?
options: South
East
West
North
questions.rationale: Post A is on the east end and Post B is on the west end, so moving from A to B means traveling west. East would move away from Post B, and north or south are not along the east-west hallway.

questions.stem: In Housing Unit 3, the cells are arranged in a single row: Cell 301, Cell 302, Cell 303, and Cell 304, in that order from left to right. An inmate in Cell 303 wants to know which cell is immediately to his left. Which cell is it?
options: Cell 303
Cell 301
Cell 304
Cell 302
questions.rationale: Immediately to the left of Cell 303 is Cell 302, the cell just before it in the left-to-right order. Cell 301 is two positions to the left (not immediate), Cell 304 is to the right, and Cell 303 is the inmate's own cell.

questions.stem: A facility map shows the Visitation Room in the northeast corner of the building and the Laundry in the southwest corner. Traveling in a straight line from the Visitation Room to the Laundry, you move generally toward which corner of the map?
options: Toward the northwest corner
Toward the southeast corner
Toward the northeast corner
Toward the southwest corner
questions.rationale: The Laundry is in the southwest corner, so heading from the Visitation Room to the Laundry moves you toward the southwest. The northeast corner is where you started, and the northwest and southeast corners are not the destination.

questions.stem: The control room has a bank of monitors mounted side by side. From the operator's point of view, Monitor 1 is on the far left, then Monitor 2, then Monitor 3, then Monitor 4 on the far right. Which monitor is adjacent to Monitor 4?
options: Monitor 3
Monitor 1
Monitor 4 is at the end, so no monitor is adjacent to it
Monitor 2
questions.rationale: Monitor 4 is at the far right, and the only monitor next to it is Monitor 3. Monitor 1 and Monitor 2 are farther to the left and not adjacent, and being at the end does not mean nothing is beside it.

questions.stem: Officer Nakamura is walking north down a corridor. She turns to her right at the next intersection. After completing that turn, in which cardinal direction is she now facing?
options: East
North
West
South
questions.rationale: Turning right (clockwise) from a northward heading points you east. South would be a full reversal, west would be a left turn, and north would mean no turn was made.

questions.stem: On the yard map for Talon State Prison, the Basketball Court is in the center. Directly north of it is the Weight Pit, directly south is the Track, directly east is the Handball Wall, and directly west is the Pavilion. Which structure is across the Basketball Court from the Weight Pit?
options: The Pavilion
The Handball Wall
The Weight Pit
The Track
questions.rationale: The Weight Pit is directly north of the center, so directly opposite it across the court is the item to the south, the Track. The Handball Wall (east) and Pavilion (west) sit on the perpendicular axis, not across from the Weight Pit, and the Weight Pit cannot be across from itself.

questions.stem: A map of the administration wing is oriented with north at the top. The Warden's Office is on the left side of the building and the Human Resources Office is on the right side. Which cardinal direction is the Warden's Office from the Human Resources Office?
options: West
North
East
South
questions.rationale: With north at the top, the left side of a map is west, so the Warden's Office (left) is west of Human Resources (right). North and south are top and bottom, and east would be to the right, not the left.

questions.stem: At Brackenridge Detention Center, the Central Control room sits at the middle of a straight east-west hallway. The Visitation Room is directly to the east of Central Control, and the Property Storage room is directly to the west. If Officer Nunez leaves Central Control and walks toward the Visitation Room, which direction is she traveling?
options: North
West
South
East
questions.rationale: The Visitation Room is stated to be directly east of Central Control, so walking toward it means traveling east. West is the direction of Property Storage, the opposite way. North and South are perpendicular to the east-west hallway and are not involved in this movement.

questions.stem: The Kestrel County Jail lobby has four exits, one on each wall. The Main Entrance is on the north wall, the Sally Port is on the south wall, the Staff Door is on the east wall, and the Loading Dock is on the west wall. An officer standing in the center of the lobby faces the Main Entrance. Which exit is directly behind the officer?
options: Sally Port
Main Entrance
Staff Door
Loading Dock
questions.rationale: Facing the Main Entrance means facing north, so directly behind the officer is south, where the Sally Port is located. The Staff Door (east) and Loading Dock (west) are to the officer's right and left, not behind. The Main Entrance is what the officer faces, not what is behind.

questions.stem: On the Fairmont Correctional Facility map, Housing Unit A is at the north end of a single straight north-south corridor, and the Dining Hall is at the south end. Officer Pratt is in the Dining Hall and needs to reach Housing Unit A by the most direct path. Which direction should he walk?
options: West
South
North
East
questions.rationale: Housing Unit A is at the north end and the Dining Hall is at the south end of the same straight corridor, so the shortest route is simply to walk north. South would move him away from the unit. The corridor runs north-south, so east and west are not options along it.
questions.source: shortest route on a facility map

questions.stem: A simple map of Rosewell Jail shows the Medical Clinic in the northeast corner and the Laundry in the southwest corner of the building. Which general direction is the Laundry from the Medical Clinic?
options: Northwest
Southeast
Northeast
Southwest
questions.rationale: The Laundry is in the southwest corner and the Clinic is in the northeast corner, so from the Clinic the Laundry lies to the southwest. Northeast is where the Clinic itself is. Southeast and Northwest are the other two corners and do not match the Laundry's position.

questions.stem: The intake area at Coldwater Detention has a hallway running straight from west to east. Booking is at the west end, then Fingerprinting, then Holding Cell 1, and the Nurse Station is at the far east end. Officer Diaz starts at Booking and must escort an inmate east to the Nurse Station. Which rooms will she pass, in order?
options: Fingerprinting, then Holding Cell 1
Nurse Station, then Holding Cell 1, then Fingerprinting
Fingerprinting only
Holding Cell 1, then Fingerprinting
questions.rationale: Traveling east from Booking, the order along the hallway is Fingerprinting, then Holding Cell 1, then the Nurse Station, so she passes Fingerprinting then Holding Cell 1. The first option lists the rooms in reverse (west-to-east order flipped). The third option reverses those two rooms, and the fourth omits Holding Cell 1.

questions.stem: Ellsworth Correctional's yard is a square. The Weight Pit is at the north edge, the Track is at the south edge, the Basketball Court is at the east edge, and the Handball Wall is at the west edge. An officer at the center walks to the Basketball Court, then turns around and walks straight across the yard. What does he reach?
options: Basketball Court
Handball Wall
Weight Pit
Track
questions.rationale: The Basketball Court is on the east edge; turning around and walking straight across the yard means heading west, which leads to the Handball Wall on the west edge. The Weight Pit (north) and Track (south) are perpendicular to this path. The Basketball Court is his starting point, not his destination.

questions.stem: On a compass rose, north is at the top, south at the bottom, east on the right, and west on the left. At Thornbury Jail, an officer notes the Armory is to her right when she faces north. In which cardinal direction is the Armory?
options: West
South
North
East
questions.rationale: When facing north, the right-hand side is east, so the Armory lies to the east. West would be to her left. North is straight ahead and south is behind her, neither of which is to her right.

questions.stem: Marlowe Detention Center has one long straight corridor. From the west end the rooms are, in order: Staff Break Room, Supply Closet, Control Booth, and Roll Call Room at the east end. Officer Vance is at the Control Booth and needs to reach the Supply Closet by the shortest path. Which direction does he go?
options: East
South
North
West
questions.rationale: The Supply Closet lies just west of the Control Booth in the west-to-east order, so the shortest path is to walk west. Walking east would lead toward the Roll Call Room, away from the Supply Closet. The corridor runs east-west, so north and south do not apply.
questions.source: shortest route on a facility map

questions.stem: The map of Aldergrove Jail shows the Chapel directly north of the Gymnasium. The Library is directly east of the Chapel. Starting at the Gymnasium, an officer walks north to the Chapel and then east to the Library. From the Gymnasium, in which general direction is the Library?
options: Southwest
Northwest
Northeast
Southeast
questions.rationale: The Library is north (to reach the Chapel) and then east of that point, placing it northeast of the Gymnasium overall. Northwest would require going west, not east. Southeast and Southwest both require going south, but the path only moved north and east.

questions.stem: At Pinehaven Detention, a straight walkway runs north to south. The Sally Port is at the south end and Housing Pod 4 is at the north end. An officer walking from the Sally Port to Housing Pod 4 is moving north. On the return trip, what direction is he walking?
options: East
North
South
West
questions.rationale: If the trip from the Sally Port to Housing Pod 4 is northward, the return trip retraces the same walkway in the opposite direction, which is south. North is the outbound direction, not the return. The walkway runs north-south, so east and west are not applicable.

questions.stem: Grayson County Jail's main floor forms a plus sign of hallways meeting at Central Control. Intake is at the end of the north hallway, Kitchen at the end of the east hallway, Medical at the end of the south hallway, and Visitation at the end of the west hallway. An officer at Central Control needs to reach Medical. Which hallway should she take?
options: West hallway
South hallway
North hallway
East hallway
questions.rationale: Medical is at the end of the south hallway, so from Central Control she should take the south hallway. The north hallway leads to Intake, the east hallway to the Kitchen, and the west hallway to Visitation, none of which is Medical.

questions.stem: On the Wexford Facility map, the Guard Tower is drawn at the top of the page and the Motor Pool at the bottom. Standard maps place north at the top. In which cardinal direction is the Guard Tower from the Motor Pool?
options: East
West
South
North
questions.rationale: With north at the top of the map, the Guard Tower at the top lies north of the Motor Pool at the bottom. South would describe the Motor Pool relative to the Tower, the reverse. East and West correspond to the left-right axis, which is not involved here.

questions.stem: At Larkfield Detention Center, the main corridor runs east-west. Standing at the west end and facing east, the Laundry is the first room on your left, the Barber Shop is the first room on your right, and the Chapel is the second room on your left. Which room is on the north side of the corridor if the Laundry is on the north side?
options: Barber Shop
Chapel
The Laundry only
None of the rooms
questions.rationale: Facing east, your left hand points north, so the Laundry and the Chapel (both on your left) are on the north side; therefore the Chapel is on the north side. The Barber Shop is on your right (south). 'The Laundry only' is wrong because the Chapel shares the same left/north side. 'None' is wrong because the Chapel qualifies.
questions.source: identifying a location from a description

questions.stem: The Ashmoor County Jail visitor lot is directly south of the front entrance. The intake sally port is on the east wall of the building, and the recreation yard is on the north side. An officer standing in the visitor lot faces the front entrance to enter. In which direction is the officer facing?
options: West
North
South
East
questions.rationale: The lot is south of the entrance, so to face the entrance the officer looks from south toward the building, meaning they face north. South is the direction they came from, not where they look. East and west are perpendicular to the line between the lot and the entrance.
questions.source: identifying a location from a description

questions.stem: On the ground floor of the Redhaven Correctional Annex, the Control Room is in the exact center. The Medical Unit is directly north of Control, the Kitchen is directly south of Control, the Property Room is directly east of Control, and the Visitation Hall is directly west of Control. Which two rooms are directly opposite each other across the Control Room?
options: Property Room and Visitation Hall
Medical Unit and Kitchen
Medical Unit and Property Room
Kitchen and Visitation Hall
questions.rationale: Medical (north) and Kitchen (south) are on the same north-south line through Control, so they are directly opposite each other. Property (east) and Visitation (west) are opposite on the other axis, but that pair is offered separately. Options pairing a north/south room with an east/west room are not opposite because they sit on perpendicular axes.
questions.source: identifying a location from a description

questions.stem: A patrol officer must check three areas in order, starting at the Guard Post. From the Guard Post he walks north to the Dining Hall, then from the Dining Hall he walks east to the Library, then from the Library he walks south to the Gym. Relative to the Guard Post, in which general direction is the Gym?
options: Directly north
To the east
Directly west
Directly south
questions.rationale: The officer went north then south by equal implication returns to the Guard Post's latitude, but he also moved east once, so the Gym is east of the Guard Post. It is not directly north or south because the north and south legs cancel vertically while the east leg remains. It is not west because he never traveled west.

questions.stem: In Cellblock C at Millgate Prison, the cells are numbered 1 through 8 in a single straight row from left to right. An officer stands facing the row so that Cell 1 is on his far left and Cell 8 is on his far right. Which cell is immediately to the left of Cell 5?
options: Cell 7
Cell 3
Cell 4
Cell 6
questions.rationale: Numbers increase left to right, so the cell immediately left of Cell 5 is the next-lower number, Cell 4. Cell 6 is to the right of Cell 5. Cell 3 is two positions left, not immediate. Cell 7 is two positions right.

questions.stem: The Bellrock Facility floor plan shows a hallway shaped like a plus sign. The Sergeant's Office is at the top of the plus (north end), the Armory is at the bottom (south end), the East Wing is at the right end, and the West Wing is at the left end. All four meet at the central junction. To go from the Armory to the Sergeant's Office by the shortest route, in which direction does an officer travel?
options: East
North
South
West
questions.rationale: The Armory is at the south end and the Sergeant's Office is at the north end, so the officer travels straight north through the junction. South would move away from the office. East and west lead into the wings, not toward the office.

questions.stem: At Copperline Jail, the Booking Desk is described as being at the northeast corner of the intake room. If an officer stands in the center of the intake room and looks toward the Booking Desk, which two compass directions is the officer looking between?
options: Between north and west
Between north and east
Between south and east
Between south and west
questions.rationale: Northeast lies between north and east, so an officer looking at a northeast-corner desk is looking between those two directions. Northwest would be between north and west, southeast between south and east, and southwest between south and west, none of which match the stated corner.
questions.source: identifying a location from a description

questions.stem: A round in the Hawthorne Unit follows this order: Break Room, then Supply Closet, then Interview Room, then Control Booth. The officer has just finished checking the Supply Closet. Which area does she check next?
options: Interview Room
Break Room
Control Booth
The round is complete
questions.rationale: The Supply Closet is second in the sequence, so the next stop is the third area, the Interview Room. The Break Room was first and already done. The Control Booth is last and comes after the Interview Room. The round is not complete until the Control Booth is checked.

questions.stem: The Norwell Correctional map uses a scale where 1 inch equals 50 feet. On the map, the distance from the Watchtower to the Front Gate measures 3 inches. What is the actual distance from the Watchtower to the Front Gate?
options: 300 feet
150 feet
100 feet
50 feet
questions.rationale: At 50 feet per inch, 3 inches equals 3 x 50 = 150 feet. 50 feet corresponds to only 1 inch. 100 feet corresponds to 2 inches. 300 feet would require 6 inches on this scale.

questions.stem: In the Pinecrest Facility yard, a compass rose on the map shows north pointing up, as usual. An officer notes that Tower 2 is drawn directly below Tower 1 on the map. In real terms, Tower 2 is in which direction from Tower 1?
options: East
South
West
North
questions.rationale: On a standard map, up is north and down is south, so a tower drawn below another is south of it. North is up, not down. East is to the right and west is to the left, neither of which is 'below.'
questions.source: identifying a location from a description

questions.stem: At Stonebridge Jail, an officer walks out of the Control Room heading east down the main hall. To reach the Nurse Station, she is told to make a right turn at the first junction. After the right turn, which direction is she now facing?
options: West
South
East
North
questions.rationale: When facing east, a right turn (clockwise 90 degrees) points you south. A left turn would have pointed north. Continuing east means no turn, and west would be a U-turn or two right turns.

questions.stem: The Deerpath Annex has three floors. The map legend states that the Kitchen is on the lowest floor, the Housing Units are on the middle floor, and Administration is on the top floor. An officer takes the stairs up one flight from the Kitchen. Which area does she reach?
options: Administration
Housing Units
The roof
Kitchen
questions.rationale: The Kitchen is the lowest floor, so one flight up reaches the middle floor, which holds the Housing Units. The Kitchen is where she started. Administration is the top floor, two flights up. The roof is above Administration, not one flight up from the Kitchen.

questions.stem: At Rockvale Detention Center, the intake hallway runs left to right. From left to right, the rooms are: Booking, Fingerprinting, Holding, and Property Storage. Which room is directly to the right of Fingerprinting?
options: Booking
Property Storage
Holding
Fingerprinting
questions.rationale: Reading left to right, Holding comes immediately after Fingerprinting, so it is directly to the right. Booking is two positions to the left of Holding, not adjacent to Fingerprinting on the right. Property Storage is at the far right end, one room beyond Holding. Fingerprinting cannot be to the right of itself.

questions.stem: In Cell Block C, six cells line one wall from left to right in this order: C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, C6. Which cell is directly to the left of C4?
options: C6
C3
C5
C2
